key_facts: The EA never drives a controller directly: even a single-symbol session goes through CSSRReplayGroup (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1320 Add, :1328 Align, :2788 g_group.Pump(delta)). Every group-level behaviour, including the idle gap skip, is therefore production behaviour.

Master clock contract [CODE]: master.Advance(delta) computes the instant; every member gets PumpTo(instant) (forward-only via SSRReplayClock::AdvanceTo). After a backward SeekAllTo the master re-seeks to member[0].Now() because sinks cut bar-granular. MaxSkewMsc() over non-COMPLETED members is the alarm; T11 asserts it is 0 after pumps, speed changes, jumps, steps, restart.
Align() narrows every member's end to the common window permanently (NarrowEndTo never widens) and JumpTo(lo)s members that start earlier; it is re-run after GroupPort.Reset.

Tick synthesis [CODE]: path O->L->H->C when close>=open else O->H->L->C; stamps open + i*59999/(n-1) so first tick is exactly at the open, last at open+59999, strictly increasing for n<=59999; flags BID|ASK|LAST; last tick forced onto the close. BAR fidelity = one tick at open+59999.

EmitWindow re-reads and re-synthesises the bar containing the clock on EVERY pump that advances (controller 380-442), then trims ticks to (emitted, now]. Consequences: SpreadFor() runs once per pump per bar (counters inflate ~pumps-per-bar, ~1500x at 1x/40ms), and cursor.bar_count / BarsConsumed() counts (pump x bar) events, not bars. bar_count is shown by the panel as BARS, persisted in .pos and session files, fed to Metrics, and used by RestoreFrom as the fingerprint-less consistency check (controller 1858-1863).
Bulk writes bypass observers: SeedBars is used by warmup, JumpForward, rewind-then-forward and the group's gap skip; none publish OnBarContext/OnTicks to the trading engine (controller 1369-1392).

Future guard is inclusive (msc <= horizon allowed); FilterRates compares bar OPEN time so the partial bar containing the horizon passes and is handled by ClipBar (observers) and tick trimming (sink). Guard is disarmed only for Discover and re-armed at start; SetHorizon moves it before every read.

Snapshot = verbatim copy of state/clock/cursor/timeline; cursor.emitted may lag clock.now when the pump budget deferred work. RestoreSnapshot truncates the sink at taken_at, restores the cursor and rewinds it further only if the sink cut earlier (actual < emitted).

SnapshotStore checkpoints are taken only after Pump/PumpTo (every 5 min replay time), never in StepBars/JumpForward/SeekTo. StepBackward restores the nearest checkpoint at-or-before the target then JumpForward(target) in bulk; without a checkpoint it falls back to SeekTo and counters restart (logged).

PositionFile key defaults to the origin symbol (controller 1556/1573/1588) with only \ / : . sanitised; file is CRLF key=value text under MQL5\Files\SSReplay\positions\<key>.pos; Load only uses taken_at_msc on resume (JumpTo), so counters in the file are informational.

MT5 sink (cross-ref) hard-fails EmitTicks when ticks[0].time_msc < m_last_emit_msc and resets that watermark only in TruncateFrom (actual-1); the recording sink counts the same regression as an OrderViolation instead of failing.

The generic CSSRBarProvider::NextBarOpen goes through the guarded ReadBars and is overridden only by the Mt5 provider (CopyTime, no guard); the memory provider inherits the generic one, so the group's gap skip can never fire under any test in the tree.
No test calls CSSRMemoryDataSource::LoadTicks (grep), so FULL_TICK fidelity is only ever exercised as a degradation to SYNTHETIC in tests.
Metrics.RecordPump is documented as per-pump but Pump/PumpTo pass the cumulative cursor.bar_count as `bars` (controller 1033-1035, 1108-1110); SSRPerfSnapshot.bars has no consumer today.

findings.title: Group idle gap-skip fires mid-bar at human speeds and bulk-writes the unfinished bar, so observers (trading engine) never receive the rest of that bar's ticks
findings.claim: State: 8 synthetic ticks/bar (default), speed <= ~8x (the speeds a trainee actually trades at; any speed < 60x at BAR fidelity), 40 ms pumps, the clock inside bar B whose first tick was just emitted, and the next TWO M1 bars after B missing from the origin history (any index/futures CFD daily close, any weekend edge, any 2-minute hole in thin forex). Outcome: after 25 pumps with no tick (1 s of wall time, while the next synthetic tick is 8.57 s away), NextBarAcross returns the bar >= B_open+3min, the '> now + 2 min' test passes, SeekAllTo(nb-1) runs JumpForward on every stream, and JumpForward writes bar B in BULK (SeedBars) because bar_lo = BarOpen(emitted+1) = B_open < last_bar = BarOpen(nb-1). Ticks i=1..7 of bar B (its high, low and close path) are never emitted to observers; the trading engine's last price stays at B's open, its bar context stays the clipped first-tick bar, and a stop or target inside B's range is not evaluated until the next bar's first tick (a gap price). At BAR fidelity the bar's ONLY tick (at open+59999) vanishes, so the whole bar is invisible to the account. The printed 'market closed from <mid-bar time>' message is also misleading. On index CFDs this happens on the last bar of every trading day.
findings.evidence: Trigger arithmetic: synthetic stamps are open + i*59999/7 (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:147), so at 1x consecutive ticks are 8571 ms apart and 25 pumps x 40 ms = 1 s of idle is reached inside every minute; the condition 'nb > now + 120000' with now = B_open + ~1s holds whenever the next existing bar is >= B_open + 3 min. Skip path: SeekAllTo (line 296) -> m_member[i].JumpTo(t) -> controller JumpTo (1484) -> JumpForward (1333): lo = m_cursor.emitted_msc + 1; bar_lo = SSRBarOpenMsc(lo) (1363-1364) which is B_open when B is partially emitted; last_bar = SSRBarOpenMsc(target) = nb - 60000 (1365); 'if(last_bar > bar_lo)' (1370) is true because nb - 60000 > B_open; ReadBars(bar_lo, last_bar - 1) returns bar B and m_sink.SeedBars(bulk, n) (1383) writes it; m_cursor.Advance(last_bar - 1, 0, n) (1390) moves the cursor past B. JumpForward never calls PublishBar/PublishTicks/OnClock (1333-1420) — the header comment says so ('publishes none of them', EA 2792-2794). The comment at lines 202-204 assumes 'the pause between two live ticks - never more than a minute of bar time - is left untouched', but the threshold is measured from the mid-bar clock, not from the current bar's end. Mt5 provider NextBarOpen (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:302-321) returns the first open strictly after after_msc via CopyTime, confirming nb = next EXISTING bar. Fix direction (RECOMMENDATION): measure the gap from the end of the current bar (BarOpen(now)+60000) rather than from now, or skip only when cursor.emitted >= BarOpen(now)+59999.

findings.title: Spread statistics count synthesis calls, not bars: the bar containing the clock is re-synthesised every pump so BarsWithRecordedSpread/BarsWithFixedSpread inflate by ~pumps-per-bar
findings.claim: State: SYNTHETIC or BAR fidelity, playing at 1x with 40 ms pumps. Every pump that advances the clock calls Synthesize()/SynthesizeClose() on the current bar again (line 123 'double spread = SpreadFor(bar);' / line 197), so one M1 bar increments m_bars_recorded or m_bars_fixed ~1500 times. Outcome: the EA's ReportSpreadOnce (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2239-2300) waits for 'total >= 120 bars' and reaches it after ~5 s of the FIRST bar, then prints 'from the data on N of the first M bars' with N and M in the thousands for a handful of bars, and the average/widest are pump-weighted (bars replayed at low speed or stepped through weigh hundreds of times more than bars replayed at 30x). The author explicitly tells users to send that line as the diagnostic for whether their history carries a spread; it reports a number that is not what it says. The same counters are exposed as SpreadBarsRecorded/SpreadBarsFixed/SpreadAverage/SpreadWidest on the controller.
findings.evidence: Controller EmitWindow: bar_lo = SSRBarOpenMsc(lo) with lo = emitted+1 (380); ReadBars(bar_lo, bar_hi) returns the bar whose open == bar_lo (383); the skip loop 'while(first < nb && SSRToMsc(m_bars[first].time) < bar_lo)' (408) does not skip it; Synthesize/SynthesizeClose is called for it (441-442) and its ticks are then trimmed to (lo, hi] (461-470). Since the cursor advances to hi each pump (531) and the next pump's lo is hi+1, the same bar is read and synthesised on every pump until the clock leaves the minute. SpreadFor is unconditional inside Synthesize (123) and SynthesizeClose (197). The only test of these counters (QA smoke 2985-3001) calls Synthesize directly three times and so cannot see the inflation. RECOMMENDATION: count only when the bar's open time differs from the last counted open, or count in the controller when a bar is fully consumed.

findings.title: Generic CSSRBarProvider::NextBarOpen reads through the guarded ReadBars: it is useless inside a gap and raises up to four 'future access' violations per call
findings.claim: State: any provider that does not override NextBarOpen (the memory provider, and any future CSV/external source) with the guard armed at horizon == now. The controller calls NextTimelineBarOpen(now) from StepBars (1166) and the group from StepBars/NextBarAcross (SSR_MasterClock.mqh:348) and the idle skip (211). Each call passes from_msc = now + 1 > horizon, so CSSRFutureGuard::ClampRange records Violation(from) and returns false for every one of the four spans. Outcome: (a) the answer is always SSR_INVALID_TIME from inside a gap, so the gap skip and 'land on a bar that exists' logic silently never work with such a source; (b) the guard's violation counter — the product's leak alarm, summed into the UI vitals by GroupPort (line 143) — climbs by 4 on every step forward and by 4 per second of idle playback, indistinguishable from a real leak. T1.4 asserts Violations()==0 after pumps only; adding a single StepBars to that test would fail it.
findings.evidence: SSR_FutureGuard.mqh:312-316: 'if(from_msc > m_horizon_msc) { Violation(from_msc); return false; }'. Memory provider ReadBars (SSR_MemoryDataSource.mqh:122-127) calls GuardRange first and returns 0 when it is false. The comment at lines 143-148 acknowledges the INVALID answer ('correctly, and uselessly') but not the violation count. Production is unaffected because CSSRMt5BarProvider overrides with CopyTime (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:302). RECOMMENDATION: make the generic implementation a times-only walk that bypasses the guard (a bar's open time is schedule, not price — the Mt5 override already argues this) or have it not count violations.

findings.title: CSSRMetrics accumulates the controller's cumulative bar counter as if it were per-pump, so m_bars / SSRPerfSnapshot.bars grow quadratically
findings.claim: State: any playing session. RecordPump is documented 'One pump completed' and sums `bars`, but both callers pass `(int)m_cursor.bar_count` — the cumulative (and itself per-pump-inflated, see key facts) counter — so after P pumps m_bars is the sum 1+2+...+P of running totals. Outcome: SSRPerfSnapshot.bars is meaningless (and overflows int-cast arithmetic within a long session: at 25 pumps/s with bar_count itself in the tens of thousands, m_bars passes 2^31 in well under an hour, although it is a long so it only becomes absurd, not negative). No consumer reads perf.bars today (GroupPort reads calibrated/us_per_tick/p95 only), so the impact is confined to anyone who starts using it — which is why this is LOW rather than MEDIUM.
findings.evidence: SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1033-1035 'm_metrics.RecordPump((double)(GetMicrosecondCount() - t_pump), m_pump_emit_us, emitted, (int)m_cursor.bar_count, m_pump_deferred);' and identically at 1108-1110. `emitted` in the same call IS per-pump, so the two arguments are inconsistent. RECOMMENDATION: pass bars_used from EmitWindow (or the delta of bar_count) and, separately, fix bar_count to count distinct bars.

findings.title: CSSRMemoryDataSource::Ticks() returns NULL while no ticks are loaded, so the base SetGuard/DetachGuard skip the tick provider: ticks loaded after Attach are unguarded and the provider can keep a stale guard pointer
findings.claim: State A: ctrl.Attach(src, sink) (controller 573 -> CSSRDataSource::SetGuard, which does 'CSSRTickProvider *t = Ticks(); if(t != NULL) t.SetGuard(g)' at SSR_IDataSource.mqh:251-252) BEFORE src.LoadTicks(...). Outcome: m_ticks.m_guard stays NULL for the session; its GuardRange (SSR_IDataSource.mqh:80-85) returns from<=to without clamping, so 'guard layer 2' — the structural guarantee the header promises for every provider — does not exist for FULL_TICK reads from this source (layer 1 in the controller still clamps, so no leak today; a direct ReadTicks by a test or a future caller is unguarded). State B: ticks loaded before Attach, later LoadTicks(src, 0), then the controller is destroyed -> ~CSSRReplayController calls DetachGuard (controller 558-559) which skips m_ticks because Ticks() is NULL; a later LoadTicks + ReadTicks dereferences the freed guard. Unlike CSSRMt5DataSource, this class does not override SetGuard/DetachGuard (Mt5DataSource does at line 103). No test in the tree calls LoadTicks, so neither state is exercised.
findings.evidence: CSSRDataSource::DetachGuard (SSR_IDataSource.mqh:232-241) and SetGuard (244-253) both reach the tick provider only through the virtual Ticks() accessor; this class conditionally returns NULL from it and provides no override that touches m_ticks directly. RECOMMENDATION: override SetGuard/DetachGuard here to address m_hist/m_bars/m_ticks members directly (as the Mt5 source does), keeping the NULL-when-empty Ticks() contract for the engine.

findings.title: SnapshotStore::DropFrom leaves holes in the ring without adjusting m_count/m_head, so Count() over-reports and the next checkpoints overwrite the oldest survivors instead of refilling the holes
findings.claim: State: ring full (64 checkpoints = 5h20m of replay at the 5-min interval), user steps back through the last k checkpoints (StepBackward -> DropFrom(now+1), controller 1475). Outcome: k slots become Init()'d holes but m_count stays 64 and m_head keeps advancing over the OLDEST live slots, so the next k checkpoints destroy 5h of rewindable history at the far end while the holes near the head stay empty until the head wraps round to them; Count() (shown by GroupPort as 'checkpoints') keeps reporting 64. Rewind depth after a step back is therefore 64-k until a full wrap. Correctness of NearestAtOrBefore is unaffected (it skips taken_at<=0), which is why this is an IMPROVEMENT, not a defect in behaviour the user can observe as wrong.
findings.evidence: m_count is only incremented in Checkpoint (line 107-108 'if(m_count < SSR_CHECKPOINT_RING) m_count++') and reset in ClearCheckpoints; m_head is only advanced in Checkpoint (106). DropFrom (140-160) touches neither. T8.2 tests DropFrom with 10 entries (no wrap) and asserts only the dropped count and the newest survivor. RECOMMENDATION: on DropFrom, rewind m_head to the slot after the newest survivor and set m_count to the survivor count (entries are written in time order, so dropped entries are always the newest contiguous run behind the head).

findings.title: Position file key is the origin symbol only, so two slots or two sessions replaying the same symbol overwrite and resume each other's saved position
findings.claim: State: InpSlot=1 and InpSlot=2 (or two named InpSession sessions) both replaying EURUSD over overlapping windows in the same terminal data folder. Controller SavePosition/PeekPosition/ResumePosition default the key to m_state.symbol (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1556, 1573, 1588); GroupPort.SavePosition passes no key; the EA peeks with `origin` (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1520). Outcome: both write SSReplay\positions\EURUSD.pos; whichever saved last wins, and the other slot's next start passes the EA's only guard (saved.taken_at inside its window, >= 50 bars ahead) and resumes at a place it never reached. Marked POTENTIAL_RISK because the key choice is confirmed but the collision needs two concurrent same-symbol sessions, which the product's slot input explicitly allows but no test or documentation covers.
findings.evidence: Path() derives the file name from the key alone; no slot, session name or window is folded in. The session file (CSSRSessionManager, separate mechanism) is keyed by session name, so the two persistence paths disagree on identity. RECOMMENDATION: have the host pass a key that includes the slot or session name (the API already accepts one) and keep the symbol default for tests.

performance_notes: Per-pump floor (controller EmitWindow, evident): at 25 pumps/s the bar containing the clock is ReadBars()'d and fully re-synthesised (8 ticks) on every pump, plus three ArrayResize calls for seg_at/seg_len/seg_bar and a PublishSegment ArrayCopy; cheap in absolute terms (~tens of us) but it is why 'idle' pumps are never free, and it is the cause of the spread/bar_count inflation in core-sync-2.

Group idle heuristic (SSR_MasterClock.mqh:208-218, evident): whenever tick spacing exceeds 1 s of wall time (1x-8x with 8 ticks/bar; every speed below 60x at BAR fidelity) NextBarAcross runs every 25 pumps, i.e. one CopyTime on the origin symbol per stream per second, and each fired skip also runs RepairWarmupIfLost -> SeriesInfoInteger on the replay symbol. Not measured; likely sub-millisecond but it is a terminal call on the timer thread.

CSSRMetrics::Percentile (SSR_Metrics.mqh:162-175) allocates and ArraySorts a 256-double copy on every call and Snapshot() calls it three times; GroupPort.PerfInto runs per panel state refresh. Bounded but avoidable (keep a sorted mirror, or compute p50/p95/max in one pass).

CSSRMemoryTickProvider::ReadTicks (SSR_MemoryDataSource.mqh:190-225) scans the entire tick store twice per call (count then copy) instead of a binary search on time_msc — O(total ticks) per pump, so a FULL_TICK memory test with a realistic tick set would be dominated by this loop, not by the engine it measures.

CSSRRecordingSink::EmitTicks (SSR_RecordingSink.mqh:80-81) grows m_ticks with an exact-size ArrayResize on every emit with no reserve argument; over a long T7 run this is potentially O(n^2) copying and will skew the very numbers T7 reports (measured: not by me; the author's T7 figures include it).

CSSRSnapshotStore::Clear/ClearCheckpoints Init() 64 (+16) snapshots each holding three strings; NearestAtOrBefore/DropFrom are linear over 64 — negligible, noted only because Reset() calls ClearCheckpoints and Load() calls Clear().
test_gaps: The group's idle gap skip (SSR_MasterClock.mqh:206-219) is never executed by any test: with the memory source the generic NextBarOpen always returns INVALID inside a gap, so no test can build a dataset with a hole and observe the skip, its mid-bar trigger (core-sync-1), or its 'market closed' log line.
PropagatePause / GroupPauses / PauseReason propagation from an observer-driven auto pause on one stream to the others is not asserted (T11.9 checks only that a manual pause carries no reason).
No test asserts ctrl.Violations()==0 after StepBars/StepBackward or after group navigation; doing so would expose core-sync-3 with the memory source.

The spread counters are tested only by three direct Synthesize calls (QA smoke 2985-3001), never through a pumped session, so core-sync-2 is invisible to the suite; likewise BarsConsumed()/bar_count is never asserted against the number of distinct bars replayed.

FULL_TICK fidelity is never exercised with real ticks: no test calls CSSRMemoryDataSource::LoadTicks, so ReadTicks' half-open range, its guard clamping, the FilterTicks second layer, and duplicate-stamp tolerance for real ticks are untested.

Checkpoint-with-deferred-cursor followed by a step back: T7 forces a deferral (budget 2 ms, 30-min pump) and then only pumps forward; no test restores a checkpoint whose cursor.emitted < taken_at (the actual < emitted branch in RestoreSnapshot is the only one covered by construction).
SnapshotStore ring wrap: T8.2 uses 10 checkpoints; nothing fills 64, wraps, DropFroms and checks how many remain rewindable (core-sync-6).

CSSRPositionFile: no test for a truncated/malformed file, unknown keys, a future version string, key sanitisation of odd symbol names (e.g. '#US30', 'EURUSD.r'), an empty key, or two streams sharing a key (core-sync-7).
Align() re-run after GroupPort.Reset with members whose own start precedes the common start (JumpTo(lo) forward path inside Align) is not covered; T11 members always share g_start.

SeekAllTo partial failure (one member's JumpTo fails, the others move, master follows member[0]) and MaxSkewMsc when members' sinks cut at different bar boundaries are untested — every test uses the recording sink, which cuts at the exact instant, so the 'master follows the streams back' logic is only exercised in its trivial case.
Group StepBars when the pump budget cap bites (PumpTo leaves work owed while the member is immediately re-paused) is untested; observers would receive the remainder only on the next Play.

key_facts: Production never calls CSSRReplayController::Pump(wall_ms); the host pumps through CSSRReplayGroup::Pump -> ctrl.PumpTo(target). The stream's own clock speed is irrelevant to playback speed in production; the master clock scales the wall delta (host caps delta at max(4*InpPumpMs,100) ms).

All navigation from the panel goes through the group: StepBars -> group.StepBars (same formula as the controller, then Play();PumpTo(t);Pause() per stream); StepBackward/JumpTo/Restart -> group.SeekAllTo -> ctrl.JumpTo -> JumpForward (forward) or StepBackward (backward). Panel Restart does NOT call ctrl.Reset().

The emit window is half-open (cursor.emitted, clock.now]. The MT5 sink's TruncateFrom floors the cut to the M1 open and deletes [cut, inf); the controller re-seats the cursor from the returned cut (SeekTo/Reset: always; RestoreSnapshot: only when cut < emitted).

EmitWindow bar path reads whole M1 bars including the one containing `now`; ClipBar rebuilds the forming bar's O/H/L/C from synthesised ticks <= now so observers never see the unfinished bar's future range; ticks are trimmed to [lo,hi]. Synthetic stamps: open + i*59999/(n-1); BAR fidelity stamps one tick at open+59999.

Checkpoints: first pump after Load/Reset, then every 5 replay-minutes, taken AFTER emission (snapshot.cursor.emitted == taken_at). Ring of 64. Backward navigation restores the nearest checkpoint <= target and then JumpForward()s to the target, which writes the intervening bars to the sink in bulk (SeedBars) and publishes nothing to observers.

Fidelity: m_ticks_available is set once at Load from range.has_ticks (MT5 Discover probes only the last 24h of held data) and the host requests FULL_TICK whenever that probe succeeds. Nothing re-evaluates tick availability per window; EmitWindow at FULL_TICK consumes a window that returned 0 ticks as if it were emitted.

Warmup is expressed as 'bars' (InpWarmupBars=1000) but SSRReplayTimeline::SetWarmupBars computes warmup_first = start - bars*60000, i.e. calendar minutes; the host's replay window is counted in real bars via CopyRates but the warmup is not.

CSSRPumpBudget's ceiling is derived from measured us/tick (wall clock) -> the per-pump cap value is machine-dependent; uncalibrated fallback is 4096 ticks (512 bars at 8 tpb), calibrated floor is 32 ticks (4 bars at 8 tpb). Budget is 12 ms; the host never calls SetPumpBudgetMs.

The commit 771fab2 states the test suite was run once on a terminal (1,157 assertions, 1,143 passed) - so the tests have been executed at least once, but T1.7 asserts only `after10 > start` for ten StepBars(1) calls and T7.6 asserts only that ticks keep arriving after a capped pump; neither assertion can detect the StepBars no-op or the cap-drop found below.
The controller writes nothing to charts and nothing to disk except CSSRPositionFile (SavePosition) and the session file via SaveInto; every market write goes through CSSRReplaySink.

findings.title: Per-pump budget cap silently DROPS bars instead of deferring them (dead 'stop short' branch)
findings.claim: When EmitWindow reads more M1 bars than the budget allows, the bars above the cap are never emitted: the cursor is advanced to `hi` (the clock), so the next pump starts after them. Scenario: calibrated us/tick = 400us (MaxTicks clamps to 32 -> MaxBars(8) = 4); user at 10:05:59.999 presses PgDn (StepBars(10) -> group Play();PumpTo(10:15:59.999)); EmitWindow reads 10 bars, nb is overwritten to 4, bars 10:10..10:15 are neither written to the custom symbol nor published to the trading engine, cursor.emitted becomes 10:15:59.999. The chart shows a 6-minute hole, any SL/TP inside those bars is never evaluated, and the UI reports the pump as 'deferred' (m_pump_deferred / NoteDeferral) although the data was discarded. The same happens for any pump whose owed span exceeds the cap (large delta after a stall at high speed).
findings.evidence: Line 399-404 overwrite `nb = cap`. The loop at line 437 runs `i = first..nb-1` and increments `bars_used` for every iteration (w > 0 is guaranteed because m_ticks was resized to `need` at line 418), so after the loop `first + bars_used == nb` always holds and the condition at line 524 `(first + bars_used) < nb` is false whenever the cap bit. `consumed_to` therefore stays `hi` and line 531 `m_cursor.Advance(consumed_to, ...)` moves the cursor past the unread bars. The comment at lines 519-522 documents the opposite intent ('Anything above it stays owed'). T7.6 cannot catch this: after the capped pump it only checks that TicksEmitted keeps rising, which the following bars satisfy. Because the cap comes from wall-clock measurement (CSSRPumpBudget::MaxTicks via CSSRMetrics::UsPerTick), the emitted stream also becomes machine-dependent, breaking the determinism claim. Trigger frequency on a real terminal depends on the measured cost of CustomTicksAdd (unmeasured in the repo); the logic error itself is unconditional.

findings.title: StepBars(n) from a bar end advances n-1 bars; StepBars(1) is a no-op after the first step
findings.claim: Every StepBars lands the clock on xx:59.999 (the last ms of a bar). From that position the formula yields target == now for bars==1, so the next '->' press does nothing; PgDn (10) advances only 9 bars. Scenario: fresh Load (now = 10:00:00.000) -> StepBars(1): base = 10:01:00.000, target = 10:00:59.999, one bar emitted. Press '->' again: now = 10:00:59.999, SSRNextBarOpenMsc = 10:01:00.000, NextTimelineBarOpen = 10:01:00.000 (dense data), target = 10:01:00.000 - 1 = 10:00:59.999 == now; `m_clock.now_msc > before` is false, nothing is emitted, returns 0. The step key therefore works once per play/pause cycle. The group's StepBars in SSR_MasterClock.mqh line 347-351 uses the identical formula on the master clock, so the production path (Panel -> GroupPort -> group.StepBars -> PumpTo(t)) has the same no-op: AdvanceTo(t) with t <= now returns without advancing.
findings.evidence: SSRNextBarOpenMsc(msc) = SSRBarOpenMsc(msc)+60000 (SSR_Time.mqh line 37-43). For now = open+59999, SSRBarOpenMsc floors to `open`, so base = open+60000 and target = open+60000-1 = open+59999 = now. `nb` (first bar strictly after now) equals base in dense data and cannot raise it. Lines 1173-1178 then skip emission because now did not move. T1.7 (SSR_T1_CoreEngine.mq5 line 283-291) calls StepBars(1) ten times but asserts only `after10 > start`, which the first step alone satisfies; no test asserts the position after repeated steps.

findings.title: JumpForward feeds bulk bars to the sink but never to observers; StepBackward routes through it, so every step back replays up to 5 minutes blind to the trading engine
findings.claim: The bulk range [bar_lo, last_bar-1] is written with SeedBars only; no PublishBar/PublishTicks call exists on that path, so CSSRTradingEngine (which evaluates SL/TP only inside OnTicks) never sees those bars. StepBackward (line 1451-1459) restores the nearest checkpoint (<= 5 replay-minutes earlier) and then calls JumpForward(target). Scenario: long opened 10:40 with SL 1.1000; SL is hit at 10:45:40; at 10:47:30 the user presses '<-' (StepBackward(1), target 10:46:00). Checkpoint 10:45:00 is restored, OnRewind(10:45:00) unwinds the 10:45:40 stop-out (position open again), JumpForward(10:46:00) bulk-writes bar 10:45 and publishes nothing, then emits only the 10:46:00.000 open tick. The position is now open at 10:46 although the chart shows the stop being hit inside bar 10:45; on the next tick CheckStops fires at whatever the current price is (or never, if price recovered). Every '<-' press, bookmark return, J-jump forward and session resume through JumpTo reproduces the same divergence between chart and account.
findings.evidence: JumpForward lines 1333-1420 contain m_sink.SeedBars and m_cursor.Advance for the bulk part and EmitWindow only for the bar containing the target (line 1397-1398). Observers are reached exclusively via PublishBar/PublishTicks/PublishSegment (lines 191-231), which are called only from EmitWindow (lines 366, 506-515). CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh line 599-614) is the only place CheckStops/CheckPendings/CheckStopout run; OnBarContext only caches the bar. StepBackward calls JumpForward at line 1458 after RestoreSnapshot. The host comment at SSReplayStandalone.mq5 ~line 2795 ('A JUMP WRITES ITS BARS IN BULK and publishes none of them') acknowledges the behaviour for the strategy view but nothing compensates for the account. The design rationale (avoid tick injection for fast-forward) is sound for the sink; it does not require observers to be skipped.

findings.title: FULL_TICK window with zero broker ticks is consumed silently; tick availability is never re-evaluated per window
findings.claim: When the requested fidelity is FULL_TICK and ReadTicks returns 0 for a window in which M1 bars exist, EmitWindow advances the cursor to `hi` with no ticks, no bar context and no fallback. The chart does not move, the trading engine receives no prices, and no error or degradation is reported. Scenario: broker keeps 1 month of tick history but years of M1; user starts a replay 3 months back (InpStart, picker, or random start). Load sets m_ticks_available = range.has_ticks, which MT5 Discover computes by probing only the last 24 h of held data (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh line 133-139), so it is true; the host requests FULL_TICK (SSReplayStandalone.mq5 line 1153). Every pump reads (lo-1, hi] ticks -> 0 -> `m_cursor.Advance(hi, 0, 0)`. The clock runs, Progress advances, the panel says 'FULL TICK', and the market is frozen for the whole tick-less stretch. The group's weekend-skip does not help because NextBarOpen finds M1 bars 1 minute ahead.
findings.evidence: Lines 349-369: no branch handles n == 0 while bars exist; the only degradation trigger is `tp == NULL` (line 337-346), and CSSRFidelityPolicy::Decide (SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh line 114-118) consults m_ticks_available which is set only at Load (line 806) and at line 344. CSSRTickProvider::HasTicks(symbol, from, to) exists (SSR_IDataSource.mqh line 179) but is never called by the controller. Whether a given broker's tick depth is shorter than its M1 depth is an inference about deployments (it is the common case for MT5 brokers); the engine behaviour for that case is confirmed from code.

findings.title: bars_consumed counts a bar once per pump that touches it, not once; the panel 'Bars' figure and the legacy resume check are wrong by 10-1500x
findings.claim: EmitWindow re-reads and re-synthesises the M1 bar containing `now` on every pump (needed for ClipBar), and `bars_used++` runs unconditionally for every bar read, so cursor.bar_count grows by one per pump per overlapping bar. At 1x with InpPumpMs=40 (about 25 pumps/s) a single replay minute adds ~1500 to bars_consumed; at 100x each bar is counted ~15 times. Consequences: the Stats tab 'Bars' line (SSR_Panel.mqh line 1687, from GroupPort BarsConsumed()) is meaningless; RestoreFrom's fallback for session files without a fingerprint (line 1858-1863) compares this inflated live count with the count produced by JumpTo (which counts bulk bars once) and will always warn that broker history changed; CSSRTickSynthesizer::SpreadFor is likewise invoked once per pump per bar, so SpreadBarsRecorded/SpreadBarsFixed (used in the host's session summary, SSReplayStandalone.mq5 line 2239-2298) are inflated the same way.
findings.evidence: Lines 380-383 read bars [floor(lo), floor(hi)] every pump; a 40 ms pump at 1x has floor(lo) == floor(hi) == the current bar, so nb == 1 and the loop at 437 executes once, incrementing bars_used (line 472) regardless of `keep`. Line 531 `m_cursor.Advance(consumed_to, emitted, bars_used)` adds it to bar_count; Publish() copies bar_count into m_state.bars_consumed (line 185). Synthesize() is called at line 440-442 on every iteration and calls SpreadFor (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh line 123), which increments m_bars_recorded/m_bars_fixed.

findings.title: Warmup 'bars' are calendar minutes: a Monday-morning start seeds almost no warmup and the HTF chart opens empty
findings.claim: SetWarmupBars(1000) subtracts 1000 calendar minutes (16h40m) from the start instead of walking back 1000 existing M1 bars. Scenario: replay start Monday 02:00 server time (a natural 'start of the week' choice); warmup_first = Sunday 09:20; forex has no bars until Monday 00:00, so SeedWarmup reads ~120 bars instead of 1000. An H4 chart opens with one candle and a D1 chart with one; a 200-period MA on M15 has 8 bars of context. This is exactly the failure the file header says the warmup field exists to prevent ('my H4 chart is empty when replay starts'). WarmupBarsFor(tf, visible) (line 94-100) has the same calendar arithmetic, so the setup panel's quoted cost is also in minutes. The host already counts the replay window in real bars via CopyRates (SSReplayStandalone.mq5 line 1078-1085) precisely because of this weekend effect, but does not do so for the warmup.
findings.evidence: Line 80 is pure time arithmetic on start_msc; SeedWarmup (SSR_ReplayController.mqh line 880-885) then reads bars whose open lies in [warmup_first, start-1], so every weekend/holiday minute inside that span yields no bar. No caller converts a bar count to a timestamp through the data (grep: SetWarmupBars is called with InpWarmupBars directly at SSReplayStandalone.mq5 line 498 and 1149).

findings.title: RestoreSnapshot re-seats the cursor only when the sink cut strictly before the checkpoint; a checkpoint on an M1 open loses that bar's open tick
findings.claim: The sink contract deletes everything AT or after the returned cut, while the cursor claims everything up to and INCLUDING emitted_msc was delivered. A checkpoint is taken after emission, so snap.cursor.emitted == snap.taken_at. When the MT5 sink's cut (floor to M1 open) equals taken_at - i.e. the checkpoint fell exactly on a bar open - `actual == emitted`, the cursor is not rewound, and the tick stamped exactly at that instant (the synthesised open tick, i=0) is deleted from the custom symbol but never re-emitted. The rebuilt M1 bar then opens at the second synthetic tick's price (open + 8571 ms, ~43% along the first path segment), so the chart shows a candle whose open differs from the broker's bar. Trigger requires a pump to land on an exact minute boundary at checkpoint time, which is rare with jittery wall deltas but not impossible (with fixed 40 ms pumps at 100x every 5-minute checkpoint lands on a boundary). SeekTo (line 1236) and Reset (line 1285) use RewindTo(actual) unconditionally and are correct.
findings.evidence: SSR_IReplaySink.mqh line 304-317 defines TruncateFrom as 'Everything at or after from_msc must cease to exist'; SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh line 720-743 deletes rates and ticks from floor(from) and returns floor(from). SSR_ReplayCursor.mqh line 25 defines emitted_msc as the last instant handed to the sink. Pump line 1015-1017 emits PendingRange(now) -> cursor.Advance(hi=now) before the checkpoint at line 1039-1044, so emitted == taken_at. The strict `<` at line 1637 leaves emitted == actual when the two coincide.

findings.title: RestoreSnapshot overwrites live settings (fidelity, speed, status, last_error) with the checkpoint's copy, desynchronising m_state from the policy object
findings.claim: SSRReplayState carries fidelity, speed_x100, status and last_error. Restoring a checkpoint copies all of them back, but CSSRFidelityPolicy (m_fidelity) and the master clock are not restored. Scenario: user starts at SYNTHETIC, later switches the panel to BAR (SetFidelity -> m_state.fidelity = BAR, m_fidelity.SetRequested(BAR)), then presses '<-'. RestoreSnapshot puts m_state.fidelity back to SYNTHETIC while m_fidelity.Requested() stays BAR; GroupPort line 110 reads c.Fidelity() (m_state) and line 111 EffectiveFidelity() (policy), so the panel shows requested SYNTHETIC / effective BAR as if the policy had degraded, and SaveInto persists the stale value. m_clock.speed_x100 also reverts (harmless for playback in group mode because PumpTo ignores it, but SaveInto writes the stale per-stream speed). ClearError() at line 1612 is undone by the copy of last_error.
findings.evidence: SetFidelity (line 671-676) writes both m_state.fidelity and m_fidelity; RestoreSnapshot restores only m_state. Fidelity() accessor (line 628) returns m_state.fidelity. SSRReplayState fields at SSR_ReplayState.mqh lines 33-40.

findings.title: RecordPump is handed the cumulative bar_count as the per-pump bar figure, so CSSRMetrics.m_bars grows quadratically
findings.claim: CSSRMetrics::RecordPump does `m_bars += bars` (SSR_Metrics.mqh line 476), expecting the bars consumed by THIS pump, but both Pump (line 1035) and PumpTo (line 1110) pass the cursor's running total. After k pumps SSRPerfSnapshot.bars equals the sum of the totals seen so far, not the total. The figure is exposed through PerfInto() but no UI consumer reads perf.bars today, so the impact is confined to diagnostics/flight recorder output; it becomes wrong the moment someone displays it.
findings.evidence: Line 1035/1110 pass `(int)m_cursor.bar_count`; SSR_Metrics.mqh line 470-476 accumulates it. Contrast `emitted`, which is correctly per-pump.

findings.title: Load() leaves the future guard disarmed on every failure path after Discover
findings.claim: The guard is disarmed for discovery and only re-armed at SeedWarmup (line 878) or line 832. If Discover, SetWindow, Ensure, clock Configure or sink Prepare fails, the controller is in ERROR with an unarmed guard that is still installed in the data source's providers. Any later provider read through this source (e.g. the catalogue or a group NextBarAcross call on a stream that failed to load, or FingerprintUpTo if the previous timeline is still valid) is unguarded. No production path currently emits such data to the user, so this is a hardening gap rather than a demonstrated leak.
findings.evidence: Disarm at line 764; the only Arm calls in Load are at lines 878 and 832, both after every early return. Reset() re-arms (line 1288) but is only reached if the host calls it.

findings.title: Improvements: stale cursor comment in SaveInto, dead SSR_BAR_READ_CEILING, bulk threshold off by 1 ms for PgDn, degraded FULL_TICK skips the bulk rule
findings.code:
//  The cursor goes too. Without it a resumed session would re-emit
  //  bars the sink already holds, or skip ones it does not.
findings.claim: (a) SaveInto writes emitted/ticks/bars but RestoreFrom never reads them (it rebuilds via JumpTo), so the comment misdescribes the mechanism. (b) `#define SSR_BAR_READ_CEILING 8192` (line 42) is referenced nowhere. (c) StepBars(10) from xx:59.999 owes 599,999 ms, one millisecond under SSR_BULK_THRESHOLD_MSC (600,000), so PgDn is never a 'bulk moment' while an 11-bar step is; the threshold comparison should be on bar count or use `>`-style rounding. (d) In CSSRFidelityPolicy::Decide the NO_TICK_DATA branch is an `if/else if`, so a FULL_TICK request that degrades to SYNTHETIC ignores the bulk rule and a 33-hour catch-up runs at 8 ticks/bar instead of BAR.
findings.evidence: RestoreFrom lines 1766-1866 read origin/now/speed/fidelity/auto_pause/bookmarks/fingerprint/bars only. grep shows SSR_BAR_READ_CEILING only at its definition. SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh lines 114-129.

performance_notes: EmitWindow re-reads the current M1 bar from the provider and re-synthesises 8 ticks for it on EVERY pump (25 pumps/s at InpPumpMs=40), even when the 40 ms window contains no synthetic tick (ticks are spaced ~8.6 s apart at 1x). At low speeds >90% of pumps do a ReadBars + Synthesize + ClipBar + two ArrayResize(seg_*) calls for zero output. Caching the last bar/its synthesised ticks keyed by bar open would remove almost all of that work.

EmitWindow allocates three local arrays (seg_at, seg_len, seg_bar) with ArrayResize per call (line 426-434) and PublishSegment copies each segment via ArrayCopy; at 8 ticks/bar this is small, but it is inside the hot path on every pump.

FULL_TICK path applies no budget cap: a StepBars(10) on a busy symbol reads up to 10 minutes of real ticks in one CopyTicksRange and pushes them through sink.EmitTicks in a single call (tens of thousands of ticks -> seconds of stall at ~100 us/tick). The bulk rule only kicks in at >= 10 minutes and only degrades to BAR when the policy is not locked.
FingerprintUpTo hashes every M1 bar from start to now (SaveInto); called at OnDeinit and on session save - O(session length), fine for 2000-bar sessions, noticeable for InpHistoryBars-scale windows.
CSSRMetrics::Percentile sorts a 256-sample copy on every PerfInto call; cheap but called on each panel refresh if vitals are shown.
Checkpoint snapshots copy four structs incl. strings every 5 replay-minutes; negligible. StepBackward cost is bounded by one checkpoint interval of bulk SeedBars plus a partial EmitWindow.
test_gaps: No test asserts the clock position after repeated StepBars(1) (T1.7 checks only `after10 > start`), so the 'step works once' defect (core-engine-2) is invisible to the suite.
T7.6 checks that ticks continue after a capped pump but not that the withheld bars are the ones delivered (no per-bar accounting against the source), so cap-induced bar loss (core-engine-1) passes.
No test drives a StepBackward/JumpForward with an open virtual position whose SL/TP lies inside the bulk range and asserts the account outcome equals the straight-play outcome (core-engine-3).
No test feeds a source whose tick provider returns 0 ticks for a window that has bars while has_ticks is true, and asserts degradation or an error (core-engine-4).
No test asserts bars_consumed == number of distinct M1 bars after N pumps at 1x (core-engine-5), nor SpreadBarsRecorded == distinct bars.
No test places the replay start on a Monday after a weekend gap and asserts the warmup bar count equals InpWarmupBars (core-engine-6).
No test takes a checkpoint at an exact M1 open and asserts the rebuilt bar's open price after RestoreSnapshot (core-engine-7).
No determinism test compares two full runs with identical target sequences on different budget calibrations (i.e. with the cap forced to bite) and asserts identical sink content.

Tests that reach MetaTrader (T3+, T7.6 on a real sink) have been run once per commit 771fab2; the core tests use the in-memory source and recording sink, whose TruncateFrom semantics (exact instant) differ from the MT5 sink (floor to M1 open), so cursor/cut boundary cases are exercised only in the easy mode.

key_facts: Sink lifecycle per controller Load: OnWarmupPlanned(from,start-1) -> Prepare (cache check BEFORE Create/Adopt, because Create destroys the symbol) -> NeedsWarmup=!reused -> SeedBars (warmup as CustomRatesUpdate) -> EmitTicks (replay as CustomTicksAdd) -> TruncateFrom on rewind/reset/snapshot (both stores cut at the same M1 open, returns the actual cut).

Three doors into a live symbol: Create (fresh; unconditional Destroy of any same-named symbol first, forces SYMBOL_CHART_MODE_BID with read-back, added v120 commit 9235491), Adopt (cache hit or one-window pass 2; re-applies SPREAD_FLOAT/TRADE_MODE/sessions/money props but NOT chart mode), and Create's leftover-adopt fallback (uses SYMBOL_DIGITS>0 as the existence test).
SSR_VERSION is "0.1.0" and has never changed in 169 commits (only dc87fa3 touches it); SSR_BUILD (v125) is a separate header. The seed-cache manifest version guard therefore never rejects anything.

The seed cache only gets a real hit in the product on pass 2 of the one-window handover (Release() runs only on REASON_REMOVE/PROGRAM/CLOSE, EA:2152-2204, so symbol and manifest survive REASON_CHARTCHANGE). SetCacheEnabled has no callers; cache is always on.

CSSRCustomSymbolSink destructor destroys the symbol whenever m_own_symbol (default true) and IsCreated(); SetOwnsSymbol(false) is called only by test T6, never by the EA, whose g_sink/g_sink2 are globals.

Manager::CloseCharts() closes every chart whose ChartSymbol equals the replay symbol with no exclusion for ChartID(); Destroy() is reached from Release() during pass-2 OnDeinit right after an asynchronous ChartSetSymbolPeriod back to the origin (EA:2194-2204).

Manager::Destroy() sets m_created=false and calls Succeed() regardless of whether CustomSymbolDelete succeeded; the bool return is the only signal and no caller in the sink reads it. Prepare ignores the return of Truncate(warmup_to+1) and ClearAll() cannot fail by signature.
m_chart_mode_ok is written only by Create and read by nobody (grep across MQL5/); SessionDays/SessionNote likewise have no reader outside the manager's own PrintFormat.

Timeline snaps start_msc to an M1 open (ReplayTimeline:63) so warmup_to = start-1 is the last millisecond of the previous minute; Reset truncates at start and therefore never invalidates the manifest.
All non-M1 SSRBarOpenMsc callers (StrategyHost, MarketView, ChartManager) guard with SSRIsSupportedTimeframe first, so the helper's documented W1/MN1 misalignment is not reachable.

findings.title: Warmup repair after a jump is silently skipped whenever the seed was reused from the cache
findings.claim: Session where CanReuse() returned true (m_reused_seed=true, e.g. pass 2 of the one-window handover, or T6 run 2). User jumps forward; the terminal drops the tick-less warmup bars (measured behaviour documented at SSR_IReplaySink.mqh:84-90 and SSR_ReplayController.mqh:913-918). RepairWarmupIfLost (controller:934-968) sees OldestMsc() > warmup_first, reads the warmup bars again and calls SeedBars(seed,n). The bars end at start-1 so is_warmup is true, and because m_reused_seed is still true the method returns true without calling WriteBars. Nothing is written back, yet the controller logs 'the sink dropped the warmup ... N bars written back' (controller:963-967). The chart keeps only the post-jump tail for the rest of the session; every subsequent jump repeats the same silent no-op.
findings.evidence: m_reused_seed is set once in Prepare (line 162) and never cleared for the life of the session; the early return keys only on it and on the bar range, so it cannot distinguish the initial warmup delivery (which the cache legitimately covers) from a later repair of bars the terminal has since discarded. The controller cannot tell either: SeedBars reports success. The next session self-heals only because CanReuse's SERIES_FIRSTDATE evidence check misses.

findings.title: Adopt() does not force SYMBOL_CHART_MODE_BID, so an adopted LAST-mode symbol keeps building no candles from ticks
findings.claim: A replay symbol for an index/futures CFD (e.g. US30.SSR1) created by a build before v120 (commit 9235491 added the BID force to Create only) carries SYMBOL_CHART_MODE_LAST. When v125 enters through Adopt instead of Create - the EA starting on a leftover replay chart (on_replay=true, the exact 'the next run will simply reuse' case at EA:2197-2199), or a seed-cache hit whose manifest passes the inert version check (mt5-symbol-6) - the mode is never corrected. Replay ticks are accepted and build no bar: the 'candles do not build from the ticks' symptom the Create comment (356-382) calls the defect that outlived every other. m_chart_mode_ok also stays at its constructor value false after Adopt, so the read-back diagnostic reports a failure that did not happen (no reader exists today).
findings.evidence: Create sets SYMBOL_CHART_MODE at line 383 and reads it back into m_chart_mode_ok at 387-389; Adopt (431-497) lists the overrides it re-applies and CHART_MODE is absent, contradicting its own comment about symbols 'created before one of them existed'. CustomSymbolSetInteger properties persist with the symbol across terminal restarts, so a pre-v120 clone keeps LAST. Reachability requires a pre-v120 symbol to survive into an Adopt path; within a single build both entry points produce BID symbols.

findings.title: Create()'s leftover-adopt fallback uses the SYMBOL_DIGITS>0 existence test that Adopt() documents as wrong for whole-point instruments
findings.claim: Origin is an instrument with SYMBOL_DIGITS == 0 (the case the Adopt comment at 434-450 says it hit on US30). Destroy() at line 318 fails to remove a leftover replay symbol (a chart still open on it, or the ChartClose race the header describes), CustomSymbolCreate then fails because the name exists, and the fallback evaluates exists=false because DIGITS is 0. Create returns SSR_ERR_INTERNAL 'CustomSymbolCreate(...) failed' and the session dies with SINK_FAILED, instead of adopting and clearing the leftover as the comment at 332-336 intends. T3.7 ('a leftover symbol is adopted, not fatal') passes only on instruments with digits>0.
findings.evidence: The Adopt() comment explicitly records that '<= 0 digits' was misread as 'no such symbol' and replaced it with SYMBOL_EXIST plus SYMBOL_CUSTOM; the same test survived unchanged in Create's fallback 100 lines earlier. Note also the fallback does not check SYMBOL_CUSTOM, so it is both stricter (digits) and looser (ownership) than Adopt.

findings.title: CloseCharts() will close the chart the EA itself runs on if that chart still reports the replay symbol during teardown
findings.claim: One-window mode, pass 2: the EA is attached to the chart showing the replay symbol. User removes the EA. OnDeinit calls ChartSetSymbolPeriod(ChartID(), g_origin, _Period) - documented as asynchronous at EA:2186 - then g_ctrl.Release() -> sink.Release() -> m_mgr.Destroy() -> CloseCharts(). If ChartSymbol(ChartID()) still returns the replay symbol at that instant, ChartClose(ChartID()) closes the user's own window instead of returning it to the origin. The EA comment (2178-2189) anticipates only that the DELETE may lose the race, not that the close loop may hit the host chart.
findings.evidence: CloseCharts iterates every chart and matches purely on symbol; there is no `id == ChartID()` exclusion, and the same loop runs from the destructor and from Create()'s Destroy(). Whether ChartSymbol() reflects a pending ChartSetSymbolPeriod synchronously is terminal behaviour the author has not measured, so the outcome is not verifiable from source.

findings.title: Sink destructor tears the symbol down on any object death; the EA never transfers ownership for the REASON_CHARTCHANGE handover
findings.claim: Pass 1 of the one-window handover: Load() has created the symbol (m_own_symbol=true, IsCreated()=true), then the first timer tick calls ChartSetSymbolPeriod to the replay symbol. OnDeinit(REASON_CHARTCHANGE) deliberately does not call Release() (EA:2122-2125, 2152-2204) so the symbol survives for pass 2. But g_sink is a global object (EA:190) and SetOwnsSymbol(false) is never called by the EA (only T6 does). If the terminal destroys and re-creates EA globals on a chart change - which the EA's own comment at ~1866 asserts ('globals are re-initialised') - this destructor runs, CloseCharts() closes the chart being handed over, and CustomSymbolDelete removes the symbol pass 2 is about to adopt; pass 2 then fails with 'no symbol to adopt'. If instead MQL5 preserves EA globals across REASON_CHARTCHANGE, the destructor never fires and the finding is latent only.
findings.evidence: The intent to keep the symbol across CHARTCHANGE is expressed only in the EA by not calling Release(); the sink has no knowledge of that intent, and its ownership flag defaults to true. The author reports pass 2 adopting successfully on the user's terminal, which suggests the destructor does not run there; the code nonetheless has two contradictory beliefs about global lifetime and no guard that makes the handover safe under both.

findings.title: Prepare() discards the result of the truncate/clear that removes the previous session's replay data
findings.claim: Cache-hit path: the adopted symbol holds the previous session's replay bars and ticks after start_msc. If CustomRatesDelete or CustomTicksDelete returns -1 here (Truncate returns -1 and sets SINK_FAILED on the manager), Prepare still sets m_prepared=true and returns true; the previous session's candles remain on the chart as this session's future, and the engine proceeds to emit ticks into a symbol that already contains them (the 'hidden-but-present future' the header at 18-21 names as the product's defining failure). The adopt-existing and fresh paths have the same shape: ClearAll() (Manager:747-756) drops both delete return values and always returns true.
findings.evidence: Truncate() has a documented -1 failure return that TruncateFrom() honours (Sink:348-353) but Prepare ignores; ClearAll has no failure path at all. Whether the delete calls can fail in this state on the user's terminal is not verifiable from source, so the trigger is unproven; the unchecked result is.

findings.title: Seed-cache version guard compares against a constant that has never changed, so it never rejects a manifest
findings.code:
if(m.version != SSR_VERSION)
  { m_last_reason = "written by another version"; m_misses++; return false; }
findings.claim: SSR_VERSION is "0.1.0" (SSR_Types.mqh:35) in every one of the 169 commits; the build stamp that actually changes (SSR_BUILD, v125) is not part of the manifest. A manifest and symbol written by any earlier build - including pre-v120 builds whose index-CFD symbols are LAST-mode (mt5-symbol-2) - are accepted for reuse by v125 as long as range and origin match. The guard's stated purpose ('written by another version') is unfulfilled.
findings.evidence: git log -S on the SSR_VERSION definition returns only the initial Phase 1 commit dc87fa3; SSR_Build.mqh carries the per-build stamp separately and SSRSeedManifest.Init() copies only SSR_VERSION.

findings.title: Destroy() reports SSR_OK and marks the symbol gone even when CustomSymbolDelete fails
findings.claim: A chart remains open on the replay symbol (or the 50 ms pause was not enough for the terminal to release it). CustomSymbolDelete returns false; m_created becomes false and LastError is reset to OK. Sink::Release()/destructor ignore the bool, so nothing is logged and IsCreated() now says the symbol is gone while it still sits in the terminal - the orphan accumulation the file header (10-15) warns produces 'forty dead symbols in the Market Watch tree'. The extra-stream sinks (g_sink2) have no host-side log for this case at all; only the on-replay path prints at EA:2197.
findings.evidence: The Succeed() call is unconditional and the comment justifies it only for the never-existed case; GetLastError() after the failed delete is discarded (ResetLastError at 556 precedes it, nothing reads it after).

performance_notes: WriteBars/AddTicks copy every slice element-by-element into a fresh local array (Manager:609-616, 668-675) before each CustomRatesUpdate/CustomTicksAdd; for a 100k-bar warmup that is 10 allocations plus 100k struct copies on top of the API cost. ArrayCopy on struct arrays would remove the loop; measured seed rate is recorded by the controller (SeedBarsPerSec) so the effect is directly measurable.

CanReuse() reads SERIES_BARS_COUNT/FIRSTDATE/LASTBAR_DATE on the replay symbol's M1 series without priming (SeedCache:189-195). Ground truth says an untouched timeframe answers 0 on first read; if that applies to M1 of a custom symbol with no chart open (pass 1 after a terminal restart), the cache always misses there and the full Destroy (170 ms of pauses) + recreate + reseed runs. Harmless for correctness, but it would make the cache benefit exist only on pass 2.

Destroy() sleeps 50 ms + 120 ms unconditionally on every successful delete; Create() calls Destroy() first, so every fresh session and every extra stream pays 170 ms before CustomSymbolCreate, and OnDeinit pays it per symbol.

Apply247Sessions() issues at least 14 CustomSymbolSetSession* calls plus 7 read-backs per Create/Adopt and up to 16 more deletes per uncovered day; runs once per symbol per session so it is not a hot path.
EmitTicks is the pump hot path: one ArrayResize+copy per 4096-tick slice and one CustomTicksAdd; the pump budget (40 ms) bounds the count, and m_emit_time_ms/TicksPerSecond expose the measured cost.
test_gaps: No test covers RepairWarmupIfLost when the seed was reused (mt5-symbol-1): T6 tests reuse and T3/T11 test jumps, but never a jump inside a reused session followed by a check that OldestMsc() returned to warmup_first.

No test enters Adopt() with a symbol whose SYMBOL_CHART_MODE is LAST and asserts that ticks build bars afterwards (mt5-symbol-2); T3.7 only exercises Create's fallback on a leftover and T6 adopts a symbol the same build just created.

T3.7 ('a leftover symbol is adopted, not fatal') will pass on a forex origin and fail on a SYMBOL_DIGITS==0 instrument (mt5-symbol-3); it should run against a whole-point origin or a symbol whose digits are forced to 0.

T5.2 encodes the retired 8-stop ladder: CheckEq(8, SSR_SPEED_LADDER_SIZE), CheckEq(SSR_SPEED_50, SSRSpeedLadder(7)), CheckEq(2, SSRSpeedLadderIndex(SSR_SPEED_1)) (SSR_T5_Ui.mq5:109-112) against SSR_Types' 20-stop ladder where size is 20, Ladder(7) is 300 and 1x sits at index 4 - the test is stale and would fail as written.

No test exercises CloseCharts()/Destroy() while the calling program's own chart is on the replay symbol (mt5-symbol-4), nor the global-destructor path across REASON_CHARTCHANGE (mt5-symbol-5); both are only observable on a real terminal and neither T3/T4 nor QA Smoke simulate the one-window handover.

Session boundary of 86399 s vs the synthesizer's last tick at bar.time + 59.999 s (TickSynthesizer:132,147,194): spike B3 measures session behaviour but nothing asserts that the 23:59:59.999 tick of the day's final bar is used to build the 23:59 candle; the author explicitly declined to change 86399 without a measurement, so that measurement is the gap.

SeedCache.Path() sanitises only backslash, slash and colon; no test writes a manifest for a replay symbol containing other Windows-illegal filename characters to confirm Save() fails loudly rather than silently returning false.

No test asserts the sink's Prepare() fails when Truncate()/ClearAll() cannot remove prior replay data (mt5-symbol-6); T6's 'reused symbol carries no replay data' check passes vacuously if the deletes never fail on the test terminal.

key_facts: All four files read completely (317 + 152 + 1278 + 261 lines). None contains OrderSend/CTrade/PositionClose, any Object* call, ChartRedraw, FileOpen or Print; the only disk output is SaveInto() into the session file written by CSSRSessionManager.

CSSRTradingEngine is registered FIRST among observers (Expert 1176) and processes each tick in the order AccrueSwap -> CheckPendings -> CheckStops -> CheckStopout (engine 610-613). AutoPause is registered after it (Expert 1212) and diffs position states.

Rewind is delivered as OnRewind(cut) from four controller paths: SeekTo backward (cut = sink's M1-aligned truncation), Reset (cut = start_msc, no ticks re-emitted, state READY), RestoreSnapshot (cut = checkpoint bar-open, checkpoints every 5 replay-minutes, SSR_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_MSC), NotifyRestored (cut = now). After RestoreSnapshot, JumpForward bulk-seeds bars strictly before the target minute via sink.SeedBars WITHOUT any observer callback (controller 1370-1391; recorded as core-engine-3).

OnRewind (634-702) drops positions placed after the cut from the log without reversing their balance effects; kept positions have their legs unwound, but sl/tp/trail_peak/mae/mfe are not versioned anywhere (SSRTradeLeg 143-169 has no such fields).
Neither OnSessionStart (570-591) nor OnRewind resets m_bid/m_ask; Open() (716-717) and all GroupPort trade guards test only Bid() > 0.

SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL, when > 0 on the custom symbol, silently replaces InpMarginLot as the full per-lot margin with no leverage division (588-590). FreeMargin() is called nowhere in the codebase; Open() performs no margin check.

FillPrice() applies adverse slippage to every fill including limit-order entries (120-126, 345), while TP exits fill exactly at tp (544) with the file's own comment (486-490) stating limit orders must not be slipped.

BarIsAmbiguousFor (141-175) and the fill-time ambiguity check (371-384) compare the WHOLE cached bar range to sl/tp regardless of where inside the bar the position was opened; the clipped bar (controller ClipBar) only trims at pump-window boundaries.

The author has never run this on a terminal; T9 (SSR_T9_Trading.mq5) asserts rewind only for an OPEN, commission-free trade (T9.7 lines 340-383), never balance after rewinding a CLOSED trade, never trailing/Modify across a rewind, never swap, never stop-out, never the checkpoint path over a stop hit.

RiskEngine rounds lots DOWN with MathFloor(v/step + 1e-9)*step (27-32) but does not NormalizeDouble the result; ConfigureFromSymbol silently substitutes 1.0 for a non-positive SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE (53).

findings.title: Rewind drops positions placed after the cut without reversing their P/L, commission and swap from the balance
findings.claim: State: a BUY is opened at 10:05 and closed at 10:10 with realised +50 (or by SL with -30), commission 7/lot charged twice. Action: step back to 10:00 (OnRewind(10:00)), or press Reset ('0' key -> GroupPort.Reset -> controller.Reset -> PublishRewind(start_msc)). Outcome: the position vanishes from the log but m_balance keeps the +50 (or -30) and the -14 commission and any accrued swap. After Reset the account shows an empty log with the whole session's realised P/L still in the balance; Equity, stats, prop-evaluation daily-loss/target and the next LotForRisk (sized off Equity()) are all computed on the corrupted figure. A later Save/Restore then prints the 'balance replayed from the trades is X, but the file recorded Y' warning because RestoreFrom recomputes balance from the log.
findings.evidence: The `continue` at line 643 skips the position entirely, so it is never copied to m_pos[keep] and none of the money it moved is reversed. The money was moved at Open() line 754 (`m_balance -= m_pos[i].commission`), CheckPendings line 356, BookExit line 222 (`m_balance += realised - fee`) and AccrueSwap line 427. The only reversal code, UnwindLegsAfter (263-291) and the un-fill branch (660-690), is placed AFTER the continue and only runs for kept positions. Nothing else recomputes m_balance from the log (grep of m_balance: lines 222, 273, 356, 427, 563, 579, 664, 754, 1167, 1221 only). T9.7 (lines 340-361) only asserts the ticket is gone, with an OPEN trade and commission 0, so the leak is invisible to the test. Fix: before `continue`, run UnwindLegsAfter(i, msc) (all legs are > msc) and then `m_balance += m_pos[i].commission - m_pos[i].swap`.

findings.title: SL/TP changes, trailing-stop movement, break-even and MAE/MFE are not versioned, so they survive a rewind
findings.claim: State: long at 1.1000 with trail_points=200 (SetTrailing is applied automatically to every new trade when a trail distance is set, GroupPort 1062-1063). Price runs to 1.1100 so ApplyTrailing moves sl to 1.1080 and trail_peak to 1.1100. Action: step back to the minute when price was 1.1020. Outcome: OnRewind keeps the position (placed before the cut) but leaves sl=1.1080 and trail_peak=1.1100. The first re-emitted tick has bid 1.1020 <= sl, so CheckStops closes the trade at StopFill = 1.1020 - slip, reason SL, and AutoPause announces 'stop loss hit' - at a moment when the stop had really been at 1.1000 and the trade was +20 pips. The same applies to a manual Modify() or BreakEven() done in the deleted future: the un-happened stop/target stays. mae/mfe and spread_at_exit likewise keep values from the deleted future for kept positions.
findings.evidence: SSRTradeLeg (SSR_TradeTypes.mqh 143-169) records only volume/price/msc/realised/fee/closing/prev_swap_locked/prev_swap_from_msc/prev_ambiguous. OnRewind (634-702) touches sl/tp/trail_peak/mae/mfe only in the un-fill branch for pendings (676-679) and never for a kept open position. ApplyTrailing (302-323) is the only writer of trail_peak and it only ever moves the long stop up (`if(want > m_pos[i].sl)`), so a future-trailed stop is never lowered again. CheckStops 526-527 then compares the current bid to that stale sl.

findings.title: Checkpoint-path step back un-closes trades whose exits fell inside the checkpoint interval and never re-runs those exits
findings.code:
//--- every exit taken in the deleted future, newest first
UnwindLegsAfter(i, msc);
findings.claim: State: checkpoint taken at 10:00 (every 5 replay-minutes). A long opened at 09:50 is stopped out at 10:02; the user keeps replaying to 10:04. Action: step back ONE candle (StepBackward(1) -> target 10:03). Controller restores the 10:00 checkpoint and calls OnRewind(10:00), so the engine unwinds the 10:02 closing leg and the position is OPEN again with its loss refunded; the controller then JumpForward(10:03) bulk-seeds bars 10:00-10:02 to the sink with no OnTicks, and only 10:03's partial bar reaches the engine. Outcome: at 10:03 the chart shows the stop crossed at 10:02, yet the account holds the position open with no stop event, the loss is gone from the balance, and the SL will only fire if a later tick crosses it again. Pendings that filled in 10:00-10:02 are un-filled and not re-filled; manual trades placed in 10:00-10:03 are dropped (and leak their money per trading-exec-1).
findings.evidence: Engine OnRewind honours the cut it is given (unwinds legs with msc > cut, lines 265-266). The controller hands it the checkpoint time, not the target: StepBackward 1450-1460 (`RestoreSnapshot(cp)` then `JumpForward(target)`), RestoreSnapshot 1623-1644 (`actual = m_sink.TruncateFrom(snap.taken_at_msc); ... PublishRewind(actual)`), JumpForward 1370-1391 (`m_sink.SeedBars(bulk, n)` with no PublishBar/PublishTicks; only `EmitWindow(tlo, thi)` for the target's own minute at 1397-1398). The engine has no interface to receive a bulk stretch, so the exits in that stretch are lost. Related to core-engine-3; reported here because the account-level consequence (a stopped-out trade resurrected as open, balance restated) is the harmful outcome.

findings.title: Stale bid/ask survive session start, reset and rewind; a trade taken before the next tick fills at a price from the deleted future
findings.claim: State: a session has replayed to 15:00 where bid=1.1050. Action: user presses '0' (Panel 2241 -> GroupPort.Reset 425-437 -> controller.Reset 1268-1297, which calls PublishRewind(start) and emits NO ticks, leaving the replay READY), then draws lines and presses Tab / Buy before Play. Outcome: GroupPort.MarketAt/Market pass their only guard (Bid() > 0), sl/tp are derived from the stale 15:00 bid, and Open() fills at ask=1.1050+slip while the chart is at the session start (say 1.1000). On the first real tick CheckStops evaluates px=1.1000 against a stop placed 1.1050-dist: an immediate SL (or, for a short, immediate TP) at a price that never existed at that time. Until that tick, Equity()/FloatingPL()/PreviewLot also report values against the future price. The same applies after Load of a new session on the same object (OnSessionStart does not clear prices) and after a SeekTo-based step back that lands exactly on the sink's cut with no pending range to re-emit.
findings.evidence: OnSessionStart (570-591) and OnRewind (634-702) assign m_now_msc but never m_bid/m_ask; the only writer of m_bid/m_ask is OnTicks 604-607. Open() 716-717 and GroupPort 1045/1072/600/699/720 guard on Bid() > 0 only. Controller Reset (1268-1297) contains no EmitWindow call and transitions to READY, so no tick arrives until the user presses Play. Fix: zero m_bid/m_ask in OnRewind/OnSessionStart (a re-emitted tick restores them immediately), so the existing 'no price yet' guard fires.

findings.title: Ambiguity test uses the whole bar range, so a target hit after a mid-bar entry is booked as a stop loss when the bar's earlier low was below the stop
findings.claim: State: SYNTHETIC_TICK, 8 ticks per bar, an O-L-H-C shaped M1 bar (low printed at tick 2, high at tick 5). The trader buys the breakout at tick 3 (after the low), with SL 5 points below that bar's low and TP below the bar's high. Tick 5's bid >= tp -> tp_hit. Outcome: BarIsAmbiguousFor sees bar.low <= sl and bar.high >= tp and ClosePosition(i, StopFill(i), SSR_CLOSE_SL, true) books a LOSS at the stop and flags the trade ambiguous, although every synthesised tick after the entry (3..8) is above the stop and the engine itself observed them in order. The same whole-bar test at fill time (371-384) flags a pending filled at tick 6 as ambiguous because of a low printed at tick 2. Common pattern: buying a breakout of the current minute with the stop under that minute's low converts every same-minute target hit into a loss.
findings.evidence: m_bar is the bar cached by OnBarContext (593-598); ClipBar in the controller only trims it to the pump window end (controller 446-459), so inside one emitted segment it is the full minute. BarIsAmbiguousFor (141-175) never compares open_msc with the ticks already seen nor uses the running excursion (mae, updated at 293-300, already records the worst move since entry). CheckStops 537-541 calls it whenever either level is touched. This is a stated pessimism policy, but the pessimism is applied to price that occurred before the position existed, which the design comment (9-20) does not claim.

findings.title: No margin check on entry when margin is modelled: an unaffordable order is accepted, charged, then stopped out on the next tick
findings.claim: State: InpMarginLot=1000, InpStopout=50, balance 10000, commission 7/lot, slippage 10. Action: Open(BUY, 50.0) (via Publisher external trade, or a large risk percent). Outcome: accepted; commission 350 charged; UsedMargin=50000, margin level 19% < 50 on the very next tick so CheckStopout closes it at bid-slip with a further 350 commission and 50 lots x 10 points of slippage - a loss of several hundred plus spread for an order a terminal would have rejected with 'not enough money' at zero cost. Stopouts counter and auto-pause 'stop out' fire for a trade that should never have existed.
findings.evidence: Open() 705-756 checks capacity, volume > 0, price > 0 and nothing else; OpenWithRisk/OpenPendingWithRisk (759-801) add only sizing checks. FreeMargin() (946) is defined but a repository-wide grep finds no caller outside the engine. CheckStopout (436-470) is the only margin enforcement and runs after the fill.

findings.title: SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL is taken as the whole per-lot margin with no leverage division and silently overrides InpMarginLot
findings.claim: State: broker reports SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL = 100000 for EURUSD (several brokers publish the contract size there; the terminal divides it by ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE and the margin rate). The custom symbol inherits the origin's properties (CustomSymbolCreate copies the template; the manager also clones trade props 282-289). InpStopout=100, InpMarginLot=0 or any value. Outcome: a 0.1-lot position 'uses' 10000 margin against a 10000 account -> margin level ~100% -> CheckStopout closes it on its first tick as STOPOUT. With InpStopout=0 nothing fires but MarginLevel/FreeMargin shown to the user are 100-500x too pessimistic. The user's explicit InpMarginLot is also discarded without a message whenever the symbol reports any positive number.
findings.evidence: The value is used directly in UsedMargin() 935-944 (`v * m_margin_per_lot`) and in CheckStopout 441. ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE and SYMBOL_MARGIN_* rates are read nowhere in the four files. Whether a given broker reports a non-zero SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL on the origin cannot be verified from source, hence POTENTIAL_RISK; the arithmetic path is confirmed.

findings.title: BreakEven/Modify accept a stop on the wrong side of the market and the engine then closes the trade instead of rejecting the change
findings.claim: State: long just filled at ask 1.10020 (bid 1.10000, 20-point spread). Action: user presses the panel's 'be' button (BreakEvenAll -> BreakEven) or the row's break-even action before price has moved more than the spread. Outcome: sl = 1.10020 > bid, so on the next tick CheckStops (526-527, `px <= sl`) closes the trade at StopFill = bid - slip = 1.09990: a guaranteed loss of spread + slippage, recorded as reason SL, counted as a losing trade in stats, and auto-pause halts the replay with 'stop loss hit'. A real terminal rejects an SL above the bid ('invalid stops') and the position keeps running. Modify(ticket, sl, tp) (844-853) has the same gap, as does the ambiguity flag: nothing marks the close as a rejected modification.
findings.evidence: BreakEven (920-927) and Modify (844-853) write sl/tp with only a state check; neither compares against m_bid/m_ask. GroupPort.BreakEven/BreakEvenAll (867-915) add no price check either. CheckStops treats any sl on the wrong side as an immediate hit and StopFill (492-511) takes the worse of level and price, so the fill is at the current market minus slippage.

findings.title: Limit-order entries receive adverse slippage and can fill worse than their limit price
findings.claim: State: InpSlippage=10, BUY_LIMIT at 1.10000. Tick with ask 1.10000 triggers (`m_ask <= request_price`). Outcome: FillPrice(true, true) = 1.10000 + 0.00010 = 1.10010, above the limit price. A limit order fills at its price or better by definition - the file's own comment at 486-490 makes exactly this argument for take-profit and fills TP at its level (544). Entry limits are treated inconsistently, penalising limit entries by the slippage input on every fill, and risk_at_entry/LotForRisk (sized from the request price in OpenPendingWithRisk 797) then understate the risk actually carried.
findings.evidence: FillPrice (120-126) adds slip unconditionally; CheckPendings (345) uses it for all four pending types. Only with InpSlippage > 0 (default 0).

findings.title: SSRPendingFor classifies a long entry inside the spread as BUY_STOP, which fills on the next tick like a market order
findings.claim: State: bid 1.10000, ask 1.10020 (InpSpreadPoints=20), caller min_dist = 2 points (GroupPort 1010: `pt * 2.0`). User drags a long entry line to 1.10010 (10 points above bid, below ask). Outcome: |entry-bid| = 10 points >= min_dist so the 'entry line is on the price' refusal (113-118) does not fire; entry > bid -> BUY_STOP at 1.10010; CheckPendings (337) sees ask 1.10020 >= 1.10010 on the very next tick and fills at ask + slip. The user placed a 'pending' that behaves as a market order at a worse price than the line, which is exactly what the refusal text says it prevents.
findings.evidence: The limit-vs-stop decision (122) and the on-the-price guard (113) both use bid for the long side; the long trigger price in CheckPendings is the ask. Any entry in (bid + min_dist, ask) is therefore an immediately-triggering stop. With min_dist of 2 points and a 20-point spread the window is 18 points wide.

findings.title: AmbiguousPercent divides ambiguous fills of still-open positions by the closed count
findings.claim: State: one trade closed unambiguously; one pending filled on a synthetic tick in a minute whose range also reaches its stop, still open. m_ambiguous_count = 1 (incremented at fill, 381-382), ClosedCount = 1. Outcome: the honesty figure reports 100% of results resting on assumed tick order while the only closed result was not assumed; with two such open fills it reports 200%.
findings.evidence: m_ambiguous_count is incremented in CheckPendings (382) for OPEN positions and in BookExit (239) for closes, but the denominator counts only state == CLOSED (988-994).

findings.title: Open() accepts any positive volume from the external path without step/min/max validation
findings.code:
if(volume <= 0.0)
  { m_last_error = "volume must be positive"; return 0; }
findings.claim: State: InpAllowTrade=true; an external client sends BUY with volume 0.003 or 7.777 (Publisher 301: `m_acct.Open(SSR_ORDER_BUY, a1, a2, a3, 0.0, "external")`). Outcome: the position is booked at that size; the journal, stats, R and margin all carry a size no venue would accept, and GroupPort.ClosePartial later refuses it as 'too small to split'. The risk engine already knows vol_min/vol_max/vol_step (VolMin/VolMax exposed) but Open() does not consult them.
findings.evidence: Open() 705-756 validates only volume > 0; m_risk.VolMin()/VolMax() and the step are unused on this path. The UI paths go through LotForRisk which rounds, so only the Publisher and Strategy raw paths are affected.

findings.title: Auto-pause reasons are English literals with a hard-coded 5-digit price format
findings.claim: State: InpLanguage=fa, symbol US30 (2 digits). A pending fills. Outcome: the pause banner shows 'entry filled - BUY 0.50 @ 41234.56000' in English on an otherwise Persian panel, and the price carries three spurious decimals. The reason text bypasses T(SSR_S_*) because Core repeats it verbatim; audit A19 only scans Ui files.
findings.evidence: Lines 124-126, 137-138, 142, 146, 153 build literals; the position's digits are available via m_acct.Digits() but not used.

findings.title: Swap accrues on UTC-midnight calendar days with no rollover hour or triple-swap day
findings.claim: State: InpSwapLong=-5, position opened Wednesday 23:00 server time and closed Thursday 01:00. Outcome: one day charged (correct by count), but a position held Wednesday-to-Thursday on a 3-day-swap broker is charged 1x instead of 3x, and a position opened 00:30 and closed 23:30 the same day is charged nothing though it never crossed midnight - consistent with the comment ('per REPLAY day held') but a documented modelling gap for a tool that reports execution costs as a coaching metric.
findings.evidence: AccrueSwap 401-430 uses integer day division of the server-time msc; no day-of-week or rollover-hour logic exists in the four files.

performance_notes: Per tick the engine runs up to four O(N) passes over ALL log entries including CLOSED/CANCELLED ones (AccrueSwap 409, CheckPendings 328, CheckStops 515, CheckStopout 450 + UsedMargin/Equity loops when margin is modelled); m_count never shrinks except on rewind. With 512 positions and 8 synthetic ticks per bar that is ~16k iterations per bar at the default fidelity; bounded and evident, not measured.
AccrueSwap and CheckStopout early-return when swap inputs are 0 / margin is not modelled (default inputs), so the default hot path is two loops per tick.
BookExit calls AccrueSwap() (a full O(N) pass) once per exit; FloatingPL/Equity are recomputed on every UI read, PreviewLot, LotForRisk and stop-out check (no caching).

At(i, out) copies a ~660-byte struct with 8 legs and 2 strings; CSSRTradeAutoPause::Scan copies every position once per OnTicks call (once per bar segment), and CSSRGroupPort::SetTrailing/ClosePartial/BreakEvenAll loop the same way. Find()/ByTicket are linear scans called per panel row.
