SaveInto builds each position row by repeated string concatenation (30 SSRPackAdd calls per position, 10 per leg) - fine at 512 positions, but each SSRPackAdd allocates a new string.
OnRewind compacts the array with struct copies (m_pos[keep] = m_pos[i]) - O(N) per rewind, negligible.
test_gaps: No test asserts m_balance after rewinding past a CLOSED trade, or after Reset with closed trades; T9.7 rewinds only an OPEN, commission-free trade and checks the ticket is gone (finding trading-exec-1 is invisible to it).
No test rewinds across a trailing-stop move, Modify() or BreakEven() and checks sl/tp/trail_peak afterwards (trading-exec-2).
No test steps back through a checkpoint over a stop that was hit inside the checkpoint interval and checks the position is still closed at the target time (trading-exec-3).
No test trades immediately after Reset/Load/step-back without a new tick and checks the fill price against the chart (trading-exec-4).
No test of a market entry mid-bar with the stop below that bar's earlier low and the target inside the bar (trading-exec-5); T9.4 opens before the ambiguous bar.
No swap test at all: per-day accrual, partial-close locking (swap_locked), rewind refund, sign conventions.
No stop-out test: ordering (worst loser first), repeated closes until level recovers, margin from SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL vs InpMarginLot, Open() with insufficient margin.
No test of BreakEven pressed within the spread of entry, or of Modify() with a stop on the wrong side.
No test of pending fill ambiguity flag (371-384), of limit fills with slippage > 0, or of SSRPendingFor with an entry inside the spread.
No test of LotForRisk with a non-0.01 step (0.1 / 1.0 index lots), the vol_max cap path, or a symbol whose tick value is 0 (fallback to 1.0).
No test of session save/restore round-trip for a position with partial legs followed by a rewind over those legs, nor of the balance_check warning path; T12 should be checked for leg coverage.
No test of AutoPause across a rewind (Reseed) or of a pending that fills and stops between two scans with SSR_PAUSE_ON_ENTRY set.
None of the T9 assertions have ever been executed on a terminal (author cannot run MT5), so all 'tests exist' statements are about intent, not evidence.

key_facts: All four analytics classes read the account only via CSSRTradingEngine::Total()/At(i) (full struct copy) in SLOT order = creation order; nothing here orders by close time.
Per-trade net used for wins/losses/net_profit is profit + swap - commission (SSR_Statistics.mqh:431); RMultiple() in SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:270 is (profit + swap)/risk and excludes commission.
profit_factor is deliberately left 0.0 when gross_loss == 0 (SSR_Statistics.mqh:529-530); only the HTML 'Every measure' table translates that to 'undefined'.

Equity curve: 4096-slot ring sampled every 60 000 replay ms from OnTicks (last tick time) and OnClock; oldest half dropped when full; persisted as section [equity] key e; restored via O(n*m) GetNth scans.

CSSRPropEvaluation judges only inside OnClock, which the controller publishes once per Pump/PumpTo after all ticks of the pass (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1027-1029) and never inside JumpForward (1333-1420); Pump returns 0 unless PLAYING (998).
CSSRPropEvaluation has no SaveInto/RestoreFrom; CSSRSessionManager persists only the account and the stats equity curve (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:195-200, 367-375).

A session resume calls CSSRReplayController::NotifyRestored() = PublishRewind(now) (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1668-1669 via SSR_SessionManager.mqh:381); the prop observer is already registered and RUNNING at that point (host l.1197-1200 then l.1483).
Prop 'day traded' is detected from m_acct.Total() rising; Total() = m_count which is incremented for pending orders at placement (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:719-738).
Journal CSV and HTML are written FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI; the HTML head declares charset utf-8 (SSR_ReportStyle.mqh:21). CSV escaping is comma->semicolon and newline->space only.

CSV 'profit' column is raw p.profit with commission and swap as separate columns; HTML 'Profit' column and '# net_profit' are net. The class report (SSR_ClassReport.mqh:259,266) reads the CSV 'profit' column to decide won/lost.
MAE/MFE are in price units (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:296-299, mae <= 0); the CSV prints them %.5f, the HTML statement %.2f.

ShotBook queues on OnTicks state transitions and the host flushes at the top of the next timer pass (host l.2731); files go to SSReplay\journal\shots\<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>\t<ticket>-in|out.png; nothing is ever deleted; cap 500 per run.

The panel Stats tab does not use CSSRStatsEngine at all (SSR_Panel.mqh:1671-1722 reads balance/equity/floating/bars/ticks from the port model); Compute() is only called for the review card, the reveal card, exports and the strategy report.

Tags in live sessions come from the port's TagOrDefault() and strategy m_tag; note is only ever set by RestoreFrom (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1210). Session name in the CSV/HTML header is the user's CfgSession().

findings.title: Resuming a saved session voids a running prop evaluation on startup
findings.claim: InpProp=true and InpResume=true with an existing session file -> the evaluation is VOID before the first candle is played, the replay auto-pauses with 'evaluation VOID - the clock was moved backwards at <now>', and the user must press Reset (which restarts day counting from zero, see finding 2).
findings.evidence: Host SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1197 calls g_prop.Reset() (state RUNNING when enabled) and :1200 Watch(g_prop); g_ctrl.Load (:1252) fires OnSessionStart -> Reset() again (RUNNING); then :1483 g_session_mgr.Restore() -> SSR_SessionManager.mqh:381 m_group.At(i).NotifyRestored() -> SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1669 PublishRewind(m_clock.now_msc) -> every observer's OnRewind including this one, whose only guard is m_state != RUNNING. g_ctrl is in g_group (host :1320). The rewind is to 'now', so no clock actually moved backwards, yet the reason text says it did.

findings.title: Prop evaluation state is not persisted; a resumed or reset run re-bases every rule on current equity
findings.claim: Trailing rules, start 10000, trader at 9400 after 2 sittings, 25 of 30 days used: after resume (and the Reset finding 1 forces) the first OnClock sets m_peak_eq=9400, m_total_days=1, m_trading_days=0, m_day_open_eq=9400. TotalFloor becomes 8400 instead of 9000, the deadline restarts at day 1 of 30, the min-days count restarts at 0, and the daily floor is measured from the resumed equity. The verdict then differs from what the same trades would produce in one sitting.
findings.evidence: The class has no SaveInto/RestoreFrom (grep of the file). SSR_SessionManager.mqh:195-200 and 367-375 save/restore only m_acct and m_stats. Reset() (l.327-341) and the first-clock branch (l.366-377) initialise every counter from m_rules.start_balance / current Equity(). The trading engine and the equity curve ARE restored, so the account carries its history while the judge forgets it.

findings.title: Closed-only drawdown walks trades in open order, not close order
findings.claim: Three overlapping trades, slot order A(net -100, opened first, closed last), B(+1000), C(-500). Real balance path 10000 -> 11000 -> 10500 -> 10400 has a closed drawdown of 600; the loop visits A,B,C and computes 9900 -> 10900 -> 10400, reporting 500. The statement's 'Max drawdown, closed only' and the gap it asks the reader to compare with the equity drawdown are wrong whenever positions overlap.
findings.evidence: At(i) returns positions in slot (creation) order (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1005-1011, m_pos appended in Open() l.719). Nothing sorts by close_msc before accumulating bal/peak/worst. The same slot-order walk also drives win_streak/loss_streak/revenge in ComputeFor (l.406-513). T10.2 (SSR_T10_Statistics.mq5:204) only checks a sequential, non-overlapping case.

findings.title: Class report and CSV consumers see a different per-trade result than the statement (raw profit vs net)
findings.code:
p.profit, p.commission, p.swap,
         //--- R is left EMPTY, never zero, when it does not exist:
findings.claim: InpCommission=3 per lot, a 1-lot trade that made +2: statement/headline count it as a loss (net -4 after two sides), CSV 'profit' column says +2, and the class report marks it won (SSR_ClassReport.mqh:266 'out.won = (pnl > 0.0)' from the 'profit' column). The header '# net_profit' no longer equals the sum of the 'profit' column, which is the exact contradiction the comment at SSR_Statistics.mqh:415-430 says was fixed - it was fixed for the HTML (l.394) but not the CSV.
findings.evidence: Row() writes p.profit raw (l.82) with no net column; ExportHtml computes net = p.profit + p.swap - p.commission for its Profit column (l.394) and ComputeFor uses the same net for wins/losses (SSR_Statistics.mqh:431-450). ClassReport ReadOne locates only 'open_time', 'profit', 'r' columns (l.243-245) and derives won/lost from 'profit' (l.259, 266). With the default commission 0 and swap 0 all three agree, which is why no test catches it.

findings.title: A day on which only a pending order was placed (even if cancelled) counts as a trading day
findings.claim: min_trading_days=3: placing a buy-limit far from price on each of three days and cancelling it satisfies the minimum with zero fills, so a target hit on day 1 passes on day 3 with no trade. Conversely a pending placed on day 1 and filled on day 2 credits day 1, not the day the trade was actually opened, contradicting the comment 'a trade was OPENED that day'.
findings.evidence: Positions() returns m_acct.Total() (l.134-135) = m_count, and CSSRTradingEngine::Open() does m_count++ for a pending order at placement (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:719-738) before any fill; cancellation does not decrement m_count. The evaluation only compares the count, never the state.

findings.title: Undefined profit factor is printed as 0.00 in the KPI grid, by-setup table, CSV header and Summary
findings.code:
FileWriteString(h, StringFormat("
Profit factor%.2f
\r\n", st.profit_factor));
findings.claim: A session of five winners and no loser: the headline KPI reads 'Profit factor 0.00', the by-setup row (l.359-363) reads 0.00, the CSV header (l.200) writes '# profit_factor,0.0000' which the class report ingests as 0 (SSR_ClassReport.mqh:224), and Summary()/ToString prints 'PF 0.00' - the worst possible reading for the best possible session - while the 'Every measure' table on the same page says 'undefined' (l.1099-1103).
findings.evidence: SSR_Statistics.mqh:529-530 leaves profit_factor at 0.0 when gross_loss == 0 by design ('the caller reads trades/losses to know why'); only WriteAllMeasures honours that contract, the other four printers format the raw double.

findings.title: Revenge detection compares only with the previously OPENED trade, not the most recent loss
findings.code:
if(prev_was_loss && prev_close != SSR_INVALID_TIME &&
            p.open_msc >= prev_close &&
            (p.open_msc - prev_close) <= SSR_REVENGE_WINDOW_MSC)
            out.revenge_trades++;
findings.claim: A opened 10:00 and stopped out at 10:30 (loss); B opened 10:01 and closed 10:02 for a win; C opened 10:31. C is a textbook revenge entry one minute after A's loss, but prev for C is B (slot order), prev_was_loss is false, and revenge_trades stays 0. The statement text (l.1196-1198) promises 'opened within two replay minutes of the previous trade closing at a loss', which C satisfies.
findings.evidence: prev_close/prev_was_loss are overwritten unconditionally per slot (l.511-512) so 'previous' means previous in creation order, not the latest close before this open. With a tag filter the same applies within the tag. QA smoke only asserts revenge_trades >= 1 in a sequential scenario (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:2911).

findings.title: Average MAE/MFE printed at two decimals in price units and compared with money
findings.code:
Measure(h, "Average MAE", DoubleToString(st.avg_mae, 2),
              "maximum adverse excursion: how far the average trade went the wrong "
              "way before it ended");
      Measure(h, "Average MFE", DoubleToString(st.avg_mfe, 2),
findings.claim: EURUSD session with an average MAE of 15 pips (-0.00150) prints 'Average MAE -0.00' and 'Average MFE 0.00'; on any instrument the caption 'Much larger than the average win means profit was given back' compares a price distance with a money figure.
findings.evidence: mae/mfe are accumulated as price moves (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:295-299: move = price - open_price) and averaged unchanged (SSR_Statistics.mqh:466-468, 540-541). The CSV prints them %.5f (l.87) so the two exports disagree in readability; neither is converted with MoneyFor.

findings.title: Equity ring drops its oldest half, so the live max drawdown can shrink and the peak be lost
findings.claim: Replay window longer than 4096 minutes (InpReplayBars > 4096; default 2000 is safe): peak at minute 100, trough at minute 3000 gives DD X until sample 4096 arrives, after which EquityDrawdown starts from sample 2048 and reports a smaller number - a max drawdown that decreases as the session goes on, and a statement whose SVG no longer contains the trough it names.
findings.evidence: EquityDrawdown (l.347-364) starts peak at m_eq_val[0] of whatever survived; the drop keeps only samples [2048..4095]. The comment admits it ('drop the oldest half rather than the whole curve') but the peak-carrying half is the one discarded. SaveInto/RestoreFrom likewise cap at 4096.

findings.title: R multiple excludes commission while every money measure includes it
findings.claim: Commission 5/lot, 1 lot, risk 50, trade closes +3 before fees: net = 3 - 10 = -7 (a loss, counted in losses/gross_loss) but R = +0.06 (a positive R). Over a scalping session average_r can be positive while expectancy in money is negative, and the statement prints both side by side as if they measured the same trades.
findings.evidence: RMultiple() = (profit + swap)/risk_at_entry (SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:269-270) has no commission term; ComputeFor's net (l.431) and the CSV/HTML rows do. The file's own header comment (l.15-20) defines R as the result over the risk taken, and the commission is part of the result per l.415-430.

findings.title: Headline floor shows the day-open equity when the daily rule is switched off
findings.code:
double            DailyFloor(void)
     { return m_day_open_eq - m_rules.start_balance * m_rules.max_daily_loss_pct / 100.0; }
findings.claim: InpPropDaily=0 (daily rule off), total 10%: OnClock never applies rule 1, but DailyFloor() = m_day_open_eq, Floor() picks the higher of the two floors and the headline/panel/port report 'floor <today's opening equity>' - a floor the run cannot actually hit. The same happens for TotalFloor when the total rule is 0.
findings.evidence: OnClock guards the rules with max_daily_loss_pct > 0.0 / max_total_loss_pct > 0.0 (l.391, 401) but DailyFloor/TotalFloor/Floor (l.295-308) and Headline (l.319-321) have no such guard; GroupPort copies Floor(), DailyFloor(), TotalFloor() into the panel model (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:214, 225-226).

findings.title: A jump forward never runs the evaluation; a jump that completes the window leaves it IN PROGRESS
findings.claim: Evaluation running with max_days=30 on day 20; the user jumps to the end of the window 15 replay days later. JumpForward bulk-writes the bars, transitions to COMPLETED and never publishes OnClock; Pump() returns 0 once not PLAYING, so no OnClock ever fires again. The deadline (and a target reached in the partial bar's ticks) is never judged; the review card and the statement print 'IN PROGRESS'. During normal play the rules are also judged only once per pump, after all ticks of the pass, not per tick.
findings.evidence: SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1333-1420 JumpForward calls EmitWindow, m_sink.OnSeek, Publish() and Transition(COMPLETED) but contains no m_obs[i].OnClock loop, unlike Pump (l.1027-1029) and PumpTo (l.1102-1104); Pump early-returns when status != PLAYING (l.998). The evaluation has no OnTicks override, so OnClock is its only judging point.

findings.title: Exports written FILE_ANSI while the statement declares UTF-8 and the product is localised to Persian
findings.code: int h = FileOpen(path, FILE_WRITE | FILE_TXT | FILE_ANSI | FILE_SHARE_READ);
findings.claim: A user on the Persian UI names the session in Persian (CfgSession -> m_sess_name, printed at CSV l.190 and HTML l.269 via Html(name) / '# session'): FILE_ANSI converts the string through the terminal's ANSI codepage, producing '?' on a non-Persian Windows or Windows-1256 bytes on a Persian one, while the HTML head says charset=utf-8 (SSR_ReportStyle.mqh:21) so the browser shows mojibake. The project already recorded the mirror-image trap for reading (overview lesson 5).
findings.evidence: Both ExportCsv (l.173) and ExportHtml (l.254) open with FILE_ANSI; no CP_UTF8 conversion or FILE_UNICODE anywhere in the file. Whether any non-ASCII text reaches the file depends on the user's session name and tags, hence potential.

findings.title: CSV escaping does not handle double quotes, so a quote in a tag or session name can merge rows in spreadsheet readers
findings.claim: A session named 12" chart or a tag beginning with a double quote is written verbatim; RFC-4180 readers (Excel, pandas) treat a field starting with a quote as a quoted field and consume delimiters and line breaks until the next quote, shifting or merging the rows that follow. The project's own class report splits on commas only, so it is unaffected.
findings.evidence: Csv() neither doubles quotes nor wraps the field; tags originate from TagOrDefault()/strategy names and the session name from user input (host l.1355). No live path sets a quote today, hence potential.

findings.title: Screenshots are taken on the chart the control panel is drawn on
findings.code: if(!ChartScreenShot(m_chart, path, w, h, ALIGN_RIGHT))
findings.claim: m_chart is the replay chart, which is also where the 310x336 panel and its dialogs live (established ground truth). Every entry/exit PNG therefore contains the panel and whatever card is open, and ALIGN_RIGHT anchors the capture on the latest bars - the region the panel most plausibly covers depending on its corner. The 'chart they were looking at when they pressed the button' includes the button.
findings.evidence: SetChart receives g_replay_chart (host l.1281, 2655); nothing hides or moves panel objects around the ChartScreenShot call. Whether the panel occludes the entry bar depends on the runtime corner (SSR_Panel.mqh SetCorner/SnapToCorner), which cannot be verified without a terminal.

performance_notes: CSSRStatsEngine::ComputeFor makes up to three full passes over m_acct.Total() slots (main, wide-spread second pass, ClosedDrawdownFor) plus OpenCountFor, each iteration copying an SSRVirtualPosition (~660 B with 8 legs + two strings) via At(); at the 512 cap that is ~1500 struct copies (~1 MB) per Compute. Only called on review/reveal/export/strategy report, not per timer pass, so it is fine today; do not wire it into the panel render loop without a cache.

CSSRStatsEngine::RestoreFrom is O(samples x file entries): f.Count("e") plus f.GetNth("e", i) for each of up to 4096 samples, and GetNth is a linear scan of every entry in the session file (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:322-344). A full curve on a file that also holds 512 positions is ~4096 x ~5000 string compares (~20 M) once per resume.
CSSRJournal::Line(index) walks the position array from 0 for every call; a caller rendering N rows costs O(N^2) copies (N <= 512, harmless, but note if a list view is added).

CSSRJournal::ExportHtml: WriteEquity walks the curve twice (range/decimation) and calls EquityAt per point; string building is chunked at 3000 chars so no quadratic concatenation. HasAnyShot + WriteShotCell do up to 2 FileIsExist calls per closed trade (disk stat per trade).

CSSRShotBook::Scan runs on every OnTicks batch: one At() struct copy per slot (up to 512) per batch; at 8 ticks/bar this is per bar, not per tick, and cheap. Shoot() calls FolderCreate on every shot (redundant after the first) and ChartScreenShot is synchronous and I/O bound - one call per entry/exit at the top of the timer pass, which is the deliberate deferral.

CSSRStatsEngine::Sample is called on every OnTicks batch and every OnClock but returns immediately unless 60 s of replay time has passed; the ring compaction copies 2048 longs + 2048 doubles once per 2048 samples.
test_gaps: No test exercises max_drawdown_closed, win/loss streaks or revenge detection with OVERLAPPING trades (T10.2 uses a sequential set; SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:2911 only asserts revenge >= 1). Findings 3 and 7 would surface with a three-trade overlap case.

No test runs CSSRPropEvaluation through a session save/restore (T12 has no prop coverage; SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:1215 checks a rewind voids the run but not that NotifyRestored on resume does). Findings 1 and 2 have no coverage.

No test sets a non-zero commission or swap and then compares the CSV 'profit' column, the HTML Profit column and '# net_profit' against each other, nor the class report's won/lost against the statement's wins (finding 4).
No test of an all-winning session's printed profit factor across the four printers (finding 6); T10 only checks the computed field.
No test that a pending order placed and cancelled does NOT count as a prop trading day, or that a pending filled on the next day is credited to the fill day (finding 5).
No test of the prop rules across JumpForward/JumpTo (no OnClock) or of a breach that occurs inside a pump and recovers before the pass ends (finding 12).
No test of the equity ring past 4096 samples (drop-oldest-half) checking that max_drawdown is monotone non-decreasing over a session (finding 9).

No round-trip test writing a session name or tag containing a comma, a double quote or non-ASCII (Persian) text through ExportCsv/ExportHtml and reading it back with the class report (findings 13, 14). The QA smoke round-trips only ASCII.

No test of ShotBook against a chart id: Shoot/RelPath/Flush are exercised only in SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:1920 in the build environment where ChartScreenShot cannot run; the entry-while-paused and rewind-past-fill paths are untested.
No test that DailyFloor/TotalFloor/Floor/Headline behave when the corresponding rule percentage is 0 (finding 11).

Default InpReplayBars=2000 M1 bars (~33 replay hours) can span at most three server days, so the default min_trading_days=3 is only reachable if the window straddles two midnights and a trade is opened on each day - worth a documented check in the setup panel rather than a test.

key_facts: Two window modes decide everything: one-chart mode (InpOneChart=true, default) hands the EA's OWN chart to the replay symbol with ChartSetSymbolPeriod (Expert:2702), so after the forced restart g_replay_chart == ChartID() == g_panel_chart (Expert:1276, 1463); two-window mode opens a separate chart via CSSRChartManager::OpenChart.
CSSRChartManager holds no engine pointer. Its registry is keyed on ChartSymbol(id) == m_symbol (SSR_ChartManager.mqh:344); a chart the user re-symbols simply drops out and is reported as closed.

ViewOffset (SSR_ChartManager.mqh:118-126) is the ONE number used by both the detach test and the snap test: CHART_FIRST_VISIBLE_BAR - (CHART_VISIBLE_BARS-1), clamped at 0. Its stated assumption is that the zero bar sits at the right border, while ApplyPolicy sets CHART_SHIFT=true (line 315).

Redraw() (531) is the only code that moves a view: ChartNavigate(CHART_END) when the newest M1 bar changed AND follow AND !user_detached AND ViewOffset>0. A user_detached chart is never snapped again until Follow()/FollowAll().

m_last_bar_time is written only in Redraw (548) and read by DetectScroll (452) to drop votes_needed from 2 to 1 - so the two-vote safeguard against mistaking bar arrival for a drag is alive only before the first bar of the session.

The observer surface (CSSRChartObserver: OnChartOpened/Closed/TimeframeChanged/UserScrolled/UserFollowed) is dead in production - SetObserver (141) is called only from Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T4_ChartIntegration.mq5:40, so m_observer is always NULL in the EA.
SetPeriodAll (593) has no caller anywhere in the tree.

Host ordering, every 5th pump (~200ms): g_charts.Sync() 2817 -> blind re-Apply 2822-2824 -> g_charts.Redraw() 2828 -> g_charts2[i].Sync() 2830. ScanLeaks every 50th pump (2845). FollowAll on each play transition (2778). g_charts2[i].Redraw() is never called.

Object namespace this layer owns: SSR_LINE_{SL,TP,EN} (draggable HLINEs), SSR_POS_<ticket>_{E,S,T} (position levels, swept each pass), SSR_HIST_<ticket>_{A,B,L} (closed-trade arrows + trend, drawn once), SSR_NEWS_<index> (calendar VLINEs, BACK=true), SSR_MARK_<unixsec>_<registry index> (bookmark VLINEs).
Nothing in the tree deletes SSR_MARK_* objects; ObjectsDeleteAll is called only for SSR_NEWS_ (CalendarLines:116) and the Ui widget prefix (SSR_Widgets.mqh:639).

Trade lines are polled, not event-driven (SSR_TradeLines.mqh:10-25, Poll at 286) and are the source of truth for stop distance/R:R; the host must only READ them mid-session (NoteLineDistances, Expert:2891), never SetStopPoints, or a short setup gets flipped back (comment at 253-270).
digits/point handed to CSSRTradeLines come from the ORIGIN symbol (Expert:1139-1141 -> 1295); on the handover-refused fallback path they come from the replay symbol (Expert:2658).

Blind mode's record of the user's original chart settings is instance-scoped (three arrays + m_id, 48 slots) and is never persisted; RestoreAll clears m_applied but leaves m_policy on, and the class exposes no Off()/ClearPolicy().

Calendar lines are never drawn in a blind session: LoadCalendar returns early when CfgBlind() != SSR_BLIND_OFF (Expert:925), so the 'blind mode is the exception and the host enforces it' comment is accurate.
Virtual tickets start at 1 and increment (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:550, 721), so the (int)ticket casts in SSR_POS_/SSR_HIST_ object names cannot overflow or collide.

Flight recorder column counts were verified during this audit and are consistent: header 26 fields (196-198), Event emits 26 (213-214), Write emits 25 values plus an empty trailing note = 26 (242-260).
CSSRLog's file sink is dead code: SetFile() has no caller anywhere, so m_to_file is always false and the logger is Print-only.
A19 (no drawn literals, i18n) only inspects paths containing '/Ui/' (tools/ssr_audit.py:1458), so every string the Chart layer draws or hands to the panel is outside its reach.

findings.title: DetectScroll cannot tell bar arrival from a drag at high speed: one false positive kills following for the rest of the session
findings.claim: State: one-chart mode, speed at 200x or MAX (SSR_SPEED_MAX=100000 means 'as fast as the sink accepts', SSR_Types.mqh:131), chart on M1/M5, user's hands off the mouse. Sync() runs at Expert:2817 and Redraw() at Expert:2828, i.e. the offset DetectScroll measures is everything that accumulated in the 200ms since the previous snap. If more than SSR_SCROLL_DETACH_BARS (3) chart bars land in that window without MetaTrader's own autoscroll pulling the view along, DetectScroll concludes the user scrolled: user_detached=true, follow=false, CHART_AUTOSCROLL is switched off (line 463). Redraw's snap is then gated off for good (line 574 requires !user_detached), so the view freezes on an advancing replay - the product's most-reported defect - with no automatic recovery and only the F key (FollowAll) to undo it.
findings.evidence: votes_needed collapses to 1 as soon as m_last_bar_time>0 (set in Redraw, line 548), so a single sample is enough. The justification written at lines 439-451 is explicit that this is safe because 'the snap zeroes the offset each pass, so anything past the threshold within one pass is a hand on the chart' - an assumption that holds only while fewer than 4 chart bars can arrive between two passes. At MAX speed the engine emits as fast as the sink accepts within the 40ms pump budget, so tens of M1 bars per 200ms pass is arithmetically reachable, and nothing in DetectScroll compares the drift against how many bars actually arrived (m_last_bar_time is available but only used to choose the vote count). The precondition - autoscroll not keeping the newest bar in view on an EA-written custom symbol - is the exact behaviour the file documents at lines 509-521 as the reason Redraw exists at all.

findings.title: Secondary-symbol charts never get Redraw(): the explicit view-snap and ChartRedraw exist only for the primary stream
findings.claim: State: InpAlsoSymbols set (a multi-instrument board). Each extra stream gets its own CSSRChartManager and its own chart (Expert:511-513: g_charts2[built].Configure(...); OpenChart(InpChartTf); OpenLayout(...)). The host calls g_charts2[i].Sync() (Expert:2830) but never g_charts2[i].Redraw() - grep of g_charts2 shows only Configure/OpenChart/OpenLayout/IdAt/FollowAll/CloseOwned/Sync. So on every secondary chart there is no explicit ChartNavigate(CHART_END) and no ChartRedraw at all: the view depends entirely on CHART_AUTOSCROLL, which this file documents (509-521) as not reliably honoured on a custom symbol written from an EA, and at SSR_FIDELITY_BAR no tick arrives to repaint them either (the host's own comment at Expert:2825-2827 says Redraw 'is the only thing that moves the chart at bar fidelity'). Outcome: the extra instruments show a still picture of a running replay, while the primary chart moves correctly - the same symptom, on the path that has no instrument to detect it (Snaps()/vitals only report g_charts).
findings.evidence: Redraw() is per-instance state (m_last_redraw_us, m_last_bar_time, m_snaps) and per-instance work; nothing inside CSSRChartManager reaches other instances. The primary manager is the only one the host redraws. Secondary charts do receive one ChartNavigate per play press, because Follow() (484) is reached from g_charts2[i].FollowAll() at Expert:2780, so they snap once on each Play and then drift for the rest of the run.

findings.title: The blind-mode reveal is undone within ~200ms: RestoreAll leaves the policy on and the host re-applies on IsOn()
findings.claim: State: InpBlind=STANDARD or FULL, session reaches SSR_STATE_COMPLETED, user presses the reveal card. Expert:3021 calls g_blind.RestoreAll(), which puts CHART_SHOW_DATE_SCALE / OHLC / PRICE_SCALE back and clears m_applied - but not m_policy. The housekeeping block runs unconditionally every 5th timer tick (Expert:2807-2808, outside the if(playing) guard) and tests IsOn(), not IsApplied(): 'if(g_blind.IsOn()) for(...) g_blind.Apply(g_charts.IdAt(bi));' (Expert:2822-2824). Apply() re-hides everything on the next pass. Net effect: the date scale (and in FULL the price scale and OHLC) come back for at most one 200ms frame and then disappear again, so the payoff of a blind session - looking at the chart you just traded with its dates restored - never happens. The chart only truly comes back when the EA is removed (Expert:2176).
findings.evidence: IsOn() returns m_policy.AnyOn() (line 136) and nothing in the class's public surface can clear m_policy - there is no Off()/ClearPolicy(); SetPolicy is called once, in BuildSession (Expert:1002). Apply() is idempotent by design (152-165) and re-saves the freshly restored state as the new 'original', so the record stays correct while the visible state flips back to blind.

findings.title: Blind mode's record of the user's original chart settings does not survive a reinit, and the next Apply saves the blinded state as the original
findings.claim: State: one-chart mode, InpBlind=FULL, session running with the chart already blinded (date scale, OHLC and price scale off, saved correctly on pass 2). The user then changes the chart's timeframe - the product's headline feature - or changes an input, or the EA is recompiled. That is REASON_CHARTCHANGE / REASON_PARAMETERS / REASON_RECOMPILE, and OnDeinit only calls g_blind.RestoreAll() inside 'if(user_removed)' (Expert:2152, 2176), so the chart stays blind while the instance - and with it m_id/m_had_* - is destroyed. The rebuilt instance starts with m_saved=0, Apply() finds the chart absent from its registry and records the CURRENT (already hidden) properties as the originals. From then on Restore() writes false back, so when the user finally removes the tool their chart keeps no date scale, no OHLC line and no price scale, and they must find and re-enable three chart properties by hand - precisely the trap the class header (lines 22-24) says it exists to avoid.
findings.evidence: The save-once guard is keyed on Find(chart_id) within the live instance only; nothing persists m_had_dates/m_had_ohlc/m_had_price (no session-file field, no terminal global - grep for CHART_SHOW_DATE_SCALE matches only this file). The chart properties themselves are terminal state and outlive the program, so after a reinit the 'before' state is unrecoverable. One-chart mode guarantees at least one reinit per session (the handover), and that first one is harmless only because pass 1 has no chart on the replay symbol yet (Expert:1421-1425 with Count()==0); every later reinit while blind is applied poisons the record.

findings.title: Blind FULL claims the price level is hidden while the entry-line label and the panel's deal buttons print the absolute price
findings.claim: State: InpBlind=SSR_BLIND_FULL (hide_price_scale=true). Leaks() therefore omits the price level from the list of what is still visible - i.e. it tells the user the price is hidden. It is not: SSR_TradeLines.mqh:413-422 writes the description 'BUY 0.20 at 4438.48' onto the entry line of every open and pending position (Level(base+"_E", ..., tip, tip)), with CHART_SHOW_OBJECT_DESCR forced on by Attach (line 183), and SSR_Panel.mqh:1479-1484 prints Price(ask)/Price(bid) on the Buy and Sell buttons unconditionally. A trader who chose FULL because they would recognise the period from its price levels sees an exact price the moment they look at the deal buttons, and permanently on the chart once they take a trade. The class whose stated ethic is to list what it cannot hide (lines 233-237) is silent about the one channel that is always open.
findings.evidence: Leaks() branches on !m_policy.hide_price_scale, so in FULL the price clause is suppressed; no other string mentions it. CSSRTradeLines has no knowledge of blind mode - it takes prices and formats them with m_digits - and the panel's price formatting is not routed through MaskTime/MaskSymbol (GroupPort:180-184 masks only the clock text and the symbol name).

findings.title: Bookmark vertical lines are never deleted and survive on the user's own chart after the session
findings.claim: State: one-chart mode (default), user presses B a few times during a session (GroupPort:490 -> MarkTime), then removes the EA. CSSRChartManager offers no ClearMarks(); grep for SSR_MARK_ finds exactly one hit in the whole tree - the creation site - and ObjectsDeleteAll is called only for SSR_NEWS_ (CalendarLines:116) and the widget prefix (SSR_Widgets.mqh:639). At teardown the host does not close this chart: it hands it back to the origin symbol (Expert:2194, ChartSetSymbolPeriod(ChartID(), g_origin, _Period)), and chart objects survive a symbol change and are saved with the chart. Outcome: dashed vertical lines at the bookmarked timestamps stay on the user's live origin chart indefinitely, one set per session, removable only by hand (they are HIDDEN=true, so they do not even appear in the terminal's object list where a user would look for them).
findings.evidence: MarkTime creates OBJ_VLINE objects with OBJPROP_HIDDEN=true (line 184) and no deletion path exists in this class or any caller. OnDeinit deletes the panel (g_panel.Destroy()), the calendar lines (g_cal_lines.Clear(), Expert:2120) and the trade lines (CSSRTradeLines destructor -> Clear()), but nothing named SSR_MARK_.

findings.title: LeakGuard::Advice is written far longer than the 49 characters its only consumer can display, so the actionable half never reaches the user
findings.claim: State: origin EURUSD open on one chart. Advice() returns 'EURUSD is open on 1 chart(s) - close it or your backtest is not blind' (68 chars). The single consumer is SSR_Panel.mqh:1892-1894: Clip(StringFormat("%-12s %s", T(SSR_S_CHARTS), advice), 62). T(SSR_S_CHARTS) is "Charts" (SSR_Strings.mqh:433) padded to 12 plus a space = 13 characters of prefix, leaving 49 for the advice, so the user reads 'Charts       EURUSD is open on 1 chart(s) - close it' and the instruction is cut mid-clause. The Market-Watch variant is 54 characters and is also truncated. The class's stated contract - 'never silent when dirty ... a backtesting tool that says nothing while the user can see the real price is lying to them' (SSR_ChartTypes.mqh:110-112) - degrades to a fragment, and there is no second channel: nothing renders other_live_charts, and Leaks()/ToString() only go to the log.
findings.evidence: Plain arithmetic on the format strings plus the 62-character Clip. The panel's own comment (SSR_Panel.mqh:1888-1891) records that this line 'has been ending "- close it or your" on the chart, mid-sentence' and clips it deliberately; clipping stopped the ragged cut, it did not make the sentence fit. The wording lives here, so this is where a 49-character message has to be authored.

findings.title: ViewOffset's stated assumption is contradicted by ApplyPolicy turning CHART_SHIFT on
findings.claim: The comment above this function (lines 111-113) states the premise: 'MetaTrader indexes bars from the right, so at the right edge the leftmost visible bar is (visible_bars - 1)'. That is a statement about a chart whose zero bar sits at the right border, and ApplyPolicy deliberately makes sure it never does: ChartSetInteger(id, CHART_SHIFT, true) at line 315, on every chart this manager opens or discovers. With the shift on, an empty gap of CHART_SHIFT_SIZE percent of the window sits to the right of the newest bar. Depending on whether CHART_VISIBLE_BARS counts the whole window in bar-slots or only the slots holding bars, ViewOffset at the right edge is either systematically negative (clamped to 0, so DetectScroll ignores any scroll smaller than the shift width - typically tens of bars - and Redraw keeps yanking the user back, the exact UX defect the feature exists to prevent) or systematically positive (permanent false detach on every chart the moment the first bar lands, killing follow for the whole session). Both branches are serious and the same number drives the detach test and the snap test (line 568), so they cannot be decoupled.
findings.evidence: The contradiction between the comment's premise and ApplyPolicy is in the source. Which branch occurs depends on MetaTrader's runtime definition of CHART_VISIBLE_BARS under CHART_SHIFT, which cannot be resolved from this tree: no spike, test or QA check measures the offset with the shift on (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:670-702 reuses the same formula rather than validating it, and reports 'the snap is untested on this screen' when it cannot scroll away).

findings.title: A live chart on a correlated symbol is counted and then discarded: the panel says 'no leak'
findings.code:
else if(!SSRIsReplaySymbol(s))
            m_report.other_live_charts++;
findings.claim: State: replaying US30 while a live SP500 (or DAX) chart is open in the next window. Scan() counts it in other_live_charts, but SSRLeakReport::IsClean() (SSR_ChartTypes.mqh:105-108) tests only origin_in_watch and origin_charts, and Advice() (89-97) returns "" when IsClean(). GroupPort:168-169 copies exactly those two values into the port state, so the Session tab prints T(SSR_S_CHARTS_CLEAN) - 'no leak' - while a live, highly correlated instrument is on screen telling the trader which way the market went. The vocabulary file declares this case as a leak that is not structurally impossible (ENUM_SSR_LEAK::SSR_LEAK_OTHER_SYMBOL_CHART, SSR_ChartTypes.mqh:89), and the count exists, so the measurement is taken and then dropped.
findings.evidence: other_live_charts appears in exactly three places: the increment here, ToString() (101-104, log only) and the struct. No caller reads it (grep: only T4 reads OriginCharts/ReplayCharts/OriginInWatch). The enum value is never assigned to anything.

findings.title: A detached chart has no user-visible surface: the observer is never wired and charts_detached is never rendered
findings.claim: State: any chart that detaches - deliberately (the user scrolled back) or falsely (chart-1). CSSRChartManager::SetObserver (line 141) has no production caller (grep: only Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T4_ChartIntegration.mq5:40), so m_observer is NULL in the EA and OnUserScrolled/OnUserFollowed/OnTimeframeChanged/OnChartOpened/OnChartClosed fire into nothing. The one remaining channel, DetachedCount() -> GroupPort:122 -> SSRReplayPortState.charts_detached, is never read by SSR_Panel.mqh (grep for charts_detached matches only the struct declaration, its Init and the assignment). Outcome: the replay advances, the candles stop moving, and the interface says nothing at all; the user has to already know that F re-attaches. This is also why a false detach (chart-1) would be reported as 'the candles do not move' rather than as a scroll problem - the flight recorder writes a 'following' column (Expert:2421-2423) but the panel shows nothing.
findings.evidence: Confirmed by absence of callers for both channels, plus the deliberate CHART_AUTOSCROLL=false at line 463, which means the terminal will not recover on its own either.

findings.title: The draggable planning lines are created after the panel and are not behind it, so they are drawn across it
findings.claim: State: one-chart mode, so the panel and the lines share one chart. The panel's objects are created in OnInit; the SL/TP lines are created later, when the user presses the SL/TP button (Arm/ArmSide -> Ensure). An OBJ_HLINE spans the full chart width with BACK=false, so once the stop or target price falls at a y-coordinate inside the panel's 310x336 frame, the dash-dot line is painted across the panel's rectangles and text. Creation order is the only z-order MQL5 has, and the later object is the one on top, so nothing keeps the line behind the panel: OBJPROP_ZORDER (set to 0 here, 100 on every widget via SSR_Widgets.mqh:164) governs which object receives a click, not what is painted over what.
findings.evidence: Confirmed from code: the lines are BACK=false and created on demand, after the panel; ZORDER is a click-priority property in MQL5, and the only two values in this tree (0 here, 100 for widgets) are consistent with that use - clicks are correctly won by the panel. What cannot be verified from source is MetaTrader's painting order across object classes (OBJ_HLINE vs OBJ_RECTANGLE_LABEL/OBJ_BUTTON), which is why this is a risk rather than a confirmed rendering defect. It needs one screenshot on a terminal with the stop dragged to the panel's height.

findings.title: Every word the Chart layer draws or hands to the panel is a hardcoded English literal, outside audit A19's reach
findings.code: ObjectSetString (m_chart, n, OBJPROP_TEXT, tip);
findings.claim: State: InpLanguage="fa", the Persian file complete at 190/190. The planning lines print 'STOP - drag me', 'TARGET - drag me' and 'ENTRY - drag me' on the chart (tips passed in at lines 200, 243-244, 277-278, 298-299, 315, drawn as OBJPROP_TEXT here with CHART_SHOW_OBJECT_DESCR forced on at line 183); position levels print 'BUY'/'SELL'/'SL'/'TP' and 'stop of BUY 0.20 at ...' (411-438); closed trades print '#12 buy 0.21 in at ...' (546-564); and the leak advice reaches the panel itself in English (SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:94-96). So a Persian user gets a translated panel with English labels on the only objects they are asked to interact with, and one English sentence inside the Session tab. Nothing reports this: audit A19's literal check skips every path that does not contain '/Ui/' (tools/ssr_audit.py:1458), so the Chart layer is invisible to the audit that exists to catch exactly this, and its vacuous-pass guard (>=100 resolved T() calls) still passes on the Ui files alone.
findings.evidence: The literals are in the source at the lines quoted; SSR_Strings.mqh has no entries for them; the audit's directory filter is explicit.

findings.title: The flight recorder truncates chart_id to 32 bits, corrupting the column that identifies which chart a fault happened on
findings.code: s.chart_count, (int)s.chart_id,
findings.claim: State: any recorded session. The host fills s.chart_id with a real chart id (Expert:2408-2409, long from ChartID()/IdAt()). MetaTrader chart ids are 64-bit values derived from creation time and routinely exceed INT_MAX, so the (int) cast writes a truncated - frequently negative - number into the chart_id column of the black box. The one artefact the author relies on for remote diagnosis (they cannot run the product themselves) then carries a chart id that matches nothing the user or the log can show, in a file whose whole purpose is to remove a round trip. Same cast, same effect, for s.emit_ticks/emit_calls on a long session.
findings.evidence: The truncation is in the source; the %d specifier forces a 32-bit argument, so the fix is %I64d or IntegerToString rather than the cast. The claim that real chart ids exceed 32 bits is an inference from MT5's id scheme, not from this tree - but the cast is lossy for any id above 2^31 regardless.

findings.title: OpenLayout counts each chart twice against SSR_MAX_CHARTS
findings.code:
if(m_count + opened >= SSR_MAX_CHARTS)
            break;                        // the ceiling, honoured quietly
findings.claim: State: InpExtraTfs listing many timeframes. OpenChart() (204) ends with Sync(), which registers the chart it just opened, so m_count already includes it; `opened` then counts it a second time. The ceiling therefore trips at roughly half of SSR_MAX_CHARTS (16) and silently stops opening charts the user asked for, with no message - the comment calls it 'honoured quietly'.
findings.evidence: OpenChart calls Sync() at line 213 before returning the id, and Sync's discovery branch (346-370) Adds any chart whose symbol matches, incrementing m_count. Whether the newly opened chart is visible to ChartSymbol() on that same Sync depends on how synchronously the terminal completes ChartOpen, which cannot be settled from source - hence POTENTIAL_RISK rather than confirmed; if it is visible (the likely case, since ChartOpen returns the id), the ceiling is halved.

findings.title: SetPeriodAll would restart the EA in one-chart mode; it is unreachable today, so nothing has caught it
findings.claim: State: one-chart mode, where g_replay_chart == ChartID() (Expert:1276) and Sync() therefore registers the EA's own chart (line 344 matches on symbol alone). If anything ever calls SetPeriodAll - it is labelled 'Phase 11 sync uses this' - the loop calls ChartSetSymbolPeriod on the chart the program is running on, which is REASON_CHARTCHANGE: the EA is torn down and rebuilt mid-call, so the rest of the loop, the Sync() and everything the caller intended never run. The host already treats this exact call as a deliberate, announced, once-per-session event (Expert:2694-2703, with a Comment() explaining the blank second), which is the measure of how much a 'sync the timeframes' button would cost if it went through here.
findings.evidence: No caller exists anywhere in the tree (grep for SetPeriodAll returns only this definition), so this is latent rather than live, and the registry's own contract makes the host chart a member. The class has no notion of 'the chart we are standing on' outside CloseOwned (280-291), where the same hazard is spelled out at length.

findings.title: Calendar line objects are named by collection index, so the idempotence check pins stale events if the feed is ever redrawn
findings.claim: The object identity is the item's position in CSSRCalendar, not the event. Draw() is documented as idempotent and safe to call from the timer (lines 66-70), but if it is ever called after the collection changes - a reload with a different importance floor, a different window, a second Load() - every index that already has an object is skipped, so the line keeps the previous event's time and its 'USD Non-Farm Payrolls' label while the item behind that index is now a different release. The user then sees a news line on a candle that had no news. Today this cannot fire: LoadCalendar is the only caller and runs once per program instance (Expert:921-940), with Clear() on every deinit (Expert:2120) - so this is a latent trap for whoever adds a reload, not a live defect.
findings.evidence: Name construction and the ObjectFind short-circuit are in the source; Clear() (111-120) is the only way the objects go, and it is not called from Draw.

findings.title: MarkTime puts the registry index in the object name, so bookmarks duplicate after a chart closes
findings.claim: State: two replay charts (M5 at registry index 0, H1 at index 1). The user bookmarks 10:37: chart A gets SSR_MARK_t_0, chart B gets SSR_MARK_t_1. The user closes chart A; Sync's Remove() (98-106) shifts the array down so chart B is now index 0. Bookmarking 10:37 again (after a rewind, or pressing B twice) creates SSR_MARK_t_0 on chart B, which already carries SSR_MARK_t_1 at the same time - two identical dashed lines on one chart, and one more for every further shift. The suffix is meant to make the name unique per chart, but the index it uses is not a chart identity.
findings.evidence: Remove() renumbers by copying entries down, and the name is rebuilt from the current loop index on every call. Combined with chart-6 (nothing deletes SSR_MARK_*), the duplicates are permanent.

performance_notes: Hot path, every 5th pump (~200ms) per manager: Sync() walks EVERY chart in the terminal (ChartFirst/ChartNext + ChartSymbol per chart, SSR_ChartManager.mqh:341-409) and then 2 ChartGetInteger per managed chart inside DetectScroll. With a multi-symbol board this happens 1 + g_extra times (Expert:2817 and 2830), i.e. up to 4 full terminal-wide chart walks per 200ms. Cheap per call, but it is proportional to how many charts the USER has open, not to how many the tool manages.

Redraw() adds one SeriesInfoInteger(m_symbol, PERIOD_M1, SERIES_LASTBAR_DATE) plus, per managed chart, 2 ChartGetInteger (ViewOffset) and 1 ChartRedraw. Throttled by SSR_REDRAW_MIN_INTERVAL_MS=100 with m_redraws_skipped as the instrument, so the throttle is measurable at runtime (T4 asserts >40 skips).

CSSRTradeLines has NO property cache, unlike the Ui layer (SSR_Widgets.mqh's 512-slot FNV-1a cache, justified by the measured 561 writes = 39.05 ms). Level() unconditionally rewrites 5 properties per level (86-94) and DrawPosition adds 1-2 ChartGetInteger for CHART_COLOR_STOP_LEVEL/BACKGROUND per position (417-418). At 3 levels per position that is roughly 17-20 property writes per open position per sweep, every 200ms (Expert:2915). Ten open positions is ~200 writes per pass on the same chart the panel is already repainting at 10 fps - the single most likely place in this subsystem to starve the timer (the host already tracks g_starved for exactly this failure).

EndPositions() (445-475) enumerates every OBJ_HLINE on the chart and does a StringFind/StringSubstr/StringToInteger per name plus a linear scan of m_seen per object, then one ChartRedraw - O(hlines x positions) every 200ms. The host comment at Expert:2908-2912 shows this was already reduced from 25 Hz to 5 Hz for this reason. SSR_HIST_ objects are arrows/trend lines so they do not inflate this list; SSR_LINE_* and any user HLINE do.

Poll() runs at full pump rate (25 Hz at InpPumpMs=40): 2-3 ObjectGetDouble plus up to 3 ObjectGetInteger and 3 ObjectSetInteger for the SELECTED re-assertion (321-333). The SELECTED writes happen only when the read says false, so the steady-state cost is reads only.
CSSRCalendarLines::Draw costs one ObjectFind per event per call and is called once per session - the file's claim (lines 5-8) matches the code.
CSSRFlightRecorder flushes on every line (FileFlush, 115) - deliberate, and bounded to ~2 samples/second by Due() plus the 5000-row cap, so ~2 flushes/sec steady state.

CSSRLog::Emit opens, seeks, writes and closes the log file per line (44-51). Harmless today because SetFile() is never called, but it would be a per-line file open on the pump path if a future caller enabled the sink at DEBUG/TRACE.
test_gaps: Nothing exercises DetectScroll's false-positive boundary: there is no test where many bars arrive between two Sync passes (high speed / MAX) with no user input, which is the chart-1 scenario. SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:670-702 deliberately avoids Sync while testing the snap ('NO Sync in between'), so the interaction between the snap and the detach vote is untested by construction.

ViewOffset is never validated against CHART_SHIFT/CHART_SHIFT_SIZE, which ApplyPolicy turns on. Both the QA smoke test (671-687) and the vitals/flight code (Expert:2333-2336, 2413-2417) re-implement the same formula instead of checking it, so a wrong premise would agree with itself everywhere.

No test or QA check covers the secondary streams' charts (g_charts2[]): nothing asserts that a chart of an extra symbol follows the right edge or repaints, which is why the missing Redraw call (chart-2) is invisible.

Blind mode is tested only in-process (SSR_T11_AdvancedReplay.mq5:479-487 for MaskTime/MaskSymbol/Anonymous, SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:3667-3701 for Apply/RestoreAll). Nothing tests (a) restore across an EA reinit (REASON_CHARTCHANGE/PARAMETERS/RECOMPILE) or (b) that a RestoreAll is not immediately undone by the host's IsOn() re-apply loop - the two defects chart-3 and chart-4.
No test asserts that SSR_MARK_* objects are removable or that a second bookmark at the same time does not duplicate; MarkTime is not covered at all (its only caller is GroupPort::Bookmark).
CSSRCalendarLines has no test for a second Draw() after the collection changes, which is the only way the index-based naming (chart-16) can bite.

LeakGuard: T4 checks only that the origin is detected (OriginInWatch || OriginCharts>0). Nothing asserts that Advice() fits the 49 characters the panel can render, and nothing covers other_live_charts reaching the user at all.

CSSRChartObserver is implemented only by a test double (SSR_T4_ChartIntegration.mq5:40); no test asserts that the production host wires an observer, so the fact that it never does (chart-10) passes unnoticed.
SetPeriodAll has neither a caller nor a test - including no test that it refuses to touch ChartID().

CSSRFlightRecorder has no test at all: the header/Event/Write column counts (which I verified by hand here), the 5000-row cap, the 500ms Due() gate and the GetTickCount wrap are unexercised, and no test reads a written file back to prove chart_id round-trips.
CSSRLog: the file sink (SetFile/Emit's file branch) is never called by any program or test - dead, untested code on disk.

findings.title: has_ticks is probed over the last 24 hours of history but then selects FULL_TICK fidelity for a replay window that may be years earlier — the replay emits nothing, the clock runs to the end, and nothing reports it
findings.claim: Broker keeps 30 days of tick history for EURUSD but 5 years of M1 bars. The user replays 2021.03.01..2021.03.15. Discover() probes ticks over the LAST day of history (today), finds them, and sets out.has_ticks=true. The host then does g_ctrl.SetFidelity(range.has_ticks ? SSR_FIDELITY_FULL_TICK : SSR_FIDELITY_SYNTHETIC_TICK) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1153) and the controller does m_fidelity.SetTicksAvailable(range.has_ticks) (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:806). Every pump then calls ReadTicks over March 2021, CopyTicksRange returns 0 (no tick base that far back), ReadTicks returns 0 with Succeed(), and EmitWindow's FULL_TICK branch does `emitted = 0; m_cursor.Advance(hi, 0, 0); return emitted;`. No bar is ever written to the custom symbol. The chart sits on the warmup, the clock walks to end_msc, the session reaches COMPLETED, and no error, warning or fidelity degradation is produced. The one diagnostic that does fire prints the opposite: SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2267 prints "this session is replaying the broker's REAL ticks, so the spread on every one of them is the broker's own".
findings.evidence: The probe range is hardcoded to [last_msc-86400000, last_msc] — the newest day of history — and is the only thing that sets out.has_ticks. CSSRMt5DataSource::Ticks() (SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:91-96) returns the provider whenever m_has_ticks is true, so the engine's only fallback (`if(tp == NULL) { ... m_fidelity.SetTicksAvailable(false); }`, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:337-345) never fires. CSSRFidelityPolicy::Decide degrades FULL_TICK only on !m_ticks_available (SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:114-118), which was set true. The range-aware question already exists — CSSRMt5TickProvider::HasTicks(symbol, from_msc, to_msc) at SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:379 — and a repo-wide grep shows it has no caller. This is exactly the failure the Ticks()-returns-NULL contract was written to prevent: its own comment at SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:86-89 says "Returning it unconditionally would let the engine run at FULL_TICK fidelity against an empty tick history and emit nothing - a replay that silently shows a frozen market." The file header itself states "Tick history is OPTIONAL and usually shallow, especially for CFDs" (lines 16-19). If CopyTicksRange instead returns -1 while the terminal tries and fails to fetch old ticks, ReadTicks burns its 15 s retry budget per pump and then returns -1, which at least surfaces an error — so the silent variant is the 0 case.

findings.title: One invalid-OHLC or non-positive M1 bar voids the ENTIRE read window (up to 60,000 bars), and the provider reports that as zero bars with success, so the engine advances the clock showing nothing
findings.claim: A single M1 bar anywhere in the loaded range has high < low, or any of O/H/L/C == 0.0 (a broker zero-print or bad tick, which the file's own header calls out: "broker history is not guaranteed clean"). SanitizeBars does not remove such bars — it only drops duplicates and backwards stamps — so m_last_report.invalid_ohlc (or .nonpositive) stays non-zero, IsUsable() returns false, and Ensure() discards the whole window: every good bar in it too. The window reload span is max(requested span, m_window_bars), and m_window_bars comes from SuggestWindowBars, i.e. 5,000..60,000 minutes. So one bad print silently blanks between 3.5 and 41 days of replay. Worse, the error code chosen is SSR_ERR_NO_DATA, and CSSRMt5BarProvider::ReadBars turns that into `Succeed(); return 0;` (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:265-275). The controller then does `nb = m_guard.FilterRates(m_bars, 0); if(nb <= 0) { m_cursor.Advance(hi, 0, 0); return 0; }` (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:388-393): the clock advances, no candle appears, no error is set, no log line is written. The same path kills the warmup: SeedWarmup at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:885-897 gets n=0, skips SeedBars entirely, and the session starts with no context candles at all and no message.
findings.evidence: The rejection is unconditional on the whole loaded array, while the repair step above it (line 209, SanitizeBars) only enforces strictly-increasing open times — CSSRDataValidator::SanitizeBars (SSR_DataValidator.mqh:265-282) never inspects prices. The comment on line 207 states the intent ("broker history is not guaranteed clean; make it replay-safe") which the OHLC branch then contradicts by refusing rather than repairing. The choice of SSR_ERR_NO_DATA over SSR_ERR_LOAD_FAILED is what makes the failure silent: SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:268-272 reads `if(m_window.LastError() == SSR_ERR_NO_DATA) { Succeed(); return 0; }` with the comment "no data in range is not an error; a failed LOAD is". SSR_T2_DataEngine.mq5:136-143 asserts only that the REPORT flags bad OHLC ("unusable data is flagged", !rx.IsUsable()); no test covers what the window or the engine then does, so the whole-window blanking and the silent clock advance are untested.

findings.title: CSSRRandomPicker draws candidate symbols WITH REPLACEMENT, so a symbol that has enough history can be skipped entirely and the pick reported as impossible
findings.claim: InpRandom=true with InpAlsoSymbols="XAUUSD,US30" on origin EURUSD gives a pool of 3 and attempts=3. The draws are independent, so XAUUSD can be drawn on all three attempts. If XAUUSD lacks the depth but EURUSD and US30 have it, Pick() returns false with "no candidate had enough history: XAUUSD (needs ...) XAUUSD (needs ...) XAUUSD (needs ...)" and the host falls back to a non-random window (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1043-1046). With a pool of 3 where exactly one symbol qualifies, the chance of never drawing it in 3 independent draws is (2/3)^3 = 29.6%; with two of three failing it is (2/3)^3 for the good one and the feature fails roughly three times in ten with no indication that the answer was available.
findings.evidence: m_rng.Index(m_pool_count) samples uniformly over the whole pool on every iteration; nothing removes or marks a rejected candidate, and the loop body only appends to m_skipped and continues. attempts is capped at min(m_pool_count, 8), so for any pool of size n the loop makes at most n draws from n with replacement — by construction it cannot guarantee coverage of the pool it is bounded by. The bound's own comment ("how many symbols to try before giving up. Bounded, because a list where nothing has enough history must produce an error the user can read, not a loop", lines 31-34) shows the intent was to try each candidate; the code tries n random candidates instead. A secondary effect: AddSymbol returns true for a duplicate without adding it (lines 78-82), so AddSymbolList's "added" count and the duplicate entries in m_skipped both overstate what happened.

findings.title: warmup_bars is used both as a count of M1 bars and as a span of wall-clock minutes; on any instrument that does not quote every minute this produces false "not enough history" refusals and silently short warmup context
findings.code:
q.available_bars  = m_range.bar_count;
      q.exceeds_history = (m_range.available && q.total_bars > m_range.bar_count);
findings.claim: Two concrete wrong outcomes on the same instrument. Take a stock/index CFD quoting ~6.5 h a day, 5 days a week (~1,950 M1 bars per week), for which the broker holds 2 years of M1 = about 203,000 bars, and a request of D1 context with visible_bars=200. (a) FALSE REFUSAL: WarmupFor(PERIOD_D1, 200) = 200 * (86400/60) = 288,000, so q.total_bars = 288,000 + replay_minutes > 203,000 and exceeds_history is true. SSRValidateRange returns "not enough history: needs 290000 M1 bars, broker has 203000" (SSR_SessionRange.mqh:90-91) and CSSRRangeDialog refuses to start — even though 2 years is roughly 500 trading days, two and a half times the 200 daily candles asked for. CSSRRandomPicker skips the same symbol by name via LatestStart/EarliestStart. (b) SILENT SHORTFALL: when the request is accepted, EarliestStart(288000) = first_msc + 288,000 * 60,000 msc = first_msc + exactly 200 CALENDAR days (SSR_HistoryCatalog.mqh:174). 200 calendar days on a 5-day week is about 143 trading days, so a start at that floor delivers ~143 D1 candles of context, not the 200 requested, and nothing reports the shortfall.
findings.evidence: WarmupFor (lines 126-132) returns `visible * (secs/60)`, i.e. the number of MINUTES the requested number of tf-candles spans on a 24 h clock. Quote then compares that number against m_range.bar_count, which CSSRMt5HistoryProvider::Discover fills from SERIES_BARS_COUNT (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:99, 131) — a count of bars that actually exist, not of minutes elapsed. EarliestStart/LatestStart (lines 161-175) multiply the same number by SSR_MSC_PER_MIN, treating it as elapsed time. The two readings are only equal when the instrument quotes every minute of every day; for anything else they diverge by the quote-density factor, and the code has no notion of that factor anywhere. SSR_T6_History.mq5:39-47 asserts only the arithmetic of WarmupFor itself (288000 for D1/200), never that the number is usable as either a bar count or a time span, so the conflation is untested in both directions.

findings.title: CSSRMt5HistoryProvider::Ensure has no SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED early-out, so a range that legitimately holds zero M1 bars blocks the terminal for 20 seconds and then fails the session load
findings.claim: A session window that contains no M1 bars at all — a range entirely inside a weekend or a market holiday, reachable through a resumed session file, a hand-set InpStart, or a picked range whose warmup_first_msc..end_msc falls in a closure — makes CopyRates return 0 on every pass. Only got>0 exits the loop, so the loop runs the full SSR_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS (20,000 ms) at Sleep(50) per iteration — roughly 400 full-range CopyRates calls and 20 seconds during which the EA thread is blocked and the terminal shows an unresponsive chart. It then reports Fail(SSR_ERR_LOAD_FAILED, "could not prepare ... err=0") and CSSRReplayController::Load turns that into SetError(SSR_ERR_LOAD_FAILED, "history could not be prepared") + Transition(SSR_STATE_ERROR) (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:789-795) — a hard session failure for a condition the codebase elsewhere calls normal data.
findings.evidence: CSSRBarWindow::LoadRange, written for the same async problem in the same subsystem, has exactly the missing branch (SSR_BarWindow.mqh:93-98): `if(got == 0) { long synced = 0; if(SeriesInfoInteger(symbol, PERIOD_M1, SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED, synced) && synced != 0) break; }` with the comment "Zero bars means the range genuinely holds none - a weekend, a holiday, a session break - and that is normal data, not a failure. Only retry it while the series is still syncing; once synced, believe the zero instead of spinning out the whole timeout." Ensure's loop has no such test, so the asymmetry is internal to the subsystem rather than a judgement call. SSRPause(50) is Sleep(50) for an EA (SSR_Platform.mqh:27-32), so the 20 s is a real block, not a poll. Ensure is called once per Load (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:789) so this is a startup/resume stall, not a per-pump one.

findings.title: CSSRCalendar loads the whole replay window and exposes every item with no "has the clock reached it" filter, so its only consumer creates a vertical line for every future release at session start
findings.claim: A user replays 2024.03.04..2024.03.08 with InpNews=SSR_NEWS_MODERATE. The host calls g_cal.Load(origin, win_start, win_end, ...) with the ENTIRE window (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:938, 1282) and immediately g_cal_lines.Draw(GetPointer(g_cal)) (:940). CSSRCalendarLines::Draw walks At(0..Count-1) and does ObjectCreate(m_chart, n, OBJ_VLINE, 0, (datetime)(it.msc/1000), 0) for every item (SSR_CalendarLines.mqh:71-95). At the moment the replay begins on Monday, an OBJ_VLINE already exists on the replay chart at Friday's Non-Farm Payrolls, with OBJPROP_TEXT and OBJPROP_TOOLTIP set to "USD  Nonfarm Payrolls". Any of those lines that falls inside the chart's right margin/shift is future information the replay has not reached — the trader can see a release is coming and roughly when, which is the one thing a market-replay trainer must not show.
findings.evidence: Load's window is the caller's full replay window widened by ±1 day (SSR_Calendar.mqh:217-218), and nothing between Load and At filters on the clock. CSSRCalendar is a CSSRTickObserver and already receives OnClock(now_msc) (line 275) — it has the clock and uses it for the pause — but offers no now-bounded accessor, so the drawing layer cannot do better without new API here. The class's own header says "IT READS, IT DOES NOT DRAW", which is why the omission lands on the consumer. The design was clearly considered for the adjacent risk: the host refuses to load the calendar at all under blind mode because "a line labelled 'USD Non-Farm Payrolls' on a date the mode exists to hide gives away the whole session in one object" (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:912-916) — the same reasoning applies to a line the replay has not reached, and is not applied. I cannot verify from source how far past the last bar MT5 actually renders an OBJ_VLINE (it depends on chart shift and zoom, and OBJPROP_HIDDEN=true does keep them out of the Ctrl+B object list), so the object's existence is confirmed and its on-screen visibility is not.

findings.title: Discover() discards the last COMPLETE M1 bar whenever the market is closed, shortening every available range by one minute
findings.claim: The user starts a session on a Saturday. SERIES_LASTBAR_DATE is Friday 23:59 (a complete bar — the market is shut, no further tick will ever land in it) and SYMBOL_TIME_MSC is Friday's final quote, say 23:59:58.3. The test last_quote <= lastbar_close (23:59:59.999) is true, so out.last_msc becomes 23:58:59.999 and the 23:59 bar is excluded from the available range. The host uses this directly as win_end (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1075), so the replay stops one minute earlier than the data allows, and CSSRHistoryCatalog::LatestStart/CanStartAt inherit the same one-minute shortfall.
findings.evidence: The test asks "does the symbol's last quote fall inside the last bar?" as a proxy for "is that bar still forming", but the two differ precisely when quoting has stopped: for a closed market the last quote always falls inside the last bar, and the bar is nevertheless final. There is no check of the symbol's trade/quote session state (SymbolInfoSessionQuote, SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE) or of how far behind the last quote is relative to wall time, either of which would separate the two cases. The cost is bounded at one M1 bar, which is why this is LOW, but it is a systematic off-by-one on the timeline bound that every other class in the subsystem trusts.

findings.title: The calendar's availability probe treats "no events anywhere in this window" as "this terminal has no calendar" — the exact confusion the probe was added to prevent
findings.claim: A short replay window — say two hours on 2024.12.25 — widened by ±1 day still spans only 2024.12.24..2024.12.26. On a terminal whose calendar is present and working but holds no scheduled releases across those dates, the unfiltered probe returns 0, m_available is set false, Load returns false, and Note() reports "this terminal returned no calendar at all for 2024.12.24..2024.12.26 (error 0) - some servers do not publish one. This is not the same as a quiet week." The host prints that verbatim (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:948-949). The user is told the feature is missing when it is working and the week is genuinely quiet — the inverse of the distinction the probe exists to make.
findings.evidence: The probe measures event COUNT over the same narrow window rather than the presence of the calendar facility. The comment block immediately above it (lines 239-242) states the goal: "A terminal with no calendar and a quiet week both produce zero events; only one of them is a missing feature" — and the implementation then uses zero events as the discriminator. A window-independent question exists in the same API family (CalendarCountries / CalendarEventByCurrency, or inspecting GetLastError for the no-calendar error rather than printing it inside a message that has already decided), and the code already calls GetLastError() here but only to quote it.

findings.title: SSR_NEWS_ALL ("Everything the calendar has") floors importance at LOW, silently excluding CALENDAR_IMPORTANCE_NONE events such as bank holidays
findings.claim: A user sets InpNews=SSR_NEWS_ALL, whose enum comment reads "Everything the calendar has", and replays a week containing a US bank holiday. MetaTrader publishes holidays and non-scheduled entries with importance CALENDAR_IMPORTANCE_NONE (0). Pull's filter `if((int)ev.importance < min_importance) continue;` with min_importance = CALENDAR_IMPORTANCE_LOW (1) drops every one of them, so the chart shows no line on the day whose thin, rangeless price action the trader is about to draw a conclusion from — and Note() then says "the calendar is there, and holds nothing at this importance for these currencies in this window", attributing the absence to the filter the user just set to maximum.
findings.evidence: ENUM_CALENDAR_EVENT_IMPORTANCE is NONE=0, LOW=1, MODERATE=2, HIGH=3. The fall-through branch returns LOW, not NONE, so the widest setting the UI offers is still a filter. Nothing downstream re-adds them: Pull (line 152-153 region) is the only insertion point. The fix is one token (return (int)CALENDAR_IMPORTANCE_NONE for the ALL case), and the label "Everything the calendar has" is what makes the current behaviour a defect rather than a choice.

findings.title: SSRValidateRange never compares end_msc against the catalogue's last available instant, so a request that runs past the broker's history validates clean
findings.claim: A request with start_msc = cat.LastMsc() - 10*60000 and end_msc = cat.LastMsc() + 10*SSR_MSC_PER_DAY passes every test in this function: origin set, catalogue available, start positive, end > start, start above EarliestStart, start below LastMsc, and q.exceeds_history false because total_bars (warmup + 14,410) is comfortably under a deep symbol's bar_count. SSRValidateRange returns "", CSSRRangeDialog::CanStart() is satisfied, and the session is accepted with only ten minutes of data behind a window ten days long — the replay would run out of bars after ten minutes and walk the remaining ten days emitting nothing.
findings.evidence: The validation chain (lines 71-98) tests start_msc against both cat.EarliestStart and cat.LastMsc but tests end_msc only against start_msc ("the end must come after the start"); cat.LastMsc() never appears on the right-hand side of an end_msc comparison. q.exceeds_history is not a substitute: it compares a total bar count against the symbol's whole bar_count and is blind to WHERE in the timeline the range sits. This is latent rather than live in v125 — CSSRRangeDialog seeds end_msc = cat.LastMsc() and only ever edits start_msc (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:109, 272), and the host uses a confirmed range only as a jump inside the already-loaded window (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3183-3192) — but it is a hole in the one function whose entire job is to be the complete answer to "why can this request not be served", and any future caller that builds a range from a duration will hit it.

findings.title: Every data-quality number this subsystem measures is computed on the hot path and then discarded; the only route to a human is a ToString() with no caller
findings.claim: A user reports "some candles are missing in the middle of Tuesday". The information needed to answer that already exists: CSSRBarWindow ran ValidateBars on the exact range (duplicates, out_of_order, micro_gaps, session_gaps, largest_gap_msc) and counted m_dropped for every bar SanitizeBars removed. None of it reaches the log, the vitals line, or the flight recorder: ReportInto (SSR_BarWindow.mqh:329) has no caller, Dropped() has no caller, and the only expression that formats them — m_bars.Window().ToString() inside this function — is itself unreachable (`grep -rn "src.ToString\|source.ToString\|g_src.ToString"` returns nothing). The author, who cannot run this on a terminal, has no way to learn that bars were silently dropped or that the range was gappy.
findings.evidence: Repo-wide grep confirms the chain is dead at both ends: no caller for CSSRMt5DataSource::ToString, none for CSSRBarWindow::ReportInto or Dropped(), and no occurrence of "dropped", "micro_gap", "session_gap" or "duplicates" anywhere in MQL5/Experts, Ui, Common or Core outside the validator itself. CSSRMt5TickProvider::Pages/TicksRead/ReadTimeMs are equally unread. The instrumentation was written deliberately — SSR_BarWindow.mqh:53 says "instrumentation, so Phase 7 tunes with numbers not opinions" — so this is an unfinished wiring, not an absent idea. It compounds data-2 and data-1: both of those failures are silent precisely because this telemetry never surfaces.

findings.title: ReadTicks resumes a truncated page at last+1 ms, so any ticks sharing the truncation-boundary millisecond are dropped from the replay
findings.claim: A FULL_TICK pump over a fast-market minute: CopyTicksRange truncates its answer mid-millisecond, so the page ends with the first of four ticks stamped 10:31:05.123 and the remaining three are not returned. cursor becomes ...123+1, so the next page starts at .124 and those three ticks are never read. At FULL_TICK fidelity the sink therefore receives a minute whose extreme (a spike high or low that happened in those three ticks) is absent, and a virtual stop placed at that level is not hit when it would have been in reality — the one thing FULL_TICK exists to get right.
findings.evidence: The +1 is correct and necessary for the non-truncated case (the provider's contract is half-open at the bottom, and re-requesting from `last` would re-emit the boundary tick), but it also excludes every other tick that shares `last`. CSSRDataValidator::SanitizeTicks in the same file deliberately preserves equal stamps ("two ticks MAY share a millisecond legitimately", SSR_DataValidator.mqh:284-288), so the subsystem elsewhere acknowledges exactly the case this line loses. A safe variant is to resume at `last` and drop the already-taken prefix, or to walk back to the first tick carrying `last` before setting the cursor. I cannot verify from source whether CopyTicksRange ever truncates mid-millisecond — the loop's own comments say truncation happens and that "a truncated read looks exactly like a quiet market", but the boundary behaviour is undocumented and cannot be measured without a terminal — so this is a risk, not a confirmed loss.

key_facts: The subsystem is the ONLY MT5 implementation of the three provider contracts in Core/SSR_IDataSource.mqh. Everything above CSSRMt5DataSource believes it is talking to abstractions; every CopyRates/CopyTicksRange/CopyTime/SeriesInfoInteger call in the replay path lives in SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh and SSR_BarWindow.mqh.

Nothing in the data subsystem writes to disk or draws on a chart. CSSRCalendar is the only class that reads a non-price terminal facility; CSSRCalendarLines (Chart layer) is the only thing that draws its output.

CSSRBarWindow is a bounded FORWARD read window, not a cache: reload extends from bar_open(from) by max(requested span, m_window_bars) minutes, so it routinely holds bars LATER than the future-guard horizon. The guard is applied only on the way out (GuardRange in ReadBars, m_guard.Allows in ReadBarAt) — never on the way in.

Coverage is deliberately recorded WIDER than the bars present (SSR_BarWindow.mqh:245-246), and a window holding zero bars is a valid, successful answer. Only SSR_ERR_LOAD_FAILED / SSR_ERR_INTERNAL are treated as errors; SSR_ERR_NO_DATA is converted to 'zero bars, success' by CSSRMt5BarProvider::ReadBars.

CSSRDataValidator::SanitizeBars enforces strictly-increasing open times only. It never repairs or removes bad-OHLC or non-positive bars, while SSRDataReport::IsUsable() treats a single such bar as fatal — the two halves of the contract do not meet.

Session-gap thresholds are read from the instrument, never hardcoded: SSRSymbolSessionGap returns the WIDEST weekly silence (for 'is this damage?') and SSRSymbolSessionBreak the NARROWEST (for 'did the market reopen?'), both floored at one hour, both falling back to SSR_SESSION_GAP_MSC when the symbol declares no sessions. The ~40-line collection loop is duplicated verbatim between them.
