SSRDataRange.has_ticks, set by a single probe over the LAST 24 hours of history, is what selects FULL_TICK fidelity (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1153) and is the only input to the policy's degrade path (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:806, SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:114-118). CSSRMt5TickProvider::HasTicks(symbol, from, to) — the range-aware question — has no caller.

CSSRHistoryCatalog::WarmupFor returns a number used as a BAR COUNT by Quote (compared against SERIES_BARS_COUNT) and as a MINUTE SPAN by EarliestStart/LatestStart/CanStartAt (multiplied by SSR_MSC_PER_MIN). The two readings are equal only for an instrument that quotes every minute of every day.

CSSRMt5BarProvider::NextBarOpen is deliberately unguarded and deliberately CopyTime-only, because a timestamp is the exchange's schedule rather than a price. Its spans are in SECONDS ({3600, 86400, 691200, 3456000}); the base class's generic version at SSR_IDataSource.mqh:155-158 uses the same four spans in MILLISECONDS. Both are correct in their own units — do not 'unify' them.

Seed reproducibility: SSRRandom is xorshift64* with explicit state, SSRPickSeed is documented as the ONE place a wall clock may be read, and a seed of 0 universally means 'pick one and report it'. SSRSeedText prints (long)seed, so seeds above LONG_MAX display negative — SSRSeedFromText round-trips that correctly through two's complement, and SSRFingerprintPack uses the same trick for the digest for the same documented reason.

CSSRRandomPicker's candidate pool is InpAlsoSymbols plus the origin, so the input that supplies the master clock's extra streams doubles as the list of symbols that may REPLACE the origin. On success the host re-Opens the data source on the picked symbol.

The fingerprint is intentionally weak (FNV-1a over integer-scaled OHLC plus time, no volume, no spread) and a mismatch only produces a warning string, never a refused resume. It is computed through bp.ReadBars, so it inherits every failure mode of CSSRBarWindow — including returning no fingerprint at all when the window rejects the range.

CSSRCalendar takes its currencies from SYMBOL_CURRENCY_BASE/SYMBOL_CURRENCY_PROFIT and never parses the symbol name; its items are appended per currency and are therefore NOT sorted by time; item stamps carry InpNewsShift but the query window does not (absorbed by the ±1-day widening); and the news pause fires on CALENDAR_IMPORTANCE_HIGH only, deliberately.

CSSRSessionWatcher tracks the last tick and day even when the mode is OFF, so switching the mode on mid-replay does not fire on accumulated silence; OnRewind re-bases to the rewind instant so the boundary being stood on is not re-announced. Its m_symbol is overwritten by OnSessionStart with the REPLAY symbol while m_threshold_msc was learned from the ORIGIN — m_symbol is otherwise unused.

Thirteen public members of this subsystem have no caller anywhere in the repo, including CSSRDataValidator::ValidateTicks, CSSRMt5TickProvider::HasTicks, CSSRHistoryCatalog::CanStartAt, CSSRBarWindow::ReportInto/Dropped and CSSRMt5DataSource::ToString/SetTickFlags/SetAllowTicks. The full inventory is section 13 of the map.
performance_notes: Blocking waits on the pump path. CSSRBarWindow::LoadRange can Sleep up to SSR_WINDOW_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 15,000 ms inside a window MISS, and a miss happens inside CSSRMt5BarProvider::ReadBars, which the controller calls from OnTimer (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:383). SSRPause is Sleep() for an EA (SSR_Platform.mqh:27-32). A 15 s freeze on a window boundary is the worst case and there is no instrumentation surfacing it (LoadTimeMs has no reader).

CSSRMt5HistoryProvider::Ensure copies the ENTIRE requested range into a throwaway array purely to test availability. At Load time the range is warmup_first_msc..end_msc, so for D1 context (288,000 M1 bars) that is one 288,000 x 60-byte = ~17 MB MqlRates allocation, and on a range returning zero bars the same full-range copy is repeated roughly 400 times over the 20 s timeout (see finding data-5). A bounded probe (CopyRates with a small count, or SeriesInfoInteger) would answer the same question.

CSSRMt5BarProvider::NextBarOpen re-scans from k=0 on each of its four widening spans, and the widest span asks CopyTime for 40 days of M1 (up to ~57,600 datetime elements, ~460 KB) after three cheaper attempts already failed. It is reached only from StepBars/NextTimelineBarOpen and only when the earlier spans found nothing (i.e. inside a weekend or holiday), so it is cold, but the cost is paid entirely in the case it exists for.

CSSRCalendar::Load issues up to THREE CalendarValueHistory calls over the same widened window: one per currency (base, profit) plus an unfiltered probe used only to set m_available. The probe duplicates the widest of the other two. One-off at session start, so the cost is negligible; it is listed because the probe is also the source of finding data-8.

SSRSymbolSessionGap and SSRSymbolSessionBreak each make up to 56 SymbolInfoSessionQuote calls (7 days x 8 indices) and are ~40 lines of identical collection code. CSSRBarWindow::Ensure calls LearnFrom whenever symbol != m_symbol, and Invalidate() does NOT clear m_symbol on failure — but m_symbol is only ASSIGNED on success, so a repeatedly-failing Ensure re-runs the 56 calls on every attempt. Cheap per call, but avoidable and wasted exactly on the failure path.

CSSRBarWindow::Read and CSSRMt5TickProvider::ReadTicks only ever GROW their output array (ArrayResize is guarded by `ArraySize(out) < need`), which is correct and deliberately avoids per-pump reallocation — but it means the return value is the only valid length and ArraySize(out) is stale. Every current caller respects this; a future one that does not will read leftover bars from an earlier, larger pump.

The seed-throughput default is deliberately pessimistic (SSR_SEED_BARS_PER_SEC_DEFAULT = 6,000 vs a real measurement of 35,159 bars/sec on terminal build 6090), and SetMeasuredSeedRate replaces it after the first seed (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2849). So the first quote a user ever sees overstates the wait by roughly 6x on purpose; every quote after that is measured on their own machine.
test_gaps: No test covers what CSSRBarWindow does with a range containing an invalid-OHLC or non-positive bar. SSR_T2_DataEngine.mq5:136-143 asserts only that the REPORT flags it (!rx.IsUsable()); nothing asserts that a 5,000-bar window survives one bad print, and nothing asserts what CSSRMt5BarProvider::ReadBars or the controller then do. This is exactly the gap that lets finding data-2 be silent.

Nothing tests the FULL_TICK path against a window with no tick history. There is no test that ReadTicks returning 0 for every pump is noticed by anyone, and no test that has_ticks (probed over the last day) is a valid answer for the window actually being replayed — finding data-1.

CSSRDataValidator::ValidateTicks has no caller AND no test. Its tick nonpositive rule (`bid <= 0.0 && ticks[i].last <= 0.0`) is untested, which matters given the project's own hard-won rule that SYMBOL_CHART_MODE must be BID for custom symbols fed BID/ASK ticks — a tick with only `last` set would be passed as valid here.

CSSRMt5TickProvider::ReadTicks paging is untested: no test exercises a truncated page, the retries<200 budget, the SSR_TICK_PAGE_GUARD=64 ceiling, or the cursor = last+1 boundary (finding data-12). SSR_T2_DataEngine.mq5 tests SanitizeTicks in isolation only.

CSSRHistoryCatalog's warmup semantics are tested only as arithmetic. SSR_T6_History.mq5:39-47 checks WarmupFor(D1,200)==288000 but nothing checks that the number works as a bar count against bar_count OR as a minute span in EarliestStart, so the conflation in finding data-4 passes every test.

CSSRRandomPicker has no test at all — no test of seed reproducibility across two Pick() calls with the same seed, no test that a pool containing one good and two bad symbols reliably finds the good one (finding data-3), and no test that PickedStart is M1-aligned and inside [EarliestStart, LatestStart].

CSSRCalendar has no functional test. SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:2189 only instantiates it. Untested: the availability probe's two answers (finding data-8), SSRNewsFloor's ALL case (data-9), the InpNewsShift arithmetic, Label()'s 63-char truncation, the OnClock pause window, and OnRewind's un-announcement. Note also that two Raise()-worthy HIGH events inside one warn window produce only one pause reason because Raise() no-ops while m_want is pending — behaviour that is arguably right but is nowhere asserted.

SSRSymbolSessionGap / SSRSymbolSessionBreak are tested only through SessionGap() bookkeeping (SSR_T6_History.mq5:296-301). Neither the day-of-week projection, the week wrap, the n==0/n<2 fallbacks, nor the one-hour floor is tested against a synthetic session table — and the functions' answers cannot be checked at all without a real symbol, since SymbolInfoSessionQuote cannot be faked.

Diagnostic mismatch worth an explicit test: SSR_QA_Preflight.mq5:251 and SSR_B4_BrokerDataAudit.mq5:98 probe tick availability with COPY_TICKS_ALL, while the product decides with COPY_TICKS_INFO (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:137, and m_flags defaults to COPY_TICKS_INFO with SetTickFlags never called). Preflight can therefore report ticks that the engine will not find, or vice versa, and no test compares the two answers.

Nothing asserts that SSRValidateRange is complete. SSR_T6_History.mq5:120-141 checks the empty-request and one valid case; no test constructs a range whose end_msc runs past cat.LastMsc() and asserts it is refused (finding data-10).

Round-trip coverage for the fingerprint exists and is good (SSR_T12_Session.mq5:176-221, including the huge-digest pack/unpack case), but nothing tests FingerprintUpTo's dependence on the bar window — in particular that a window rejection produces no fingerprint at save time and therefore a silent fall-back to the weaker bar-count check on resume.

key_facts: The panel is created on the EA's OWN chart: MQL5/Experts/SSReplay/SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1463 `g_panel_chart = ChartID();` then :1467 `g_panel.Create(g_panel_chart, ...)`. After the one-window handover that chart IS the replay chart, so CHARTEVENT_KEYDOWN and CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE do reach CSSRPanel::OnEvent (forwarded verbatim at :3228). SSR_Panel.mqh:929 ('it never receives a mouse coordinate') and SSR_Widgets.mqh:437-443 assert the opposite premise. The caption drag handler (SSR_Panel.mqh:2938-2969) and the trackbar drag (2915-2936) are therefore LIVE code, not dead code - and the '[]' move button was removed on a premise the wiring contradicts. This is a contract that must be settled before anyone redesigns the panel.

The overview's claim that the command palette is unreachable is contradicted by SSR_Panel.mqh:2828-2833, which binds Ctrl+K (`(int)lparam == SSR_VK_K && TerminalInfoInteger(TERMINAL_KEYSTATE_CONTROL) < 0`). The palette IS reachable from the keyboard.

Render() is throttled to 10 fps by the host (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3063 `now_ms - g_panel_paint >= 100`), on the same thread as the 40 ms engine pump. PollClicks() runs on every timer beat (:3057), unthrottled.

Rail geometry, derived not guessed: SSR_PANEL_W 310, SSR_PANEL_H 336 (23+32+27+21+21+186+18+8), SSR_PANEL_TALL_H 476, SSR_PANEL_COMPACT_H 128; sheet width 245 (310-16-44-5); sheet y+128..y+314; status strip y+317..y+335; transport primary button pw=91; speed track x+120 w=130 (6.5 px/stop); PosCap 5 standard / 12 tall.

There are four hide/remove lists and they disagree: HideSheets (1284, 154 Remove calls, run every frame), HideSheetArea (2042, 8 ids, no tab4), HideBody (2077, 30 ids + tab0..4 + spdseg0..19 + _tk + _th, run every frame), HideCaption (2067, 13 ids).
CSSRWidgets::Hide() and Remove() both call Forget() UNCONDITIONALLY (SSR_Widgets.mqh:624, 632), so every Hide() on an already-visible object invalidates that object's 512-slot property cache entry.

CheckFrame/the layout-overflow instrument can only see SIZED objects - Extent() is called only from Rect, Button/ButtonC and Edit (SSR_Widgets.mqh:129, 199, 292, 363). Labels are invisible to it, and FrameOverflowRight()/FrameOverflowBottom() are read by no test and no caller anywhere in the repo.

m_next_ticket is reset only in CSSRTradingEngine::OnSessionStart (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:578), which CSSRReplayController::Reset (:1268-1297) does not call - so tickets are monotonic across a Reset and the panel's m_last_ticket toast guard stays valid. (Checked and cleared as a non-finding.)
Every command the key table binds (SSR_Keys.mqh:125-222) is either implemented by ExecuteInner (2281) or declined by Owns() (2165) and handed to the host - there is no dead key in v125.

findings.title: DrawSheet deletes and recreates the entire visible sheet on every repaint, defeating both caches
findings.claim: On the Trade tab with lines armed, with nothing at all changed between two frames, Render() deletes every object of the sheet currently on screen and recreates it from scratch. The panel's own label cache (Text(), :194) requires m_w.Exists(id), and the widget property cache (Same(), SSR_Widgets.mqh:80) requires ObjectFind >= 0 - both are false because HideSheets() just deleted the object. So Writes() is never zero on a still frame, and the documented invariant at :2994-2998 ('On a frame where nothing changed this must be ZERO') and the assertions in SSR_T5_Ui.mq5:236 (`spent <= 2`) and SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:5045 (`cached_labels == 0`) cannot hold.
findings.evidence: HideSheets() (:1284) is called unconditionally as the first statement of DrawSheet, and its id list at :1301-1316 contains the ids of EVERY sheet including the one about to be drawn ('risklbl','riskval','riskmon','slrow','tprow','rrrow','sizerow','hintrow','setuprow','openln','flipbtn','enbtn','clrbtn','buy','sell','g1_fr','g1_lb','g1_lg','g2_fr','g2_lb','g2_lg'...). CSSRWidgets::Remove (SSR_Widgets.mqh:627-633) does ObjectDelete then Forget. DrawSheet is called from Render() at :752 (rail) / :757 (fallback) on every frame, i.e. every 100 ms (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3063). Per frame the cost is 70 named Remove() + 4*3 meter Remove() + SSR_POS_MAX(12)*6 row Remove() = 154 ObjectFind+Forget, plus ~20-25 ObjectCreate and their full property writes to rebuild the sheet. The project's own measurement is 561 property writes = 39.05 ms mean repaint (SSR_Widgets.mqh:31-38), which is the whole reason the cache exists.

findings.title: HideBody(false) runs every frame and Forget()s the property cache for ~44 sized objects, which are then rewritten in full
findings.claim: On a still frame the transport row (7 buttons), the speed row (spdn, spdbox, spup), the whole 20-cell slider plus its groove and thumb (22 objects), the status rect, the tabline, the three action buttons and up to 5 tab buttons are all rewritten with 9 ObjectSet* calls each - roughly 400 property writes per frame that the 512-slot cache exists to eliminate. The slider alone is 22 objects x 9 = 198 writes. At the project's own measured ~0.07 ms per property write (561 writes = 39.05 ms) that is the order of a whole repaint budget, reintroduced on every frame.
findings.evidence: HideBody's id list (:2079-2098) covers 'bar_bg','bar_fill','restart','back10','back','toggle','step','step10','reset','spdn','spdbox','spup','tabline','lines','sessions','fidelity','status','fill_bg','fill_ac' plus `for(int t=0;t<SSR_TAB_MAX;t++) m_w.Hide("tab"+IntegerToString(t), hidden);` and `for(int t=0;t<SSR_SPEED_LADDER_SIZE;t++) m_w.Hide("spdseg"+IntegerToString(t), hidden);` plus 'spdseg_tk' and 'spdseg_th'. CSSRWidgets::Hide (SSR_Widgets.mqh:616-625) writes OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES when the object exists and then calls Forget(n) UNCONDITIONALLY - the comment at 622-624 says visibility is not in the fingerprint, so the cache entry has to be dropped. Line 729 is reached on every non-collapsed, non-closed frame, and lines 732-734 and 750-751 then redraw exactly those objects, so Same() returns false for each and ButtonC/Rect execute all 9 writes (SSR_Widgets.mqh:377-386, 211-220).

findings.title: HideBody(false) at line 729 undoes HideSheetArea(true) at line 682 inside the same Render(), so compact mode leaves the tab rail and action strip on the candles
findings.claim: A user who has the panel running on a chart taller than 360 px and then opens the Toolbox (chart shrinks below SSR_PANEL_H+24) gets compact mode - and the rail tab buttons tab0..tab4, the hairline 'tabline' and the three action buttons 'lines'/'sessions'/'fidelity' stay VISIBLE at their full-layout coordinates. The compact body is 128 px tall (status strip at y+109..y+127), while the rail cells sit at y+128, y+153, y+178, y+203, y+228 (22 px each) - up to 122 px of stray, still-clickable tab buttons painted on the candles below the panel, and the action strip at y+103..y+124 overlapping the compact status strip. This is precisely the failure compact mode was built to prevent.
findings.evidence: HideSheetArea (:2042-2050) hides those ids, but it runs at :682, forty-seven lines BEFORE :729 `HideBody(false);` - and HideBody's id list (:2079-2098) contains 'tabline','lines','sessions','fidelity' and the loop `for(int t = 0; t < SSR_TAB_MAX; t++) m_w.Hide("tab" + IntegerToString(t), hidden);`. With hidden==false, CSSRWidgets::Hide writes OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES = OBJ_ALL_PERIODS (SSR_Widgets.mqh:620-621), making every one of them visible again in the same call. The `if(!m_compact)` guard at :735 then skips DrawActions/DrawRail/DrawSheet, so nothing removes or repositions them; only the sheet contents are genuinely gone, because HideSheetArea's HideSheets() (:2049) Removes rather than Hides. HideSheetArea is therefore a no-op for everything it names.

findings.title: HideSheetArea's id list stops at tab3, so the fifth (Prop) tab is never hidden
findings.claim: With InpProp=true the rail draws five tabs (TabCount() returns SSR_TAB_MAX when prop_on, :1104). When the chart shrinks into compact mode, tab4 - the 'Prop'/'PASSED'/'FAILED' button - is not in this list and is left on the chart. Fixing ui-panel-3 (moving HideSheetArea after HideBody, or making HideBody not unhide what compact mode hid) would still leave this one tab stranded on the candles. It is the exact bug HideBody already had and fixed.
findings.evidence: SSR_TAB_MAX is 5 (SSR_Theme.mqh:544) and DrawRail draws tab0..tab(TabCount()-1) (:1212-1221). HideBody solved the identical problem with a loop and documented it at :2088-2090: 'SSR_TAB_MAX, not four written out. This list said tab0..tab3 and Phase 8 added a fifth tab, so closing the panel left a lone "Prop" button sitting on the candles.' HideSheetArea was not updated with it.

findings.title: Two cache slots (12 and 17) write the same object 'setuprow' at the same coordinates, so order_why is visible for one frame only
findings.claim: With lines armed and an illegal geometry (order_why = e.g. 'drag the stop below the price'), the reason is drawn on the frame the string first changes and is overwritten by 'LONG setup'/'SHORT setup' on every subsequent frame - so at 10 fps it is on screen for ~100 ms and then gone for good. The user is told only 'cannot place' on the openln button and never why, which is the opposite of what the comment at :1424-1430 claims the slot split achieved.
findings.evidence: Both Text(12, "setuprow", x + 8, gy + 12, ...) at :1402 and Text(17, "setuprow", x + 8, gy + 12, ...) at :1432 target the SAME object id at the SAME x,y. Text() (:194-207) keys its early return on (slot, text, x, y, Exists(id)) and returns after only setting OBJPROP_COLOR. Because HideSheets() deletes 'setuprow' at the top of every DrawSheet (:1270, id listed at :1306), Text(12) always finds Exists==false and writes the side text; Text(17) then finds the object present with m_cache[17] == order_why and x,y unchanged, takes the early return, and leaves the side text in place. Only on the frame where order_why's value differs from m_cache[17] does the second call actually write.

findings.title: Status strip draws the fidelity readout at x+330 in a 310 px panel - permanently outside the frame, on the candles
findings.code:
Text(53, "stfid", x + 330, y + 4,
           SSRFidelityName(m_state.fidelity_effective) + (degraded ? " !" : ""),
           degraded ? SSR_C_HOLD : SSRFidelityColor(m_state.fidelity_effective),
           SSR_FS_SMALL);
findings.claim: In the shipping rail layout the panel frame is x..x+310 (SSR_PANEL_W, SSR_Theme.mqh:487). The label's ANCHOR is at x+330 - 20 px past the right edge before a single glyph is drawn - and the text is 'SYNTHETIC TICK' (14 chars) or with degradation 'SYNTHETIC TICK !', which at SSR_FS_SMALL runs roughly another 70-80 px further, so ~90 px of text sits on the price on every frame of every session. The layout overflow instrument cannot report it.
findings.evidence: The x offsets in DrawStatus (:2015-2036: x+8, x+116, x+218, x+268, x+330) carry no #ifdef SSR_LAYOUT_RAIL, unlike DrawClock (:956-965), DrawTransport (:990-1008), DrawSpeed (:1047-1056) and TabName (:1112-1140), all of which were given rail variants. x+330 fits the 420 px fallback (SSR_Theme.mqh:491) and not the 310 px rail. SSRFidelityName returns 'SYNTHETIC TICK' (SSR_Types.mqh:179). CheckFrame (:3019-3034) compares m_w.MaxRight() against x+W, and MaxRight only sees objects that call Extent() - Rect, Button/ButtonC and Edit (SSR_Widgets.mqh:199, 292, 363); Label does not (SSR_Widgets.mqh:226-253, and the comment at 125-128 says so), so this label is invisible to the instrument and to the LAYOUT OVERFLOW log line.

findings.title: Position-row note column collides with the P/L column in the rail layout: 9 px of room for a 9-character note
findings.claim: Open a position with no stop. The row draws '  no stop' anchored at x+120 while the money column is anchored at x + w - 116 = x + 129, because the rail sheet is 245 px wide (310 - 2*8 - 44 - 5). Nine characters get nine pixels, so the note is printed straight over the P/L figure - the two things on that row a trader reads. The same applies to the spread note '  sp 20.0'. The comment at :1563-1574 claims 'The row now has four columns that do not touch' and shows its own arithmetic for a 295 px sheet ('the P/L column starts at x+w-140, which on a 295 px sheet is x+155'); the rail sheet is 50 px narrower than that.
findings.evidence: DrawSheet is called with w = W - 2*SSR_PAD - SSR_RAIL_W - SSR_GAP (:752-753) = 310-16-44-5 = 245. 'pl'+t is anchored at x + w - 116 (:1582, :1585) = x+129; 'pn'+t at x + 120 (:1576). Gap = 9 px. note is T(SSR_S_NO_STOP) = '  no stop' (SSR_Strings.mqh:391) or '  ' + T(SSR_S_SPREAD_SHORT) = '  sp %.1f' (SSR_Strings.mqh:495) - 9 characters either way, which cannot occupy 9 px at SSR_FS_SMALL (7 pt) under any font metric. Persian 'no.stop' is longer still (fa.txt:61).

findings.title: Speed 'meaning' text at MAX is 21 unclipped characters drawn into a 56 px reserve at the panel's right edge
findings.code:
Text(6, "spdmean", x + W - SSR_PAD - mw + 4, y + 5,
           SSRSpeedMeaning(m_state.speed_x100), SSR_C_TEXT_DIM, SSR_FS_SMALL);
findings.claim: Press '+' until the speed reaches SSR_SPEED_MAX (a real rung of the 20-stop ladder, also reachable by clicking the last groove cell). SSRSpeedMeaning then returns the 21-character 'as fast as ticks feed', drawn unclipped from x+254 with only 56 px to the panel edge - it runs somewhere between 30 and 50 px onto the candles beside the panel, and it does so for as long as MAX is selected. Every other rung ('1h in 12m', 9 chars) fits, so the overflow appears only at the top of the ladder.

SSRSpeedMeaning (SSR_Types.mqh:350-363) returns "as fast as ticks feed" when speed_x100 >= SSR_SPEED_MAX - 21 characters, which cannot fit 56 px at SSR_FS_SMALL. No Clip() is applied here, unlike 'prog' (:960), 'pp_rules' (:1760), 'pp_head' (:1840) and 'ses3' (:1892). Being a label, it is also invisible to CheckFrame (SSR_Widgets.mqh:125-128). The fallback layout reserves 92 px (:1055), which is still short of 21 characters.

findings.title: Fill toast takes its colour from pos_no_stop[0] instead of the row that produced it
findings.claim: With one stop-protected position already open (row 0) and a second fill arriving on row 2 with no stop, the toast text ends '   NO STOP' while its accent and left bar are drawn in SSR_C_RUN (the green 'fine' colour), because index 0 is read instead of index 2. The inverse is worse: row 0 has no stop and row 2 fills correctly protected - the toast for the protected fill is drawn in SSR_C_HOLD, the warning colour. The toast can also outlive the rows: m_toast_until is GetTickCount()+4000 (:800) while pos_rows can fall to 0 in that window, at which point pos_no_stop[0] is whatever SSRUiState::Init left (false, SSR_ReplayPort.mqh:282).
findings.evidence: The producing loop at :787-801 iterates pi over m_state.pos_rows and correctly uses the per-row fields (pos_text[pi], pos_spread[pi], pos_no_stop[pi] at :793-799) to build m_toast_text, but does not record pi. The consumer at :806 hard-codes index 0. pos_no_stop is a per-row array of SSR_POS_MAX entries (SSR_ReplayPort.mqh:209) and the Positions sheet reads it per row correctly (:1555, :1577).

findings.title: In compact mode the fill toast is drawn on top of the speed trackbar and blocks it for four seconds
findings.code:
m_w.Toast("fill", x + SSR_PAD, y + H - SSR_STATUS_H - 24,
                   W - 2 * SSR_PAD, m_toast_text,
findings.claim: On a chart between roughly 128 and 360 px tall the panel is compact (BodyH() = SSR_PANEL_COMPACT_H = 128) and the toast is placed at y + 128 - 18 - 24 = y+86, height 20, i.e. y+86..y+106. The speed row occupies y+82..y+101 with the groove at y+87..y+96 and the thumb at y+84..y+99. Every fill therefore covers the speed control for four seconds, and because the toast background is an OBJ_RECTANGLE_LABEL created after the slider cells (creation order is the only z-order) it is drawn on top and swallows clicks on the groove. Compact mode is the mode in which the speed control is one of only four things left on the panel.
findings.evidence: The toast y is computed from H (:804), and H = BodyH() (:716) returns SSR_PANEL_COMPACT_H when m_compact (:427). SSR_PANEL_COMPACT_H is 128 and SSR_STATUS_H is 18 (SSR_Theme.mqh:504, 518), giving y+86. DrawSpeed is called at cy = y+82 (DrawClock returns +32 from y+23, DrawTransport returns +27) and sets m_track_y = y + 5 = y+87 with SSR_TRACK_H 16 (:1083, SSR_Theme.mqh:524); the thumb is drawn at y-3 with h+6 (SSR_Widgets.mqh:492). The toast block at :803-806 is outside the `if(!m_compact)` guard at :735, so it is unconditional. In the full layout the same expression gives y+294, which is clear of everything.

findings.title: The Setup tag box is hidden, re-shown and fully rewritten on every repaint while the user is typing in it
findings.code:
ReadTag();
      m_w.Hide("tagbox", true);
findings.claim: While the Trade tab is open, every Render() (10 per second) sets the OBJ_EDIT's OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES to OBJ_NO_PERIODS, then back to OBJ_ALL_PERIODS, and rewrites all nine of its other properties - all while the box may hold the keyboard. The file's own comment at :1286-1297 records that destroying and rebuilding this object 'does not merely lose the text - it makes the box impossible to type in at all'; hiding and re-showing it ten times a second is the same class of interference, and it is the one control whose contents belong to the user. Whether MetaTrader drops focus or keystrokes when OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES is toggled on a focused OBJ_EDIT cannot be determined from source, so this is a risk rather than a confirmed failure.
findings.evidence: HideSheets() (:1298-1299) calls ReadTag() then m_w.Hide("tagbox", true) and runs as the first statement of DrawSheet (:1270), i.e. every frame. SheetTrade then calls m_w.Edit("tagbox", ...) (:1375) followed by m_w.Hide("tagbox", false) (:1376). CSSRWidgets::Hide writes OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES on both calls (SSR_Widgets.mqh:619-621) and CSSRWidgets::Edit has NO cache at all - it writes XDISTANCE, YDISTANCE, XSIZE, YSIZE, BGCOLOR, COLOR, BORDER_COLOR, FONTSIZE and READONLY unconditionally on every call (SSR_Widgets.mqh:305-319, m_writes += 9).

findings.title: The key card is torn down and rebuilt from scratch by the panel ten times a second while it is up
findings.code:
if(m_keys.IsUp())
         m_keys.Show(m_chart);
findings.claim: Press H to open the shortcut card and the panel calls CSSRKeyCard::Show() on every repaint, i.e. every 100 ms. Show() begins with m_w.RemoveAll() - ObjectsDeleteAll over the SSRK_ prefix - and then recreates one rectangle plus about 40 labels, rebuilding the key-binding array each time. That is ~41 ObjectDelete + 41 ObjectCreate + roughly 450 property writes per frame, on the same thread as the 40 ms engine pump, against the project's own measurement of 561 property writes = 39.05 ms. It will show up as the replay stuttering while the help card is on screen.
findings.evidence: CSSRKeyCard::Show (SSR_KeyCard.mqh:55-104) calls SSRKeyBindings(b) (:61), m_w.Attach (:71) and m_w.RemoveAll() (:72) before drawing 'bg', 't', 't2', two labels per listed binding (:92-93) and 'foot' (:97). m_w.RemoveAll is ObjectsDeleteAll + ForgetAll (SSR_Widgets.mqh:637-643), so nothing can be cached between frames by construction. SSRKeyBindings itself rebuilds a 22-entry array with ArrayResize per call (SSR_Keys.mqh:112-122, 125-222). The panel invokes it unconditionally whenever m_keys.IsUp(), and the comment at :767-775 explains why the redraw is needed for z-order - the redraw is right, the destructive implementation is the cost.

findings.title: Caption chip row overruns the collapse button by 6 px when fidelity is degraded and both BLIND and PROP chips are shown
findings.claim: With InpBlind on, InpProp on, and the requested fidelity degraded (FULL_TICK asked for, SYNTHETIC_TICK actually running), the chip row lays out as: chfid 'SYNTH !' plate x+140..x+192, chblind 'BLIND' x+196..x+236, chprop 'PROP' x+240..x+274. The collapse button starts at x + W - 42 = x+268, so the last 6 px of the PROP plate and the tail of its text are drawn under the collapse button - the chip looks clipped, which on a mode indicator reads as a rendering fault. Without the degradation marker the row ends at x+262 and clears the button by 6 px, so the layout has no margin.
findings.evidence: CSSRWidgets::Chip returns w = 10 + StringLen(text) * 6 (SSR_Widgets.mqh:529) and each caller adds 4 (:894, :898, :904). SSRFidelityShort returns 'SYNTH' (SSR_Types.mqh:198) and the degraded suffix is ' !' (:891), giving 7 characters -> 52 px. T(SSR_S_BLIND) is 'BLIND' -> 40 px and T(SSR_S_PROP) is 'PROP' -> 34 px (SSR_Strings.mqh:458-459). 140+52+4 = 196; 196+40+4 = 240; 240+34 = 274 > 268. The collapse button is at x + W - 42 with W = SSR_PANEL_W = 310 (:936, SSR_Theme.mqh:487). The chips' plates are Rects so CheckFrame sees them, but they end inside the 310 px frame and the instrument only reports overflow past the frame, not collisions inside it.

findings.title: The reset confirmation - the one destructive question on the panel - is a hardcoded English literal
findings.claim: A Persian-language user who presses Reset or 0 with trades on the books gets the highest-priority line of the status strip - the line that decides whether they destroy their session - in English, inside an otherwise fully translated panel. It is the only user-facing panel string not routed through T(), and fa.txt has 190/190 entries for everything else.
findings.evidence: m_reset_warning is drawn on the status strip at :1929 `Text(50, "stbal", x + SSR_PAD, y + 4, m_reset_warning, SSR_C_STOP, SSR_FS_SMALL);` - the top rung of the ladder documented at :1956-1972. Every other drawn string on this panel goes through T(SSR_S_*) (e.g. :1037 T(SSR_S_RESET_ASK), which IS translated at fa.txt:23 'reset.ask'). Audit A19's stated rule is that no text may be drawn from a literal; it passes here because the literal is assigned to a member at :2253 and drawn from that member at :1929, not written at the draw site.

performance_notes: Cost basis, from the project's own measurement (SSR_Widgets.mqh:31-38): 561 object property writes = 39.05 ms mean repaint, i.e. ~0.07 ms per write, against a 40 ms engine pump and a 100 ms repaint interval. Every figure below should be read against that.

Hot path 1 - HideSheets() from DrawSheet, every frame (SSR_Panel.mqh:1270): 70 named Remove() + 12 meter Remove() + 72 position-row Remove() = 154 ObjectFind+Forget calls, of which ~20-25 actually delete an object that is recreated 3 lines later at full ObjectCreate + ~12-write cost. See ui-panel-1.

Hot path 2 - HideBody(false) from Render, every frame (:729): ~57 Hide() calls = 57 ObjectFind + up to 57 ObjectSetInteger(OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES) + 57 Forget(), which then forces ~44 sized objects to be rewritten at 9 properties each (~400 writes). The 20-cell slider plus groove and thumb alone is 22 objects x 9 = 198 writes per frame. See ui-panel-2.

Hot path 3 - CSSRKeyCard::Show() from Render while the card is up (:776): ObjectsDeleteAll + ~41 ObjectCreate + ~450 property writes + a full SSRKeyBindings() array rebuild, ten times a second. See ui-panel-12.
CSSRWidgets::Edit has no property cache at all (SSR_Widgets.mqh:288-326, m_writes += 9 unconditionally). On the Trade tab the tagbox therefore costs 9 writes + 2 Hide() calls per frame, forever.

DrawCaption issues three unconditional m_w.Remove() calls per frame for objects that were deleted in v125 and can never come back: m_w.Remove("palette"); m_w.Remove("keys"); m_w.Remove("move"); (:932-934). Three ObjectFind + three Forget per frame, permanently. A one-shot sweep in Create() would do the same job.

DrawStatus calls m_w.Hide("stflt"/"stopen"/"stspread"/"stfid", false) on every resting frame (:1937-1940), writing OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES to objects that are already visible and Forget()ing four more cache entries. These are labels so Text()'s own slot cache still absorbs them, but the four OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES writes are pure waste.

PollClicks is O(buttons on the chart) per timer beat (40 ms, not 100 ms - it is called at SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3057 outside the repaint throttle): ObjectsTotal(m_chart,-1,OBJ_BUTTON) then one ObjectName + StringFind + ObjectGetInteger per button. A full rail panel carries roughly 60-70 OBJ_BUTTONs (20 of them slider cells), plus the palette's 8 rows when it is up.

SSRKeyToCommand rebuilds the entire 22-entry binding table on every call (SSR_Keys.mqh:224-232 -> 125-222, with ArrayResize per Add), and every CHARTEVENT_KEYDOWN calls it twice: once in the host's flight-recorder line (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3204) and once in the panel (:2856). Not a frame cost, but it is a table that could be static.

RenderDragging() thins drag repaints to one per 30 ms (:615-622), but each one is a full Render() with all of the above in it - roughly 33 full repaints a second while the caption is being dragged, on the pump thread.
test_gaps: The layout-overflow instrument is write-only: FrameOverflowRight() and FrameOverflowBottom() (:3036-3037) and CheckFrame (:3019) are read by nothing outside SSR_Panel.mqh - grep across all 123 files returns no other caller. An off-frame object produces a Print and nothing else, on a terminal the author cannot run.

CheckFrame structurally cannot see labels: Extent() is called only from Rect, ButtonC and Edit (SSR_Widgets.mqh:199, 292, 363), never from Label (226-253), and the comment at 125-128 says so. Every x-offset defect in this audit (ui-panel-6, -7, -8) is a label and therefore outside the instrument's reach. The missing instrument is a label-extent estimate (StringLen x a per-font-size advance, asserted against the frame), which would need no terminal to run.

Compact mode is never exercised, only skipped: SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:4151, 4388 and 4644 all take the form `if(pp.IsCompact())` and bail out. No test drives full -> compact -> full and asserts which SSRP_ objects remain visible, which is why ui-panel-3, -4 and -10 are unseen.

There is no 'nothing is visible outside the frame' assertion for any of the four mode transitions (closed, collapsed, compact, tall). A single test that renders each state and walks ObjectsTotal for SSRP_ objects whose XDISTANCE/YDISTANCE fall outside x..x+W / y..y+BodyH() would catch ui-panel-3, -4, -6 and -10 at once.

Both cache assertions that this audit contradicts have never been executed on a terminal: SSR_T5_Ui.mq5:236 (`spent <= 2` over 20 identical renders) and SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:5045 (`cached_labels == 0`). They are the right assertions; they are just unrun, and ui-panel-1 predicts both fail.

The status ladder has no test. Nothing drives ResetArmed + TradeError + m_pro_why + TooNarrow together to prove the documented priority at :1956-1972 holds, and nothing asserts that the four displaced labels come back when the message clears.

order_why never reaching the chart (ui-panel-5) is invisible to the current mocks: the T5 fake port would have to hold order_why non-empty across two consecutive Render() calls and the test would have to read back OBJPROP_TEXT of prefix+'setuprow'. No test reads any object's text back.

No translated-layout test exists. Every x offset in DrawStatus (:2015-2036), SheetPositions (:1561-1665) and DrawCaption (:887-939) is tuned to English glyph widths; fa.txt is loaded and has 190/190 entries, but no stage renders a Persian frame and measures it. Persian 'spread.short' (fa.txt:211) and 'row.hint' (fa.txt:63) are both materially longer than the English strings the offsets were fitted to.

Two drawn strings bypass the string catalogue entirely and so are invisible to audit A19: SSRSpeedMeaning's 'as fast as ticks feed' / '1h in %dm' (SSR_Types.mqh:350-363) and SSRFidelityName's 'SYNTHETIC TICK' (SSR_Types.mqh:174-183), plus m_reset_warning (:2253). An A19 extension that follows a member variable from assignment to draw site, or that flags literals returned by any function whose result reaches Text()/Label(), would close it.

Slots 30, 31 and 32 are each shared by two different object ids (posmore/st1, poshint/st2, trlbl/st3). It is safe today only because HideSheets deletes the objects every frame and because the two texts always differ - fixing ui-panel-1 removes the first of those two protections. A test that switches Positions -> Stats -> Positions and reads back the three labels' text would pin the invariant before anyone relies on it.

Nothing covers the reopen path from m_closed: Render's closed branch (:649-656) draws the 'reopen' button at m_x, m_y without calling ClampToChart (which happens at :717, after the early return), so a chart resized while the panel is closed can put the only way back off the edge. Untested, and not reported as a finding because m_closed is not persisted, so a restart recovers it.

key_facts: SSR_Strings.mqh holds exactly 190 enum ids and 190 SSRAddString rows - verified programmatically: no duplicate ids, no enum id without a row, no row naming a non-existent id. No English string exceeds 63 characters (longest is 62).

MQL5/Files/SSReplay/lang/fa.txt: 190/190 keys present, zero unknown keys, zero missing keys, zero printf-specifier mismatches against the English rows. 24 values exceed 63 BYTES while all are inside 63 CHARACTERS, which is the correct side of MetaTrader's limit.

All 22 vk codes in SSRKeyBindings() are distinct - there is no duplicate or conflicting VK in the table. 18 of the 22 are `listed` (the key card's row count). Five enum commands have no key at all: PLAY, PAUSE, RESTART, REPLAY_FROM_HERE, COLLAPSE.
All three palettes in SSR_Theme.mqh define exactly the same 51 SSR_C_* tokens - the symmetric difference of the three token sets is empty, so no palette switch position can leave a token undefined.

The property cache is a 512-slot open-addressed table keyed on the full object name, FNV-1a for slot choice, linear probe capped at 8, -1 (never cache) on a full run. Text is stored whole in m_ct[] and compared with ==; only the NUMBERS are folded, by Mix(a,b) = a*1000003 + b.

Same() ends with ObjectFind(m_chart, name) >= 0, so a cache hit requires both `unchanged` and `still there`. Hide(), Remove() and RemoveAll() are the only invalidators, and Forget()/ForgetAll() are private - there is no public way to tell the cache that a property was written behind its back.

Extent() (the layout-overflow instrument) is called from Rect, ButtonC and Edit only, and always BEFORE the Same() early return, so measurement is complete on a fully cached frame. Labels are excluded by design (MQL5 has no text measurement), so CheckFrame cannot see a long label.
ButtonC deliberately never writes OBJPROP_STATE: the latch is how the panel learns about a click on a chart whose events it cannot receive, and clearing it during a repaint would erase presses.

The command palette IS reachable in v125 - SSR_Panel.mqh:2827-2832 opens it on Ctrl+K, checked before the key table - contradicting the stated ground truth that it is unreachable. Its `move` action still works via Dispatch (SSR_Panel.mqh:2605), so the palette is now the only way to move the panel.

Widget prefixes in use: SSRP_ panel, SSRS_ setup, SSRD_ range dialog, SSRSD_ session dialog, SSRK_ key card, SSRX_ palette, SSRF_ first run, SSRV_ reveal card, SSRR2_ review card. None is a string prefix of another, so per-prefix RemoveAll() cannot cross-delete. SSRPurgeChart() sweeps everything matching "SSR" except one kept name.

SSR_PANEL_H expands to 23+32+27+21+21+186+18+8 = 336 and SSR_PANEL_W to 310 under the active SSR_LAYOUT_RAIL, matching the overview. SSR_TAB_PROP == SSR_TAB_COUNT == 4 is intentional and all call sites use SSR_TAB_MAX (5) for sweeping.
SSR_Strings.mqh and SSR_ReviewCard.mqh are the only two non-ASCII source files in the whole project; neither has a BOM.

findings.title: SSR_Layout.mqh is dead in production: nothing outside the QA smoke test positions anything through it, so the RTL plan it exists to enable has no backing

SSRCentre and SSRInner have zero call sites anywhere including the test. Mirroring the panel therefore still means rewriting the inline pixel arithmetic in SSR_Panel.mqh, SSR_SetupPanel.mqh, SSR_RangeDialog.mqh, SSR_SessionDialog.mqh, SSR_ReviewCard.mqh, SSR_RevealCard.mqh, SSR_FirstRun.mqh and SSR_KeyCard.mqh by hand.
findings.evidence: The file's header states the constraint it was built to impose: "The localization plan therefore places one constraint on every phase after this one - position through here, never by hand - and this file is that promise made concrete." The constraint was never adopted; every UI file computes x positions inline (e.g. SSR_KeyCard.mqh:74-93 `int x = 14; ... x + 12 ... x + 86`, SSR_Panel.mqh:889 `int cx = x + 140`). The smoke test's own note (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:4984) records the file as "written and deliberately OFF", which is true of the mirroring flag but understates it: the helpers are not merely off, they are uncalled.

findings.title: The property cache has no tombstones: Forget() can silently clear nothing and Keep() then writes a duplicate, leaking slots until the cache stops working
findings.claim: Take two names A and B whose FNV-1a lands on the same home slot h, with A stored at h and B pushed to h+1. Remove("A") frees h. Now Hide("B", true) -> Forget("B") -> Slot("B") returns h (the FIRST free-or-matching slot, Widgets:70-76), m_ck[h] is "" which is not "B", so Forget returns having cleared nothing; B's entry at h+1 survives. The next draw of B calls Keep("B") which also resolves to h and writes B there, so B now occupies two slots and h+1 holds a stale tuple for ever. Every Hide/Remove-then-redraw of a name that sits off its home slot can leak one more slot this way, and the panel does that at 10 Hz: SSR_Panel.mqh:1937-1940 calls m_w.Hide("stflt"/"stopen"/"stspread"/"stfid", false) unconditionally on every render, and SSR_Panel.mqh:2091-2098 hides/unhides 5 tabs, 20 speed cells and 2 slider parts on every collapse. As leaked slots accumulate in the 512-slot table (the panel already uses roughly 200-260 distinct names under SSRP_), some 8-slot probe run fills, Slot() returns -1 for every name hashing into it (Widgets:76), Same() returns false and Keep() no-ops - the cache is switched off for those objects and they take their full 6 or 9 ObjectSet* writes every frame, which is the 561-writes / 39.05 ms repaint the cache was built to remove.
findings.evidence: Slot() stops at the first slot that is either free or matching, so after any deletion earlier in a probe chain the lookup for a later name resolves to the wrong (free) slot. Forget() guards on m_ck[k] == name and therefore becomes a no-op instead of finding the real entry; Keep() then stores a second copy at the earlier slot. Nothing ever reclaims the old copy: ForgetAll() runs only from Attach() (when chart or prefix changes) and RemoveAll(). The failure is not a wrong pixel - the shadowed duplicate is only reachable once a third name occupies the earlier slot, and by then the object's real state matches the tuple that is found - but the slot is permanently consumed.

findings.title: Mix() is a 64-bit polynomial hash that overflows, so the cache's central claim - "NO HASH, AND THEREFORE NO COLLISION" - is false for the numeric half of the fingerprint
findings.code: long              Mix(const long a, const long b) { return a * 1000003 + b; }
findings.claim: Rect()'s fingerprint expands to fp = x*M^5 + y*M^4 + w*M^3 + h*M^2 + bg*M + edge (mod 2^64), M = 1000003. Two different states of the same object collide whenever the weighted difference is a multiple of 2^64, and for the lowest two terms that needs no overflow at all: any pair (bg, edge) and (bg+d, edge-d*1000003) with |d*1000003| <= 0xFFFFFF - i.e. d from -16 to +16 - produces an identical fingerprint. ButtonC chains seven Mix calls (x,y,w,h,bg,edge,fg,size), whose leading coefficient M^7 is about 1e42 and therefore wraps; bg's coefficient M^3 is 1e18, the same order as 2^64, so the numeric fingerprint is a lossy hash of a tuple whose colour components span 24 bits each. When two states of one widget collide, Same() returns true, the nine writes are skipped, and the button keeps the previous geometry or colour - silently, on a trading panel.
findings.evidence: Widgets:40-44 states the safety argument: "NO HASH, AND THEREFORE NO COLLISION. The numbers are mixed into one long, but the TEXT is kept and compared as a string. A hash collision here would silently leave the wrong word on a button on a trading panel, and 'vanishingly unlikely' is not a property worth having in that sentence." The text half is genuinely collision-free (m_ct[] stores it whole, compared with == at Widgets:85). The numeric half is not: `a * 1000003 + b` over signed 64-bit MQL5 arithmetic is exactly a mod-2^64 polynomial hash, and Same() trusts it without reading a single property back off the object. I could not exhibit a colliding pair from this project's 51-colour palette, so the defect is the falsified invariant and the absent verification, not a demonstrated wrong pixel.

findings.title: Label()'s fingerprint identifies the font by the LENGTH of its name, so a font change to an equal-length face is skipped
findings.claim: Call Label("clock", x, y, "12:30", col, 13, "Tahoma") and then, with everything else unchanged, Label("clock", x, y, "12:30", col, 13, "Verdana"). StringLen is 7 for both, so fp is identical, Same() returns true, and ObjectSetString(OBJPROP_FONT) is never written - the label keeps Tahoma while Verdana was asked for. The other five properties of a Label are stored faithfully; only the font is reduced to a scalar that throws away its identity.
findings.evidence: font is the one string argument Label folds into the numeric fingerprint instead of storing whole, unlike text which is kept in m_ct[] precisely so it cannot be confused. Today it cannot bite, because SSR_FONT and SSR_FONT_MONO are both "Tahoma" (SSR_Theme.mqh:424-425) and every call site passes one of them. SSR_FONT_MONO exists only so they can be split later - SSR_Theme.mqh:29-31: "SSR_FONT_MONO is kept as a separate name pointing at the same face, so if a terminal ever proves otherwise it is one line to split them again" - and that one line is the trigger for this.

//| + tabs 21 + sheet 222 + status 18 + margin 14 = 390               |
findings.claim: A designer adding a row reads this block and budgets against a 390 px panel with a 222 px sheet, a 33 px speed row and 14 px of margin. The sum above was a comment for eleven builds and the two rows v69 added went straight past the end of it") but the prose sum above SSR_SHEET_H was left as the older set of numbers, so the file now carries two disagreeing totals - the failure mode it was rewritten to prevent, one comment higher up.

findings.title: List() clamps its window only at the upper end, so a negative `first` indexes rows[] out of range and aborts the program
findings.claim: Call List("r", x, y, w, rh, rows, -1, 8, 0) with a non-empty rows[]. k = n+1, clamped to shown = 8, so the loop runs with i = 0 and idx = -1, and rows[-1] raises MQL5's "array out of range" - which terminates the program and takes the whole panel off the chart, mid-session. The only guard is `if(k < 0) k = 0`, which protects first > n and does nothing for first < 0.
findings.evidence: No caller can reach it today: CSSRPalette clamps m_first at Refilter (SSR_Palette.mqh:136) and Move (line 148 with the `m_first = m_sel - SHOWN + 1` branch bounded by `if(m_first < 0) m_first = 0` in Refilter), and CSSRReviewCard clamps at SSR_ReviewCard.mqh:99 (`if(m_first < 0) m_first = 0`). The primitive is a public widget API with a `first` parameter and no precondition documented, and the class's stated posture is that the caller pages the window - so the next list that pages by a delta will hit it. An index range check here is one line and turns a program abort into a blank list.

findings.title: The palette's only live entry point, Ctrl+K, is not in the single key table, so the generated key card cannot show it and the code comments say it does not exist

findings.claim: SSR_Panel.mqh:2827-2832 opens the command palette on Ctrl+K, checked before the key table so nothing can shadow it, and the whole registry is wired (RunChosen at SSR_Panel.mqh:2423 dispatches both cmd and action entries; `move` still runs SnapToCorner at 2605, making the palette the only surviving way to move the panel). findings.title: The property cache has no public invalidation seam, and a caller already writes a cached property behind its back
findings.code:
//--- true when this object already holds exactly this, and exists
   bool              Same(const string name, const long nums, const string text)
findings.claim: Same()/Keep()/Forget() are private and the only public invalidators are Hide(), Remove() and RemoveAll(), all of which either delete or re-hide the object. SSR_Panel.mqh:190-199 (Text()) already writes a cached property directly on a cache hit - `ObjectSetInteger(m_chart, m_w.N(id), OBJPROP_COLOR, col); return;` - without going through Label(), so the widget cache's fingerprint for that object keeps the colour of the last full Label() write while the object holds a different one. The moment a second panel-level cache miss asks for the recorded colour with the recorded text and position, Same() returns true and the colour is not re-written, leaving a semantic colour (green=running / amber=paused / red=error) stale.
findings.evidence: Today the two caches are always cleared together - CSSRPanel::ClearCache() is called only from the constructor (SSR_Panel.mqh:292) and from Create() (line 312), and Create() calls m_w.RemoveAll() one line earlier (310), which runs ForgetAll() - so the divergence window cannot open. It is a structural hazard rather than a live defect: the widget class documents deletion as "THE DANGEROUS CASE" and guards it with ObjectFind, but offers no way for a caller that legitimately writes one property to say so. A public Invalidate(id) - the existing private Forget - would close it in one line and make the panel's fast path safe by construction.

performance_notes: Slot() is called TWICE per cached-miss draw (once from Same, once from Keep) and once per cached hit. Each call is an FNV-1a pass over the full object name (prefix + id, ~10-14 chars) plus up to 8 MQL5 string comparisons. On the panel's ~77 cached objects per still frame that is 77 FNV passes plus up to 616 string compares per frame at 10 Hz - cheap next to 561 ObjectSet* calls, but it is the residual cost the 39.05 ms measurement was replaced by, and it is not instrumented (m_writes counts only property writes).

Edit() is the one primitive with NO cache: it writes 9 properties (10 when set_text) on every call, unconditionally (SSR_Widgets.mqh:305-319). CSSRPalette::Render() is called from the panel's paint on every frame while the palette is up (SSR_Panel.mqh:816-817), so the query box takes 9 property writes 10 times a second, including OBJPROP_XDISTANCE/YDISTANCE/XSIZE/YSIZE/READONLY, while MetaTrader holds the keyboard focus in it. The text is deliberately excluded; whether re-writing the other nine disturbs the caret or selection in a focused OBJ_EDIT is unverified.

SSRKeyToCommand() rebuilds the entire 22-row binding table - 22 struct writes each carrying two string assignments, plus an ArrayResize - on EVERY keystroke (SSR_Keys.mqh:224-232). SSRCommandKey() does the same per palette row, so one palette Render() with 31 matches rebuilds the key table up to 31 times (SSR_Palette.mqh:176). Both are outside the 10 Hz paint path except the palette's, which is inside it.

Each CSSRWidgets instance carries string m_ck[512], long m_cn[512] and string m_ct[512] - roughly 20 KB of MQL5 string descriptors per instance. Nine UI surfaces own one by value (panel, setup panel, range dialog, session dialog, key card, palette, first-run card, reveal card, review card), and CSSRPalette is itself a by-value member of CSSRPanel. Surfaces that draw once and never animate (key card, reveal card, first-run card) pay the full 512 slots for no elision benefit.

Meter() deletes and recreates its _fill object every time the value crosses zero (SSR_Widgets.mqh:550-557), which for the prop sheet's daily-loss meter is once per replay day. Because creation order is the only z-order, the recreated _fill lands AFTER _lim, so from then on the fill paints over the left-hand pixel of the 2 px limit mark. All four prop meters start at value 0 on a fresh evaluation (SSR_Panel.mqh:1778-1818 pass prop_progress / prop_daily_used / prop_total_used / prop_days_progress against limit 1.0), so they all take that path. Cosmetically one pixel; mechanically it is an ObjectDelete + ObjectCreate pair per crossing.

Progress() and Meter() clamp their fraction with `if(f < 0.0) f = 0.0; if(f > 1.0) f = 1.0;` (SSR_Widgets.mqh:405-406, 547-548). NaN fails both comparisons and reaches MathRound/(int) unchecked; inf is handled correctly by the upper clamp. A 0.0/0.0 progress would therefore produce an undefined fill width, and because Extent() has already run the overflow detector would report whatever came out.
test_gaps: Nothing cross-checks any hand-written key list against SSRKeyBindings(). A static audit could parse the letters out of SSR_S_KEYS_1..4, SSR_S_ROW_HINT, SSR_S_FIRSTRUN_*, SSR_S_FOLLOW/LINES_ON/LINES_OFF/BOOKMARK/JUMP/SESSIONS/FIDELITY/FLIP and SSRKeyHint() and assert each names the command the table binds it to. Findings 2, 3, 4 and 14 would all have been caught by one such audit; instead the only test on SSRKeyHint (SSR_T15_Ux.mq5:404) asserts a substring that is still true.

There is no audit that every user-facing string reaches the screen through T(). A19 finds literals only where they appear directly in a drawing call's text argument, so SSR_KeyCard.mqh's `b[i].label` / `b[i].what` - 36 English cells - are invisible to it, and A19's own vacuous-pass guard (`seen[1] < 100`) does not help because the count of T() calls elsewhere is well over 100.

The 63-character check runs on literals and on translation-file values, never on a FORMATTED result. 39 English strings carry printf specifiers, and three of them substitute %s values of unbounded length (SSR_S_SU_SUMMARY '%s  ·  %s  ·  %s  ·  %.2f%% risk', SSR_S_STOP_ROW and SSR_S_TARGET_ROW 'Stop      %s      %s'). Clip() exists but is applied by hand at some draw sites and not others.
No audit asserts that a declared theme token is referenced by a draw site. SSR_C_THUMB_EDGE and SSR_C_TICK are dead in all three palettes and A17/A18 both pass.

No audit detects two tokens collapsing to the same value in one palette, so the RAIL palette's primary/engaged-toggle and edge/fill collisions clear A18 by being measured against SSR_C_PANEL instead of against each other. The contrast table is hand-maintained (SSR_Theme.mqh:344-348 says so), so a pair that is never listed is never checked.

No test exercises the property cache under Remove/Hide churn. A test that draws N>512 distinct names, or that Hides and redraws a set of names in a loop and then asserts Writes() is still near zero on a still frame, would expose the tombstone leak (finding 6). The existing instrument (Writes()) is the right probe and nothing asserts against it across a long run - SSR_Panel.mqh:2995-3001 documents the intent ("on a frame where nothing changed this must be ZERO") without a test that holds it over time.

SSR_Layout.mqh is tested (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:3354-3386 checks mirroring is symmetric) but nothing tests that any production surface USES it, which is why a fully-tested file has zero production callers. An audit asserting that each of the eight UI drawing files contains at least one SSRLead/SSRTrail/SSRColX call would have kept the promise the header makes.

Nothing asserts the project's sources are ASCII, so the two non-ASCII BOM-less files (finding 13) pass every gate; and nothing renders a Persian frame and measures the resulting object extents, so the hard-coded advance-width constants in Chip (10 + len*6, SSR_Widgets.mqh:529) and Group (7 + len*5, SSR_Widgets.mqh:507) are calibrated on ASCII Tahoma only. Persian values in fa.txt include U+200C zero-width non-joiners that StringLen counts as characters (e.g. grp.keyboard = 9 chars, 8 visible), so those plates are sized from a count that does not match what is drawn.

key_facts: The setup panel is created on ChartID() (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2069) and the panel/dialogs on g_panel_chart = ChartID() (:1463) - so every surface in this subsystem lives on the chart the EA IS attached to, and CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK / ENDEDIT / KEYDOWN do reach the two dialogs. The latch-polling design (Pressed()) is used by SetupPanel, ReviewCard, RevealCard; RangeDialog and SessionDialog use OnEvent(CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK) instead.

CSSRSetupPanel surfaces 14 of the 61 expert inputs (balance, risk_percent, spread_points, speed, chart_tf, extra_tfs, blind, session_name, prop_on/target/daily/total, random_start, seed). The other 47 are reachable only from MetaTrader's own Inputs dialog - documented, not hidden.

The wizard is 4 steps (0 QUICK / 1 SETTINGS 17 rows / 2 MODE / 3 START). Centring uses SSR_SETUP_H_MAX = 30+17*24+44 = 482 (the settings step, the tallest) so the window does not move under the hand pressing Next. RenderSettings really is 17 rows - 4 group headings plus 13 fields - verified by walking r.

ReadAll() is called on every 'next' press and on 'go', and it reads boxes that may not exist on the current step. Num() returns its fallback for an absent box; Str() returns "" - the asymmetry is the subsystem's most damaging defect (ui-dialogs-1).
CSSRWidgets::RemoveAll uses ObjectsDeleteAll(chart, prefix, 0), i.e. by name prefix, so the range dialog's hand-rolled SSRD_start OBJ_EDIT is torn down correctly and no object leaks from Close().

m_menu (which pseudo-combo is open) is never cleared on a step change, and Render() always ends with DrawMenu() - so an open dropdown is redrawn over steps 2 and 3, on top of the START button (ui-dialogs-2).

CSSRSessionDialog::RequestSave and the whole SSR_SD_CONFIRM_SAVE mode have NO caller anywhere in MQL5/** - named sessions are saved by the host in OnDeinit via g_session_mgr.Save(CfgSession(), set) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2135-2143). The port's SaveSession() is therefore dead code too.

SSR_Review.mqh is the only file in the subsystem that defends the 63-character draw limit (SSR_REVIEW_ROW_MAX 60 + SSR_REVIEW_PREFIX 2). Audit A14 measures only literal-only text arguments at the widget call site (tools/ssr_audit.py:895-950), so every runtime-assembled string drawn by this subsystem is unmeasured - and two observation sentences and one validator message exceed 63 for every possible value.

SSRReviewRows() always returns exactly 43 rows and SSRReviewObservations() at most 6 (and 0 when trades < 3), which is what makes ReviewCard's fixed 12-row page window and 8-slot observation loop safe.

The v124 layout-overflow instrument (ResetExtent/MaxRight/MaxBottom/CheckFrame) is used only in SSR_Panel.mqh:634,765,3019. None of the seven files here measures its own frame, and CSSRWidgets::Label never feeds Extent() at all, so a label drawn outside a card's frame is invisible to every instrument in the product.

Files written by this subsystem: SSReplay\setup.ini (14 keys), SSReplay\presets.ini (name|on|target|daily|drawdown, written only when absent), SSReplay\seen.txt. Chart globals: SSR_SETUP_X / SSR_SETUP_Y (written only by the drag handler, which cannot fire - see ui-dialogs-6).

findings.title: ReadAll() wipes session_name and extra_tfs whenever it runs on a step that has no edit boxes
findings.claim: Walk the wizard normally - step 1 (type "monday" into Save as, "H1,H4" into Extra timeframes) -> Next -> step 2 MODE -> Next. The second Next calls ReadAll() on a step that contains no OBJ_EDIT at all, Str("ses") and Str("xtf") both return "", and m_v.session_name / m_v.extra_tfs are silently cleared. Step 3 then recaps "Save as: not saved", Save() writes session= to setup.ini, CfgSession() is "", and OnDeinit's `if(CfgSession() != "")` never runs - the whole session (account, trades, position) is never written to disk and cannot be resumed. The same wipe happens on the quick path: qlast -> step 3 -> go also calls ReadAll() with no ses/xtf boxes present.
findings.evidence: CSSRWidgets::EditText returns "" both for an empty box and for an ABSENT box (SSR_Widgets.mqh:350-356 - `if(ObjectFind(m_chart,n) < 0) return ""`). Num() defends against this by returning its fallback (SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:285-287), and ReadAll's seed read defends explicitly with `m_w.Exists("eseed")` plus a comment naming this exact hazard (:1180-1189) - but Str() cannot tell the two cases apart and ReadAll calls it unguarded at :1174-1175 (`m_v.extra_tfs = Str("xtf", m_v.extra_tfs); m_v.session_name = Str("ses", m_v.session_name);`). ReadAll runs on every 'next' press regardless of step (:1061-1067) and on 'go' (:1076). Repaint() calls m_w.RemoveAll() (:658) which is ObjectsDeleteAll by prefix (SSR_Widgets.mqh:637-643), so on steps 0/2/3 the ses/xtf objects genuinely do not exist. Host chain: SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2518-2520 Values->Save, :224-241 CfgSession(), :2135-2143 the OnDeinit save gated on CfgSession() != "".

findings.title: An open dropdown survives a step change and is redrawn on top of the START button
findings.claim: On step 1 click the Preset field to open its list, then - without choosing - click Next, Next. m_menu is still "pre" and m_menu_y is still the settings-step row position, so Render() ends with DrawMenu() and paints the 5 preset buttons at m_y+291..m_y+391 over the MODE step and then over the START step, where back/go sit at m_y+316..m_y+342. The menu items are created last, so they are on top: the click the user aims at "START REPLAY HERE" is consumed by Poll()'s menu block, applies a preset, and the replay does not start.
findings.evidence: m_menu is only ever cleared in DrawMenu when the option list is empty (:625), after an option is chosen (:1092) and by the toggling field handlers (:1100-1103). Neither Repaint() (:656-662) nor the step handlers reset it, and Render() unconditionally calls DrawMenu() last (:673 'last, because last is on top'). m_menu_y is written only inside Row() (:221-222), which only runs from RenderSettings, so it keeps the step-1 value. Geometry: Row("pre") is r=10 -> ry = m_y+270 -> fy = m_y+291 (:629), 1+4 default presets x 20 px = 100; RenderStart puts back/go at gy = by+42 = m_y+316 (:930-941). Poll checks the menu items (:1084-1096) and there is no 'go' press to find because the top-most object under the cursor is m1/m2.

findings.title: Recompute() erases the two messages the range dialog sets just before calling it, so a bad date and Load-more's result are never shown
findings.claim: Press J, type "march 5" into the start box and press Enter. StringToTime returns 0, the refusal text is assigned to m_problem, and then Recompute() - on the very next line - does `m_problem = ""` and overwrites it with SSRValidateRange's verdict on the UNCHANGED old date, which is usually empty. The user sees no error at all, the field keeps the text they typed, and START stays enabled against the previous start instant - exactly the 'a typo must not silently become 1970' failure the comment claims to prevent. The identical pattern makes LOAD MORE mute: `m_problem = "gained %d more bars" / "the broker has nothing older"` (:304-306) is discarded by the Recompute() on :307.
findings.evidence: Recompute() begins with `m_problem = "";` (:127) and ends with `m_problem = SSRValidateRange(m_req, m_cat);` (:135), so any value assigned before the call is dead. Render() draws only m_problem into the "problem" label (:234). Both call sites assign m_problem and then call Recompute() immediately (:274-275 and :304-307). There is no other channel - the dialog has no toast and prints nothing to the log.

findings.title: Two review-card observation sentences exceed MetaTrader's 63-character draw limit for every possible value
findings.claim: Any session with >=3 spread samples and one wide-spread entry produces a 71..79 character sentence that the card draws into one OBJ_LABEL. MetaTrader shows 63: "3 of 12 trades were entered at a spread wider than this session" - the words that say what the comparison IS ("'s average.") are cut off. The ambiguous-bar line at :210-213 is worse: "1 trade(s) closed on a bar that reached both the stop and the target." is 69 characters and renders as "...reached both the stop and the t", which reads as a plain stop-out and loses the fact that the bar hit the target too - the single most important caveat this product reports about a fill.
findings.evidence: Measured: the wide-spread literal is 75 characters before substitution and >=71 after (two 1-digit counts); the ambiguous literal is 70 before and >=69 after. Both are drawn verbatim by CSSRReviewCard::Render via `m_w.Label(oid, m_x+12, oy+16+i*14, m_obs[i], ...)` (SSR_ReviewCard.mqh:190) with no truncation. SSRReviewLine truncates measure ROWS to SSR_REVIEW_ROW_MAX 60 (:91-93) but nothing truncates observations. Audit A14 cannot see them twice over: it measures only literal-only arguments at the widget call site (tools/ssr_audit.py:938-948, `lit = LITERAL_ONLY.match(args[idx]); if lit is None: continue`) and the argument here is m_obs[i]; and the source literals are split across two lines so a per-literal scan sees two short pieces. These sentences also bypass the T(SSR_S_*) rule, so they are untranslated as well.

findings.title: The range dialog draws an unbounded validator message into one label, so the 'start too early' refusal loses the date it is about
findings.code:
color pc = (StringFind(m_problem, "warning") == 0) ? SSR_C_HOLD : SSR_C_STOP;
      m_w.Label("problem", x + SSR_PAD, cy, m_problem, pc, SSR_FS_SMALL);
findings.claim: Press J and pick D1 context on a broker with limited M1 history. SSRValidateRange returns "start too early - PERIOD_D1 context needs history back to 2019.01.03 00:00:00" (77 characters; 78 with PERIOD_M15). MetaTrader draws 63, so the user reads "start too early - PERIOD_D1 context needs history back to 2019." - a sentence that looks complete and names a year instead of the instant, while the real requirement (month, day, time) is invisible. The refusal is the dialog's whole purpose and it is the one message that cannot be read.
findings.evidence: The message is built at MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Data/SSR_SessionRange.mqh:84-85 as `StringFormat("start too early - %s context needs history back to %s", EnumToString(r.max_tf), SSRFormatMsc(earliest))`; the literal part is 48 characters, EnumToString of the four offered timeframes is 9-10, and SSRFormatMsc returns TIME_DATE|TIME_MINUTES|TIME_SECONDS = 19 characters (SSR_Time.mqh:62-67). Minimum total 76. The dialog passes it straight to m_w.Label with no length guard, unlike SSRReviewLine which truncates to 60 (SSR_Review.mqh:91-93). A14 cannot measure it because the argument is a variable (tools/ssr_audit.py:944-947).

findings.title: The setup panel's drag handler can never fire: nothing enables CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE on the chart it lives on
findings.claim: Drop the EA on a chart with InpPickStart on. The setup window opens centred over the candles the user must now drag the orange start line onto, and it cannot be moved: MetaTrader only delivers CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE to programs on a chart whose CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE property has been switched on, and no code path switches it on for this chart before the setup panel exists. Every branch of OnChartEvent is therefore unreachable, SavePlace() is never called, SSR_SETUP_X/Y never exist, m_placed is always false, and the panel re-centres on every run - the 'DRAG IT BY ITS CAPTION' behaviour described at :946-953 does not exist on a real terminal.
findings.evidence: The only writer of that property in the whole tree is CSSRPanel::Create - `ChartSetInteger(m_chart, CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE, true)` (SSR_Panel.mqh:324) - and CSSRPanel::Destroy puts the saved value back (:370), so nothing leaks across runs. The host creates the setup panel during the picking phase at SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2069 and only calls g_panel.Create() later, inside BuildSession (:1467), after the setup panel has already been destroyed (:2522). grep over MQL5/** for CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE returns exactly the four SSR_Panel.mqh lines. The property's platform default is off, and MT5 exposes no user setting for it. Secondary: the drag exit also writes CHART_MOUSE_SCROLL = true unconditionally (:970) instead of restoring what the chart had, unlike SSR_Panel.mqh:371.

findings.title: The range dialog enables START for any date the broker can serve, but its only caller can only jump inside the already-loaded window
findings.claim: Press J, type a date three months before the replay window but well inside broker history, press START. Every check passes (the catalogue has that history), m_confirmed is set and the dialog closes - and then nothing at all happens on screen: the host only jumps when the date lies inside [g_group.StartMsc(), g_group.EndMsc()) and otherwise just prints 'that range needs a fresh session' to the Experts log. The dialog refuses what the BROKER cannot serve and accepts what the SESSION cannot serve, which is the opposite of what its only use needs; the title 'NEW SESSION' and the button 'START' reinforce the wrong expectation.
findings.evidence: g_dialog.Open() is reached only from RunHostCommand(SSR_CMD_JUMP) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3096-3103), which seeds start=g_group.Now(), end=g_group.EndMsc(). The confirm handler is SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3181-3192: `if(r.start_msc >= g_group.StartMsc() && r.start_msc < g_group.EndMsc()) g_group.JumpTo(...) else Print(...)`. CanStart's validation comes from SSRValidateRange(m_req, m_cat) (:135), which measures against cat.EarliestStart/cat.LastMsc - the broker's M1 range - and knows nothing about the loaded window. Close() runs before the host's check (:313-318), so there is no surface left to report the refusal on.

findings.title: Num() turns a thousands separator into a decimal point and then accepts the truncated number
findings.claim: Type "10,000" into Balance - a natural way to write it, and the comma is there precisely because the field is meant to accept comma decimals. The comma becomes a dot, StringToDouble("10.000") = 10.0, the value passes the `<= 0.0` guard, and the session starts with a balance of 10 instead of 10000. Risk sizing then produces lots below the symbol minimum for every trade and the user is told nothing. "1,234.56" is worse: it becomes "1.234.56", which parses as 1.234.
findings.evidence: The replacement is unconditional and happens before parsing (:289), and StringToDouble parses the leading numeric prefix and stops at the second dot. The only post-checks are the `v == 0.0 && first char != '0'` unreadable-guard (:295) - which 10.0 passes - and ReadAll's clamps (:1194-1199), which only reject <= 0. Nothing rejects a value that lost two orders of magnitude, and nothing in the panel or the log echoes the parsed number back before the replay is built (Summary() is printed only after 'go', at SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2521).

findings.title: ReadAll clamps balance, risk, spread and speed but not the three prop numbers, so a typed 0 silently deletes a prop rule
findings.claim: Turn Prop evaluation on and clear the Max daily loss box to 0 (or type a negative, or type text that parses to 0 with a leading '0'). ReadAll passes it through untouched, and CSSRPropEvaluation guards every rule with `> 0.0` - so the evaluation runs with NO daily loss limit, the panel still shows the prop chips and meters, and nothing anywhere says a rule was dropped. The same typed into Profit target % produces a challenge that can never be passed (TargetProgress returns 0 forever). The panel's own preset loader refuses exactly this shape - `nm == "" || (on != 0 && tg <= 0.0) -> continue` (:342) - so the file is validated and the keyboard is not.
findings.evidence: ReadAll assigns prop_target/prop_daily/prop_total from Num() at :1176-1178 and the clamp block at :1191-1199 never mentions them. Downstream: SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:391 `if(m_rules.max_daily_loss_pct > 0.0 && eq <= DailyFloor())`, :401 the same for max_total_loss_pct, :429 the same for profit_target_pct, :207 `if(!m_started || m_rules.profit_target_pct <= 0.0) return 0`. The values reach the rules via the host's CfgPropTgt/Dly/Tot accessors (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:239-241).

findings.title: The quick step builds the session path itself and skips the session manager's sanitiser, so 'Continue' disappears for names containing a slash or colon
findings.claim: Name a session "eu/us open" or "NY:2024-03-05". CSSRSessionManager stores it as sessions\eu_us open.ssr (it replaces \ / : with _), but the quick step tests for sessions\eu/us open.ssr, which cannot exist - so the "Continue ..." button is never offered and the user concludes the session was not saved. The same unsanitised name is what the panel writes to setup.ini and hands to the host.
findings.evidence: CSSRSessionManager::Path sanitises before use: `StringReplace(safe, "\\", "_"); StringReplace(safe, "/", "_"); StringReplace(safe, ":", "_");` (MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Session/SSR_SessionManager.mqh:92-97), and both Save (:167) and Exists (:117) go through it. SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:713-715 is the only place in the subsystem that concatenates a session path by hand, and Str("ses", ...) (:1175) applies no character validation or length limit of any kind.

findings.title: The session dialog's DELETE button is enabled, looks live, and deletes nothing
findings.claim: Press S, select a session, press DELETE. The button is drawn enabled (`m_selected >= 0`), carries the label T(SSR_S_SD_DELETE) = "DELETE", and does nothing except print a sentence in the dialog's message line - which is also the only place that sentence can be read, and it is 86 characters so MetaTrader shows only the first 63 ("deleting is done from the session folder - this dialog does not "). The user is left with a control that claims a destructive action, performs none, and half-explains why.
findings.evidence: The handler at :288-297 never calls any delete; CSSRSessionManager::Delete (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:406-409) exists and is never reached from here, and CSSRReplayPort declares no delete method at all. The button is created enabled at :210-211. The comment above the handler argues about CONFIRMATION for a deletion that does not happen, so the comment and the code disagree. The message length was measured against MetaTrader's 63-character draw limit.

findings.title: RequestSave and the whole overwrite-confirm mode are unreachable, and would discard their own outcome message if reached
findings.claim: Nothing in the product can reach RequestSave, so the header's promise - 'IT ASKS BEFORE IT OVERWRITES' - is not a behaviour the shipped tool has; sessions are overwritten without a question by the host's OnDeinit save. And if a future caller is wired up, the outcome is invisible: Open() is called on the next line and its first act is to overwrite m_message with "" (or "no saved sessions yet"), so both "saved <name>" and "could not save: <error>" are destroyed before Render() ever draws them. The 'yes'/'no' handlers (:243-250) have the same shape.
findings.evidence: grep over MQL5/** finds RequestSave defined at :304 and called nowhere; CSSRReplayPort::SaveSession is called only from :242 and :318, both inside these dead paths. Open() sets `m_message = (m_count == 0 ? "no saved sessions yet" : "");` (:94) after refreshing m_count from the port, so after a successful save the message is always "". Named sessions are actually written by the host: SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2135-2143 calls g_session_mgr.Save(CfgSession(), set) with no existence check. A second consequence of the early `return` at :153: the CONFIRM render never hides the list rows, up/down/load/del or msg, and the PICK render never removes q1/q2/yes/no - so if the mode is ever reached the two screens are drawn on top of each other, with the later-created yes/no buttons floating over the list after the confirm is answered.

findings.title: SetStartText draws the orange-line caption at the START step's coordinates while another step is on screen
findings.claim: Reach step 3 once (so m_start_y is set, e.g. m_y+300), press Back to step 2, then drag the orange line on the chart. The host calls SetStartText on the next 200 ms timer beat; m_start_y is still the step-3 position, which is 12 px BELOW the MODE step's frame (h = 34+4*48+62 = 288), so an amber "Start: 2024.03.05 14:00" label appears floating on the candles outside the panel, and stays there until the next button press repaints. m_start_y is never invalidated when the step changes.
findings.evidence: m_start_y is written only in RenderStart (:933) and never reset by Repaint/Render/step changes. The host calls g_setup_ui.SetStartText(...) on every timer beat while picking, whenever the pick line exists and regardless of the panel's step (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2489-2491). Only Repaint()'s RemoveAll (:658) clears the stray. The overflow instrument cannot see it either: CSSRWidgets::Label never calls Extent() (SSR_Widgets.mqh:226-253) and the setup panel never calls CheckFrame at all.

findings.title: CSSRFirstRun::Show reports success without checking the card fits, so the once-ever card is consumed unseen on a short chart
findings.code:
int x = 14, y = SSR_PANEL_H + 40, w = 396, h = 104;
      m_w.Rect("bg", x, y, w, h, SSR_C_PANEL, SSR_C_PANEL_EDGE);
findings.claim: On a chart shorter than 480 px - which is common with the Toolbox open, and which the host already warns about at 356 px - the card is drawn entirely below the visible area at y=376..480.
