Show() still returns true, so the host writes seen.txt and the card is never shown again on that installation: the one piece of onboarding the product has is spent without anybody reading it, and the only recovery is to know that MQL5/Files/SSReplay/seen.txt has to be deleted.
findings.evidence: SSR_PANEL_H = 23+32+27+21+21+SSR_SHEET_H(186)+18+8 = 336 (SSR_Theme.mqh:499), so y = 376 and the card ends at 480. Show() reads no chart dimension and its only failure path is `chart_id == 0` (:82-83) - it returns true unconditionally otherwise (:121). The host writes the marker on that return value: `if(g_first.Show(g_panel_chart)) CSSRFirstRun::MarkSeen();` (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1742-1743). The host's own height warning fires only below SSR_PANEL_H+20 = 356 (:1676-1682), i.e. it does not cover the 356..480 band where the card is invisible but the panel is fine.

findings.title: MenuClear only sweeps 32 menu items while presets.ini is unbounded, so a longer preset file orphans buttons on the chart
findings.claim: presets.ini is a user-editable file with one preset per line and no row limit; a trading desk listing 40 firms gives ArraySize(m_presets) = 41. Opening the Preset list creates SSRS_m0..SSRS_m40, and MenuClear only deletes m0..m31 - so m32..m40 are left on the chart as clickable buttons after the list closes and after every subsequent step change, each one still applying a preset when pressed. The list is also drawn 820 px tall with no paging, so most of it is off-chart in either direction.
findings.evidence: LoadPresets sizes m_presets from `int rows = f.Count("p")` with no cap (:331-371); PresetNames returns all of them (:426-433) and DrawMenu creates one button per option (:639-641). Only Repaint()'s RemoveAll (:658, ObjectsDeleteAll by prefix) can clear the surplus, and Render() calls MenuClear - not RemoveAll - on every paint (:668). DrawMenu's off-screen defence is a single flip-upwards test (:633-635), which cannot help a list taller than the chart.

findings.title: Review-card measure rows are OBJ_BUTTONs whose latch nothing consumes, so a clicked statistic stays visually pressed
findings.code:
m_w.List("m", m_x + 12, ly, SSR_RV_W - 24, SSR_RV_ROW_H,
               lines, m_first, SSR_RV_SHOWN, -1);
findings.claim: Click any of the 12 visible measure rows on the review card. MetaTrader latches the button down; the card polls only up/down/stmt/close, nothing clears OBJPROP_STATE, and the next Render early-returns on that object because its fingerprint is unchanged - so the row stays drawn in the pressed state until the user pages. On a card whose whole purpose is to be read, a row that looks selected but is not is a false affordance.
findings.evidence: CSSRWidgets::List draws each row with Button()/ButtonC() (SSR_Widgets.mqh:565-587), and ButtonC deliberately does not clear the pressed state on repaint (:388-394, 'THE PRESSED STATE IS NOT CLEARED HERE ANY MORE'). Only Pressed() consumes a latch (:337-346) and CSSRReviewCard::Poll asks about up/down/stmt/close only (:213-222). The card passes selected = -1, so it never intends selection. Nothing else routes the click either: RouteEvent hands unmatched object clicks to g_panel.OnEvent, which filters on the SSRP_ prefix (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3228).

performance_notes: CSSRSessionDialog::Render calls m_port.SessionSummary(idx) for up to 8 rows (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:176-177), and CSSRGroupPort::SessionSummary calls m_sessions.Peek(name) (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:932-940), which OPENS AND PARSES the .ssr file. Every render - i.e. every click, every up/down step, every row selection - re-reads up to 8 session files from disk. This is the heaviest paint path in the subsystem and it is unmeasured; a cached summary per name would remove it. Note also that SessionCount() re-lists the folder and refills m_names on every call, so SessionName(i) is only valid immediately after it.

Every step change in the setup panel is Repaint() = RemoveAll + full Render (SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:656-662). RemoveAll calls ForgetAll (SSR_Widgets.mqh:641), so the 512-slot property cache is emptied and the rebuilt step pays ObjectCreate plus the full uncached write count for ~35 widgets (roughly 300+ ObjectSet* calls) - against a measured 561 writes = 39.05 ms for the main panel. This is once per click, so it is affordable, but it is the reason 'pressing its buttons works very slowly' was ever reported, and the ChartRedraw at :696 is what fixed the visible half of it.

A preset click paints twice: Choose -> ApplyPreset calls Render() (:447) and Poll then calls Render() again after clearing m_menu (:1093). CyclePreset (:422) has the same shape. Harmless but it doubles the most expensive paint.

CSSRRangeDialog::Recompute quotes the catalogue twice per user action: once directly (:134) and once inside SSRValidateRange (SSR_SessionRange.mqh:90), plus an EarliestStart walk. Each tf button press and each date edit therefore costs two quotes; if Quote ever touches history rather than arithmetic this becomes the dialog's hot path.

CSSRSetupPanel::Poll runs on the host's 200 ms picking timer and asks Pressed() for up to ~19 ids, each an ObjectFind plus ObjectGetInteger. That is ~40 API calls per beat with nothing on screen changing - cheap, but it is the only work happening during the whole picking phase, so it is where a regression would be invisible.

CSSRReviewCard::Render rebuilds the whole 43-entry lines[] array with its group prefixes on every paint (:146-159) even though m_rows never changes after Show. Only 43 string concatenations, and Render only runs on Show and on a page, so this is noted rather than a problem.
CSSRFirstRun::Tick is polled from the host timer and compares uint GetTickCount() deltas (:131); the arithmetic is wrap-safe, and the card costs nothing after it is cleared.
test_gaps: No test anywhere drives the setup wizard's STEP SEQUENCE. QA smoke stage 21 presses qcust then bpre, but stages 21b and 21c press SSRS_bpre immediately after Create() - i.e. on step 0, where RenderQuick draws no bpre at all - so ObjectSetInteger targets a non-existent object, Poll applies nothing, and the check 'a preset from the file fills all four fields' cannot pass. That stage is either failing or vacuous on a real terminal, and nothing covers step1 -> next -> step2 -> next, which is the path that loses the session name (ui-dialogs-1).

Nothing asserts what ReadAll() returns when a box is ABSENT rather than empty. A three-line test - render step 1, type into eses, Repaint to step 2, press next, assert Values().session_name is unchanged - would have caught ui-dialogs-1, and the same shape covers extra_tfs.
There is no test for the pseudo-combo lifecycle: open a menu, change step, assert no SSRS_m* object exists. That is ui-dialogs-2 in one assertion.

CSSRRangeDialog and CSSRSessionDialog are not included by any Tests/ or QA/ program (grep over MQL5/Scripts finds neither class). Their OnEvent state machines - date parse failure, LOAD MORE, tf switching, overwrite confirm, paging past the end - are entirely uncovered, which is why the two messages discarded by Recompute (ui-dialogs-3) and the dead RequestSave path (ui-dialogs-12) have survived.

No test measures the LENGTH of a string this subsystem draws at runtime. Audit A14 only measures literal-only arguments at the call site, so SSRReviewObservations' sentences and SSRValidateRange's messages are unmeasured. A cheap fix is a unit check over SSRReviewObservations and SSRValidateRange asserting len <= 63 for representative inputs - it would have caught ui-dialogs-4 and ui-dialogs-5 statically.

The v124 layout-overflow instrument is never applied here: ResetExtent/CheckFrame exist only in SSR_Panel.mqh. The setup panel (482 px tall at step 1, centred on a computed maximum) and the review card (320..422 px tall, 520 px wide) are exactly the surfaces that need it, and Label() does not feed Extent() at all, so no instrument in the product can see a stray or overflowing label (ui-dialogs-13).

Nothing tests a dialog or card against a SMALL chart. The review card's close button sits at m_y+h-28 and the first-run card at y=376..480, both of which fall off a short chart; the host warns only below 356 px. A test that sets CHART_HEIGHT and asserts every control is inside the viewport would cover ui-dialogs-14 and the review card's unreachable Close.

No test asserts input REFUSAL in the setup panel. Balance '10,000', a zero prop target, a session name containing '/' - all three produce a silently wrong session and none is covered (ui-dialogs-8, -9, -10).
Nothing covers presets.ini with more than a handful of rows, so the 32-item MenuClear cap (ui-dialogs-15) has never been exercised; the existing stages use 1 and 4 rows.

key_facts: The seam is one abstract class plus one flat struct: CSSRReplayPort (13 pure-virtual verbs, ~28 defaulted-to-refusal verbs, virtual dtor) and SSRUiState (~90 fields, fixed arrays + strings, pointer-free so an IPC port could fill it from a wire). SSR_ReplayPort.mqh contains no logic beyond SSRUiState::Init/IsRunning/CanPlay/CanStep.
CSSRGroupPort is the ONLY implementation of CSSRReplayPort. The 'Ipc' port promised in the header comment does not exist anywhere in the codebase.

Transport verbs (Play/Pause/StepBars/StepBack/JumpTo/SeekTo/Restart/SetSpeedX100) go to CSSRReplayGroup; readouts come from the primary stream (m_group.At(0)), the sink and the chart manager. Reset() is the exception: it loops At(i).Reset() then calls m_group.Align() and drops Align's bool result (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:425-437).

The clock, window, progress, speed and skew in SSRUiState all come from the GROUP, never from a stream (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:114-124). Blind-mode masking of clock_text and symbol happens in the port (l.180-190), never in the panel.

Lot size and money always come from the trading engine's own PreviewLot/PreviewPendingLot on the same fill price the order would use; the port does no lot arithmetic. Per-row P/L uses MoneyFor with an explicit sign, which is arithmetically identical to the engine's RealisedOf (both funnel into CSSRRiskEngine::RiskOf, which MathAbs-es the distance), so the rows do sum to `floating`.

CSSRSessionManager sits above everything, depends downward on Core/Trading/Chart, and nothing depends on it. It holds three non-owned pointers (group, account, stats) and has NO slot for the prop evaluation, the journal or the shot book.

Session file layout in write order: [session] [settings] [stream]+[bookmarks] per stream [account] [execution] [positions] [equity]. `status` and `master_now` are written and never read by Restore; the whole [settings] block is write-only (nothing in the product calls ReadSettings).

Restore()'s documented ordering rule is 'streams first, account after' because winding a stream re-emits ticks. The account is only emptied inside m_acct.RestoreFrom (TradingEngine sets m_count=0 at l.1165), i.e. AFTER every wind-forward.

The stream's own RestoreFrom is the real guard: it refuses a different `origin` and an instant outside its own window. It winds FORWARD only (ReplayController.mqh:1826) even though JumpTo handles backwards (l.1494).

Two independent save paths disagree: the host autosaves CfgSession() with CollectSettings() on every OnDeinit reason (Standalone.mq5:2139), while the panel's Session dialog saves through CSSRGroupPort::SaveSession with a default-initialised SSRSessionSettings (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:949-955).

CSSRSessionFile is a linear sectioned key/value store with dynamic parallel arrays (deliberately heap, not stack, because the object is a local inside Save/Restore). Ceilings: 16384 entries, 1024 sections, format 1. Reads refuse a newer format, a missing '# format' line, or either ceiling; writes check and count nothing.

Backward/forward compatibility is achieved by appending packed-row fields and reading with SSRField* accessors that cannot walk off a short row, which is why SSR_SF_FORMAT has never been bumped. The 'append, never insert' rule is enforced only by a comment.
True worst-case entry count today is ~12,800 of 16,384 (4096 equity + 512 pos + 4096 legs + ~60 keys) - the constant's own comment omits the leg rows and claims 3x headroom.
CSSRGroupPort::LoadSession is reachable mid-session from CSSRSessionDialog (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:273) and does nothing to pause the board, clear prior bookmarks, or empty the account first.

Warnings never block a resume: HadWarnings/Warnings/ResumeReport carry fingerprint mismatches, stream-count mismatches, skew and balance-replay mismatches, and LoadSession copies them into SessionError even on success.

findings.title: A session save reports success no matter what was actually written
findings.claim: Save() returns true unconditionally, so a write that fails half-way through (disk full, quota, sharing violation) is reported to the user as "session saved" while the file on disk is truncated - and because the '# format 1' line is written first, that truncated file then passes every check Load() has.
findings.evidence: Nothing on the write path checks anything. CSSRSessionFile::Set does `FileWriteString(m_handle, key + "=" + v + "\r\n");` (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:177) and discards the byte count; Section, Comment and Create's header writes do the same; Close() returns a bool (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:194-201) which Save ignores; and no entry is counted on the way out, so m_truncated (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:90) can only ever be set by the READ-side ceilings. [equity] is written last (l.200), so the most likely casualty is the one statistic the file exists to carry - the comment at SSR_Statistics.mqh:616-621 states it cannot be recomputed. A cut inside [positions] drops whole rows silently, because TradingEngine::RestoreFrom `continue`s any row that unpacks to fewer than 26 fields (l.1176).

findings.title: Saving truncates the previous good session before writing the new one
findings.code: m_handle = FileOpen(path, FILE_WRITE | FILE_TXT | FILE_ANSI | FILE_SHARE_READ);
findings.claim: The destination file is opened for writing directly, with no temp-file-then-replace, so the moment Create() succeeds the previous save no longer exists; any interruption between Create and Close leaves the user with neither the old session nor a complete new one.
findings.evidence: FILE_WRITE without FILE_READ resets the file to zero length on open, and CSSRSessionManager::Save passes the final path straight in: `if(!f.Create(Path(name)))` (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:167). There is no staging path anywhere in the class. This is not a rare path: the host writes CfgSession() on EVERY OnDeinit reason including REASON_CHARTCHANGE (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2130-2142), and the dialog's Replace branch overwrites in place (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:242) after telling the user there is no undo. Scenario: a trader has a 40-trade session in "friday"; they change the chart timeframe, the EA is torn down and re-initialised, the autosave opens friday.ssr (old content gone) and the terminal is closed or the write fails part-way - the whole session is lost, and finding ui-port-session-1 means they were told it was saved.

findings.title: Restore never checks that the streams reached the saved instant, and cannot rewind to it
findings.code:
long now = m_group.At(0).Now();
      m_group.SeekAllTo(now);
findings.claim: When the engine is already past the instant in the file, Restore installs the saved account over a chart that never went back: the trade log is rewound to T1 while the market stands at T2, and ResumeReport announces T2 as the resumed instant with no warning.
findings.evidence: `master_now` is written at l.176 and read only by Peek (l.224) - Restore never reads it, so it has nothing to compare against. The instant is taken from whatever the streams happen to be at, and the stream restore only moves forward: ReplayController::RestoreFrom does `if(want_now > m_clock.now_msc && !JumpTo(want_now))` (l.1826), even though JumpTo handles backwards jumps through StepBackward (l.1494-1515). SeekAllTo(now) is then a no-op (the master is already there), its result is discarded, and ResumeReport prints `SSRFormatMsc(m_group.Now())` (l.391-393) as the resume point. Scenario: save "A" at 10:00, play on to 10:30, open the Session dialog and press Load on "A" (CSSRGroupPort::LoadSession, l.960-972, has no guard of any kind). Streams stay at 10:30; m_acct.RestoreFrom replaces the account with the 10:00 log; every position the file recorded as open is re-installed and marked to 10:30 prices, so any stop or target crossed between 10:00 and 10:30 is evaluated half an hour late, with an MAE/MFE that never happened. The user is told "resumed 1 stream(s) at 10:30".

findings.title: Restore merges bookmarks into the live store instead of replacing them
findings.code: if(!m_group.At(i).RestoreFrom(f, i, w))
findings.claim: Restore is not idempotent: loading a session that is already loaded appends its bookmarks a second time, and once the 16-mark store is full every further bookmark the user takes is silently refused - after which the next autosave persists the duplicated list.
findings.evidence: The stream restore adds each saved mark with `m_snaps.Mark(mk, SSRField(c, 1, "mark"));` (ReplayController.mqh:1819) and nothing on either side clears the existing marks first; CSSRSnapshotStore::Mark returns false without a word once `m_mark_count >= SSR_BOOKMARK_MAX` (SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:165-172, cap 16). Scenario (the default configuration): InpSession="mine", InpResume=true, so the host restores the file including its 9 bookmarks at init (Standalone.mq5:1483). The user opens the Session dialog and presses Load on "mine" - 18 marks are attempted, 16 land (7 duplicates), out.bookmarks reports 16, and pressing B does nothing for the rest of the session. OnDeinit then writes the duplicated list back to disk (l.2139), so the file degrades a little more on every reload.

findings.title: The wind-forward runs against a live account, contradicting the invariant the ordering is built on
findings.claim: The comment above this loop asserts "With the account empty there is nothing for those ticks to act on", but nothing in Restore empties the account: it is cleared later, inside m_acct.RestoreFrom, so on the mid-session load path the re-emitted ticks are fed to positions the trader is actually holding.
findings.evidence: The account is only reset at l.367-373, after every stream has been wound; TradingEngine::RestoreFrom sets `m_count = 0` at l.1165. The wind-forward at l.326-333 re-emits the crossed stretch through JumpTo, and the account is a tick observer. Scenario: the trader steps back (or presses Restart), opens a position, then loads a session saved further forward - reachable from the dialog at SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:273. The crossed ticks hit the live position: its SL/TP can fire, CSSRTradeAutoPause pauses the board mid-restore, CSSRShotBook writes entry/exit PNGs, and CSSRPropEvaluation - which has no persistence at all (see ui-port-session-6) - can be pushed to FAILED, which is one-way (SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:139-141). The account itself is then wiped, so the only trace of the phantom fills is in the artefacts outside it. The ordering defect is in the code; the specific downstream effects follow from the observers the host attaches (Standalone.mq5:1195-1200).

findings.title: The prop evaluation is not part of a session, so a resumed challenge restarts silently
findings.claim: Save writes the account and the equity curve and nothing else stateful; CSSRPropEvaluation is a day-by-day accumulator with no persistence, so resuming a session mid-evaluation brings the trades back exactly and the evaluation back at day zero - re-anchored to the resumed equity - while the panel presents it as authoritative.
findings.evidence: The class has slots for group/account/stats only (l.74-76) and Attach takes exactly those three (l.106-108); there is no prop pointer and no [prop] section in the format. CSSRPropEvaluation carries m_state, m_trading_days, m_first_day, m_day, m_day_open_eq, m_day_low_eq, m_day_traded, m_peak_eq, m_low_eq and has no SaveInto/RestoreFrom anywhere (verified by grep across the file). The host calls g_prop.Reset() once at init (Standalone.mq5:1197) and Restore never touches it. Scenario: a 12-day evaluation is saved on day 12 and resumed. On the first tick the `m_first_day == 0` branch re-anchors `m_day_open_eq`, `m_day_low_eq` and `m_peak_eq` to the resumed equity (SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:369-373). Result: prop_days/prop_days_progress claim the minimum-trading-days rule is unmet, the daily floor is measured from the resume rather than the day's open, a trailing total floor is re-based upward, and a run that had already FAILED or PASSED comes back RUNNING. Every one of those numbers is copied straight onto the panel's four meters by CSSRGroupPort::ReadState l.204-234, whose own comment says the meter and the rule that ends the run must read the same number from the same place.

findings.title: Peek's session summary is roughly twice what its only consumer can draw
findings.claim: The summary is ~111 characters plus the name and symbols, and its only consumer is a chart button, which draws exactly 63 - so the window end and the saved-at date, the two facts that distinguish two similar files, are never visible to the user.
findings.evidence: SSRFormatMsc returns 19 characters (TIME_DATE|TIME_MINUTES|TIME_SECONDS, SSR_Time.mqh:62-67) and `written` is another 19 (TIME_DATE|TIME_SECONDS, l.174): 3x19 + 19 + the literals = 111 fixed characters. The only call site is CSSRGroupPort::SessionSummary (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:932-940), whose only caller draws it as OBJPROP_TEXT: `m_w.Button(id, x + 6, ry - 2, SSR_SD_W - 12, SSR_ROW_H - 3, m_port.SessionSummary(idx), idx == m_selected);` (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:176-177). With name "friday" and symbol "US30.U26" the row stops mid-way through the window start: `friday  |  US30.U26  |  at 2026.08.24 19:06:00 (48% of 2026`. The unreadable-file fallback at l.938 (`name + "  (unreadable: " + LastError() + ")"`) is cut the same way, and the loader's own messages are long sentences. Audit A19 cannot see this because the string is assembled at runtime, not a literal.

findings.title: Resume warnings are newline-joined and end up in a single 63-character label
findings.code: m_warnings += (m_warnings == "" ? "" : "\n") + text;
findings.claim: The fingerprint mismatch - the entire reason the session format carries a fingerprint - is delivered to the mid-session load path as a multi-line string rendered in one chart label, so the user sees about forty characters of it and never sees a second warning at all.
findings.evidence: CSSRGroupPort::LoadSession copies the whole warning block into m_session_error on SUCCESS (`if(m_sessions.HadWarnings()) m_session_error = m_sessions.Warnings();`, SSR_GroupPort.mqh:969-970). The dialog builds `m_message = "resumed \"" + name + "\"" + (warn == "" ? "" : "  BUT: " + warn);` (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:280-281) and draws it with `m_w.Label("msg", x + SSR_PAD, cy, m_message, ...)` (l.214) - one OBJ_LABEL, 63 characters, no newline support. The warnings it carries are full sentences: was.DiffText(now_fp) for revised history (ReplayController.mqh:1851), the bar-count mismatch (l.1860-1863), the stream-count mismatch (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:320-322), the skew message (l.361-363) and the balance-replay mismatch (TradingEngine.mqh:1254-1257). After the 23-character prefix roughly 40 characters of the first warning survive; anything after the first "\n" is unreachable. On this path nothing tells the user the complete text is in the Experts log (only the host's startup path Prints it, Standalone.mq5:1486).

findings.title: Pending orders occupy wire rows that no total on the wire accounts for
findings.code: out.pending_count++;
findings.claim: pos_rows counts open AND pending rows while open_positions counts opens only, and pending_count is written here but read nowhere - so the panel's only "hidden rows" indicator is computed from the wrong pair and a pending order can drop off the sheet with no "+N more".
findings.evidence: Rows include pendings (`bool pend = (vp.state == SSR_POS_PENDING); if(vp.state != SSR_POS_OPEN && !pend) continue;`, l.354-356) while `out.open_positions = m_acct.OpenCount();` (l.240) does not. pending_count appears only at its declaration (SSR_ReplayPort.mqh:124), its clear (l.261) and this increment - no consumer exists. The panel computes `int shown = (m_state.pos_rows < cap ? m_state.pos_rows : cap);` (SSR_Panel.mqh:1513) and then `if(m_state.open_positions > shown)` ... `m_state.open_positions - shown` (l.1640-1642), with PosCap() = (134-22)/20 = 5 on the normal panel (l.434-443). Scenario: 2 open positions and 4 pending orders - pos_rows 6, shown 5, open_positions 2; `2 > 5` is false, so no indicator is drawn and one pending order is simply absent, which is exactly the failure the "PENDING ORDERS ARE ROWS TOO / an order you cannot see is an order you forget you left there" comment at l.346-353 exists to prevent. With 20 opens and 4 pendings the same line reports "15 not shown" when 19 rows are hidden.

findings.title: A save made from the panel records settings that are not the session's
findings.claim: Every session saved from the Session dialog writes default settings into [settings], so the file claims the session was not random, not blind, ran 8 ticks per bar with zero spread on M5 - whatever it actually was.
findings.evidence: Init() sets seed 0, blind 0, pause_flags 0, session_mode 0, slot 1, ticks_per_bar 8, spread_points 0.0, chart_tf PERIOD_M5 (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:62-67) and Save writes those verbatim (l.184-191). The host's own save path uses the real values (`SSRSessionSettings set; CollectSettings(set);`, Standalone.mq5:2137-2139), so two saves of the same running session disagree depending on which button produced them. The file's own comment at l.182-183 says the seed is written "so a session that was random can be recognised as such months later" - which a panel-made save cannot do. The port's comment acknowledges the gap; the reason it is not already visible is that nothing in the product calls ReadSettings (l.244), so the wrong values are stored and never yet read.

findings.title: List() strips the extension by first match, so a name containing ".ssr" is listed wrong
findings.claim: The extension is removed by searching forward for ".ssr" rather than trimming it off the end, so a session whose own name contains that string is listed under a truncated name, and Load/Peek/Delete on that name then address a different file or none at all.
findings.evidence: StringFind returns the FIRST occurrence. A file `notes.ssr copy.ssr` yields name "notes"; the dialog shows "notes", SessionSummary calls Peek("notes") which fails with "cannot read ...\\notes.ssr" (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:937-938), and pressing Load calls Restore("notes") - which fails, or silently loads a genuinely different session called "notes" if one exists. The `dot > 0` guard also lets a file named exactly `.ssr` through as the name ".ssr", whose Path() is then `...\.ssr.ssr`. Low because it requires the literal ".ssr" inside a user-typed name, but the name is free text from the panel's edit box and nothing rejects it.

findings.title: The session list re-reads and fully parses every file on every dialog render
findings.code: if(!m_sessions.Peek(m_names[i], summary))
findings.claim: Peek does a complete file load - FileOpen, line-by-line parse, three dynamic arrays grown to the full entry count - to read five keys out of [session], and the dialog calls it once per visible row on every render, including every click.
findings.evidence: Peek constructs a local CSSRSessionFile and calls f.Load(Path(name)) (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:217-219), which parses the entire file including every `pos`, `leg` and `e` row before any key is read. The dialog calls SessionSummary(idx) inside its row loop with SSR_SD_ROWS = 8 (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:27, 158-178), and Render() runs on Open() and on every up/down/row/load click (l.255, 257, 264, 284). There is no cache and no header-only read mode. With 8 visible sessions of 400 trades each that is roughly 8 x 9,000 parsed entries per click, on a modal drawn over the replay chart while the pump timer is still firing.

findings.title: Restoring an account is O(entries x rows) because every packed row is fetched by linear scan
findings.claim: GetNth rescans the whole entry list from zero for every row, and its callers fetch rows by index in a loop, so restoring a large session costs on the order of 100 million key comparisons on the startup path with the terminal blocked.
findings.evidence: Each GetNth call walks all m_ent_count entries comparing an int and a string (l.336-341). TradingEngine::RestoreFrom does `int n = f.Count("pos");` then `f.GetNth("pos", i)` for every i (l.1172-1176) and the same for `leg` (l.1225-1230); CSSRStatsEngine::RestoreFrom does it for every `e` sample (SSR_Statistics.mqh:645-650). At the reachable worst case of ~12,800 entries that is 512x12,800 + 4,096x12,800 + 4,096x12,800 ~ 110 million comparisons for one Restore, plus the same shape again for Count(). Nothing indexes by section or key, and the class's own comment (l.45-47) justifies the linear scan on the grounds that "sessions are small enough" - which holds for a scalar Get and not for these three loops. Exact wall time is unmeasured; the operation count follows directly from the code.

findings.title: The entry ceiling is unenforced on write and its documented headroom is wrong
findings.code:
#define SSR_SF_MAX_ENTRIES   16384
#define SSR_SF_MAX_SECTIONS  1024
findings.claim: The writer counts nothing while the reader refuses any file that exceeds the ceiling, so a session too large to read can be written and reported as saved; the comment that justifies the ceiling under-counts the real worst case by a factor of two, which is how that would come to happen.
findings.evidence: The comment above this line counts "4096 equity samples + 512 positions + four streams of settings" and concludes "about three times the worst realistic case", but omits the leg rows: SSR_MAX_POSITIONS is 512 (TradingEngine.mqh:38) and SSR_MAX_TRADE_LEGS is 8 (SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:173), so [positions] alone can hold 512 `pos` + 4,096 `leg` entries, giving ~12,800 of 16,384 (78%) rather than a third. On the write side Set/Section only append to the handle - no counter, no ceiling check - while Load fails the WHOLE file once `m_ent_count >= SSR_SF_MAX_ENTRIES` (l.251, 261-269: "it was NOT fully read", return false). Scenario: a later build raises SSR_MAX_POSITIONS or SSR_EQUITY_SAMPLES on the strength of that comment; saves keep reporting success and every one of them becomes permanently unopenable. Not reachable at today's constants, which is why this is a latent risk rather than a live defect.

findings.title: The session file is written in the terminal's ANSI codepage, so non-ASCII trade tags do not survive
findings.code: int h = FileOpen(path, FILE_READ | FILE_TXT | FILE_ANSI);
findings.claim: Both ends of the session file use FILE_ANSI (one byte per character), so the two user-authored strings in it - a position's tag and its note - are converted through whatever ANSI codepage the machine has; on a Persian install this is either lossy or machine-dependent, and the product ships a complete Persian translation.
findings.evidence: The matching writer is `FileOpen(path, FILE_WRITE | FILE_TXT | FILE_ANSI | FILE_SHARE_READ)` (l.138). The tag is free text the user types into the panel's tagbox OBJ_EDIT (SSR_Panel.mqh:2540-2559) and reaches the port through SetTradeTag, which only trims and strips commas (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:799-809); it is then packed into the `pos` row alongside `note` (TradingEngine.mqh:1105-1106) and restored from it (l.1209-1210). The project's own recorded lesson is that FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI is the wrong mode for UTF-8 text (it is why the language file is read with FILE_BIN + CP_UTF8). Scenario: a trader tags trades in Persian and resumes - on a codepage that cannot represent those characters every tag returns as a run of '?', and the exported statement's Tag column with it; on CP1256 the bytes survive locally but the same file read on a Western install is mojibake. Marked POTENTIAL_RISK because the outcome depends on the terminal's ANSI codepage, which cannot be verified from here.

findings.title: data_mode is on the wire, set by nobody and read by nobody
findings.code: ENUM_SSR_DATA_MODE data_mode;
findings.claim: The one port implementation never assigns this field, so it permanently reports SSR_DATA_MEMORY; the first consumer to trust it will describe a disk-backed session as in-memory.
findings.evidence: Init() sets `data_mode = SSR_DATA_MEMORY;` (l.250) and CSSRGroupPort::ReadState never touches it, although the value exists on the controller and is written into the session file (`f.SetInt("data_mode", (int)m_state.data_mode);`, ReplayController.mqh:1728). A grep for data_mode across Ui and Integration returns only the declaration and that Init line - no writer, no reader. Either fill it in ReadState beside fidelity (l.110-112) or drop it from the struct: SSRUiState is the IPC contract, and a field that is always a default is a field the promised Ipc port will silently get wrong.

performance_notes: ReadState is called from CSSRPanel::Render (SSR_Panel.mqh:637), which the host paints at most every 100 ms (Standalone.mq5:3092-3096) plus once per dialog/keyboard event - so ~10 Hz sustained.

The position row loop walks from Total()-1 downwards and only stops once 12 OPEN-or-PENDING rows are filled (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:340). A session with 500 closed trades and nothing open therefore copies 500 SSRVirtualPosition structs (each carrying an 8-entry leg array plus two strings) per repaint via m_acct.At(pi, vp) - roughly 5,000 struct copies a second, for zero rows drawn. Iterating only open/pending positions, or asking the engine for them, would make this O(rows).

The prop block calls eight accessors that each recompute Equity() -> FloatingPL() -> a full scan of m_count (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:221-227; TradingEngine.mqh:959-971), and out.equity/out.floating add two more. With a full 512-position log that is ~10 full scans per repaint stacked on top of the row loop above.

Session restore is the heaviest thing in the subsystem: CSSRSessionFile::GetNth rescans all entries per call (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:331-344) and its callers fetch rows by index, giving ~110 million key comparisons for a ~12,800-entry file (see finding ui-port-session-13). This runs inside OnInit, where the terminal is blocked.

Opening the Session dialog parses every listed file in full, once per visible row, on every render (finding ui-port-session-12), and SessionCount() re-runs FileFindFirst/FileFindNext over the folder each time the dialog opens or a save is requested (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:91, 309).
Save cost is linear and small by comparison: one FileWriteString per key, with the packed rows keeping a position to one line (30 fields) and a leg to one line (10 fields) instead of forty keys.

CSSRSessionFile deliberately keeps its four arrays dynamic and grows them in blocks (Reserve: 256 minimum, then doubling, SSR_SessionFile.mqh:64-74) precisely because the object is a local inside Save and Restore and fixed arrays at the 16,384 ceiling would put ~1 MB on the stack. Worth preserving.

ReadState allocates and returns several formatted strings per frame (pos_text rows, symbol suffix, clock text, strategy line). At 10 Hz this is minor next to the two items above, but it is the reason the panel's property cache matters downstream.
test_gaps: No test restores into a group that is already PAST the saved instant. T12.6 always rebuilds a fresh stream at the window start, so the forward-only wind (finding ui-port-session-3) is invisible to the suite.

No test loads the same session twice, or loads a session into a group that already holds bookmarks or open positions - so both the bookmark duplication (ui-port-session-4) and the live-account wind-forward (ui-port-session-5) are untested. A test could assert BookmarkCount() is identical after one restore and after two.
No test attaches a CSSRPropEvaluation to a save/resume at all, so the fact that an evaluation does not survive a session (ui-port-session-6) is not detected anywhere.

No test truncates a session file mid-line or mid-row and asserts what Load/RestoreFrom do with it. T12.1 covers only a future format number and outright junk; nothing covers the far more likely partial write, and nothing asserts that a failed write is reported (Save has no failure test at all).

No test asserts that the strings this layer produces fit MetaTrader's 63-character draw limit. Peek's summary and the newline-joined warnings are both drawn in chart objects (ui-port-session-7, -8) and audit A19 only checks literals, not StringFormat results - a runtime length assertion in T12/T15 would close the class.
List() is never tested past max_names (64), nor with names containing ".ssr", trailing spaces, or characters FileOpen rejects (* ? " < > |).
No test round-trips a non-ASCII tag or note through CSSRSessionFile (ui-port-session-15).
ReadSettings is never called against a file written by CSSRGroupPort::SaveSession, so the default-settings save (ui-port-session-10) is not caught; T12.6 only exercises a host-style save.

CSSRGroupPort::ReadState is never driven with more than SSR_POS_MAX rows, nor with a mix of open and pending positions, so the pos_rows / open_positions / pending_count arithmetic (ui-port-session-9) has no coverage. A test with 3 open + 4 pending asserting pos_rows == 7 and a usable hidden-row count would pin the contract.
Truncated(), EntryCount() and SectionTotal() are never asserted outside T12.1's format check and are called nowhere in the product - the truncation instrument exists but nothing consumes it.
Restore drops the result of SeekAllTo (l.351) and of m_stats.RestoreFrom (l.375); no test forces either to fail, so a restore that could not reach the instant still reports success.

Nothing tests a multi-stream restore where the saved stream count differs from the rebuilt count (the warn-only branch at l.319-322), nor that the [stream]/[bookmarks] nth alignment survives a stream whose bookmark list is empty.

key_facts: The host is one translation unit with NO classes: 61 inputs, ~40 global objects, ~25 scalar globals, 22 free functions and 5 MT5 entry points. /home/user/academyss/mt5-replay/MQL5/Experts/SSReplay/SSReplayStandalone.mq5, 3255 lines.

Panel placement: g_panel_chart = ChartID() unconditionally (line 1449). The panel, both dialogs, the reveal/review cards and the first-run card are always on the chart the EA is attached to; only g_replay_chart may differ (two-window mode). In the default one-window mode the two are the same chart.

The two-pass handover is the spine of the file: pass 1 builds everything, stashes the origin symbol name in a hidden OBJ_LABEL called SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF (#define line 536) and the picked start in SSR_PICK_HANDOFF (#define line 556), arms g_switch_to, and the first OnTimer tick calls ChartSetSymbolPeriod, which reinitialises this same EA as pass 2 on the replay symbol.

Pass 2 identifies itself with SSRIsReplaySymbol(_Symbol) and must recover the origin from the stash: line 1903 `string origin = (on_replay ? stashed : (InpSymbol == "" ? _Symbol : InpSymbol));` - InpSymbol is NOT a fallback on the replay chart.

Cfg*() layer (lines 214-241): 14 accessors return the setup panel's value when g_setup_ready, else the input. g_setup_ready is set in exactly two places: the picker's START button (2518) and pass 2's unconditional CSSRSetupPanel::Restore of MQL5/Files/SSReplay/setup.ini (1948).

OnTimer guard ladder order: g_timer_ticks++ -> ReportSpreadOnce -> g_picking -> g_switching -> g_switch_to -> !g_ready -> shots/first -> delta+starvation cap -> play edge -> Pump -> flight -> publishers -> cadences (%5 charts, %5 trade lines, %25/%250 vitals, %50 leaks) -> reveal/review -> modal -> PollClicks -> 10fps Render.

Modal is computed once per timer pass (line 2888: session dialog OR range dialog OR reveal OR review) and gates BOTH PollClicks and Render - but RouteEvent's key path only withholds keys for the reveal and review cards, not for the two dialogs.

OnDeinit keeps the replay symbol, the streams and the charts on every reason except REASON_REMOVE/PROGRAM/CLOSE; it saves the named session and every stream's position whenever g_ready, on every reason.

Downstream clamps that make some inputs safe: SetTicksPerBar clamps <4 to 4 (Core/SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:106), SetWarmupBars clamps <0 to 0 (Core/SSR_ReplayController.mqh:662). InpPumpMs is clamped nowhere and reaches EventSetMillisecondTimer twice (1574, 3149).
No input is dead: every one of the 61 is read at least once. No input is range-checked anywhere in the file.
The watchdog in OnChartEvent (3145) re-arms the engine timer once if g_timer_ticks == 0 for >1500ms after ready - deliberately testing 'the timer never entered', not g_pumps == 0.

SSRPurgeChart(chart, keep) (Ui/SSR_Widgets.mqh:676) deletes EVERY object on the chart whose name starts with "SSR", keeping only the one name passed as `keep`. The host calls it as SSRPurgeChart(0, SSR_PICK_LINE) at OnInit line 1806.

findings.title: OnInit's object sweep deletes the handover stash before it is read, so the second pass of one-window mode can never find its origin symbol
findings.code:
SSRPurgeChart(0, SSR_PICK_LINE);
...
   string stashed = ReadStashedOrigin();          // line 1869
...
   if(ObjectFind(0, SSR_PICK_STASH) >= 0)         // line 1884
findings.claim: With the shipped defaults (InpOneChart=true), pass 1 stashes the origin in the chart object SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF and hands the chart to the replay symbol. Pass 2's OnInit sweeps that object away at line 1806, 63 lines before it reads it at 1869, so stashed=="", origin=="" at line 1903, the on_replay && origin=="" branch fires at 1911 and FailInit() returns INIT_FAILED. Because g_origin is "", FailInit's chart-restore branch (825: `if(g_on_replay_chart && g_origin != "")`) does nothing, so the user is left on a chart showing a custom replay symbol with no expert on it and no automatic way back - the exact outcome the FailInit comment (810-821) exists to prevent. The picked start (SSR_PICK_HANDOFF) and the failed-pass poison ("!"+origin) are destroyed by the same sweep, so neither the recovery path nor the picked window can survive the handover either.
findings.evidence: SSRPurgeChart (Ui/SSR_Widgets.mqh:676-694) enumerates ObjectsTotal(chart,-1,-1) and deletes every name where StringFind(nm,"SSR")==0 unless nm equals the single `keep` argument. Both handoff objects are named with that prefix: #define SSR_HANDOFF "SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF" (line 536) and #define SSR_PICK_STASH "SSR_PICK_HANDOFF" (line 556); keep is SSR_PICK_LINE ("SSR_PICK_LINE", Ui/SSR_Theme.mqh:508). Both are created on chart 0 (ObjectCreate(0, SSR_HANDOFF, ...) line 540; ObjectCreate(0, SSR_PICK_STASH, ...) line 2536) - the same chart the sweep runs on, and the same chart that becomes the replay chart. The sweep is the second statement of OnInit and is unconditional. git log -S confirms the call was moved into OnInit by commit f3f7ddb (v102), after the stash mechanism it breaks (v55): this is a regression, not an original design. The claim needs no assumption about whether objects survive ChartSetSymbolPeriod - the delete and the read are in the same pass of the same function.

findings.title: On the replay chart InpSymbol is ignored, so the recovery the failure message tells the user to perform cannot work
findings.claim: A user whose second pass lost the stash (which is every one-window run today, see host-expert-1) reads the printed advice, sets InpSymbol="EURUSD" and re-attaches to the replay chart. The conditional at 1903 takes the on_replay branch, so InpSymbol is never consulted; origin is "" again and OnInit fails with the identical message. The tool tells the user to do something it has made impossible, and the only real escape is to switch the chart back to a normal symbol by hand.
findings.evidence: The ternary at 1903-1904 uses `stashed` unconditionally when on_replay is true; InpSymbol appears only in the else branch. The guard at 1911 tests `origin == ""` after that assignment, and the message at 1915-1917 names InpSymbol as a remedy. A one-line change (on_replay ? (stashed != "" ? stashed : InpSymbol) : ...) would make the advice true and would also give host-expert-1 a manual workaround.

findings.title: Auto-play is suppressed on the pass that actually owns the replay chart: the guard tests one_chart_ok instead of "am I about to hand over"
findings.claim: In the default configuration (InpOneChart=true, InpAutoPlay=true) the replay never starts playing by itself. Pass 2 runs BuildSession with on_replay=true and one_chart_ok=true (OnInit line 1893 sets one_chart_ok=InpOneChart and the poison branch is the only thing that clears it), so `!one_chart_ok` is false, Play() is never called, and the log prints "auto-play waits for the handover - this pass has no chart to play on for more than a moment" on the pass that IS the final one and DOES have the replay chart. The user is left looking at a motionless chart - precisely the failure the comment block at 1696-1709 ("DROP IT AND IT WORKS") was written to remove. Auto-play still works when InpOneChart=false, because then one_chart_ok is false on the only pass there is.
findings.evidence: The intended condition is "this pass is about to hand its chart over", which this file expresses correctly twice elsewhere: line 1275 `g_replay_chart = (g_on_replay_chart ? ChartID() : (one_chart_ok ? 0 : ...))` and lines 1689-1694 `if(g_on_replay_chart) ... else if(one_chart_ok) ...`. Only `one_chart_ok && !g_on_replay_chart` identifies that pass; `!one_chart_ok` also excludes pass 2, where g_replay_chart == ChartID() (1275) and g_ready is true. Latent while host-expert-1 stands (pass 2 does not survive); it becomes the user-visible behaviour the moment host-expert-1 is fixed, and it is a defect in the condition regardless.

findings.title: The first-run card can never appear in one-window mode - same wrong guard as auto-play
findings.claim: With InpFirstCard=true and InpOneChart=true (both defaults) the onboarding card is shown on neither pass: pass 1 is excluded because one_chart_ok is true, and pass 2 is excluded by the same test because OnInit re-reads one_chart_ok = InpOneChart (1893). seen.txt is therefore never written either, so the card is not 'used up' - it simply never exists for any user who runs the default single-window mode. The comment at 1728-1735 says the file marker exists so the card cannot 'show on the pass with no replay chart and be gone on the pass that has one'; the guard beside it produces the second half of exactly that outcome.
findings.evidence: Identical mechanism to host-expert-3: `!one_chart_ok` is false on pass 2 as well as pass 1. The condition that would be right here is `!(one_chart_ok && !g_on_replay_chart)`, i.e. g_on_replay_chart || !one_chart_ok. g_panel_chart is non-zero on pass 2 (set to ChartID() at 1449), so that part of the guard is satisfied. Latent behind host-expert-1 in the same way.

findings.title: A random session does not survive the handover: pass 2 either re-rolls a new seed or drops randomness entirely, and can replay a different instrument under pass 1's symbol name
findings.claim: InpRandom=true, InpSeed="", InpOneChart=true. Pass 1 picks a window (and possibly a symbol out of InpAlsoSymbols), announces the seed in the log, seeds the custom symbol for that window and hands the chart over. Pass 2 runs BuildSession again and there are two outcomes, both wrong: (a) no setup.ini, so g_setup_ready is false and CfgRandom() is InpRandom=true -> SSRSeedFromText("")==0 -> CSSRRandomPicker::SetSeed(0) substitutes SSRPickSeed(), a brand new seed, so the session the user ends up in is a different window than the one pass 1 built and the seed printed on pass 1 reproduces nothing; if InpAlsoSymbols is non-empty the new pick can also be a different instrument, which is then replayed into the custom symbol adopted from pass 1 - a chart named EURUSD@.SSR1 carrying XAUUSD prices. (b) setup.ini exists from any earlier run, so g_setup_ready is true and CfgRandom() returns g_setup.random_start, which lines 1935-1947 never seed from InpRandom (Init() leaves it false), so randomness is silently switched off and win_start falls back to auto_start - the most recent InpReplayBars bars.
findings.evidence: SetSeed's substitution is explicit: `void SetSeed(const ulong s) { m_seed = (s == 0 ? SSRPickSeed() : s); ... }` (Data/SSR_RandomPicker.mqh:68-69) and SSRSeedFromText("") returns 0 (Common/SSR_Random.mqh:99-100). Nothing carries random_start/PickedStart across the handover: the pass-2 block at 1933-1948 assigns twelve fields from inputs and omits random_start and seed, whose Init() defaults are false and "" (Ui/SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:144-146). The symbol-mismatch consequence is reachable because BuildSession reassigns `origin` and g_origin from g_picker.PickedSymbol() (1027-1035) while the sink is pinned to the existing name by SetAdoptName(_Symbol) (1964); the sink itself flags the disagreement and adopts anyway (Mt5/SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:152-166). Latent behind host-expert-1.

findings.title: Pass 2 restores setup.ini unconditionally, so a run that never opened the setup form inherits an unrelated earlier run's balance, prop rules and session name and they overrule this run's inputs
findings.claim: Any configuration that skips the start picker still performs the handover: InpPickStart=false, or InpStart>0, or CfgRandom(), or a resumable session (the four conditions at 2025). On those runs pass 1 never opens the setup form and never writes setup.ini, so pass 1 builds from the inputs (g_setup_ready false). Pass 2 then reads whatever setup.ini is on disk from some earlier run and every Cfg*() switches to it. Concretely: a user with InpBalance=25000, InpProp=false, InpSession="" and a month-old setup.ini holding balance=10000, prop_on=1, session="demo" gets a pass-2 session with a 10,000 balance, a prop evaluation that judges and can fail them, and a session file named "demo" that is both resumed (win_start/win_end taken from that file at 1063-1070 and 1124) and overwritten in OnDeinit (2130-2141). Blind mode and the chart timeframe come from the same stale file. Nothing in the log says the values came from a file rather than from the inputs beyond one line that calls it 'carrying the setup across the handover'.
findings.evidence: CSSRSetupPanel::Restore (Ui/SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:1238-1260) only checks FileIsExist(SSR_SETUP_FILE) and overwrites every field it finds; it carries no run identity, no timestamp and no origin symbol. The only writer is the picker's START button (2520), which runs on a pass-1 path the four skip conditions bypass. The file's own comment at 1926-1931 states the rule it means to follow ('Only on the replay chart. A first pass reading the file would overrule inputs a user had deliberately set for THIS run') - the second pass overruling those same inputs is the same defect in the other direction. Latent behind host-expert-1.

findings.title: Keys are not withheld while the Sessions or Jump dialog is open: Space, Tab and the arrows drive the replay behind the dialog and the panel reprints over it
findings.claim: The user presses S to open the saved-sessions list and then presses Space (or Tab, or an arrow). CSSRSessionDialog::OnEvent returns false for anything that is not CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK, so the event falls through the two dialog blocks, past the reveal/review key guard (which only covers those two cards), into g_panel.OnEvent at 3228, which executes the command and calls Render(). The replay therefore starts running - or a virtual trade is opened by Tab - underneath a dialog the user is reading, and the Render() recreates every panel object on top of the dialog, which is the v102 z-order defect (creation order is the only z-order) coming back through the key path. Pressing 0 arms the session reset in the same way.
findings.evidence: Ui/SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:227-228 `if(m_mode == SSR_SD_CLOSED || id != CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK) return false;` - keydowns are never claimed. The same is true of the range dialog block at 3177. The panel acts on any key it owns: Ui/SSR_Panel.mqh:2854-2876 maps the key with SSRKeyToCommand, returns false only for the four commands Owns() excludes (SESSIONS/JUMP/REVIEW/REPLAY_FROM_HERE), and otherwise runs `Execute(c); Render(); return true;`. Space is TOGGLE and Tab is SSR_CMD_OPEN_LINES ('TAKE THE TRADE', Ui/SSR_Keys.mqh:165-167). The timer already computes exactly the right predicate one screen away - line 2888 `bool modal = (g_session_dlg.IsOpen() || g_dialog.IsOpen() || g_reveal.IsUp() || g_review.IsUp());` - and uses it to gate PollClicks and Render, but RouteEvent's keydown guard at 3217-3226 lists only the two cards.

findings.title: Replay and extra-timeframe chart windows are leaked on every re-init that is not a user removal
findings.claim: The header of this file says a timeframe change on the host chart 'rebuilds the session from scratch. The replay chart is unaffected'. It is worse than unaffected: OnDeinit closes no chart unless the user removed the EA, and CSSRChartManager::OpenChart always calls ChartOpen with no reuse, so the rebuild opens a fresh set of windows and orphans the old ones. Two-window mode (InpOneChart=false): each period change on the host chart leaks one replay window plus one window per entry in InpExtraTfs. One-window mode: pass 2 opens the InpExtraTfs layout (1300-1305, g_replay_chart != 0 there), and every later REASON_CHARTCHANGE or REASON_PARAMETERS on that chart opens the layout again. A user who changes the period three times with InpExtraTfs="M15,H1" ends with six stale windows nothing will ever close; once the registry passes SSR_MAX_CHARTS the newest ones also lose the follow policy (Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh Sync, m_untracked). The same path leaks a window when BuildSession returns false after opening the replay chart, because INIT_FAILED deinits with a reason that is not in the user_removed set.
findings.evidence: OnDeinit's only close site is inside `if(user_removed)` (2203, plus 2206 for the extra streams); REASON_CHARTCHANGE, REASON_PARAMETERS, REASON_RECOMPILE and REASON_INITFAILED all fall outside it, as the comment at 2115-2122 intends for the symbol but not for the windows. CSSRChartManager::OpenChart (Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh:204-215) is `long id = ChartOpen(m_symbol, tf); ... NoteOwned(id)` with no search for an existing chart on that symbol/period, and OpenLayout (229-242) just calls it per timeframe. The new pass's g_charts is a freshly constructed object, so the previous ids are no longer owned; CSSRLeakGuard only counts charts (Chart/SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:44-63), it never closes one.

findings.title: The one-shot spread diagnostic is consumed by the start-picker phase and then permanently suppressed for the real session
findings.claim: ReportSpreadOnce() is called as the second statement of OnTimer (2455), before the g_picking guard, and while the picker is up the timer runs at 200 ms (2072). A user who spends more than 100 seconds scrolling to choose a start - which is the entire purpose of the picker - reaches g_timer_ticks == 500 with the controller not yet loaded, so total == 0, the latch g_spread_reported is set to true and the log gets 'no bar has been replayed yet - press Play, or raise the speed, and this line will answer itself'. BuildSession resets g_timer_ticks (1577) but never resets g_spread_reported, so the line the comment block at 2213-2222 calls 'the one that says whether this history can show you a release at all' is never printed for that session.
findings.evidence: g_spread_reported is declared at 2222 and assigned only at 2263; no reset exists anywhere (grep shows two occurrences in the file). g_ctrl.SpreadBarsRecorded()/SpreadBarsFixed() return 0 before Load (Core/SSR_ReplayController.mqh:657-658 forward to the synthesizer's counters), and EffectiveFidelity() defaults to SYNTHETIC_TICK (Core/SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:69-73), so the 'no bar has been replayed yet' branch is the one taken. 500 ticks x 200 ms = 100 s; the comment beside the condition reasons about 'twenty seconds' at the 40 ms engine interval and did not account for the picker's slower timer.

findings.title: Extra streams and the session-settings block bypass the Cfg*() accessors, so the setup panel's spread and chart timeframe apply to the primary instrument only
findings.code:
g_ctrl2[built].SetSpreadPoints(InpSpreadPoints);
...
      g_charts2[built].OpenChart(InpChartTf);          // line 511
...
      out.spread_points = InpSpreadPoints;             // line 424
      out.chart_tf      = InpChartTf;                  // line 425
findings.claim: A user sets spread 8 points and chart timeframe M15 in the setup form and runs with InpAlsoSymbols="XAUUSD,GBPUSD". The primary stream gets CfgSpread()=8 and a CfgChartTf()=M15 chart (1145, 1275), while both extra instruments are loaded with InpSpreadPoints=20 and their windows open on InpChartTf=M5: three charts on one clock that disagree about both the execution assumption and the timeframe, with nothing in the log saying so. CollectSettings has the same bypass, so the settings block written into the session file records the inputs rather than the values the session actually ran with (blind, pause mode, slot, ticks per bar, spread, chart tf), which makes a saved session misdescribe itself.
findings.evidence: CfgSpread() (line 218) and CfgChartTf() (221) exist precisely so that 'every reader goes through these, so there is one place that knows which of the two wins - rather than thirty call sites each remembering, and one of them forgetting' (comment 206-213). OpenExtraStreams uses the raw inputs at 495 and 511 while the primary path uses the accessors at 1145 and 1275; CollectSettings uses them at 419-425. Impact is bounded because nothing reads the session file's settings block back at resume time - the host reads only ReadWindow and ReadSymbols (1066, 1325), and SSRSessionSettings/ReadSettings has a single caller, the T12 test (Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T12_Session.mq5:497).

findings.title: EnsureHistory's 60-second budget is computed with a ulong subtraction of a 32-bit tick count and breaks at the GetTickCount wrap
findings.claim: GetTickCount returns a uint that wraps to 0 about every 49.7 days of terminal uptime. Because t0 is a ulong, the uint returned by the second call is widened rather than wrapped, so any iteration taken after the wrap computes a value near 2^32 instead of a small elapsed time. If the wrap falls between t0 and the first loop test (a terminal left running for weeks, which is the normal case for a trading terminal) the loop body never executes: EnsureHistory returns whatever Bars() happened to hold, no download is attempted, and the session then reports 'SHORT ON HISTORY' (1130-1145) as if the broker were the limitation.
findings.evidence: The same pattern is written correctly elsewhere in this file with uint arithmetic - line 2894 `uint now_ms = GetTickCount(); if(!modal && now_ms - g_panel_paint >= 100)` and line 3145 `(GetTickCount() - g_ready_at_ms) > 1500` where g_ready_at_ms is uint (declared 345). Only t0 at 651 is widened to ulong. GetTickCount64() is the wrap-free primitive. Failure needs a 49.7-day-uptime coincidence, hence LOW, but the outcome is a silent no-op on the one code path whose whole job is fetching history.

findings.title: The history download gives up after ~1.8 s of no completed bars, which is shorter than an in-flight asynchronous download
findings.claim: The loop asks for history with CopyRates, sleeps 300 ms, and counts a 'stall' whenever Bars() has not grown. Six consecutive stalls - about 1.8 s plus the CopyRates calls - abandon the download and print a sentence that blames the broker ('Usually that is all the broker serves for this symbol'), even though the terminal may still be fetching the 60,000 M1 bars InpHistoryBars asks for over a slow link. The user then meets the SHORT ON HISTORY cascade at 1128-1145 and a window far smaller than they asked for, with a log line pointing them at the wrong cause. The stated 60-second budget at 653 is unreachable for anyone whose broker needs more than 1.8 s to deliver a first block. The comment itself says 'Two dead passes' while the code allows six, so the intended budget is not settled.
findings.evidence: Sleep(300) at 671, `if(++stalls >= 6)` at 681, stalls reset only on growth at 690. Nothing distinguishes 'no download is running' from 'a download is running and has not committed a bar yet' - there is no ResetLastError/GetLastError check on the CopyRates result and no SeriesInfoInteger(SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED) test. Whether MT5 commits a first block inside 1.8 s for a 60k-bar request cannot be determined from the source, and the author has never run this on a terminal, so this is a risk rather than a confirmed failure; the two supporting facts (the 1.8 s budget and the misattributing message) are confirmed from the code.

findings.title: The picker path rebuilds with InpOneChart, discarding the one_chart_ok poison OnInit had just read
findings.claim: OnInit computes one_chart_ok as a local (1893-1901): it starts as InpOneChart and is forced false when the stash carries the '!' poison written by a failed second pass. When the start picker is active, OnInit returns INIT_SUCCEEDED (2073) and the build happens later in OnTimer, where the poison is gone and InpOneChart is passed instead. A run that was told not to attempt the handover again therefore attempts it again, walking into the same wall the poison exists to avoid; the comment at 1262-1274 explains that testing the input instead of the flag at the other call site left a recovery run with no replay chart at all.
findings.evidence: one_chart_ok is a function-local in OnInit, never stored in a global, and the timer path at 2555 has no access to it. Reachability is narrow: the poison is only written when a second pass failed (825), and on such a recovery run the SSR_PICK_HANDOFF object usually still supplies g_pick_msc so the picker is skipped and the correct one_chart_ok reaches BuildSession at 2080. It is reachable when no pick stash is present (InpPickStart turned on after the fact, or the stash cleared by a REASON_REMOVE deinit at 2114 while the handoff survived). Low severity for that reason, but the discarded flag is unambiguous.

findings.title: The setup panel's drag handler can never fire, because mouse-move events are not enabled until the main panel is created
findings.claim: The setup window that accompanies the start picker is written to be dragged by its caption, and that is its only event-driven behaviour, but during the picking phase nothing has turned CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE on for the chart. CSSRSetupPanel::OnChartEvent returns immediately for every event id except CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE, so the host's forwarding call at 3110 always returns false and the window cannot be moved. Its buttons still work because the timer polls OBJPROP_STATE, so the failure is silent: a window that looks draggable and is not.
findings.evidence: The only writer of that chart property in the whole Include tree is the main panel: `ChartSetInteger(m_chart, CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE, true)` at Ui/SSR_Panel.mqh:324, inside Create, which the host calls at 1453 - i.e. after the picker has finished (grep -rn CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE returns only Ui/SSR_Panel.mqh:318, 324, 370). CSSRSetupPanel::OnChartEvent starts `if(!m_open || id != CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE) return false;` (Ui/SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:958-959). Line 370 of the panel restores the property to whatever it was before, so a previous session does not leave it enabled either.

findings.title: No bound check on InpPumpMs, which is handed straight to EventSetMillisecondTimer and to the starvation ceiling
findings.code:
EventSetMillisecondTimer(InpPumpMs);
...
   ulong ceiling = (ulong)MathMax(4 * InpPumpMs, 100);     // line 2754
...
      EventSetMillisecondTimer(InpPumpMs);                 // line 3149 (watchdog)
findings.claim: None of the 61 inputs is range-checked in this file. InpPumpMs is the one with no downstream clamp: a user who types 0 or a negative value (the field is a plain int labelled 'Engine tick interval (ms)') gets that value passed to EventSetMillisecondTimer at 1574, and the OnChartEvent watchdog re-arms the timer with the same value at 3149, so a rejected interval cannot be recovered from. The session would sit at READY with g_ready true, the panel alive through OnChartEvent, and no pump - which is exactly the failure signature ('the panel felt alive while nothing moved') the comment at 1815-1827 says cost five releases to diagnose. Nothing in the log names the input as the cause, and FlightGuard cannot fire because OnTimer never enters.
findings.evidence: grep for validation in OnInit finds none: the only guards are semantic (win_start >= win_end at 1132, origin == "" at 1911). The two inputs that could do comparable damage are clamped downstream - SetTicksPerBar raises anything below 4 to 4 (Core/SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:106) and SetWarmupBars floors negatives at 0 (Core/SSR_ReplayController.mqh:662) - InpPumpMs is clamped nowhere (its four sites are 1557, 1574, 2754, 3149). Whether EventSetMillisecondTimer(0) is rejected outright or silently coerced to the terminal's ~16 ms floor cannot be established from this source and the author has never run it on a terminal, hence POTENTIAL_RISK; the absence of any validation and the watchdog re-arming with the same unvalidated value are confirmed from the code.

performance_notes: Timer budget: OnTimer runs at InpPumpMs (default 40 ms, 25 Hz) and every cadence is derived from a single counter g_slow_tick (2806). %5 (200 ms): publisher Publish, g_charts.Sync, blind re-apply, g_charts.Redraw, extras Sync, and the trade-line position sweep. %25 playing / %250 paused: PrintVitals. %50 (2 s): ScanLeaks plus feeding the measured seed rate to the catalogue. Panel Render is separately throttled to 10 Hz by wall clock (2894-2897) and suppressed entirely while modal.

The trade-line sweep (2749-2793) is the only cadence whose cost grows with the session: it walks g_acct.Total() every 200 ms, calls DrawPosition/DrawClosed per row and ends in EndPositions (a full horizontal-line sweep plus ChartRedraw). With InpTradeHistory=true every closed trade stays in the loop for the rest of the session at one ObjectFind per pass. The comment at 2755-2759 acknowledges this and picked 5 pumps as the compromise.

Starvation instrument (2744-2758): delta is capped at MathMax(4*InpPumpMs,100) ms and the excess is DROPPED, never repaid, with g_starved counted and surfaced in the vitals LATE line (2353-2361). The comment quotes a real measurement behind the change: 73 minutes of market crossed in 52 s of wall clock at a 50x setting (an effective 84x) when the old one-second ceiling repaid stalls.

PrintVitals (2311) is the heaviest diagnostic: per managed chart it issues three ChartGetInteger calls plus ChartSymbol/ChartPeriod, and once per line Bars() and SeriesInfoInteger on the replay symbol. At most once a second while playing, once every 10 s while paused, and the first 10 lines always.

Blocking calls on the init path: EnsureHistory can occupy up to 60 s of OnInit with 300 ms sleeps (623-696), and ReplayBarsReady can sleep up to 1 s (596-620) on the handover path only. Both are bounded and logged, but both run inside OnInit/OnTimer, so the EA is unresponsive for their duration.
One-off O(n*m) scan at 1604-1636: for every symbol in SymbolsTotal(false) that looks like a replay symbol it walks ChartFirst/ChartNext to decide live-vs-leftover. Runs once per build, after g_ready.
ReportSpreadOnce is invoked on every timer tick before any guard (2455) but returns on a boolean latch after the first report, so its steady-state cost is one comparison.
test_gaps: Nothing tests the two-pass handover round trip - the write of SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF/SSR_PICK_HANDOFF on pass 1 and their read on pass 2 - which is where the CRITICAL defect lives. All 21 static audits pass over it because no rule relates the sweep's prefix to the handoff object names. An audit A22 of the form 'no object whose name matches the SSRPurgeChart prefix may be used as cross-init storage' (or simply renaming the two handoff objects out of the swept namespace) would have caught host-expert-1 statically.

No test can observe pass 2 at all, because the test harness is a set of Scripts and a script cannot host an EA re-initialisation. Every pass-2 behaviour is therefore unverified: origin recovery, setup.ini inheritance, random-window inheritance, auto-play, the first-run card, symbol adoption.

No test asserts the modal key contract. A check that 'while g_session_dlg.IsOpen() or g_dialog.IsOpen(), no CHARTEVENT_KEYDOWN reaches CSSRPanel::OnEvent' would have caught host-expert-7, and the symmetric assertion for clicks/repaint already exists as a single computed predicate one screen away (2888).

No chart-count conservation test across re-init: nothing asserts that the number of open charts on the replay symbol after a REASON_CHARTCHANGE rebuild equals the number before (host-expert-8). CSSRLeakGuard already gathers the number that would make this assertion trivial.

The host's condition guards are untested as a family. Three sites choose between g_on_replay_chart, one_chart_ok and InpOneChart (1275, 1689, 1710/1736) and two of them are wrong; a table-driven test over the three (pass, one_chart_ok, on_replay) combinations asserting 'has a replay chart', 'may auto-play', 'may show the card' and 'must arm the handover' would pin all four.

EnsureHistory has no seam - it calls Bars/CopyRates/SeriesInfoInteger on a live broker symbol - so its timeout, stall budget and the GetTickCount wrap (host-expert-11, host-expert-12) cannot be exercised. Passing a small interface, or at minimum making the 60000/6/300 constants named and injectable, would make the policy testable.

The g_picking path (OnTimer 2464-2568) has no coverage: the 200 ms timer, the 63-character info line, the START/LINE TO VIEW latches, the setup.ini write and the direct BuildSession call. A long-picking test (>100 s of simulated ticks) would also have exposed the consumed spread diagnostic (host-expert-9).

No audit asserts the Cfg*() invariant. A static rule that Inp(Balance|RiskPercent|SpreadPoints|StartSpeed|ChartTf|ExtraTfs|Blind|Session|Prop|PropTarget|PropDaily|PropTotal|Random|Seed) may appear only inside the Cfg accessor block and the pass-2 seeding block would flag lines 419-425, 495 and 511 (host-expert-10).

No input-bounds test: nothing runs the host with InpPumpMs=0, InpReplayBars=0 or InpWarmupBars greater than the available history and asserts that OnInit refuses with a message naming the input (host-expert-15).

key_facts: Publish path: CSSRReplayController::EmitWindow has two shapes. The bar-driven fidelities (SYNTHETIC_TICK, BAR) publish per M1 bar - PublishBar(ClipBar(bar)) at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:506 immediately followed by PublishSegment(that bar's ticks) at :507. The FULL_TICK branch calls PublishTicks(m_ticks, n) once for the whole window at :366 and returns at :369 without ever calling PublishBar. grep confirms PublishBar has exactly one call site (:506), inside the bar path.

SSR_FIDELITY_FULL_TICK is not exotic: SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1153 sets it whenever range.has_ticks is true, and has_ticks is probed by CopyTicksRange over the most recent day of history (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:139). For any broker holding forex tick history it is the default path.

Observer registration order (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1176-1247): g_acct, g_stats, [g_prop], g_autopause, g_shots, g_cal, g_session, g_view, g_strategies. The trading engine therefore prices every tick of a batch before any strategy hook runs, so a strategy's market order fills at the LAST tick of the batch.

CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks iterates every tick in the batch (m_bid/m_ask/m_now_msc per tick, then AccrueSwap/CheckPendings/CheckStops/CheckStopout), so the account is batch-size independent. CSSRStrategyHost::OnTicks collapses the batch to ticks[count-1] (SSR_StrategyHost.mqh:184). The asymmetry is the root of the strategy-side timing findings.

CSSRMarketView is the only holder of bars a strategy can read; it is fed exclusively by OnBarContext (SSR_MarketView.mqh:173) plus the host-driven Prime() (:389). SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2797 primes it only while M1Count()==0, so once primed it is never refreshed except by OnBarContext.

No OrderSend/CTrade/PositionClose exists on any path reachable from CSSRStrategyBroker or CSSRPublisher::Execute; both route into CSSRTradingEngine (Open/OpenWithRisk/Close/CloseAll), and both tag their positions (the strategy's Name(), or the literal "external").

Permission enforcement is on the replay side only (SSR_Publisher.mqh:262-267). The client's identical check (SSR_Client.mqh:178-188) is explicitly a courtesy for error text. Defaults: READ always, CONTROL and TRADE off unless the replay side turned them on.

The wire carries no data verb and no price: the only forward-looking field published is end_msc (the window boundary). There is no path by which a client can ask for a bar, a tick or a price at a time.

RefStrategy's Available(tf) < lookback+2 gate is exactly right for what Extremes(tf,2,lookback) needs: proceeding requires groups >= lookback+3, which is the number Extremes must see to prove the last group complete. There is no off-by-one there.

SSRBarOpenMsc floors on the epoch, and MqlRates.time is broker server time, so the view's aggregation boundaries agree with MT5's own bars for every timeframe SSRIsSupportedTimeframe admits (M1..H12, D1; W1/MN1 are refused and counted).

The class report's coupling to the journal is exact and correct: '# SS Replay journal' marker, window_start/window_end as %I64d milliseconds, session_key, ambiguous_trades as 'N (P%)', open_time written by SSRFormatMsc as 'YYYY.MM.DD HH:MM:SS' and read back by StringToTime, r written empty (never zero) when the trade had no stop, and both sides open with FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI so the encodings match on the CSV leg.

findings.title: In FULL_TICK fidelity the market view is never fed bars, so a strategy reads a snapshot frozen at the first pump
findings.claim: With InpRefStrategy=true on any symbol whose history carries ticks (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1153 then selects SSR_FIDELITY_FULL_TICK), CSSRMarketView receives no OnBarContext for the whole session. PrimeView fires once on the first pump, fills the buffer with M1 bars ending at that instant, and because SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2797 only primes while M1Count()==0 it never refreshes. An hour into the replay CSSRRefBreakout::OnBar still reads Bar(tf,1) and HighestHigh/LowestLow from bars an hour old while comparing them against a live ctx.market.Bid(), so it either refuses every bar with "stop would be the wrong side of price" or opens a risk-sized trade whose stop is hundreds of points away from the real market.
findings.evidence: CSSRMarketView's only source of bars is OnBarContext (this line) and Prime(). In SSR_ReplayController.mqh the FULL_TICK branch calls PublishTicks(m_ticks, n) at line 366 and returns at line 369 without ever calling PublishBar; grep shows PublishBar has exactly one call site, line 506, inside the bar-driven branch that FULL_TICK has already returned from. So m_count only ever changes through Prime(). SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2797 gates PrimeView on g_view.M1Count()==0, which becomes false after the first successful prime and never returns to 0 unless a rewind trims every bar. The view's m_now_msc, m_bid and m_ask keep advancing through OnTicks/OnClock, so Now()/Bid()/Ask() are live while every bar accessor is stale - the strategy has no way to detect the divergence, because Available() still reports the frozen groups.

findings.title: OnBar is detected from the last tick of a published batch, so its firing point and the resulting fill price are functions of wall-clock pump boundaries
findings.claim: SSR_IStrategy.mqh:20-24 promises "the same session replays to the same trades". It does not hold. The replay clock advances by the wall delta, so the replay instant a pump ends at depends on CPU load; the host only inspects the batch's last tick, so the moment inside the new bar at which OnBar fires - and therefore the ctx.market.Bid()/Ask() the strategy sees and the price CSSRTradingEngine fills its order at - moves with that boundary. Replay the same window twice on a loaded machine and CSSRRefBreakout takes measurably different entries, and its sl >= Bid() gate flips on the borderline cases. In FULL_TICK the same collapse skips bar closes outright: PublishTicks is called once per window, so a batch spanning two M15 boundaries (40 s of replay per 40 ms beat at the ladder's 1000x top stop, more after any timer stall) fires OnBar once instead of twice and the intervening bar close is never delivered.
findings.evidence: The host reads only ticks[count-1] and derives bar_open from it; every tick before the last in the batch is invisible to the bar-close test. Contrast CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks, which loops over all count ticks updating m_bid/m_ask/m_now_msc and calling CheckStops per tick - the account is therefore batch-size independent and deterministic, while the strategy layer is not. In the bar-driven path the batch is one M1 bar's ticks (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:506-507), and whether that bar arrives whole or clipped mid-minute depends on where the pump's `hi` landed (ClipBar, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:159). In the FULL_TICK path the batch is the entire window (line 366), so the number of bar boundaries inside one batch is unbounded and m_last_bar jumps over the ones in between, silently.

findings.title: OnTick fires once per published batch, not once per tick, so the documented intrabar-management use is unreachable and TickCalls() under-reports
findings.claim: With the default InpTicksPerBar=8 and SYNTHETIC_TICK, a strategy wanting to trail a stop intrabar gets exactly one OnTick per M1 bar and the only price it can read (ctx.market.Bid()) is that bar's close - the seven intermediate synthesised prices, including the bar's high and low, are never visible to it. A trailing stop written in OnTick therefore behaves as if it were written in OnBar, and the intrabar excursion it exists to capture is invisible. In BAR fidelity there is one tick per bar so the distinction vanishes; in FULL_TICK there is one OnTick per pump covering possibly thousands of real ticks. Separately, TickCalls() reports batches (~1 per M1 bar) while its name and ToString() ("ticks=%I64d") present it as a tick count, under-reporting by the ticks-per-bar factor.
findings.evidence: The hook takes no parameters, so the only tick data a strategy can reach is CSSRMarketView's m_bid/m_ask, which SSR_MarketView.mqh:191-198 sets from ticks[count-1] alone - the rest of the batch is discarded on arrival. CSSRStrategyHost::OnTicks calls m_strat[i].OnTick() once per OnTicks invocation (line 210) and increments m_tick_calls once (line 209). SSR_ReplayController.mqh:506-507 publishes one segment per M1 bar, whose length is m_synth.TicksForBar(fid) = InpTicksPerBar, so one OnTick per 8 ticks at the default. TickSynthesizer places those ticks across the whole minute (base_msc + i*59999/(n-1)) with the last pinned to the bar close, so the high and low genuinely exist in the batch and are genuinely dropped before the strategy is asked.
