findings.title: The per-strategy RNG stream is seeded once at registration and is never re-seeded or rewound, so a strategy that uses it is not reproducible across a step-back
findings.code: m_ctx[k].rng.Seed(m_seed ^ NameHash(s.Name()));
findings.claim: SSR_IStrategy.mqh:20-24 states the strategy's randomness is provided by the host specifically so that "the same session replays to the same trades", and offers ctx.rng in place of MathRand() for that reason. But rng state is mutated by every draw and is never restored: a user who presses the left arrow (step back one candle) or jumps back to a bookmark replays the same minutes with the RNG stream already advanced, so a strategy that draws from it takes different decisions the second time through the same bars. The strategy cannot repair this itself - the host never tells it the seed, so it has no value to pass to ctx.rng.Seed(). The same applies to a stream advanced before a snapshot restore.
findings.evidence: This is the only Seed() call in the host, and it runs inside Add(). CSSRStrategyHost::OnSessionStart (lines 160-169) resets m_last_bar[] and re-Attaches each broker but does not touch m_ctx[i].rng; CSSRStrategyHost::OnRewind (lines 214-222) resets m_last_bar[i] and forwards OnRewind to the strategy but likewise leaves the RNG state alone. SSR_ReplayController.mqh broadcasts OnRewind at lines 1240, 1286, 1644 and 1669 (step back, reset, jump, snapshot restore) and OnSessionStart only at line 837 (Load), which the EA calls once. The seed is held privately in m_seed with no accessor, and CSSRStrategyContext exposes rng but not the seed, so a strategy has no way to re-derive m_seed ^ NameHash(name).

findings.title: CSSRMarketView::IsSynthetic() can never return false, so the honesty instrument it exists to be is dead
findings.code: bool              IsSynthetic(void) { return m_synthetic; }
findings.claim: m_synthetic is initialised true and can only ever be assigned true, so ctx.IsSynthetic() is a constant. CSSRRefBreakout::Status() therefore always appends "  [intrabar order assumed]", including on a FULL_TICK session replaying the broker's real ticks, and any strategy that branches on ctx.IsSynthetic() to decide whether its intrabar logic is trustworthy takes the pessimistic branch unconditionally. The fault direction is safe (it never claims real ticks it does not have), but the documented distinction at SSR_MarketView.mqh:419-426 is not actually being reported.
findings.evidence: m_synthetic is set true in the constructor (line 151) and assigned in exactly one place, OnBarContext (line 175). Its only production caller is PublishBar at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:506, which passes `fid != SSR_FIDELITY_FULL_TICK`. That line is only reachable after the FULL_TICK branch has already returned (line 369) or degraded fid via m_fidelity.Decide() to SYNTHETIC_TICK because the source had no tick provider - in both cases fid != FULL_TICK holds, so the argument is always true. OnSessionStart (lines 159-171) does not reset m_synthetic either, so even a hypothetical false would persist across sessions.

findings.title: Prime() and OnRewind() trim on bar-open granularity, so the newest retained bar can hold prices from after the clock
findings.claim: The test is on the bar's OPEN time, so when now_msc falls inside a minute (or exactly on its open) the whole M1 bar for that minute is admitted, high, low and close included - up to 60 seconds of prices the replay has not reached. The header at lines 386-388 claims this method "TRIMS to" now_msc. After a jump the contaminated bar is shift 0 on M1 and part of the shift-0 group on any higher timeframe, so Extremes(tf,0,n) and Bar(tf,0) return future-contaminated extremes. OnRewind has the identical property: the bar containing msc is kept with the full minute it had before the rewind.
findings.evidence: SSRToMsc(bars[i].time) is the bar's open instant, and the comparison is `> now_msc`, so a bar opening at exactly now_msc is taken whole; MqlRates carries no intrabar detail that could be clipped here. OnRewind (lines 204-214) uses the same `<= msc` test on bar open times. Core does clip correctly on the live path (ClipBar, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:150-309), and in the bar-driven fidelities the next pump republishes that same minute clipped, which OnBarContext's time-match branch (lines 180-184) overwrites in place - and because PrimeView runs after g_group.Pump() in OnTimer (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2788 then 2797), that overwrite happens before the next strategy hook. So the exposure is confined to FULL_TICK, where no OnBarContext ever arrives to correct it and the contaminated bar remains the newest bar for the rest of the session.

findings.title: The publisher rejects a command whose sequence equals the last one it executed, so a restarted client has one command silently dropped and reported as a timeout
findings.claim: CSSRClient::m_seq starts at 0 in the constructor and only ever increments, while the publisher remembers m_last_seq across client lifetimes. Scenario: a client indicator sends three commands (seq 1,2,3) so m_last_seq is 3; the user changes the chart timeframe, which reloads the indicator and resets m_seq to 0. The next Pause is seq 1 (executed), Play is seq 2 (executed), Step is seq 3 - equal to m_last_seq, so Poll() returns false without executing, without writing cmd.ack and without writing cmd.rc. The client spins the full 500 ms and reports SSR_RC_REFUSED with "the replay session did not answer within 500ms", which is the wrong diagnosis for a command that was rejected as a duplicate. The same collision occurs immediately for a second client sharing the slot.
findings.evidence: The guard is a plain equality against the last executed sequence, not a monotonic comparison and not a comparison against the published cmd.ack; m_last_seq is only reset by Begin() (line 138), which runs on the replay side, never on client restart. CSSRClient initialises m_seq to 0 (SSR_Client.mqh:46), increments it at line 192, and Refresh() (lines 81-131) never reads cmd.ack, so a fresh client has no way to learn where the publisher's counter already is. When Poll() returns early, nothing is written to cmd.ack or cmd.rc, so the client's wait loop at lines 202-213 can only fall out on the timeout branch at 215-218.

findings.title: The class report declares UTF-8 and is written with FILE_ANSI, so non-ASCII student, symbol and session names come out as mojibake
findings.code: int h = FileOpen(out_path, FILE_WRITE | FILE_TXT | FILE_ANSI | FILE_SHARE_READ);
findings.claim: SSRWriteReportHead emits <meta charset="utf-8"> but every FileWriteString on this handle goes through the ANSI conversion, so a Persian student name - the expected case for this academy, which ships a full fa.txt translation - is written as Windows-1256 bytes or as '?' placeholders and the browser, told the file is UTF-8, renders it as replacement characters. The names come from the CSV file names (Scan, lines 311-315) and from the journal's session and symbol headers, and they are exactly the fields the report exists to put beside each other: a coach opens class-report.html and cannot tell which row is which student.
findings.evidence: This is the handle every FileWriteString in Write() uses, and SSR_ReportStyle.mqh:21 writes the charset declaration into it: "<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset=\"utf-8\">". FILE_ANSI makes MQL5 convert each Unicode string to the system ANSI codepage on write - one byte per character - which is the same trap the project already documents for the READ direction (overview lesson 5) and already solved for the language file with FILE_BIN + CharArrayToString(..., CP_UTF8) at SSR_Strings.mqh:686. grep shows CP_UTF8 appears nowhere in the Report layer, so no path writes UTF-8. The names reaching the page are Html(m_s[i].name) at lines 561, 618 and 650, and Html(sym)/Html(sess) at line 521.

findings.title: The class KPI row, the ranking sort and the bar scale all include students who ran a different session, which is the comparison the file says it refuses to make
findings.claim: Twenty students run session key K and one file from last week's easier window is dropped into the folder with net +5000. The page then reports "Best +5000.00" in the KPI row, shifts "Median result" and "Trades between them" by that file, scales every diverging bar in the league table against peak = 5000 so the twenty comparable students' bars shrink, and places the outsider at the top of a table sorted purely on net_profit with only a small "(different session)" label beside the name. The header at lines 19-23 states the class report "REFUSES TO RANK PEOPLE WHO RAN DIFFERENT SESSIONS" because "a league table across two different windows is not a comparison, it is a mistake with a heading on it" - the label is the only thing implementing that refusal, and it does not reach any of the aggregate numbers.
findings.evidence: The filter in this loop is `!m_s[i].parsed`, never a key test, so best, worst and total_trades span every readable file. MedianNet() (lines 373-396) filters on parsed only. peak (lines 597-600) filters on parsed only. Rank() (line 350) returns net_profit with no key term, and the insertion sort at lines 337-344 orders on Rank alone. m_key and m_key_agree are computed at lines 324-334 and are then used only for the caveat (475-481), the odd_row label in the strip (558-564), the "(different session)" span in the table (619) and Axis() (406-412) - never to exclude a row from an aggregate.

findings.title: A pre-v76 export keeps parsed=true, so its recorded reason is never rendered and the caveat points the coach at marks that are never drawn
findings.claim: A coach collects twenty journals exported before v76 (none carries session_key). Every file parses, so m_key stays "" and m_key_agree stays 0. The page then prints "Ran this session 0" in the KPI row and the caveat "0 of the 20 readable files ran the same session. The rest are marked below and are NOT comparable with the others" - but odd_row and odd are both `m_key != "" && ...`, so with m_key == "" nothing is marked anywhere, and the one string that explains why (the "exported before v76" problem) is written to out.problem and then never rendered, because the only place problem is printed is the unreadable-files table guarded by !parsed. The coach is told to look for markings that do not exist and is given no way to find out that the files simply predate the key.
findings.evidence: parsed is set true on the very next line after problem, so the file counts toward `readable` (lines 450-452). The caveat at 475-481 fires whenever m_key_agree < readable, which 0 < 20 satisfies. odd_row at line 558 and odd at line 606 are both conditioned on m_key != "", which is false here. problem is only emitted at lines 650-652, inside `if(!m_s[i].parsed)`. The companion script has the same gap: SSR_ClassReport.mq5 prints s.problem only in its `if(!s.parsed)` branch, so the reason does not even reach the Experts log.

findings.title: CSSRClient::Send spins without yielding, so a client sharing a chart thread with the replay EA can never be acknowledged
findings.claim: The acknowledgement can only be written by CSSRPublisher::Poll(), which runs from the replay EA's OnTimer (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2803). MQL5 runs every program attached to one chart in that chart's single thread, and the loop body contains no Sleep, no EventChartCustom yield and no return to the terminal. A client indicator attached to the replay chart - which after pass 2 is the same chart the EA is on (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1260-1261) - therefore holds the thread for the whole timeout while the EA's OnTimer cannot run, so cmd.ack is never written and every Play/Pause/Step/Buy returns SSR_RC_REFUSED with "the replay session did not answer within 500ms" after burning a core for half a second. A client on its own chart is unaffected.
findings.evidence: The loop is a bare spin over GlobalVariableGet with only the ack test inside it; the comment at lines 211-212 acknowledges Sleep is unavailable and accepts the spin. The write the loop waits for happens in CSSRPublisher::Poll (SSR_Publisher.mqh:241-242), and the EA calls Poll only from OnTimer. The single-thread-per-chart execution model is a property of the MQL5 runtime, not of this source, so this is marked POTENTIAL_RISK - the code and the call graph are confirmed, the scheduling consequence is inferred and needs a terminal to observe. T14 never exercises it: it drives pub.Poll() by hand from the same script.

findings.title: SetSlot is unbounded while Discover only scans 1..SSR_MAX_SLOTS, so extra-stream publishers can be invisible to clients or collide with a second session
findings.code: void              SetSlot(const int slot)     { m_slot = slot; }
findings.claim: The EA gives each extra stream its own publisher on InpSlot+1+i (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1396). With InpSlot=8 and three extra symbols those land on slots 9, 10 and 11, and CSSRClient::Discover only scans 1..SSR_MAX_SLOTS (8), so those sessions publish to names no conforming client will ever look at - and Withdraw/Begin still work, so nothing reports the problem. Conversely, a user running InpSlot=1 with three extra symbols occupies slots 1..4, so a second replay started at InpSlot=2 overwrites the first session's stream-2 variables: two sessions then fight over one namespace, which is precisely what SSR_Contract.mqh:47-49 says slots exist to prevent.
findings.evidence: SetSlot accepts any int with no range check and no error path; SSRGvName (SSR_Contract.mqh:124-127) happily builds "SSR.11.now". CSSRClient::Discover loops `for(int s = 1; s <= SSR_MAX_SLOTS; s++)` (SSR_Client.mqh:64), and SSR_MAX_SLOTS is 8 (SSR_Contract.mqh:156). Nothing in the contract reserves a range for a session's extra streams or lets a publisher claim more than one slot atomically, and Begin() does not check whether the slot is already occupied by a live heartbeat.

findings.title: Group() returns shift 0 with a wrong open and an un-aggregated spread when the group began before the buffer did
findings.claim: When the walk runs off the oldest bar in the buffer while still inside the requested group, shift 0 is returned as success. Its high, low and close are right, but out.open is the open of the oldest M1 bar the buffer happens to hold rather than the group's true open, and no refusal is counted. A strategy on H4 immediately after a session start (or after MakeRoom dropped the oldest half mid-session) reads Open(PERIOD_H4, 0) and gets a number that is silently not the H4 open, with IsForming() offering no way to distinguish "still growing" from "beginning missing". Every other partial group in this class is refused outright for exactly this reason (lines 132-135 spell out the argument).
findings.evidence: out.open is overwritten on every backward step inside the group (line 125), so when the loop terminates by exhausting the buffer rather than by crossing a group boundary, the last write came from m_m1[0] - not from the group's first bar. The shift==0 early return skips both the m_refusals++ and the false that the shift>0 case gets. out.spread has the same shape: it is copied once from the group's newest M1 bar at line 110 and never aggregated, so it describes one minute rather than the group. Available() does count such a group (it returns 1 when groups==1), so a strategy checking availability first is not protected.

findings.title: Html() escapes four of the five characters its own comment names, and SSRWriteReportHead interpolates its title unescaped
findings.claim: The apostrophe is missing. Today that is harmless: every attribute this file writes is double-quoted, and Html() output only ever lands in element text content, so a student named O'Brien.csv renders correctly. It is worth closing anyway because the comment asserts five and the next attribute written with single quotes turns a file name into markup. The ordering is correct (& first), so adding ' is a one-line change. Separately, SSR_ReportStyle.mqh:23 splices its title parameter straight into <title> with no escaping; both call sites pass literals, so nothing is wrong now, but the function is the shared skin two documents use and a session name would be the natural thing to pass next.
findings.evidence: Only four StringReplace calls follow the comment. Grepping the generated markup in Write() shows attributes written as class=\"...\", style=\"...\" and title=\"...\" throughout - no single-quoted attribute exists - and the only attribute that receives interpolated data is title=\"%s\" at line 571, fed by SSRFormatMsc, which produces digits and dots. SSR_ReportStyle.mqh:23 is "<title>" + title + "</title>".

findings.title: SSR_CMD_SPEED reports success for a value the clock silently rewrote
findings.claim: Every other command reports what the engine actually did. Speed does not: a client sending 0 or a negative x100 gets SSR_RC_OK while CSSRReplayClock::SetSpeedX100 clamps it to 1 (0.01x), and a client sending 5,000,000 also gets OK while the ladder's own top stop is SSR_SPEED_MAX = 100000 (1000x). A client that reads back SSR_GV_SPEED will notice; one that trusts the OK will show a speed the replay is not running at. Returning REFUSED for a value outside 1..SSR_SPEED_MAX, or re-reading m_group.SpeedX100() before answering, would make the verb behave like the rest.
findings.evidence: The case returns a constant OK with no inspection of a1 and no bounds test. SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:76-80 is `speed_x100 = (s < 1 ? 1 : s);` with no upper bound. SSR_Types.mqh:131 defines SSR_SPEED_MAX = 100000 and the ladder's stop 19 (SSR_Types.mqh:298) is that value, so the contract exposes a range the UI does not. Contrast SSR_CMD_STEP and SSR_CMD_JUMP, which both propagate the engine's bool.

performance_notes: CSSRMarketView::Group, Extremes and Available are each a full backward walk of the M1 buffer - up to SSR_VIEW_M1_BARS = 4096 MqlRates reads per call. Group's cost is therefore independent of shift, so the per-accessor convenience wrappers are expensive: Open/High/Low/Close/Time each call Bar(), so a strategy reading four prices of one bar performs four 4096-element walks. A Bar()-then-read pattern is one walk.

HighestHigh and LowestLow each call Extremes separately, so asking for both (which is the natural range query, and exactly what CSSRRefBreakout does at lines 102-103) costs two full walks where Extremes already computes both in one. Extremes is public, so the ref strategy could call it directly; the current shape doubles the work on every OnBar.

The FULL_TICK branch of CSSRReplayController::EmitWindow is not subject to the pump budget: m_budget.MaxBars() is applied only on the bar-driven path (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:398-404). A large owed window in FULL_TICK reads and emits every real tick in one timer beat, which is the hot path most likely to stall the terminal and - via the wall-delta clock - the mechanism that widens the tick batches behind finding 2.

CSSRPublisher::Publish performs 16-17 GlobalVariableSet calls per invocation. The EA calls it every fifth timer beat (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2809), so about 5 times a second at InpPumpMs=40, roughly 85 terminal-global writes per second, plus one more publisher per extra stream. CSSRPublisher::Poll adds one GlobalVariableGet per beat when idle (25/s) and five when a command is pending. Terminal globals are a process-wide locked map; this is the subsystem's steady-state cost and it is not measured by any spike in the repo.

CSSRClient::Send's wait is a bare spin on GlobalVariableGet with no yield (SSR_Client.mqh:202-213), so a command that is not acknowledged costs the full timeout_ms at 100% of one core. With the default 500 ms and a publisher polling once per 40 ms beat the normal case is short, but every failure case - wrong permission on the replay side, duplicate sequence (finding 7), paused EA - costs the whole budget.

CSSRClassReport::ReadOne calls ArrayResize twice per trade row (lines 263-264) with no reserve, up to SSR_CLASS_TRADES = 400 rows per student - about 800 resizes per file and 51,000 for a full 64-student folder. Pre-sizing both arrays to SSR_CLASS_TRADES once in Init would remove all of it.

CSSRClassReport::Write emits one FileWriteString per entry mark (line 570), so a full class is up to 64 x 400 = 25,600 separate writes to the HTML handle. The key-agreement pass is O(n^2) string comparisons over at most 64 students (4,096), which is negligible by comparison.
CSSRStrategyHost::OnTicks is O(strategies) per published batch with no allocation, so the host itself is not a hot path; the cost lives entirely in whatever the strategy asks the view for.
test_gaps: No test ever runs a strategy under SSR_FIDELITY_FULL_TICK. Both strategy suites pin SSR_FIDELITY_SYNTHETIC_TICK explicitly (SSR_T13_Strategy.mq5:315 and :376), yet SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1153 selects FULL_TICK whenever the broker has tick history. Findings 1, 2, 5 and 6 all live in that untested branch.

No test registers a strategy on PERIOD_M1. T13 uses PERIOD_M5 (line 319) and PERIOD_M15 (line 448), so the case where the strategy's timeframe equals the publish granularity - and shift 0 is therefore a bar that has already fully played - is never exercised.

There is no determinism test at all. Nothing replays one window twice with different pump deltas and asserts that the same strategy produced the same tickets, which is the only way finding 2 would surface. T13 pumps a fixed ctrl.Pump(1000) in a loop, which is exactly the batching the defect is invisible under.
ctx.rng is never used by any test strategy and never checked across a rewind, so the reproducibility guarantee that SSR_IStrategy.mqh:20-24 makes for randomness has no coverage.

T14 uses a single long-lived CSSRClient, so the publisher's sequence-equality rejection (finding 7) cannot appear. There is no test that constructs a second client against a live publisher, or reconstructs one after commands have already been executed.

No test covers a slot outside 1..SSR_MAX_SLOTS, nor two publishers whose slot ranges overlap (the InpSlot + extra-streams allocation), so the namespacing the contract claims is only checked for two hand-picked non-colliding slots (T14:96-98).
No test writes a class report containing a non-ASCII name, symbol or session string, so the UTF-8/ANSI mismatch (finding 8) produces a passing test and a broken page.

No test builds a class report from a folder with mixed session keys and asserts anything about the KPI row, the sort order or the bar scale - only that the caveat text appears. Finding 9 is therefore invisible to the suite.
No test feeds ClassReport a CSV without session_key (a pre-v76 export), so the parsed=true-with-a-problem state and the m_key=="" caveat path (finding 10) are never rendered.

CSSRMarketView::Prime is tested only with a synthetic cut in the middle of a bar sequence (T13:260-262) and only for the count returned; nothing asserts that the newest primed bar does not extend past the clock, and nothing tests Prime followed by OnBarContext for the same minute.

CSSRStrategyBroker::Close, ClosePartial, Modify, BreakEven and Trail take a raw ticket with no tag check. No test asserts that one strategy cannot close another strategy's or the manual trader's position, even though MyOpenCount/MyPosition exist precisely because that mistake is expected (SSR_IStrategy.mqh:125-127).
Nothing tests CSSRStrategyHost behaviour when Add() is called before Attach() - the context's market and broker stay NULL for the life of the run with no error reported.

key_facts: There is no test runner, no harness, no exit code and no cross-file aggregation. Each of T1..T8 is a standalone `#property script_show_inputs` script whose only output is Printed text ending in GREEN or RED; a human reads the Experts log. `Check()` never aborts, so a section keeps executing after its own precondition failed.

The assertion vocabulary is copied verbatim into all eight files (`Check`, `CheckEq`, `Skip`, `Section`) rather than shared. `CheckEq` takes two `long`s, so every float assertion is hand-written as `MathAbs(...) < eps`, and `Check(name, a > b)` loses both numbers unless the author formats a `detail` by hand - which roughly half the call sites do not.

Skips are counted separately and never turn a run RED (deliberate policy stated in T2's header: "this account has no M1 for this symbol" is not a code defect). T4 is all-or-nothing: two early `return`s (lines 100, 126) skip the entire file.

T5 is the only file with a test double: `CFakePort : public CSSRReplayPort` (T5:31). `CSSRReplayPort` has 13 pure virtuals and ~30 defaulted ones; CFakePort implements exactly the 13, so every trading, lines, session and statement verb the panel can reach returns false in T5.

Three terminal-touching files isolate themselves by slot number only: T3=9, T4=8, T6=7. Within a file the slot is shared by every section, so T3.2, T3.5, T3.6, T3.7 and T3.8 all operate on one symbol name.

`CSSRCustomSymbolManager::Create` calls `Destroy()` first and `CSSRCustomSymbolSink::Prepare` calls `ClearAll()` after creating, so re-preparing a slot silently wipes whatever an earlier section left there. `Prepare` also resets the emit watermark `m_last_emit_msc`, which is why T3.5's forward emit is accepted at a timestamp earlier than T3.4's.

`CSSRRecordingSink::m_seed_bars` is `+=` only and `TruncateFrom` trims ticks only (Core/Sinks/SSR_RecordingSink.mqh:71, 103-120). `SeedBarCount()` is therefore a cumulative write counter, not a live bar count - this underpins finding tests-a-8.

`CSSRReplayController::SetDataMode` (line 693) only writes `m_state.data_mode`; nothing in the controller reads it. T1's SSR_DATA_MEMORY and T2.8's SSR_DATA_BROKER change no behaviour and T7/T8 omit the call entirely; no test asserts the reported mode.

`ctrl.Violations()` is `m_guard.Violations()` and `Attach`/`Load` push `GetPointer(m_guard)` into the source (controller line 573), so T1.6's `ctrl.Violations() > 0` after a direct `src.Bars().ReadBars(future)` is a sound assertion, not a coincidence.

`CSSRPanel::OnEvent` handles only CHARTEVENT_KEYDOWN, CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_ENDEDIT and CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE. Object clicks go through `PollClicks()` (Ui/SSR_Panel.mqh:2445), which scans `ObjectsTotal(m_chart,-1,OBJ_BUTTON)` for a prefix match with OBJPROP_STATE set. The only occurrence of CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK in the whole panel is the comment at line 2878 stating it is deliberately not handled.

`SSRSpeedLadder` has 20 stops (`#define SSR_SPEED_LADDER_SIZE 20`, Common/SSR_Types.mqh:302) starting at 10 (0.1x) with 1x at index 4; `SSRSpeedLadderIndex` returns the nearest stop. The `ENUM_SSR_SPEED` enum still carries only 8 named values plus SSR_SPEED_MAX, which is what T5.2/T5.5 were written against.

`SSR_VK_R` is bound to `SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE` and reset lives on `SSR_VK_0` (Ui/SSR_Keys.mqh:162 and :200). The same drift survives in production text: `SSRKeyHint()` (SSR_Keys.mqh:273-274) still ends "D fidelity  R reset".

T6.4 asserts on an English literal inside a validator message (`StringFind(why, "too early") >= 0`, T6:133), and T7.4/T7.7 assert on `"tick history"`, `"catching up"`, `"UNCALIBRATED"` and `"measured"`. Any localisation of `SSRValidateRange` would silently break T6.4.

Audit A21 (tools/ssr_audit.py:1588) matches a timeframe argument with `([A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\s*\(\s*\))?)` immediately followed by `,\s*SERIES_BARS_COUNT`. An indexed timeframe such as `cycle[i]` does not match, so A21 cannot see T4.2's read - the audit and the test both miss the documented lazy-series trap there.

Files written to disk by this subsystem: T6 writes and invalidates `SSReplay\cache\TESTORIGIN.SSR7.manifest` and `SSReplay\cache\A.SSR7.manifest`; T8 writes and removes `SSReplay\positions\T8TEST`; T3/T4/T6 create and destroy custom symbols `<origin>.SSR9/.SSR8/.SSR7`; T5 creates and removes chart objects under prefixes `SSRT5_` and `SSRT59_`. T1, T2 and T7 write nothing.

findings.title: T5.6's click assertion cannot pass: the panel does not handle CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK at all
findings.claim: Running T5 on any terminal prints `FAIL  click reached the port  expected=1 actual=0`. `CSSRPanel::OnEvent` has no CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK branch, so the call is a no-op and `port.play` stays 0. The section titled "a click and a key take the same path" - the file header's second of three stated purposes - therefore asserts nothing about clicks and is permanently red.
findings.evidence: `grep -n CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_Panel.mqh` returns exactly one hit, line 2878, and it is a comment inside OnEvent: "//--- CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK is deliberately not handled here. //--- PollClicks is the ONE mechanism". OnEvent's branches are CHARTEVENT_KEYDOWN (palette, Ctrl+K, tag box, key table), CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_ENDEDIT and CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE; every other id falls through to `return false` at the end (line 2971). Clicks are instead consumed by `PollClicks()` (SSR_Panel.mqh:2445), which scans `ObjectsTotal(m_chart, -1, OBJ_BUTTON)` for names starting with `m_prefix` whose `OBJPROP_STATE` is set. A test of the click path would have to set OBJPROP_STATE on `SSRT5_play` and then call `panel.PollClicks()`.

findings.title: T5.2 asserts an 8-stop speed ladder against a 20-stop ladder: four assertions fail
findings.claim: All four lines fail on any run: 8 vs 20, 25 vs 10, 5000 vs 300, 2 vs 4. T5 can therefore never report GREEN, which removes the file's whole value as a gate - a reader who has learned that T5 is always red will not notice tests-a-1 or tests-a-4 when they appear beside it.
findings.evidence: Common/SSR_Types.mqh:302 is `#define SSR_SPEED_LADDER_SIZE 20`. `SSRSpeedLadder` (line 275) returns 10 for index 0 (the comment says `// 0.1x`) and 300 for index 7; 5000 is index 15 and SSR_SPEED_MAX is index 19. `SSR_SPEED_DEFAULT_IX` is 4 and `SSRSpeedLadder(4)` is 100, so `SSRSpeedLadderIndex(SSR_SPEED_1 /*100*/)` returns 4, not 2. The header comment above the ladder (lines 257-274) explicitly says "Twenty stops, not eight, because the panel now has a trackbar" - the production code documents the change and the test was never brought up to it. The test still compiles because `ENUM_SSR_SPEED` kept its eight named values; only the ladder grew.

findings.title: T5.5's three speed-clamp assertions fail against the 20-stop ladder
findings.claim: Three more guaranteed failures in the same file. From 1x (100) SPEED_UP now yields 150, not 200; from 50x (5000) it yields 7500 instead of clamping, so "cannot exceed the top" is asserting the wrong ceiling entirely; from 0.25x (25) SPEED_DOWN yields 10, not 25. Worse than the count: the middle assertion no longer tests a clamp at all, because 50x is index 15 of 20 - the real top-of-ladder clamp (index 19, SSR_SPEED_MAX) and the real bottom clamp (index 0, 0.1x) are now completely uncovered.
findings.evidence: `CSSRPanel::ExecuteInner` case SSR_CMD_SPEED_UP (SSR_Panel.mqh:2317-2322) is `int i = SSRSpeedLadderIndex(m_state.speed_x100); if(i < SSR_SPEED_LADDER_SIZE - 1) i++; return m_port.SetSpeedX100(SSRSpeedLadder(i));`. SSRSpeedLadderIndex(100)=4 -> 5 -> SSRSpeedLadder(5)=150. SSRSpeedLadderIndex(5000)=15 -> 16 -> 7500. SPEED_DOWN (2324-2328) does `if(i > 0) i--`: SSRSpeedLadderIndex(25)=1 -> 0 -> 10. `CFakePort::SetSpeedX100` records the argument verbatim into `last_speed`, and each Execute is preceded by `panel.Render()` so `m_state.speed_x100` is the value the test just set.

findings.title: T5.1 asserts R maps to reset; R has been rebound to the SL/TP lines
findings.code: CheckEq("R resets",           SSR_CMD_RESET,          SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_R));
findings.claim: Fails on every run. `SSRKeyToCommand(82)` returns SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE. Nothing in T1..T8 asserts the current binding of R or of `0`, so the rebinding that the production code went out of its way to document is verified by no test at all - and the same stale mapping still ships in a user-visible string.
findings.evidence: Ui/SSR_Keys.mqh:162-164 is `SSRAddKey(out, i, SSR_VK_R, "R", SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE, "stop and target lines on / off", true);`, with a boxed comment at lines 192-199 headed "RESET MOVED OFF R, and off every letter". Reset is now `SSRAddKey(out, i, SSR_VK_0, "0", SSR_CMD_RESET, ...)` at line 200. `SSRKeyToCommand` (line 224) is a linear scan of that one table, so R can only return LINES_TOGGLE. Cross-check: `SSRKeyHint()` at SSR_Keys.mqh:273-274 still returns "... F follow  D fidelity  R reset", so the drift this test should have caught is live in production text as well.

findings.title: T5.6's "foreign objects ignored" is now a vacuous pass - every object click is ignored
findings.claim: Both assertions pass, and neither can ever fail. Since OnEvent has no CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK branch it returns false for every object click - the panel's own buttons included - so "foreign objects ignored" proves only that object clicks are universally ignored. If someone later added a click branch that dispatched on any sparam without a prefix check, this green assertion would stay green. This is the more dangerous half of the same defect as tests-a-1: one line shouts, this one lies quietly.
findings.evidence: Same evidence as tests-a-1: CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK appears only in the comment at SSR_Panel.mqh:2878; OnEvent's trailing `return false` (line 2971) is the only path an object-click event can take. The prefix filter that the assertion means to exercise lives in `PollClicks` (SSR_Panel.mqh:2480, `if(StringFind(name, m_prefix) != 0) continue;`), which the test never calls.

findings.title: T5.9 (second) asserts on the test double instead of the panel for JumpTo and Restart
findings.claim: Four assertions that test CFakePort's own two-line bodies and nothing else. `p59.JumpTo` is `{ jump++; last_jump_msc = m; return true; }` and `p59.Restart` is `{ restart++; return true; }` - both are declared six lines above in the same file, so all four can only pass. The section is headed "the navigation verbs reach the port", but nothing here goes through `panel59`. Concretely: SSR_CMD_JUMP is on the host's side of the fence and SSR_CMD_RESTART has no key binding at all, so neither verb has any panel-side coverage - if `ExecuteInner`'s `case SSR_CMD_RESTART: return m_port.Restart();` were deleted tomorrow these assertions would still be green.
findings.evidence: CFakePort's bodies are T5:67-69. `CSSRPanel::Owns` (SSR_Panel.mqh, the switch listing SSR_CMD_NONE/SESSIONS/JUMP/REVIEW/REPLAY_FROM_HERE) returns false for SSR_CMD_JUMP, so a J keypress is deliberately not handled by the panel and cannot be tested this way at all; SSR_CMD_RESTART appears in no `SSRAddKey` call in SSR_Keys.mqh, so no key reaches it either. The two assertions immediately above (lines 310-316, LEFT and PgUp) do go through `panel59.OnEvent` and are sound - the contrast is within the same block.

findings.title: T3.8 "teardown leaves nothing behind" runs against a symbol T3.7 already deleted
findings.claim: T3.8 passes whatever `mgr.Destroy()` does, including nothing. The symbol is already gone before the section starts, because T3.7's last statement is `second.Destroy()` on the identical name. So the final assertion of the phase - that teardown removes the custom symbol - is structurally incapable of failing: if `CSSRCustomSymbolManager::Destroy` regressed to a no-op, T3.8 would still print two PASSes, and the user would discover it as a leftover symbol blocking the next session.
findings.evidence: `mgr.Create(origin, InpSlot)` (T3:99) and `a.Create(origin, InpSlot)` (T3:418) both set `m_symbol = SSRReplaySymbolNameFor(origin, slot, m_anonymous)` (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:307), so mgr, a and second all name the same symbol; T3:427 asserts exactly that (`second.Symbol() == a.Symbol()`). T3:434 calls `second.Destroy()`, which reaches `CustomSymbolDelete(m_symbol)` (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:553). `Destroy()` opens with `if(m_symbol == "") return true;` and ends with `Succeed(); return ok;` - deleting an absent symbol is explicitly "not a failure" per its own comment - so mgr.Destroy() is a silent no-op here and the assertion `e != 0 || d == 0` reads a symbol that has been absent since T3.7.

findings.title: "warmup survived the reset" is measured with a write counter that a wipe cannot decrement
findings.claim: The assertion cannot detect the failure it is named after. `SeedBarCount()` is a monotonically increasing count of bars ever written, and `TruncateFrom` never touches it, so if `Reset()` deleted the warmup history the number would not move and the test would pass. It can only fail on the opposite fault (extra re-seeding). The real risk on a terminal - Reset truncating into the warmup and leaving the higher timeframes empty - is therefore uncovered, and T8.8:320 repeats the identical pattern for Restart.
findings.evidence: Core/Sinks/SSR_RecordingSink.mqh:71 is `m_seed_bars += count;` - the only write to that field outside `Clear()`. `TruncateFrom` (line 103-120) rewrites `m_ticks`, `m_tick_count` and `m_last_msc` and leaves `m_seed_bars` alone. `CSSRReplayController::Reset` (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1276-1278) calls `m_sink.TruncateFrom(m_timeline.start_msc)` then `m_sink.OnReset()`, and `OnReset` is `{ m_resets++; }`. The sink exposes no live bar count - `FirstTickMsc`, `LastTickMsc`, `TickAt` and `CountAfter` all read the tick array - so no assertion in the current sink API could distinguish a surviving warmup from a deleted one.

findings.title: T2.6's stated dangling-guard test never lets the guard die
findings.claim: The comment names a use-after-free hazard; the code cannot reach it. `CSSRFutureGuard guard` is declared at T2:267 inside the same `else { ... }` block and is still alive at line 301, so even if `DetachGuard()` did nothing the read would dereference a live object and `na` would come back >= 0. The assertion passes either way. The lifetime this section claims to cover - source outliving the controller's guard - is exercised nowhere in T1..T8; `CSSRMt5DataSource`'s destructor calls `DetachGuard()` for exactly this reason (SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:43) and that path is untested.
findings.evidence: T2:267 `CSSRFutureGuard guard;` is a stack object whose scope is the `else` block opened at T2:265 and closed at T2:304, three lines after the read. `src` is declared far outside at T2:183, so the two objects' lifetimes are the wrong way round for the stated test: the guard dies first only after the section is over, at which point nothing reads through `src` again until T2.9 - which would crash rather than fail if DetachGuard were broken. To actually test it, the guard must go out of scope (or be `new`/`delete`d) before the post-detach read.

findings.title: T4.2 reads SERIES_BARS_COUNT on an unprimed timeframe, and the indexed argument hides it from audit A21
findings.claim: This is the exact read that ground truth #7 says cost an entire build, made in the file that carries the project's headline assertion, with no priming and no retry. If the M15 series has not finished building 900 ms after `ChartSetSymbolPeriod`, `bars` comes back 0 and T4.2 reports "M15 has bars  0" - i.e. it blames the terminal for failing to derive the timeframe, which is the precise misdiagnosis T3's header documents. T3 wrote the `SeriesBars()` helper for this and T4 does not use it. Separately, audit A21 cannot flag the line, so neither guard covers it.
findings.evidence: T3:48-63 defines `long SeriesBars(const string sym, const ENUM_TIMEFRAMES tf)` which rereads up to 10 times with `CopyRates(...,0,1,probe)` and `Sleep(100)` between attempts, under a header that says SERIES_BARS_COUNT "answers zero - not 'no bars' but 'no series yet'". T4 has no such helper and no CopyRates naming `cycle[i]` within sight of line 186 - `FutureBars()` is called four lines later and its CopyRates calls name `tfs[i]`, a different local array. Audit A21 (tools/ssr_audit.py:1588-1592) matches the timeframe argument as `([A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\s*\(\s*\))?)` immediately followed by `\s*,\s*SERIES_BARS_COUNT`; the text after `cycle` is `[i], SERIES_BARS_COUNT`, so the regex does not match and the finding is never reported. Whether 900 ms is in fact enough on a real terminal cannot be verified from source, which is why this is a risk rather than a confirmed failure.

findings.title: T2.8 closes with an unconditional `Check(..., true)`
findings.claim: A literal `true` inflates `g_pass` and prints "PASS  Phase 1 contract held with a real source", a sentence a reader will take as a verified architectural claim. It verifies nothing. If the claim is worth an assertion, the assertion is that the same controller class reached READY and emitted an ordered stream with both sources - which the twelve lines above already establish; this line adds only a false positive to the count.
findings.evidence: The argument is the literal `true`, so `ok` is always true and the `g_fail` branch is unreachable. Nothing between line 404 and 406 computes a value that is consulted. This is the only unconditional `Check` in T1..T8.

findings.title: T7.1 asserts arithmetic over its own literals and reads no production code
findings.claim: Three of T7's assertions are `Check`s over expressions built entirely from local literals - 8.0, 50.0, 60.0, 2000.0, 86400.0 - none of which come from a symbol the product defines. They cannot fail and cannot detect a change: if `InpTicksPerBar`'s default moved from 8 to 32, or the ladder top from 50x to 200x, the reasoning these lines were written to pin would be wrong and all three would still pass. The 50x figure is in fact already stale - the ladder now tops out at SSR_SPEED_MAX (index 19), with 50x at index 15 - so "a day at 50x still takes over 25 minutes" no longer describes the product's fastest setting, and the conclusion drawn from it ("which is why Jump exists rather than a bigger number") no longer follows.
findings.evidence: Lines 66-79 declare `ticks_per_bar`, `at_50x`, `need_speed` and `day_minutes` from constants written in the same statements; no SSR_* macro, enum or function appears in any of the three conditions. The current ladder is Common/SSR_Types.mqh:275-302: index 15 is 5000 (50x), index 18 is 20000 (200x), index 19 is SSR_SPEED_MAX. Written against the real constants - `SSRSpeedLadder(SSR_SPEED_LADDER_SIZE-1)` and the default of `InpTicksPerBar` - the same three lines would have caught the ladder change that tests-a-2 and tests-a-3 missed.

findings.title: T8.5's clamp and no-op assertions read only a return value, and one of them is a hardcoded true
findings.claim: "jumping to now is a no-op" can never fail: `JumpTo` returns a literal `true` on the equal-target path. "clamped past the end" never reads `ctrl.Now()` afterwards, so it cannot tell a correct clamp to `end_msc` from a clamp to the wrong instant - clamping to `start_msc`, or landing one bar short, would pass while silently rewinding the user's whole session. The section is titled "JumpTo picks the right direction" and the out-of-range case is the one place where the landing point is never checked; every other jump in T8.5 does assert `ctrl.Now()`.
findings.evidence: `CSSRReplayController::JumpTo` (SSR_ReplayController.mqh) clamps with `long target = SSRClampMsc(target_msc, m_timeline.start_msc, m_timeline.end_msc);` and then has `if(target == m_clock.now_msc) return true;` - an unconditional true for the no-op case - plus `if(delta <= 0) return true;` on the backward path. For the over-range case it falls through to `return (JumpForward(target) >= 0);`. Adding `CheckEq("landed on the end", g_end, ctrl.Now())` (or the bar-open form used at T8:220) would close both.

findings.title: T6.8's closing assertion is a tautology given the two above it
findings.code:
Check("and it differs from the flat default or matches deliberately",
            v.SessionGap() >= before);
findings.claim: The name asserts "A or not-A" and the condition is already implied by the two preceding assertions, so the line cannot fail and states nothing. `before` is the validator's default gap, line 290 has established `gap >= SSR_SESSION_GAP_MSC` and line 298 that `v.SessionGap() == gap`; since the default is that same floor, `v.SessionGap() >= before` follows. The question this section exists to answer - does a 24/5 forex symbol and a session-broken index symbol actually learn *different* gaps - is not asked.
findings.evidence: T6:289-299 sets `long gap = SSRSymbolSessionGap(origin)`, asserts `gap >= SSR_SESSION_GAP_MSC`, then `long before = v.SessionGap()` on a default-constructed `CSSRDataValidator`, then `v.LearnFrom(origin)` and `v.SessionGap() == gap`. The remaining condition reduces to `gap >= SSR_SESSION_GAP_MSC`, which line 290 already asserts.

findings.title: T2.4's discovery assertions restate postconditions that Open() already guarantees
findings.claim: All three sit inside `else` of `if(!opened)`, and `Open()` cannot return true without having set every one of them. They add three PASSes that no regression can turn red: if `Discover` started reporting a bogus range, `Open` would still have returned true and these three would still pass. Only the `first_msc < last_msc` check beside them has a reachable failure (a single-bar, still-forming history makes `last_msc = lastbar_open - 1`).
findings.evidence: `CSSRMt5DataSource::Open` (SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:56-72) returns false unless `m_hist.Discover` succeeded, and sets `m_open = true` only on the success path. `CSSRMt5HistoryProvider::Discover` (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh) returns false when `bars <= 0 || first <= 0 || lastbar <= 0` and otherwise sets `out.available = true;` and `out.bar_count = bars;`. So `opened == true` implies `IsOpen()`, `range.available` and `range.bar_count > 0` by construction.

findings.title: Two different sections in T5 are both labelled T5.9
findings.code: Section("T5.9  the navigation verbs reach the port");
findings.claim: The log prints `--- T5.9  state colours are distinct where meaning differs` and later `--- T5.9  the navigation verbs reach the port`. Anyone quoting "T5.9 passed" is ambiguous, and a reader scanning the log for a gap sees T5.1..T5.9 and concludes the file is complete. The second section should be T5.10.
findings.evidence: T5:276 is `Section("T5.9  state colours are distinct where meaning differs");` and T5:289 is `Section("T5.9  the navigation verbs reach the port");`. No other file in T1..T8 repeats a section number.

findings.title: T8.3's headline assertion admits any tick count from 1 upward
findings.code:
Check("the tick count came BACK, not to zero",
            ctrl.TicksEmitted() > 0,
...
      Check("and it is near where it was",
            ctrl.TicksEmitted() <= mark_ticks,
findings.claim: The section is titled "THE POINT: rewind restores counters, does not reset them" and its bounds are `> 0` and `<= mark_ticks` - a window of roughly seven thousand ticks wide, since 900 pumps at 1x emit on the order of 120 ticks per minute of replay. An implementation that restored the cursor to the very first checkpoint, or one that lost all but a single tick, satisfies both. The claim being made is "near where it was"; nothing quantifies "near". The one bug the section exists to catch - a plain seek that zeroes the cursor - is caught, but a partial restore is not, and a partial restore is the failure a snapshot ring actually risks.
findings.evidence: `mark_ticks = ctrl.TicksEmitted()` is captured at T8:133 after 900 x `ctrl.Pump(1000)`; the rewind is `ctrl.StepBackward((int)back_bars)` with `back_bars = (ctrl.Now() - mark_time) / SSR_MSC_PER_MIN`, i.e. exactly 300 bars, so the post-rewind count should land within one checkpoint interval of `mark_ticks`. `CSSRSnapshotStore::SetInterval` is used in T8.2 with 60000 ms, so the tolerance is computable; the assertion instead uses 0 and mark_ticks as its bounds. A `Check(mark_ticks - ctrl.TicksEmitted() < <one interval worth of ticks>)` is what the section's own prose describes.

performance_notes: Wall-clock cost of the suite is dominated by fixed sleeps, not by computation. T3 spends ~2.6 s in explicit `SSRPause` calls (500+300+500+500+500+500+200+300) plus up to 10x100 ms per `SeriesBars()` miss (three calls in T3.6, so up to 3 s more). T4 spends ~7.9 s (800+300+4x900+600+2x600+200+400+300+600+600+400+300). These are unavoidable for async `Custom*` writes but they mean T3 and T4 are minute-scale, not second-scale, and a developer will run them rarely.

T1 is the only file whose runtime is pure computation: T1.5 runs the engine twice x 300 pumps, T1.10 three times x 180 pumps, and T1.4/T1.6/T1.8/T1.9 another ~170 pumps, over a 1440-bar dataset regenerated by `BuildBars` on every `Wire()` call - eight full regenerations of the xorshift/Box-Muller walk. Cheap, but the dataset is identical every time and could be built once.

`CSSRRecordingSink::CountAfter` is an O(n) scan of the whole tick array and is called 13 times across T1/T2/T7/T8, in some cases inside a section that has just emitted thousands of ticks (T7.6 calls it after ~200 pumps following a 30-minute bulk pump). `Fingerprint()` is another full scan, run twice in T1.5. Total is still small, but these are the only quadratic-ish shapes in the suite.

T7.6's `ctrl.Pump(30 * 60 * 1000)` is the single heaviest production call in the subsystem: one pump owing 1.8 M ms of replay against a deliberately tight 2 ms budget (`ctrl.SetPumpBudgetMs(2.0)`), followed by 200 catch-up pumps. This is the suite's only real stress of the deferral path and it is worth keeping.

T6.7 is the only assertion in the suite gated on wall-clock time: `Check("reuse was not slower", second_ms <= first_ms * 1.5)`. On a terminal where the first load is fast (small warmup, warm OS cache) the 50 % headroom is a small absolute number and unrelated scheduling noise can turn the file red; conversely a reuse path that was genuinely 40 % slower than a full seed would pass. The claim it wants to make - that run 2 wrote no bars - is already available structurally through `k2.ReusedSeed()` and `k2.CacheReason()`, both of which it also asserts.

T4.5 asserts `(charts.RedrawsSkipped() - s0) > 40` over 50 tight `charts.Redraw()` calls. This is timing-dependent in the other direction: it assumes the loop completes well inside the throttle interval. It is the only throttle coverage in the suite and is reasonable, but it is measuring the loop's speed as much as the throttle's.
test_gaps: `PollClicks()` - the sole mechanism by which a user operates the panel - has zero coverage. Nothing in T1..T8 sets `OBJPROP_STATE` on a panel button and calls it. That includes the 200 ms repeat floor the code says was added after a recording caught play/pause firing four times in 350 ms, the palette-first ordering, and the prefix filter. T5.6 believes it covers this and does not (tests-a-1, tests-a-5).

The 20-button speed groove named in the ground truth is untested. `SSRSpeedFraction`, `SSRSpeedAtFraction`, `SpeedFromPixel`/`OnTrack` and the `speedN` button ids handled at SSR_Panel.mqh:2596 are reached by no assertion; T5.2 still describes an 8-stop ladder.

The Reset two-press confirmation is never exercised. `panel.Execute(SSR_CMD_RESET)` in T5.3 short-circuits to `m_port.Reset()` because `ResetWithConfirm` returns early when `m_state.closed_trades + m_state.open_positions <= 0`, and CFakePort's `SSRUiState` is left at `Init()`. The panel exposes `ResetIsArmed()` and `ResetWarningText()` specifically "for the test that proves the confirmation actually holds a press back" (SSR_Panel.mqh, comment above line ~2975) - and no test calls either.

No assertion anywhere in T1..T8 checks a string length against MetaTrader's 63-character `OBJPROP_TEXT` limit, the trap the overview says caused at least five separate defects. It is enforced only statically by audit A19, which cannot see a string assembled at runtime from a symbol name or a Persian translation.

The `Extent()` / `CheckFrame()` layout-overflow instrument added in v124 is asserted by no test. `Render()` calls `m_w.ResetExtent()` on every frame and T5 renders roughly 30 times without once asking whether anything was drawn outside the panel frame - the single cheapest assertion available for a UI its author cannot see.

Compact mode is untested. `Render()` decides `m_compact = (chart_h > 0 && chart_h < SSR_PANEL_H + 24)` from the live chart height, and the panel exposes `IsCompact()` for a test to read, but T5 never asserts which mode it got nor that the operated rows survive in the compact one. The same applies to the tall-panel wish (`m_tall` / `m_pro_why`) reached by SSR_CMD_PANEL_SIZE.

Theme coverage is one line: T5.9 compares three colour pairs. The three palette switch positions (SSR_THEME_RAIL / LIGHT / DARK) and the two layout switch positions (SSR_LAYOUT_RAIL 310 px / 420 px fallback) are exercised by the audits, not by any test - so nothing asserts that the panel still functions when a switch is flipped, only that the colours differ.

`SYMBOL_CHART_MODE` is asserted nowhere. T3.2 checks digits, point, tick size, contract size, trade mode, spread float, start time and expiry - but not the one property ground truth says decides whether an injected BID/ASK tick builds a bar at all. T3.4 would pass on a LAST-mode symbol (`st.ticks_added > 0` because CustomTicksAdd accepts the ticks) while zero bars were built; only T3.6's `SeriesBars` reads would catch it, and only on the broker-data path.

`CSSRReplayGroup` / `SSR_MasterClock` multi-symbol replay (up to 3 extra symbols, `InpAlsoSymbols`) has no coverage in this subsystem. Every engine test drives exactly one controller over one symbol; nothing asserts that N symbols stay on one clock or that a rewind truncates all of them.

No test covers a corrupt or truncated persisted file. T6.5 round-trips a well-formed manifest and T8.7 a well-formed position file; neither writes a half-line, a wrong `version`, a non-UTF-8 byte, or a manifest naming a symbol that exists with the wrong digits. The FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI mojibake trap named in the overview is untested here.

`data_mode` reporting is untested and in fact unreachable: `SetDataMode` writes `m_state.data_mode` and nothing reads it. T1 sets MEMORY, T2.8 sets BROKER, T7 and T8 set nothing, and no assertion reads it back - so the field could be wrong in the UI and in a saved session without any test noticing.

T2.4 is the only section that asserts on the still-forming-bar logic (`cat.LastMsc() <= now_quote + SSR_MSC_PER_MIN` at T6:78, and indirectly `first_msc < last_msc` at T2:201), and only against live broker state. The specific branch in `Discover` that reports `lastbar_open - 1` when the last quote falls inside the final bar is exercised by no deterministic test, despite being the code that decides whether a replay window's end is in the future.

T4's early `return`s make the whole of Phase 4 all-or-nothing: with no broker M1 history, T4.1 through T4.7 - the chart registry, the headline timeframe cycle, the partial-candle check, auto-scroll detach, throttling, the leak guard and close-only-what-we-opened - produce exactly one SKIP. Nothing in T4 runs against the in-memory source, so none of the chart layer is testable without a funded account, unlike T1/T7/T8 which run anywhere.

key_facts: All seven files (T9-T15) re-declare the same harness by copy: g_pass/g_fail, Check/CheckEq/CheckNear (+CheckStr in T12/T15, CheckExact in T12 only), Section, and a final PrintFormat that prints GREEN when g_fail==0. There is no shared test header, no aggregate runner, and the verdict is stdout only - no exit code, file or global variable, so nothing outside the Experts log can consume a result.

Nothing aborts on a failed assertion. A section continues after its own preconditions fail, so one broken fixture produces a cascade of unrelated FAILs (and, in T10.8, silently skips 8 assertions guarded by `if(h != INVALID_HANDLE)`).

Assertion counts (call sites minus the helpers' internal calls): T9 ~59 / 8 sections, T10 ~129 / 12, T11 ~130 / 10, T12 ~137 / 8, T13 ~85 / 8, T14 ~95 / 8, T15 ~75 / 10. Total ~710 across this subsystem.

Every expectation is written against the default `input` values (T10's hand-computed PF 3.5, T13.4's `bar_calls >= 8 && <= 16`, T9's pump counts). `#property script_show_inputs` lets a user change them, which silently invalidates expectations rather than skipping them.

T10 is the only file that drives the observers directly (hand-advanced `g_msc`, `Tick()`, `BarCtx()`) and the only one that configures the risk engine AFTER OnSessionStart, which is the correct order (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:582 calls m_risk.ConfigureFromSymbol on every session start).

Runtime-relevant invariant: CSSRReplayController::Load broadcasts OnSessionStart to all observers (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:835-837) and CSSRTradingEngine::OnSessionStart resets balance to m_balance_initial, zeroes the position table, resets next_ticket and re-reads the risk model from the symbol (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:570-591).
CSSRTradingEngine's constructor default balance is already 10000.0 (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:552), the same figure T9/T14 assert as proof that a session start or a publish arrived.

SSRStatistics::IsTrustworthy() is exactly `trades > 0 && ambiguous_pct <= 10.0` (SSR_Statistics.mqh:143) - no minimum sample size - so T10.3's 25%-then-5% pair is a clean test of the threshold and is not confounded.
SSR_MAX_TRADE_LEGS is 8 (SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:173), so T10.9's `SSR_MAX_TRADE_LEGS - 1` expectation means 7 of 10 attempted partial exits succeed - a real assertion, not an accident.

T10.8's journal reader and CSSRJournal::ExportCsv agree on FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI (SSR_Journal.mqh:173), and the hard-coded column indices f[2]=tag, f[12]=r, f[16]=resolution match the header written at SSR_Journal.mqh:218-220. The documented UTF-8/ANSI trap does not apply to this test.

Disk/terminal side effects: T10 leaves MQL5\Files\SSReplay\journal\t10.csv behind (never deleted); T12 deletes every file and session it creates; T14 writes and then fully withdraws the 23 SSR.7.* global variables; T15 writes MQL5\Files\SSReplay\panel.ini and does not restore it, and creates/destroys objects plus four chart properties on whatever chart the script is dropped on.

Default replay speed is SSR_SPEED_1 (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:53), so one Pump(1000) is ~1 s of replay time; every 'N pumps' figure in T9-T15 is calibrated to 1x and would break if the default speed ever changed.

Nothing in T9-T15 mentions CSSRPropEvaluation, CSSRShotBook, CSSRFlightRecorder, CSSRTradeLines, CSSRCalendarLines, CSSRChartManager, CSSRSetupPanel, CSSRKeyCard, CSSRRevealCard, CSSRReviewCard, CSSRFirstRun or SSR_Strings/T(SSR_S_*) (verified by grep over the seven files).

findings.title: T15.7 asserts R still means RESET; the key table maps R to LINES_TOGGLE, so the assertion is false at runtime
findings.code:
Check("and the other keys still mean what they did",
            SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_SPACE) == SSR_CMD_TOGGLE &&
            SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_J)     == SSR_CMD_JUMP &&
            SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_B)     == SSR_CMD_BOOKMARK &&
            SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_R)     == SSR_CMD_RESET);
findings.claim: Run T15 on a terminal: SSRKeyToCommand(SSR_VK_R) returns SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE, not SSR_CMD_RESET, so the conjunction is false and Check records a FAIL. Phase 15 can never print GREEN, and because the harness never aborts, this looks like a product regression rather than a stale assertion.
findings.evidence: SSR_Keys.mqh binds R with `SSRAddKey(out, i, SSR_VK_R, "R", SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE, "stop and target lines on / off", true);` and binds reset to '0' with `SSRAddKey(out, i, SSR_VK_0, "0", SSR_CMD_RESET, ...)`, under a comment headed "RESET MOVED OFF R, and off every letter". SSRKeyToCommand is a linear scan of that one table and returns the first vk match, so R can only yield SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE. The test was not updated when reset moved; SSRKeyHint()'s trailing literal "R reset" (same file) shows the same stale belief, which is why the mistake reads as plausible.

findings.title: T15.9's premise is false: SetCorner does not move the panel, so both of its assertions fail
findings.claim: On a terminal x_after == x_before (both are m_x + SSR_PAD, unchanged by the corner), so `Check("the label moved with the panel", x_after != x_before)` and `Check("and it moved to the right, with the panel", x_after > x_before)` both FAIL. Phase 15 reports RED for a panel that is behaving exactly as designed, and the text-cache regression the section exists to guard is never actually exercised.
findings.evidence: CSSRPanel::SetCorner is `{ m_corner = (c & 3); SavePlace(); Render(); }` (SSR_Panel.mqh:384-385) and m_corner appears nowhere in Render or in any layout computation - its only uses are the constructor, a PrintFormat, SavePlace/RestorePlace and SnapToCorner (grep for m_corner in SSR_Panel.mqh returns lines 121, 287, 350, 385, 386, 543, 579, 598, 606 only). Only SnapToCorner (line 596, reachable from the Move button that v125 removed) recomputes m_x/m_y from the corner. Every object is drawn through CSSRWidgets, whose Common() hard-writes `ObjectSetInteger(m_chart, name, OBJPROP_CORNER, CORNER_LEFT_UPPER)` (SSR_Widgets.mqh:160), so XDISTANCE is always measured from the same chart corner. Two Renders with identical m_x therefore write identical XDISTANCE. (If the object did not exist, ObjectGetInteger would return 0 twice and the first assertion would fail for that reason instead.)

findings.title: T13.8 claims seed reproducibility and asserts three tautologies instead
findings.claim: Delete SetSeed's body (or seed each context with the registration index k instead of `m_seed ^ NameHash(name)`) and T13.8 still passes all three assertions: the section named "the same seed gives the same strategy" cannot detect a non-reproducible or order-dependent RNG stream. Two hosts with DIFFERENT seeds would also pass it.
findings.evidence: The section draws no random number and never touches a context. s1.Name() and s2.Name() are two instances of CSSRRefBreakout, whose Name() is `return "ref-breakout";` (SSR_RefStrategy.mqh:48), so the comparison is a literal against itself. h2.Count() counts registrations, not streams. The claim the comment makes is about `m_ctx[k].rng.Seed(m_seed ^ NameHash(s.Name()))` (SSR_StrategyHost.mqh:141), and that is observable from a test: SSRRandom rng is a public member of the public CSSRStrategyContext (SSR_IStrategy.mqh:202) and the bound ctx is reachable from a strategy subclass - the file's own CSSRCheater already reads ctx.market and ctx.Now(). A probe strategy exposing ctx.rng.Next() would make the section real; nothing of the sort is done.

findings.title: T14.8's "the command set is exactly the documented ones" is unfalsifiable by construction
findings.claim: Add `#define SSR_CMD_PRICE_AT 12` (exactly the read verb the section exists to forbid) and T14.8 still passes: the loop stops at 11. The section's stated purpose - "a future edit that adds one of these verbs should have to delete a test that says why it must not" - is not served, because the loop's bound moves with nothing and read_verbs is provably 0 today.
findings.evidence: SSR_Contract.mqh defines exactly twelve verbs occupying 0..11 (SSR_CMD_NONE 0 ... SSR_CMD_CLOSE_ALL 9, SSR_CMD_BUY_RISK 10, SSR_CMD_SELL_RISK 11, lines 92-108) and the `if` enumerates all twelve of those names. Every iteration of 0..11 therefore hits a `continue`, making `read_verbs++` unreachable and the assertion a constant 0 == 0. A thirteenth verb takes value 12, outside the hard-coded bound. The enum's size is never asserted, and there is no SSR_CMD_COUNT/SSR_CMD_MAX to assert against.

findings.title: T15.8 never establishes its precondition, so all four keyboard-takeover assertions pass on a chart where quick navigation is already off
findings.claim: Run T15 on a chart (or from a template) where CHART_QUICK_NAVIGATION and CHART_KEYBOARD_CONTROL are already false - a user who turned them off, or a chart left that way by an earlier aborted panel - and all four assertions pass even if the two ChartSetInteger lines were deleted from CSSRPanel::Create. The 'given back' pair is weaker still: it cannot distinguish 'restored the saved value' from 'wrote the same constant twice', because it compares against a value that both behaviours produce whenever was_nav equals what Create writes.
findings.evidence: The section reads the current values into was_nav/was_key and never forces them to a known state (no ChartSetInteger(..., true) before Create). CSSRPanel::Create saves them (SSR_Panel.mqh:320-321) and writes false (343-344); Destroy writes the saved values back (372-373). With was_nav == 0 the first CheckEq compares 0 against a value that was already 0, and the restore CheckEq compares 0 against 0. This is exactly the regression class the section was added for (the comment: "Fifteen phases and 1,159 assertions never saw it"), so a guard that can silently stop guarding matters here.

findings.title: Every Risk().Configure in T9 is discarded by Load; T9's sections silently run on the unknown-symbol fallback specs
findings.claim: The risk model the six T9 sections think they installed (tick_value 1.0, tick_size 1.0, digits 2) is overwritten microseconds later by Load, which re-derives it from a symbol named "TEST" that does not exist in the terminal. The sections then run on ConfigureFromSymbol's zero-fallbacks (digits 0, point 1.0, tick_size 1.0, tick_value 1.0) - which happen to give the same RiskOf() answers, so nothing fails today. Any T9 assertion added later about lot sizing, risk_at_entry or R would be measuring the fallback path, and if a broker ever resolves a symbol literally named TEST the section's specs change under it with no assertion to notice.
findings.evidence: CSSRReplayController::Load broadcasts OnSessionStart to every observer at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:835-837, and CSSRTradingEngine::OnSessionStart ends with `m_risk.ConfigureFromSymbol(symbol);` (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:582) - a wholesale overwrite of the six fields Configure() set. ConfigureFromSymbol reads SymbolInfo* and substitutes defaults for every zero (SSR_RiskEngine.mqh:41-57). T9 makes this call before Load in all six of its wired sections (lines 112, 180, 229, 268, 331, 404). T10's Begin() documents the correct order and does the opposite: "set AFTER OnSessionStart, which reconfigures risk from the symbol" (SSR_T10_Statistics.mq5:65-67).

findings.title: T9.7's checkpoint-path claim is not asserted; a silent fall back to the plain seek would keep the section green
findings.claim: Make NearestAtOrBefore stop finding a usable checkpoint (a ring-clear regression, a changed interval, a comparison flipped to strict) and StepBackward silently takes the SeekTo fallback for both of T9.7's rewinds. Count() > 0 still holds, the trades are still gone, and T9.7 reports PASS - the snapshot-restore path that the section says it exists to cover would be untested with nothing to show it.
findings.evidence: Count() reports how many checkpoints the ring holds, not that one was restored. StepBackward chooses between two implementations at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1450-1471: `if(m_snaps.NearestAtOrBefore(target, cp)) { RestoreSnapshot(cp); m_snaps.NoteRestore(); ... } else { ... SeekTo(target) }`. The distinguishing observable is public and unused by the test: CSSRSnapshotStore::Restores() (SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:90), incremented only on the snapshot branch (NoteRestore, line 162). The path is probably taken today - the first checkpoint is due immediately because m_last_msc starts INVALID (lines 93-98) and the interval is 5 replay minutes (line 33) - which is precisely why the omission is invisible.

findings.title: T9.2's "session start reached the account" holds whether or not OnSessionStart ever arrives
findings.code:
Check("session start reached the account", acct.Balance() == 10000.0,
            DoubleToString(acct.Balance(), 2));
findings.claim: Remove the observer registration, or stop broadcasting OnSessionStart entirely, and this assertion still passes - the account reports 10000.0 because SetBalance was called on the line above and because 10000.0 is also the constructor default. The only thing it proves is that nothing has traded yet.
findings.evidence: CSSRTradingEngine::SetBalance sets both m_balance_initial and m_balance (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:562-563), the constructor initialises both to 10000.0 (line 552), and OnSessionStart's only balance action is `m_balance = m_balance_initial;` (line 579) - an identity for this fixture. The observables that would carry the claim (m_symbol, m_digits, m_point, m_now_msc, all set by OnSessionStart) are never read; the section's own `CheckEq("one observer", 1, ctrl.ObserverCount())` is the closest it gets.

findings.title: T12.5's guard against storing derived statistics can never fail - no code writes a section named "statistics"
findings.code:
//--- and the file really does not contain them
      Check("no win rate was stored", !r.Select("statistics"));
findings.claim: Add `f.Section("stats"); f.SetDouble("win_rate", st.win_rate, 2);` to CSSRStatsEngine::SaveInto - exactly the mistake the section names ("Statistics stored alongside the trades they came from, and believed over them when the two disagree", file header) - and T12.5 still passes, because it probes one section name that no writer in the codebase ever uses.
findings.evidence: CSSRStatsEngine::SaveInto opens with `f.Section("equity");` and writes nothing else (SSR_Statistics.mqh:623-625). A grep for the literal "statistics" across MQL5/Include/SSReplay finds a single hit - `virtual string Name(void) override { return "statistics"; }` (SSR_Statistics.mqh:296), the observer's name, never a section key. So `r.Select("statistics")` is false for every possible session file this build can produce.

findings.title: T15.9 overwrites the production panel placement file, MQL5\Files\SSReplay\panel.ini
findings.code:
panel2.SetCorner(0);                       // top-left
      ...
      panel2.SetCorner(1);                       // top-right
findings.claim: A user who runs T15 to check the build finds their panel placement file rewritten by the test panel: corner is left at 1, and if no panel.ini existed, one is created carrying the test instance's coordinates and tab - so the next real session starts from state a test invented rather than from the first-run defaults. Nothing in T15 deletes or restores the file, unlike T12, which FileDeletes every artefact it makes.
findings.evidence: CSSRPanel::SetCorner calls SavePlace() unconditionally (SSR_Panel.mqh:385). SavePlace's only guard is `if(!m_place_loaded) return false;` (line ~531), and RestorePlace - which Create always calls - sets `m_place_loaded = true;` on its very first line, before the FileIsExist check. So both SetCorner calls in T15.9 write SSR_PANEL_FILE ("SSReplay\\panel.ini", SSR_Panel.mqh:64) with x, y, corner, collapsed, tab and pro taken from the test panel.

findings.title: T9.1's rounding assertions are one-sided and pass when LotForRisk refuses the trade outright
findings.claim: Any regression that makes this call return 0.0 (a refusal), or round to 14.00, or to 10.00, passes both assertions: 0 <= 14.28 and RiskOf(0,7) = 0 <= 100. The section's stated subject - that rounding goes DOWN to the step rather than up - needs a lower bound (lot > 14.28 - step, or an exact 14.28) and has none, so it only proves the result is not too large.
findings.evidence: Both predicates are upper bounds satisfied by every value in [0, 14.28]. LotForRisk returns 0.0 on four separate refusal paths (SSR_RiskEngine.mqh: dist<=0, balance/risk<=0, per_lot<=0, lot<m_vol_min) and RoundToStep floors, so the true answer here is 14.28 - a figure the test writes in a comment but never asserts. The earlier CheckNear("straightforward size", 10.0, ...) catches a total failure of the function, but not a step- or direction-specific one, which is what this pair is named for.

findings.title: T9.8's "a round trip at a flat price loses money" is satisfied by losing nothing
findings.claim: bal1 is read after the entry commission was already charged, so the predicate is "balance did not increase". A regression where Close() charges nothing and the spread/slippage round trip nets exactly zero passes this assertion; only a positive balance change would fail it. The section claims the cost is always adverse and this line does not test the sign of the cost, only its direction of not-profit.
findings.evidence: `a6.Balance() < bal1 + 1e-9` is true when Balance() == bal1. The concrete loss is asserted only for commission, by the preceding CheckNear("commission charged again on exit", 14.0, p.commission, 0.001); the spread and the 10-point slippage contributions to the round trip are never bounded below (an assertion like Balance() <= bal1 - 7.0 - slippage cost would do it).

findings.title: T12 says the money is compared EXACTLY and compares it with half a cent of tolerance, while its CheckExact helper sits unused
findings.claim: A restore that reproduces the balance to within 0.4 of a cent - e.g. a leg's realised amount written with two decimals and replayed with a rounding bias - passes as "exact". The file header's first stated guarantee ("A balance a cent short after a save is a bug nobody finds for months, so the money is compared exactly") is not the guarantee the code provides; the same 0.005 tolerance is used for the restored balance in T12.4 line 374 and T12.6 line 537.
findings.evidence: CheckNear's predicate is MathAbs(e-a) <= tol with tol = 0.005. The file defines a stricter helper for precisely this purpose - `void CheckExact(const string n, const double e, const double a) { Check(n, e == a, ...); }` (line 47) - and uses it exactly once, on a format-layer double (line 119, "and money is exact"), never on an account balance. Whether the engine can actually hit bit-equality here is a design question; the defect is that the comment states a stronger claim than the assertion makes, and a reader trusting the comment will not add the missing check.

findings.title: T15.5's "cannot trade" assertion is a tautology: ReadState Init()s the struct before refusing
findings.claim: st.can_trade is false because ReadState zeroed the struct on entry and then returned early, not because the port judged itself unable to trade. Any regression in the can_trade computation is invisible here, and the panel greys its buttons from exactly this field.
findings.evidence: CSSRGroupPort::ReadState begins `out.Init();` and only then returns false when Primary() is NULL (SSR_GroupPort.mqh, ReadState head). SSRUiState::Init sets `can_trade = false;` (SSR_ReplayPort.mqh:273). The live value is computed at SSR_GroupPort.mqh:244 as `out.can_trade = (m_acct.Bid() > 0.0);`, a line this section can never reach. The section's other assertions (Buy/Sell/CloseAll/BreakEvenAll refused with a reason) do exercise the port and are sound.

findings.title: T13.6's unsupported-timeframe assertion passes only because Add checks the timeframe before the duplicate name
findings.claim: The strategy handed to the timeframe check is `b`, which the same section already had refused as a duplicate name three lines earlier. Reorder Add's guards so the name check runs before the timeframe check - a natural refactor, since the name check is the more product-specific rule - and LastError becomes "two strategies named ref-breakout ...": the assertion fails and points at the timeframe validation, which is still working. A fresh strategy with an unused name would isolate the rule.
findings.evidence: CSSRStrategyHost::Add validates in the order NULL, capacity, `if(!SSRIsSupportedTimeframe(tf))` -> "unsupported timeframe", empty name, then the duplicate-name scan -> "two strategies named ... could not be told apart". `b` is a CSSRRefBreakout whose Name() is the constant "ref-breakout" (SSR_RefStrategy.mqh:48) and the section registered `a`, the same class, at line 448 - so both refusal reasons apply to this call and only the guard order decides which message LastError carries.

findings.title: T10.8 leaves its exported CSV in the trader's journal folder
findings.code: Check("export succeeded", j.ExportCsv("t10", 2), j.LastError());
findings.claim: Running T10 creates MQL5\Files\SSReplay\journal\t10.csv (and the folder, if absent) and never removes it, so a synthetic three-trade file with a caveat header sits permanently beside the user's real session journals - and is what any "open my latest journal" workflow may pick up. T12 deletes all six of its files and all three of its sessions; T10 deletes nothing.
findings.evidence: CSSRJournal::ExportCsv does `FolderCreate(SSR_JOURNAL_DIR)` then writes SSR_JOURNAL_DIR + "\\" + name + ".csv" (SSR_Journal.mqh:171-176) with name = "t10". Section T10.8 opens the file for reading, FileCloses it (line 570) and ends without a FileDelete; no other line of T10 mentions FileDelete.

performance_notes: T13.4 and T13.5 each run 4000 Pump(1000) calls with a full observer chain (account + stats + market view + strategy host) over a 4320-bar ramp. At the default 1x speed that is ~66 replay minutes and ~8 synthetic ticks per minute, so roughly 530 ticks fanned out to 3-4 observers per section - the heaviest loop in this subsystem and the one most sensitive to a change in the default speed (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:53). If the default ever moves to the product's InpStartSpeed of 30x, the same 4000 pumps become ~33 replay hours and T13.4's `bar_calls >= 8 && <= 16` becomes ~400.

T11.1 draws 10000 + 2000 + 1500 random numbers and T11.10 runs `for(int i = 0; i < 2000 && !g.AllCompleted(); i++) g.Pump(1000)` over a two-stream group; both are bounded and cheap, but the 2000-iteration completion loop is the only place in the subsystem that relies on a break condition rather than a fixed count - if AllCompleted never turns true it costs 2000 pumps x 2 streams before failing.

T10 is the cheapest file per assertion by a wide margin: ~129 assertions with no controller, no seeding and no sink - ticks are injected one at a time through a 1-element MqlTick array. It is the model to copy for any new arithmetic-level test.

T15.8/T15.9/T15.10 each construct and destroy a full CSSRPanel on a live chart (three Create->Render->Destroy cycles). Each Create calls m_w.RemoveAll() and a full Render; with the property cache cold that is the ~561-property-write repaint the project measured at 39 ms, so the section is real work on the terminal's UI thread, not a unit test.

T13.1's fast-vs-slow Extremes() cross-check runs 20 (shift, count) combinations and re-derives each with Bar() calls - deliberately O(n^2)-ish, and the right trade: it is the only assertion in the subsystem that compares an optimised implementation against the definition it replaced.
test_gaps: No aggregate runner and no machine-readable verdict. Each script prints GREEN/RED to the Experts log and returns nothing; there is no SSR_T0_All.mq5 that runs T1..T15, no exit code and no summary file, so 'all tests pass' cannot be established in one action - and on a terminal the author never uses, the two guaranteed-failing assertions (tests-b-1, tests-b-2) would otherwise be caught in seconds.

The harness is copied seven times. A fix to Check (e.g. adding a fail-fast, a section name to the failure line, or an assertion counter per section) has to be made in seven files, and the helper set already differs between them (CheckStr in T12/T15 only, CheckExact in T12 only, no CheckNear in T11).
