No assertion anywhere in T9-T15 covers CSSRPropEvaluation (prop-firm daily/total/trailing drawdown, min/max days - an entire Trading module with five inputs), CSSRShotBook, CSSRFlightRecorder, CSSRTradeAutoPause's SSR_PAUSE_ON_ENTRY path being *taken* (T12.6 only asserts it does NOT fire), CSSRChartManager/leak guard, CSSRTradeLines, CSSRCalendarLines/news pause, CSSRSetupPanel, CSSRRangeDialog, CSSRSessionDialog, CSSRKeyCard, CSSRRevealCard, CSSRReviewCard or CSSRFirstRun.

Nothing in this subsystem asserts a rendered string's length against MetaTrader's 63-character draw limit, nor anything about SSR_Strings/T(SSR_S_*) or the fa.txt UTF-8 loader. T15 is the only file that touches the UI and it reads coordinates and command mappings, never text extents. The 63-char rule is enforced statically (audit A19) but never at runtime, where a translated string is assembled.

Statistics coverage stops at the arithmetic that T10.2 computes by hand. risk_spread_pct, revenge_trades, avg_spread_points, worst_spread_points, wide_spread_trades, recovery_factor, time_in_market_pct and avg_hold_sec are never asserted anywhere in T9-T15, although they are the coaching metrics the product is differentiated on and SSRStatistics::Init lists all of them.

Fidelity is only ever exercised as SYNTHETIC_TICK (plus T9.6's default). No section in T9-T15 replays the same trade under SSR_FIDELITY_BAR or SSR_FIDELITY_FULL_TICK, so the claim that fidelity decides whether a stop can be hit intrabar at all - and T10.3b's distinction between assumed and observed tick order - is never tested across the switch that causes it.

Multi-symbol trading is asserted only as a limitation. T15.3 checks that the board NAMES the primary stream; nothing asserts what happens when a user presses BUY while a secondary stream is under the cursor, and no section attaches the account to more than one controller.

T12's session round trip never covers a file written by an older build (only a newer one, T12.1), a truncated or half-written file, or a session whose symbol list is longer than the group that is rebuilt (the `saved_streams != m_group.Count()` warning path at SSR_SessionManager.mqh:319 is never triggered).

T14 exercises the client/publisher pair inside one process with hand-driven Send/Poll. Nothing covers two processes, a client that dies mid-command (a stale CMD_SEQ with no ACK), or two publishers claiming the same slot - and the heartbeat test fabricates staleness by writing the GV rather than by not pumping.

Every fixture is a flat or linearly ramping market with no gaps, no weekends, no session breaks and a constant spread. Nothing in T9-T15 replays a bar series with a missing minute, a Friday-to-Monday gap or a widening spread, so the swap-per-replay-day logic (T10.5) is tested only on an unbroken 6-hour-step clock and CSSRSessionWatcher's gap detection (T11.6) is tested only on hand-written ticks, never through the controller.

key_facts: The QA subsystem is five procedural scripts, no classes of its own. SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5 (5512 lines) assembles the real product classes in the real order across stages 1-43 (there is no stage 34); SSR_QA_Preflight.mq5 (716) gates the terminal in 6 sections; SSR_Z_Cleanup.mq5 (145) sweeps symbols/charts/globals; SSR_Z_Gaps.mq5 (86) reports broker M1 holes; SSR_QA_FontProbe.mq5 (348) probes the font.

Smoke's reporting surface is Ok/No/Check/Note/Step/Log/Done. Check(what,cond,detail) returns cond so stages gate on it; Note() moves NEITHER counter and is the file's deliberate way of saying 'this went unmeasured'. Ok/No move g_pass/g_fail. Every line is Print+Comment+FileWriteString+FileFlush to SSReplay\qa-result.txt (FILE_SHARE_READ, with a timestamped fallback name when the usual one is locked).

Documented invariant at SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:231-255: never put a mutating call in Check's cond argument, because MQL5 builds `detail` before it evaluates `cond` (v90 shipped six PASS lines whose evidence strings were all lies).

Bars() answers from a cache, so every bar-count comparison on the replay symbol is preceded by a CopyRates poke loop (20 x 50ms) or Sleep(250/300). The origin symbol's M1 count at line 396 is the one read with no poke.

The panel hides by OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES == OBJ_NO_PERIODS (encoded in QVisible at line 312); switching tabs REMOVES the other sheet's objects (CSSRPanel::HideSheets deletes, it does not hide), so the label-overlap sweep at line 4670 cannot see stale sheets in full mode.

The frame-overflow instrument reads the frame off the panel's own background rectangle (SSRQ_bg / SSRE_bg / SSRT_bg) rather than from a layout constant, and substitutes 12px for an OBJ_LABEL's zero OBJPROP_YSIZE. Stages 18, 38 and 39 each run their own copy of that loop.

LabelBox/LabelOverlaps (lines 5308-5402) measure real pixel widths with TextSetFont(font, -fontsize*10, 0, 0) + TextGetSize, O(n^2) pairwise, 1px tolerance, skipping <prefix>fill* because the toast is an overlay by design. Stage 40 first probes that TextGetSize works at all and emits a Note rather than passing silently if it does not.

Preflight deliberately does NOT extrapolate: it writes 3 x InpBenchBars (50,000) forward and disjoint, stops the clock when the last bar becomes READABLE (polling CopyRates with a 15s deadline) rather than when CustomRatesUpdate returns, quotes the slowest pass, and labels a 288,000-bar figure 'MEASURED' or 'extrapolates ... treat it as an estimate'.
Preflight asks CopyRates twice (up to 30 x 500ms) because a cold symbol answers -1; SSR_QA_Smoke does not do the equivalent for its one history read.

Smoke moves the user's files aside (Stash/Unstash via FileMove ... FILE_REWRITE) for setup.ini, panel.ini, presets.ini and seen.txt - but the panel.ini stash covers only stages 17-19 and 40, while stages 38, 39 and 42 also drive real panels.

SSR_Z_Cleanup's ordering is load-bearing and mirrors CSSRCustomSymbolManager::Destroy: close charts -> deselect -> wait -> delete, because a symbol selected in Market Watch cannot be deleted (error 5306). A refusal is reported BY NAME with the remedy, on the chart as well as in the log.

CSSRCustomSymbolManager.mqh:383 sets SYMBOL_CHART_MODE to BID on the product's replay symbol and verifies it took; SSR_QA_Preflight never sets it on its own test symbol, so the preflight validates a differently-configured symbol from the one the product creates.

CSSRPropEvaluation::DailyUsed()/TotalUsed() (SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:237-262) read Equity() live, so stage 38's clamp check at line 4029 is genuinely exercised by SetBalance alone without a further OnClock - it is NOT a stale read.

CSSRTradingEngine::ClosePartial books an exit LEG on the same position rather than a second closed trade (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:904), which is why stage 17's hardcoded expectation sb.trades==2 / sf.trades==1 is arithmetically correct.

CSSRPanel::Dispatch("move") and Dispatch("palette") both still work programmatically but are documented in SSR_Panel.mqh:2603 and :2747 as idle - 'NO OBJECT SENDS THIS ANY MORE'. Stage 19 drives the first and stage 33 the second, so both stages report PASS for surfaces no chart control reaches.

findings.title: The smoke harness aborts the entire run on an unprimed M1 series, and the priming call is the very next line
findings.claim: Drop SSR_QA_Smoke on an M5 (or H1, or D1) chart of a symbol whose M1 series has not been touched in this terminal session - the ordinary case, because nothing forces MetaTrader to build M1 for a chart that is not M1. Bars(origin, PERIOD_M1) returns 0 on that first read whether or not the bars exist, the Check fails, Done() runs and returns, and the harness reports '0 passed, 1 FAILED / 0 bars local, 600 needed' from a terminal on which the whole product works.
findings.evidence: This is the project's own documented trap (overview lesson 7: 'MetaTrader builds a timeframe series lazily - the first read always returns zero, and zero there means "no series yet", not "no bars". This cost an entire build.'). tools/ssr_audit.py's A21 exempts PERIOD_M1 from its priming rule, but its stated reason is 'M1 is exempt because M1 is what this program WRITES - the writes build that series themselves' - which is true of the replay symbol and NOT true of `origin`, the broker symbol, which this program only reads. The priming read exists nine lines later (line 409, CopyRates(origin, PERIOD_M1, 0, InpReplayBars, back)) but is unreachable because the Check aborts first. SSR_QA_Preflight.mq5:191-201 handles exactly this case for the same symbol with an ask-twice loop and a 15-second wait, so the two harnesses disagree about a known hazard.

findings.title: Preflight's only tick check counts acceptance and never asks whether a bar was built - the exact signal the project measured as meaningless
findings.claim: Run the preflight on an index or futures CFD (SYMBOL_CHART_MODE_LAST). CustomSymbolCreate clones that chart mode onto the test symbol, the preflight never overrides it, and the 100 ticks it adds carry flags TICK_FLAG_BID|TICK_FLAG_ASK only (line 395). MetaTrader accepts all 100, so the script prints 'OK custom ticks 100 accepted' and the run ends in 'VERDICT: GO' - on a terminal and symbol class where the replay will advance its clock, emit its ticks and produce no candle at all. The one script whose whole purpose is 'fail in ninety seconds instead of after two hours of debugging' cannot see the failure that took the longest to find.
findings.evidence: The check reads the return count and nothing else; there is no CopyRates or Bars read after the CustomTicksAdd anywhere in section 4 (lines 383-420), so 'the terminal took every tick and built nothing from them' is indistinguishable from success. The project has measured that exact case: SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:463-467 quotes '60 calls offered ticks, the terminal took 481, refused 0, and the M1 series stayed at 139 bars', and the overview names it as lesson 6. The product itself guards it - CSSRCustomSymbolManager.mqh:383 writes CustomSymbolSetInteger(m_symbol, SYMBOL_CHART_MODE, SYMBOL_CHART_MODE_BID) and then reads it back to check it took - and SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:473-481 asserts it on the replay symbol. The preflight, which runs first and gates everything, asserts neither the chart mode nor a resulting bar.

findings.title: Preflight gates its whole custom-symbol round trip on SYMBOL_DIGITS > 0, so a zero-digit instrument silently skips the section and leaks the test symbol
findings.claim: Run the preflight on an instrument quoted in whole units (SYMBOL_DIGITS == 0 - common for index CFDs and exchange futures). CustomSymbolCreate succeeds and clones digits 0, so the guard is false and lines 312-439 never run: no OK, no LIMIT and no BLOCKER is printed for create, select, the 500-bar write, the read-back, the M5 derivation, the ticks or the chart, the summary counts none of them, and the verdict is still 'GO'. The cleanup (lines 429-438) is inside the same block, so SSRPreflight.SSR9 is left behind, selected. On the next run line 294 makes the same mistake in the other direction: `bool exists = (SymbolInfoInteger(test, SYMBOL_DIGITS) > 0 && GetLastError() == 0)` is false for that leftover, so the adopt path is skipped and the script prints 'BLOCKER custom symbol create error 5304 - without this NOTHING in this product works' and 'VERDICT: NO GO' over its own litter.
findings.evidence: Both tests use digits > 0 as a proxy for 'the symbol is there', and digits is a legitimate zero. The comment block at lines 267-281 says the adopt path exists precisely because 'Being unable to start because of a previous crash is not an acceptable answer' - the proxy defeats it on this symbol class. SYMBOL_EXIST or SYMBOL_CUSTOM would answer the question the code is actually asking; SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:446-449 uses exactly those two.

findings.title: Stage 22d reports two PASSes for calendar lines that were never drawn
findings.claim: On a terminal whose server publishes no economic calendar - which stage 22c explicitly anticipates and reports as a NOTE - cal.Count() is 0. CSSRCalendarLines::Draw returns 0 without creating anything (SSR_CalendarLines.mqh: the loop runs cal.Count() times) and Clear() returns 0 because ObjectsDeleteAll found nothing. Both conditions reduce to 0 == 0, so the report carries 'PASS drawing twice draws each line once 0 created, 0 on the second pass' and 'PASS and clearing takes them all back 0 object(s) removed'. Idempotence and cleanup - the two properties the stage names - are untested, and the run's pass count says otherwise.
findings.evidence: 22d sits after the `else` block closes at line 2306, so it runs whether or not cal.Load() succeeded, unlike 22b and 22c. The file holds itself to the opposite standard four lines above: 'a stage that quietly passed because there was nothing to test would be the most misleading line in the report' (2239-2241), and 22c acts on it with a Note. 22d has no such guard, and Note() exists for exactly this.

findings.title: The blind-mode restore check cannot see a chart left with no price scale, and goes vacuous entirely when the template has OHLC off
findings.code:
Check("blind mode hides what the chart announces",
            !(bool)ChartGetInteger(probe2, CHART_SHOW_OHLC) &&
            !(bool)ChartGetInteger(probe2, CHART_SHOW_PRICE_SCALE),
      blind.RestoreAll();
      Check("and puts the chart back the way it was",
            (bool)ChartGetInteger(probe2, CHART_SHOW_OHLC) == had_ohlc,
findings.claim: Apply asserts two properties; restore asserts one. If CSSRBlindMode::RestoreAll ever fails to put CHART_SHOW_PRICE_SCALE back, the stage still reports 'PASS and puts the chart back the way it was' and the user's chart is left with no price axis - the exact 'a mode you cannot leave is a trap' outcome the check's own detail string claims to rule out. Worse, on a terminal whose default template already has the OHLC line off (a common preference, and the default in several shipped MetaTrader profiles), had_ohlc is false, so the restore assertion is false == false and holds no matter what RestoreAll did to anything.
findings.evidence: The restore comparison names only CHART_SHOW_OHLC, while the Apply comparison names CHART_SHOW_OHLC and CHART_SHOW_PRICE_SCALE; the price scale is the property whose pre-state is never captured and never re-compared. Stage 36 repeats the same asymmetry at lines 3700-3702 (back > 0 && !bl.IsApplied() && CHART_SHOW_OHLC == had_ohlc). Capturing had_scale beside had_ohlc at line 1130 and comparing both would close it; the stage already knows how, because that is what it does for OHLC.

findings.title: The opening leftover sweep and the closing Cleanup() can close the chart the script itself is running on, killing the suite in the shape of the hang it was written to diagnose
findings.claim: Drop SSR_QA_Smoke on a replay chart whose symbol ends in the tail this run uses - e.g. a leftover <origin>.SSR9 chart from a previous run, or any chart of slot N when the user sets InpSlot=N to test their real session. The sweep walks ChartFirst/ChartNext with no ChartID() exclusion, closes that chart, and MetaTrader terminates the script that was running on it. qa-result.txt then holds three lines and stops, the Comment vanishes with the chart, and from outside that is indistinguishable from the freeze the file spends sixty lines of comments (121-196, 265-279) building instrumentation for. Cleanup() at line 5472 has the same shape at the other end (`if(ChartSymbol(id) == rsym) ChartClose(id);`) and runs before Done(), so a self-close there costs the totals line and leaves g_fh unclosed.
findings.evidence: Neither loop compares id against ChartID(). The sweep's own comment (344-347) argues the danger away on the basis of the default slot ('ONLY the slot this run uses - 9 by default, chosen to stay away from real sessions'), but the slot is an input and the tail is built from it at line 350, so the guard is a default rather than a rule. One `if(id == ChartID()) { id = nxt; continue; }` in each loop closes it.

findings.title: Stage 7 increments the pass count with no condition tested
findings.code: Ok("manager redraws on demand", "Redraw(force) returned");
findings.claim: This is the only unconditional Ok() in the file and it asserts nothing: reaching the line is the whole of its evidence, which is implied by control flow. It adds one to g_pass on every run, so the headline '=== N passed, 0 FAILED ===' overstates what was measured by one, and a reader scanning the report sees a named property ('the manager redraws on demand') that no code checked. CSSRChartManager::Redraw's return value or Snaps() delta is available two lines above and is what the neighbouring checks use.
findings.evidence: grep for '^\s*Ok(' in this file returns two hits: this line and 2207, and 2207 is guarded by if(cal.Available()). Every other assertion in 5512 lines goes through Check(what, cond, detail). The file's own rule for an unmeasurable property is Note(), which moves neither counter (lines 262-263, used at 1789, 2212, 4153, 4390, 4464, 4609, 4646, 4731, 4980, 5057, 5075).

findings.title: The compact-mode assertion in stage 18 re-implements the production expression, so it cannot fail
findings.claim: CSSRPanel decides the mode with m_compact = (chart_h > 0 && chart_h < SSR_PANEL_H + 24) (SSR_Panel.mqh:679). The check compares IsCompact() against a character-for-character copy of that same expression over the same chart height, so it is an identity: whatever the panel chooses, including a wrong threshold, a wrong comparison direction or a wrong constant, the check passes. It reports PASS on a property nothing independent established, and a future change to the threshold would be mirrored in the test by whoever copies it again.
findings.evidence: Line 679 of SSR_Panel.mqh and line 1668 here are the same predicate on the same inputs; pch is read at line 1659 from the same CHART_HEIGHT_IN_PIXELS the panel reads in Render(). A check with independent content would be behavioural - e.g. that the tab strip exists in full mode and does not in compact (which the compact branch already does at 1783-1787 for its half), or that PanelH() equals SSR_PANEL_COMPACT_H when compact.

findings.title: Three stages drive real panels outside the panel.ini stash window, so a smoke run still eats the user's saved tab
findings.code:
pp.Dispatch("tab4");
         pp.Render();
findings.claim: Stash(SSR_PANEL_FILE) is called at line 1344 and undone at 1886, then called again at 4595 and undone at 4742. Between those windows, stage 38 dispatches "tab4" (line 4194), stage 39 dispatches "tab1" (4400) and twice sends SSR_VK_P (4446, 4558), and stage 42 dispatches "tab2" (5095). CSSRPanel::Dispatch writes the file on any tab change (SSR_Panel.mqh:2578-2582 -> SavePlace()) and SSR_CMD_PANEL_SIZE does the same (2349-2353), and SavePlace() is live because Create() called RestorePlace() (348), which sets m_place_loaded. So a run that finishes leaves MQL5\Files\SSReplay\panel.ini holding tab=2 (stage 42's last write) instead of whatever tab the user had chosen, and reports PASS throughout.
findings.evidence: The file opens with the rule it is breaking: 'A TEST MUST NOT EAT THE USER'S SETTINGS ... running the smoke test threw away whatever the user had typed into the setup panel, and told them PASS while doing it' (lines 76-84), and stage 19's own comment repeats it ('a QA run that resets the user's own layout has done more harm than the stage is worth', 1808-1809). Moving the Stash to just before stage 17 and the Unstash to after stage 42 - or stashing once around the whole panel-driving range - would cover it.

findings.title: SSR_Z_Cleanup closes the chart of any broker symbol whose name starts with SSR
findings.claim: The first test matches any symbol name beginning with the three letters SSR, not just the fifteen spike symbols the script owns. SSRM is a live exchange ticker (SSR Mining Inc., NASDAQ/TSX) and is carried by brokers that offer share CFDs; SSRT, SSRN and similar prefixed names exist too. A user with an SSRM chart open who runs the cleanup after a test session loses that chart with no warning, and the script reports it as 'charts closed=1' among its own.
findings.evidence: The spike symbols are enumerated exactly in g_syms[] at lines 15-17 and the product's own names are recognised by SSRIsReplaySymbol / the .SSR suffix (SSR_SymbolNaming.mqh:74-77), so both sets are already addressable precisely. The symbol-DELETE loops are correctly narrow - line 71 requires '.SSR' and line 85 walks g_syms[] by name - which makes the chart loop the only place a name outside the script's ownership is acted on. Testing against g_syms[] membership or requiring the '.SSR' suffix would make the two halves agree.

findings.title: SSR_Z_Cleanup reports 'nothing of ours is left behind' while two of the product's own global variables survive its prefix sweep
findings.claim: The sweep uses the prefix "SSR." with a dot, which matches the integration transport (SSR_GV_PREFIX is "SSR.", SSR_Contract.mqh:50) but not CSSRSetupPanel's two globals, which are named SSR_SETUP_X and SSR_SETUP_Y with an underscore (SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:1008-1009). MetaTrader persists global variables across terminal restarts, so after a cleanup that prints 'nothing of ours is left behind' the setup panel's saved screen position is still there, and the next measurement run starts on top of a leftover the script has just declared absent - the precise condition the file's header says it exists to prevent ('Run this between full test runs so numbers are never measured on top of a previous run's leftovers').
findings.evidence: GlobalVariablesDeleteAll matches on prefix, and "SSR_SETUP_X" does not begin with "SSR.". The gv count printed at line 105 therefore excludes them while the closing sentence claims completeness. A second GlobalVariablesDeleteAll("SSR_") - or naming the two directly - would make the report true.

findings.title: SSR_Z_Gaps can report more than 100% of minutes present, and InpMinRun=0 turns every bar into a hole
findings.claim: CopyRates with a start_time/stop_time pair is inclusive of both ends, so the default range 11:00..12:00 returns 61 bars for a span computed as 60 minutes and the script prints '61 bars across 60 minutes (101.7% present)'. The whole point of this script is to be the arbiter of whether missing candles are the broker's fault, and a coverage figure above 100% undermines the one number the reader is being asked to trust. Separately, InpMinRun is used unclamped: set it to 0 and every consecutive pair of bars has gap == 0 >= 0, so the script reports n-1 'holes', prints twenty lines reading 'HOLE 0 minute(s) missing after ...', and then concludes 'A replay crossing these will show the clock moving with no new candle' about a range with no holes in it at all.
findings.evidence: span counts intervals while n counts bars over an inclusive range, so n == span + 1 on a complete range - (InpTo - InpFrom)/60 + 1 is the matching denominator. The gap test at line 63 has no lower bound on InpMinRun, and the input's comment ('Report holes of at least this many minutes') does not describe 0 as a value; a MathMax(1, InpMinRun) at the top of OnStart matches the documented intent.

findings.title: Stage 18's compact assertion checks tab0 and tabline only, and can never reach the fifth tab that the panel's hide list omits
findings.code:
Check("and dropped only what is consulted",
                  !QVisible(pchart, "SSRQ_tab0") &&
                  !QVisible(pchart, "SSRQ_tabline"),
findings.claim: CSSRPanel::HideSheetArea hides a written-out list "tab0","tab1","tab2","tab3","tabline" (SSR_Panel.mqh:2044) - the same shape of hand-kept list that, per this file's own stage 43 header, once left 'a lone Prop tab further down' on the candles when HideBody was written the same way. A panel that was full (so tab4 exists) on a chart that then shrinks below the threshold would leave tab4 visible with the sheet gone. Stage 18 cannot detect that in either direction: it asserts only tab0 and tabline, and its panel is created with a NULL port (line 1663), so there is never an evaluation, never a fifth tab, and never anything for the missing list entry to leave behind.
findings.evidence: HideBody at SSR_Panel.mqh:2091 was fixed to loop `for(int t = 0; t < SSR_TAB_MAX; t++)` with the comment 'This list said tab0..tab3 and Phase 8 added a fifth tab'; HideSheetArea twelve lines earlier still writes the four out. The QA check that would have caught it enumerates two names and runs against a portless panel, so the regression the file documents as already paid for once is uncovered on the compact path. Looping the assertion over SSR_TAB_MAX, and building this stage's panel with the same port stage 38 uses, would cover it.

findings.title: Stage 19 drives a control that no longer exists and blames the chart when its evidence comes back empty
findings.claim: The stage's comment says it moves the panel 'the way a user without a mouse on this chart would: the Move button, twice', but CSSRPanel documents that button as gone - 'NO OBJECT SENDS THIS ANY MORE. The [] button was removed on request; the handler stays so putting it back is one line' (SSR_Panel.mqh:2603-2604). The PASS lines 'moving the panel leaves a file behind' and 'a new panel starts where the old one stopped' therefore describe a path no user can take, and a reader of the report concludes panel repositioning works when the product currently offers no way to reposition it at all. When x and y do not change the stage prints a single explanation - 'this chart reports no size, so the panel never left the corner' - which is only one of the two reasons; the other is that SnapToCorner moved nothing the user could have asked for.
findings.evidence: Dispatch("move") still calls SnapToCorner() + SavePlace(), so the stage does exercise real persistence code and its corner/tab round trip is genuine; the defect is that the stage's stated subject and its printed diagnosis both name a user action that was removed in v125. Renaming the stage to what it measures (corner/tab persistence through Dispatch) and adding the second possible cause to the `moved == false` note would make the report honest without losing coverage.

findings.title: Stage 12's closed-trade prices are in whole units, the mistake the comment six lines above says was fixed
findings.code: lines.DrawClosed(777, t1 - 600, lpx, t1, lpx + 3.0, true, 0.10, 42.0);
findings.claim: The exit price is the entry plus 3.0 whole units. On EURUSD that is 4.15965 against an entry of 1.15965 - a level thousands of points off the chart's range. CSSRTradeLines::DrawClosed accepts it (it only rejects prices <= 0), so the arrow and the line between the two are created and 'a closed trade leaves history on the chart' passes; but what was drawn is off-screen, so the stage cannot observe the property the class's own comment block cares about ('the arrows were drawn, correctly placed and the right colours - and at their default size they read as two specks on a candle ... "it draws" was true while "you can see it" was not'). The same call also seeds the R value 42.0 against a 3.0-unit move, so any future assertion on the label would be measuring nonsense.
findings.evidence: Lines 1006-1014 in this same stage state the rule and the cost of breaking it - 'OFFSETS IN POINTS, NOT IN WHOLE UNITS. This said lpx - 5.0. On gold at 4438 that is a stop below the entry; on EURUSD at 1.15965 it is MINUS 3.84 ... three stages failed and named the product' - and line 1016 duly uses lpx - 500 * pt and lpx + 1000 * pt. The DrawClosed call seven lines later was not converted. `pt` is already in scope from line 914.

performance_notes: SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:198-223 - Log() calls Comment() on every single line. With ~250 logged lines that is ~250 chart comment writes plus 250 FileWriteString+FileFlush pairs. Deliberate (the chart is the freeze indicator and the flush survives a crash), and cheap next to the chart work, but it is the one per-line cost in the harness.

SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:5263-5265 - OpenChart's retry waits with a busy spin, not Sleep: `uint until = GetTickCount() + 600; while(GetTickCount() < until && !IsStopped()) ;`. That is 600 ms of a core at 100% per retry, and GetTickCount() + 600 wraps every ~49.7 days of uptime (a wrap inside the window makes `until` small and the wait collapse to nothing). Sleep(600) costs nothing and yields.

SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:5346-5402 - LabelOverlaps is O(n^2) pairwise over every prefixed OBJ_LABEL, and is run four times in stage 40 (once per sheet) plus once in the compact branch. With ~120 labels that is ~7,100 comparisons per sheet, each on pre-measured boxes, so the cost is the n TextGetSize calls per sheet rather than the pairs. Not hot, but it is the only super-linear loop in the file.

SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:5069-5078 - stage 42 calls Render() 20 times to report a mean repaint. At the pre-cache figure the project measured (561 property writes = 39.05 ms) that is up to ~800 ms of the run, deliberately spent to produce the number.

SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5 sleeps, summed: 300 (sweep) + 120x2 (stage 7) + 250 (8) + 300 (9) + 3 x 550 (10) + 80x2 (13) + 50 (25c) = ~3.4 s of fixed waiting, plus the poke loops at 609-618 and 3318-3327 (up to 20 x 50 ms each) and up to 22 OpenChart/ChartClose pairs.

SSR_QA_Preflight.mq5:483-616 - section 5 is the expensive half by design: ArrayResize(b, InpBenchBars) is a 50,000-element MqlRates array (~3 MB) filled three times, three CustomRatesUpdate calls at warmup scale, up to 15 s of Sleep(1) polling per pass waiting for the last bar to become readable, then 500 single-bar CustomRatesUpdate calls. The 500-call loop is the one true hot path and is the point of the measurement (the bulk-versus-stream ratio at line 636-641).

SSR_QA_Preflight.mq5:169-173 - the cold-history wait is up to 30 x Sleep(500) = 15 s before it gives up, and section 4's read-back loops add up to 20 x Sleep(200) twice. A terminal with no M1 downloaded spends ~23 s in section 3 alone, which is within the script's own 'ninety seconds' budget.

SSR_Z_Cleanup.mq5:74 and :88 - Sleep(120) per '.SSR' symbol and Sleep(60) per spike symbol, plus a flat Sleep(500) after the chart pass. With the 15 spike names that is ~1.4 s; the 61-iteration length-probe loop at lines 95-100 builds strings up to 64 characters and issues 61 CustomSymbolDelete calls with no sleep, which is negligible.
test_gaps: Neither harness ever writes ticks and then asks whether a BAR appeared on a symbol whose chart mode was not forced to BID. The smoke asserts SYMBOL_CHART_MODE == BID on the replay symbol (473-481) and asserts the synthesiser sets TICK_FLAG_LAST (493-518), but the negative case - what the terminal does with a tick the chart mode cannot use - is only ever reported after the fact by TickVerdict(); nothing provokes it deliberately.

Fidelity is never varied. Every stage runs the default synthetic path; SSR_FIDELITY_FULL_TICK and SSR_FIDELITY_BAR are never selected, so 'whether a stop can be hit intrabar at all' - the setting the overview flags with a warning - is unmeasured end to end. Preflight only reports whether tick history exists (lines 221-232).

The reused-seed jump path says out loud that it is uncovered ('written fresh - the reused-seed path is NOT covered by this run', 819-822) and nothing in the suite arranges a reused seed, even though stage 31 already tears the session down and reloads the same slot and could.

Stage 18 builds its panel with a NULL port, so the Positions, Stats and Session sheets are measured with no account behind them and the Prop sheet cannot exist at all. The prop sheet's frame is covered only by stage 38, and the Positions row's populated columns only by stages 39 and 40.

Nothing asserts that Stash/Unstash actually restored anything. If FileMove fails - the file is open in an editor, or the .qabak already exists and the delete failed - Unstash silently leaves the QA file in place and the user's aside, and no check notices.

The suite never asserts its own cleanliness at the end. Cleanup()'s failure is a NOTE, not a FAIL, and nothing counts leftover charts, symbols or files after Done(); the sweep at the start of the NEXT run is the only thing that would report it.

Stage 33 exercises CSSRPalette thoroughly but never asserts that anything can open it. The palette has no entry in the SSRKeyBindings table (so stage 29's card and duplicate checks cannot see it) and CSSRPanel's "palette" dispatch is documented as idle since the K button was removed (SSR_Panel.mqh:2747); only a hardcoded Ctrl+K in OnEvent (2828-2833) remains. A reachability assertion - the palette is either in the key table or reachable from a drawn object - is the check that would distinguish a working surface from a working-but-orphaned one.

The report file is never checked for completeness, only for readability. Stage 30 reads the first line back (3275-3279); nothing verifies that the SLOW lines written at 218-220 exist only in the file and never in the log pane, or that g_out_n (which excludes the SLOW lines) matches the line count the closing message quotes.

SSR_Z_Gaps has no counterpart for tick history. It can prove the broker had the minutes, which answers 'the clock moved and no candle appeared', but nothing answers the same question for CopyTicksRange when FULL_TICK fidelity is selected.

Preflight never checks the two symbol properties the smoke treats as decisive: SYMBOL_CHART_MODE and a seven-day quote session on the symbol it creates. It can therefore return GO on a symbol class for which the smoke's stages 5-9 will all fail, which inverts the intended order of the two scripts.

No stage runs the suite twice in one terminal session. Stage 31 re-loads the replay, which is the engine half, but the harness's own file handling (qa-result.txt still open, .qabak files, a leftover test symbol) is only exercised across separate invocations, and the fallback filename path at SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:160-178 is never exercised at all.

key_facts: The whole suite's PASS/FAIL rests on one invariant in SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:181-191: SSR_End() prints 'SPIKE PASS' iff g_ssr_fail==0. A spike that records no SSR_Verdict at all therefore reports SPIKE PASS. Two spikes (B3, D1) print their documented PASS gate with Print() instead of asserting it.

The kit contains four wait primitives and which one a spike picks is the dominant source of bad numbers: SSR_WaitSeries (SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED, documented at kit:390-417 as 'a timer, not work' - observed at 0.002ms, 9,200ms and never), SSR_WaitLastBar, SSR_WaitLastBarBefore and SSR_WaitReadable (all 'ask the data, not the flag'). D1 and D4 were converted to the data-based waits; A3 and D2 still time the flag.

SSR_Rate/SSR_RateMetric (kit:351-388) exist because B2 once published 10.5 billion ticks/second by dividing ticks SENT by the microseconds a total rejection took. SSR_RateMetric hardcodes the unit 'ticks/s', so bar-rate metrics cannot be routed through the guard - and A2:133 and D1:101-104 both compute bars/s outside it, from the requested count rather than the accepted count.

SSR_BarToTicks (kit:562-599) interpolates along three segments with u = i*3/(cnt-1). It lands a tick exactly on the bar's high and low only when (cnt-1) % 3 == 0. cnt=4,7,10,13,16,19 hit the extremes; cnt=8 (the engine's default InpTicksPerBar) and cnt=20 (B1's default InpPerBar) do not. The product's CSSRTickSynthesizer::Synthesize (Core/SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:134-143) uses the identical formula while its header claims 'The OHLC of the resulting bar is exact'.

Neither SSR_MakeSymbol nor any spike sets SYMBOL_CHART_MODE, and the kit's tick generator emits flags = TICK_FLAG_BID|TICK_FLAG_ASK with no TICK_FLAG_LAST. The product does both (CustomSymbolManager.mqh:383 forces SYMBOL_CHART_MODE_BID; TickSynthesizer.mqh:175 adds TICK_FLAG_LAST) after measuring '481 ticks accepted, 0 bars built' on a LAST-mode symbol. grep confirms SYMBOL_CHART_MODE appears nowhere under MQL5/*/Spike/.

The 21 audits in tools/ssr_audit.py run silent across 123 files, exit 0 (verified by running it). Three views of every file are prebuilt: FILES (raw), CLEAN (comments AND string literals blanked), KEEPSTR (comments blanked, literals length-preserved), plus a per-audit _decomment (comments out, strings kept).

A18 and A19 each carry an explicit guard against the vacuous pass (declared<20 contrast pairs; fewer than 100 resolved T(SSR_S_...) calls). A14 and A20 have no such guard, and A19's language-file half is literally dead code: langdir = os.path.join(ROOT,'MQL5','Files','SSReplay','lang') while ROOT already ends in MQL5, so os.path.isdir() is False and the only check of translated string length never runs.

A20 matches only the exact shape '^   void (Render|Repaint)\(void\)$' - three spaces, no const, no arguments. It covers 8 functions in 7 Ui files. SSR_FirstRun.mqh and SSR_KeyCard.mqh each draw 5 labels from a function named Show() and are invisible to it (both happen to call ChartRedraw today).

A19's literal-text check is restricted to files with '/Ui/' in the path, so the 7 ObjectSetString(...OBJPROP_TEXT) calls in Experts/SSReplay/SSReplayStandalone.mq5 and the 2 in Chart/SSR_TradeLines.mqh are outside its i18n scope (A14's regex does still measure their length when the text is a bare literal).

Spike outputs are three shared append-only CSVs under MQL5/Files/SSR_Spike (env.csv, results.csv, verdicts.csv) plus d3_timeseries.csv, c2_heartbeat.csv and c1_service_probe.txt. SSR_Append opens with FILE_SHARE_READ only - no FILE_SHARE_WRITE - while B2, D1 and D3 all instruct the operator to run SSR_Probe_UIJitter concurrently, and that probe writes to the same results.csv every 10 s.

SSR_DropSymbol closes every chart whose ChartSymbol() equals the symbol (kit:213-224), which silently invalidates a chart id the caller is still holding. D4:106 hits exactly that: its chart, opened on M5 at line 82, is destroyed before strategies 2 and 3 run.

The metrics that feed product decisions are named in the spikes' own notes: A1 max_symbol_name_length -> the <SRC>.SSR<slot> naming convention; A3 avg_rebuild_time -> 'feeds the Reset budget'; B2 optimal_batch_size -> 'lock this into Feeder'; B4 copyticksrange_week_return -> 'sets the page size for TickSource'; D1 bars_per_sec -> 'the number the user waits for'; D4 step_back_interactive -> whether Previous Candle is a button.

findings.title: SSR_BarToTicks never emits a tick at the bar's high or low unless (n-1) is divisible by 3
findings.claim: The keypoints k[1] (one extreme) and k[2] (the other) are only reproduced exactly when some i gives u == 1.0 and u == 2.0, i.e. when (cnt-1) % 3 == 0. With cnt = 20 (B1's InpPerBar default) u steps by 3/19 and the nearest values are 1.8947/2.0526, so the synthesised stream reaches at most H - 0.0526*(H-C) and at least L + 0.0526*(O-L) on a bullish bar. The tick stream therefore reports a narrower bar than the bar it was built from, and no spike measures that error.
findings.evidence: u only hits the integer keypoints when (cnt-1) is a multiple of 3. Replaying the formula for cnt in {4,7,10,16} gives an exact high and low; for cnt in {8,20,50} it does not (shortfalls of 1.43, 0.53 and 0.20 on an O=100/H=140/L=90/C=130 bar). cnt = MathMax(n,4) at kit:565, and the final forced write at kit:595-597 fixes only the close, never the extremes. The header at kit:560 calls this 'the same assumption the engine will make, tested here first', and the engine's CSSRTickSynthesizer::Synthesize (Include/SSReplay/Core/SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:134-143) is the identical formula with a default InpTicksPerBar of 8 - the worst case measured - while its own header (line 13) claims 'The OHLC of the resulting bar is exact'.

findings.title: B1's wick_expanded_to_extremes verdict fails deterministically no matter how MetaTrader behaves
findings.claim: With the defaults (InpPerBar=20, InpBatches=20, SSR_GenM1 seed 4242, vol_points 25) the injected tick stream cannot reach within one point of the bar's high and low on more than 13 of the 20 bars, so hl_expanded <= 13 < nbars == 20 and the verdict FAILS on a terminal whose broadcast is perfect. B1 is a Tier-B blocker, so a correct terminal is recorded as 'SPIKE FAIL' against the claim 'candle builds natively from injected ticks'.
findings.evidence: The chart high can never exceed the highest injected bid. Replaying SSR_Rng/SSR_GenM1 (seed 4242, base 38000, vol 25) and SSR_BarToTicks with cnt=20 for the 20 generated bars gives an achievable high/low within one point on exactly 13 of 20 bars, identically for digits=1, 2 and 5 (the shortfall scales with point, so the symbol does not matter). With cnt=8 it is 3 of 20. The tolerance at line 139 is one point while the model's shortfall is 0.0526 x wick, and SSR_GenM1 draws wicks of |N(0,1)|*15 points, so a wick above 19 points already breaks the tolerance.

findings.title: No spike forces SYMBOL_CHART_MODE_BID or sets TICK_FLAG_LAST, so B1 reports the transport broken on an index or futures origin
findings.claim: SSR_MakeSymbol clones the origin symbol and overrides four properties but never SYMBOL_CHART_MODE, and the kit's tick generator sets flags = TICK_FLAG_BID|TICK_FLAG_ASK with no TICK_FLAG_LAST (kit:592). Drop B1 on a US30/index/futures CFD chart - which is what InpOrigin="" means, and what this project's own example symbol US30.U26 is - and the clone inherits SYMBOL_CHART_MODE_LAST. Every injected tick is accepted and no bar is built, so forming_bar_took_close and wick_expanded_to_extremes both report 0 of 20 and B1 concludes that CustomTicksAdd does not broadcast.
findings.evidence: grep -rn SYMBOL_CHART_MODE over MQL5/ returns no hit in any file under a Spike directory; the only writers are Mt5/SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:383 (the product, which forces BID) and QA/SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:473 (which asserts it). Core/SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:157-175 documents the measured failure in exactly this shape - '60 calls offered ticks, the terminal took 481, refused 0, and the M1 series stayed at 139 bars' - and fixes it with both TICK_FLAG_LAST and forced BID mode, calling that 'the belt to that braces'. The spike kit has neither. B3, C4, D2 and D3 build their ticks inline with the same BID|ASK-only flags.

findings.title: A3 has no positive control: on M5..D1 an unbuilt series gives the same answer as 'no future data'
findings.claim: All four read paths in AuditCut only ever record a verdict when they find something beyond T. Nothing anywhere in A3 asserts that data BELOW T exists on each of the seven timeframes. A terminal that never builds the M5..D1 series for this custom symbol answers 0 bars / iTime 0 / Bars 0 / SERIES_LASTBAR_DATE 0 on every path, which A3 scores as zero leaks and publishes as 'zero_future_leaks PASS across 2800 assertions' - the strongest claim in the suite, from a test that cannot distinguish absence of data from absence of a series.
findings.evidence: Path 2 is iTime(sym,tf,0) > T, path 3 is Bars(sym,tf,T+1,far) > 0, path 4 is (datetime)lastbar > T - each of which is false when the value is 0. The lazy-series behaviour that makes 0 ambiguous is the documented reason audit A21 exists (tools/ssr_audit.py:1556-1583) and is handled explicitly by A2 (SSR_A2_RatesAndAggregation.mq5:208-209, 'an unasked-for series answers zero, and this metric is the whole point of the experiment') and by D1 (SSR_D1_SeedPerformance.mq5:117-120, 'TOUCH EACH SERIES BEFORE COUNTING IT'). A3 primes only PERIOD_M1 (line 141) and never touches the other six with a non-future read.

findings.title: A3's avg_rebuild_time times the SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED flag, then declares it the Reset budget
findings.claim: The timed region (t0 at line 131) spans CustomRatesDelete + CustomTicksDelete + CustomRatesUpdate + a SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED poll with a 10 s ceiling. Per the kit's own measurement that flag takes about nine seconds after a custom-symbol rewrite regardless of size, so avg_rebuild_time reports roughly 9,000-10,000 ms per rebuild when the data is readable in tens of milliseconds - and that inflated number is explicitly labelled as feeding the product's Reset budget.
findings.evidence: SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:390-404 states the flag 'takes about nine seconds after a custom-symbol rewrite - for 10,000 bars and for 100,000 bars alike. Size-independent, so it is a timer, not work', that CopyRates returns the fresh bars in tens of milliseconds, and that D1 'called the same operation twenty times slower' for exactly this reason. The kit supplies SSR_WaitLastBarBefore for the tail-delete case and SSR_WaitLastBar for the re-seed case; A3 uses neither. Secondary effect: 100 cuts x up to 10 s of flag wait makes A3's own runtime up to ~17 minutes.

findings.title: D2 measures timeframe-switch cost by polling SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED, so its under-1s gate fails on a flag
findings.claim: Every switch_to_<TF> number, and the worst_switch that gates 'tfswitch_<d>k_<mode>_under_1s', is the time until SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED is set for the new timeframe, capped at 15 s (line 78) and then recorded as the elapsed time anyway on timeout (line 89). On a terminal where that flag takes ~9 s after a custom-symbol rewrite, or is never set, D2 publishes 9,000-15,000 ms per switch and FAILS the 1 s gate on an explicit product requirement ('M1 -> M5 -> M15 -> H1 without breaking replay'), while the chart is in fact usable in tens of milliseconds.
findings.evidence: SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:390-417 documents the flag as size-independent, 'a timer, not work', and 'observed at 0.002ms, at 9,200ms, and never'. D1:74-77 caps its own flag wait at 3 s precisely because 'This run spent 300 of its 315 seconds waiting for a flag that was never going to be set', and D4:64-70 records that the flag 'sat on BOTH sides of this spike's headline ratio'. D2 was not converted: it still polls the flag, on six MeasureDepth passes x 10 repeats x 7 switches = 420 timed waits.

findings.title: D2's 'live' pass re-sends identical tick timestamps, so 69 of its 70 injections are refused and live == idle
findings.claim: m1[depth-1] is a fixed bar, so SSR_BarToTicks produces the same 50 time_msc stamps on every one of the 70 iterations (10 repeats x 7 switches) within a MeasureDepth pass. CustomTicksAdd refuses a stamp the symbol already holds, so only the first call writes anything; the other 69 are rejected in full and the return value is never inspected. The with_ticks=true pass therefore measures switch cost with no feed running - identical to the idle pass - and the spike's headline claim ('again while ticks are actively being injected - which is the real condition a user will switch timeframes in') is not measured at all.
findings.evidence: SSR_BarToTicks sets time_msc = bar.time*1000 + i*59000/(cnt-1) (SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:586), a pure function of the bar - and the bar index depth-1 never changes inside MeasureDepth. B2:84-92 states the rule the code violates: 'CustomTicksAdd only appends: a tick at a stamp the symbol already holds is refused outright... All of them were rejected in full, returned in microseconds'. B2 fixed this by carrying one forward-only t_msc base; D2 did not. Nothing in D2 records accepted counts, so the rejection is invisible in the results file.

findings.title: D4's 1-bar tail-delete timing skips the series rebuild on 16 of 20 trials, inflating the rewind ratio
findings.claim: SSR_WaitLastBarBefore returns as soon as the last M5 bar's OPEN time is < cut. In strategy 1 the cut is the currently-last M1 bar, so the enclosing M5 bar's open time is already strictly below it whenever that minute is not a multiple of five - which is 16 of the 20 trials with InpStart M5-aligned and InpDepth=100000. Those trials return on the first CopyRates, before the delete has propagated, so tail_1bar.avg is mostly the bare call-return time. That average gates step_back_interactive (<=500 ms), step_back_usable (<=3000 ms) and the published rebuild_over_tail_ratio, whose other half (strategy 3) does wait properly via SSR_WaitLastBar on M1 with exact equality.
findings.evidence: D'2023.01.02 00:00' is 1672617600, divisible by 300, and m1[k].time = start + k*60, so the M5 slot of cut is start + (k/5)*300 which is < cut unless k % 5 == 0. For i = 0..19 the cut indices are 99999..99980, of which only 99995, 99990, 99985 and 99980 are multiples of 5 - replaying the comparison gives 16 of 20 waits satisfied before the delete. Strategy 2 (cut 100 bars below the last bar) is unaffected. The spike's own comment at lines 64-70 says every timing here used to include SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED and that the published '317x cheaper' 'was mostly a measurement of a flag' - the data-based wait it was replaced with is vacuous here for a different reason.

findings.title: D4 loses its chart at the strategy-2 restore, so the three rewind strategies are not measured under the same conditions
findings.claim: SSR_DropSymbol closes every chart showing the symbol, so the M5 chart opened at line 82 is destroyed here and never reopened. Strategy 1 is measured with a chart attached (and whatever indicator recalculation it causes); strategies 2 and 3 are measured with no chart at all. The published rebuild_over_tail_ratio therefore compares a with-chart tail delete against a no-chart full rebuild, and the 'with and without indicators' comparison the header promises is never performed - cid also becomes a stale id that line 158 still passes to ChartClose.
findings.evidence: SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:213-224 walks ChartFirst/ChartNext and calls ChartClose(cid) for every chart whose ChartSymbol() matches, inside SSR_DropSymbol. Strategy 3 calls SSR_DropSymbol again at line 134 on every trial. The header (lines 9-14) states the spike 'Compares three strategies at a realistic seed depth, with and without indicators on the chart, because indicator recalc is the cost that is easy to forget' and instructs 'Attach MA, RSI and Bollinger to the test chart before running the indicators pass' - but the chart is created by the script at line 82 and there is no input, pause or second pass that would let that happen; ChartIndicatorsTotal(cid,0) at line 85 is read two seconds after ChartOpen.

findings.title: D1 turns a readable-wait timeout into a zero wait and publishes the flattering write-only rate as 'the number the user waits for'
findings.claim: SSR_WaitReadable returns -1.0 on timeout. MathMax(t_read, 0) converts 'the seed never became readable within 60 seconds' into 'the seed became readable instantly', so total_time collapses to the write-call time and bars_per_sec reports the highest number of the whole run for the case that failed hardest - published with the note that it is the number a user waits for. This is the regression the surrounding comment says was already fixed once.
findings.evidence: SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:448-461: the loop runs while SSR_ElapsedMs(t0) < timeout_ms and 'return -1.0' on fall-through. D1:93-105 documents the mistake being guarded against: 'dividing by write_time alone reported 5.5 MILLION bars/second on a seed that took 9.2 seconds to become usable - a number 500x too flattering'. A timeout makes t_total == t_write/1000, i.e. exactly that discarded number, under the label that is supposed to distinguish it from write_call_bars_per_sec. readable_wait does record -1 in the same row, so the evidence is present but the derived headline metric is wrong and no verdict exists to catch it.

findings.title: D1 computes seed throughput from bars requested, not bars accepted, and never asserts they are equal
findings.claim: Both rates divide `total` (what was asked for) rather than `written` (what CustomRatesUpdate returned and the loop accumulated at line 62). If the terminal accepts only part of a chunked seed - or returns -1 for a chunk - D1 still publishes the full-throughput figure, and no verdict compares written to total. The same spike's bars_written metric records the truth one row away, so the two rows silently disagree. This is the 'a rate is only a rate if the work actually happened' rule the kit was extended to enforce.
findings.evidence: Line 53-63 accumulates `written` only when w > 0, and lines 80-81 record bars_target and bars_written separately; nothing uses `written` in a rate or a verdict. SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:351-372 mandates routing throughput through SSR_Rate, which returns -1 when accepted < sent - but SSR_RateMetric hardcodes the unit 'ticks/s' (kit:382-387), so a bar-rate cannot use it and the guard is bypassed here and in A2:133 ('bars_per_sec' from `written` over t_write with no check that written == n and no guard against CustomRatesUpdate's -1).

findings.title: B3 prints its PASS criterion instead of asserting it, so the session-behaviour spike always reports SPIKE PASS
findings.claim: B3's only SSR_Verdict call is the creation-failure path at line 33. If both symbols are created, g_ssr_pass and g_ssr_fail stay 0 and SSR_End prints 'SPIKE PASS' - even when sessions_247 acceptance_rate is 0%, i.e. when the terminal silently drops every tick, which is the exact defect the spike exists to detect. A reader of verdicts.csv sees no B3 row at all and a reader of the log sees PASS.
findings.evidence: SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:187-189 prints '(g_ssr_fail == 0 ? "SPIKE PASS" : "SPIKE FAIL")', and g_ssr_fail is only incremented inside SSR_Verdict (kit:169). B3 computes accept_rate at line 101 and records it as a metric at line 106, and computes silent_drops at 116-118, but asserts nothing about either. The comparison between the no_sessions and sessions_247 cases - the whole hypothesis at lines 6-9 - is left to a human reading two rows of a CSV.

findings.title: D1 also prints its PASS gate rather than asserting it
findings.claim: D1 records a numeric gate (100k bars in <= 20 s, 500k in <= 120 s) and has total_time per case in hand at line 91, but issues no SSR_Verdict for it. Its only verdict is symbol_ready on the setup path, so a run where every seed takes 60 s still ends 'SPIKE PASS' and contributes nothing to verdicts.csv. Combined with finding 10, a seed that never became readable reports both the best bars/s and a PASS.
findings.evidence: The only SSR_Verdict in the file is at line 143 (symbol_ready, inside the early-return branch). SeedCase records eleven metrics and zero verdicts. SSR_End (SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:187) prints SPIKE PASS whenever g_ssr_fail == 0. Every other timing spike encodes its gate - D2:100-101, D4:149-156, B2:177-182, D3:214-217 - which is why D1 and B3 standing outside that pattern is a gap rather than a style choice.

findings.title: C3's torn-read test runs the writer and the reader sequentially in one thread, so 'race-free' cannot fail
findings.claim: The four writes always complete before the three reads in the same loop iteration of the same program, so a1/a2/a3 are always consistent with seq and `torn` is structurally always 0. The verdict seq_last_protocol_safe therefore passes on any terminal and would pass even if the seq-last discipline were removed or the writes reordered - it is evidence about nothing. The claim it certifies (header line 7: the channel is 'fast, lossless and race-free'; line 74: 'the seq-last protocol must never expose a half-written command') requires a second program reading while the first writes, which C3 never creates.
findings.evidence: Lines 79-98 are one for-loop in OnStart: writer block then reader block, no Sleep, no second program, no EventSetTimer, and no indicator or service involved. The only way `a1 != seq*7` at line 95 is if GlobalVariableSet/Get lose data within one thread - which section 1 of the same spike already tests separately. The real product shape (a Service writing while an Indicator panel reads, header lines 6-7) is never instantiated anywhere in the spike suite; C1 and C2 each run alone.

findings.title: C4's timecurrent_is_unsafe verdict is a tautology, and C4 never checks that its ticks were accepted
findings.claim: InpStart is required to be in the past (line 21), so TimeCurrent() differs from the replay symbol's SYMBOL_TIME by years and the verdict passes unconditionally. It would pass in a world where TimeCurrent were perfectly safe; it demonstrates only that two clocks read differently at one instant, not the stated counter-claim that other live symbols drag TimeCurrent forward. Separately, CustomTicksAdd's return is discarded at line 70, so if the ticks are rejected (wrong chart mode, session, duplicate stamp) SYMBOL_TIME stays at the previous value and C4 reports 1000 sec_mismatches - indistinguishable from 'SYMBOL_TIME does not track injected ticks'.
findings.evidence: tc is TimeCurrent() at line 99 and sym_t is SYMBOL_TIME after injecting ticks stamped from D'2024.01.08'; the inequality is guaranteed by the input contract. The supporting metric symbols_ahead_of_replay (lines 109-119) counts every Market Watch symbol whose SYMBOL_TIME exceeds the 2024 replay base - which is every symbol quoted since then, closed markets included - yet its note claims 'each one can drag TimeCurrent forward'. Line 70 is a bare `CustomTicksAdd(InpTest, tk);` with no accepted count, while SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:351-364 makes checking acceptance the suite's first rule.

findings.title: A1 and C1 delete a custom symbol immediately after deselecting it, against the kit's own load-bearing 200 ms rule
findings.claim: The kit states that MetaTrader refuses to delete a symbol still selected in Market Watch (5306) and needs a beat after being told to deselect one, and enforces a 200 ms pause between the two calls. A1's 'deletion must be clean' section and C1's teardown both skip the pause, so on the behaviour the kit documents they get err=5306, deleted=false, and record symbol_deleted FAIL / service_can_CustomSymbolDelete FAIL. A1 then reports the symbol lifecycle as broken, and C1 - the spike that decides Core = Service vs Core = EA - reports that a Service cannot delete a custom symbol.
findings.evidence: SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:225-234: 'THE ORDER AND THE PAUSE ARE BOTH LOAD-BEARING. MetaTrader refuses to delete a symbol that is still selected in Market Watch (5306) and needs a moment after being told to deselect one. Without the beat the delete fails... That exact chain already cost a round trip once, in the Preflight script.' SSR_DropSymbol pauses 200 ms and retries after 800 ms. A1:185-187 and Services/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_C1_ServiceApiAccess.mq5:162-164 ('SymbolSelect(InpTest, false); r = CustomSymbolDelete(InpTest);') have no pause and no retry, and both feed the result straight into a verdict. A1 also verifies no_residue_after_delete (line 198) on the assumption the delete succeeded.

findings.title: A1's max_symbol_name_length attributes any CustomSymbolCreate refusal to name length and leaves residue behind on failure
findings.claim: The loop breaks on the first CustomSymbolCreate that returns false and publishes the last success as max_symbol_name_length, the number said to drive the <SRC>.SSR<slot> naming convention. Any other refusal reason - the name already exists from an interrupted earlier run whose CustomSymbolDelete failed, a custom-symbol count limit, a locked bases folder - is recorded as a name-length limit. If 'AAAA' already exists the metric is 0 and name_len_usable FAILs while nothing indicates why; the error code is never captured despite the ResetLastError on line 169.
findings.evidence: Lines 169-176: ResetLastError() is called but GetLastError() is never read, and the else branch is a bare break. CustomSymbolDelete(probe) at line 173 is unchecked, so a failed delete leaves AAAA-style symbols under SSReplay\Spike\len that poison every later run of A1. SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:236-246 shows the author already knows deletes fail and need a retry plus a named log line; this loop has neither.

findings.title: B4 turns a missing series into '20,700 days of history' and inverts its Load-More-History conclusion
findings.code:
SSR_Metric(sym, "m1_first_local_days_ago",
           (double)(TimeCurrent() - (datetime)first_local) / 86400.0, "days",
           TimeToString((datetime)first_local, TIME_DATE));
...
SSR_Metric(sym, "m1_downloadable_more",
           ((datetime)first_server < (datetime)first_local ? 1 : 0), "bool",
           "Load More History would gain data");
findings.claim: SeriesInfoInteger leaves first_local/first_server at their initialised 0 when the series does not exist or the call fails, and neither return value is checked. For a symbol with no local M1 history the audit publishes m1_first_local_days_ago of about 20,700 days with the note '1970.01.01' - read as 57 years of history - and m1_downloadable_more = 0 ('Load More History would gain data' false) because first_server is not less than 0, when the correct answer is that everything is downloadable.
findings.evidence: Lines 35-38 declare `long first_local = 0, first_server = 0, bars_m1 = 0;` and call SeriesInfoInteger three times discarding each bool result. The subtraction at line 42 is unguarded, so first_local == 0 yields TimeCurrent()/86400. The inversion at lines 47-49 follows directly: 0 < 0 is false and real_server_date < 0 is false, so both the 'nothing local' and 'nothing anywhere' cases report the same 0. B4's whole purpose (header lines 6-9) is to decide whether full-tick fidelity is fiction at this broker, so an inverted or absurd history figure changes a roadmap decision.

findings.title: B4's tick-depth walk samples the same hour of the day at every depth, so a symbol closed in that hour reports zero tick history
findings.claim: Because the step is exactly 86400 seconds, all twelve probes land on the same clock hour on twelve different days. For an instrument whose session excludes that hour - an index CFD audited at 03:00, a symbol with a daily break - every sample is empty, misses reaches InpEmptyTolerance and the walk breaks, publishing tick_history_depth = 0 with the note 'no ticks in any sampled day' for a symbol that may hold years of ticks. The tolerance fixes the early stop but not the reported depth, and the depth is the number that decides whether fidelity F1 is real.
findings.evidence: `from = now - d * 86400` with d doubling keeps the time-of-day of `now` fixed for every d. The comment at lines 53-68 identifies the right cause ('An empty hour is a closed market, not an absent history') and applies a tolerance rather than varying the sampled hour or scanning a session-aware window. A second inconsistency compounds it: the depth walk uses COPY_TICKS_INFO (bid/ask changes) while the ceiling probe at line 98 uses COPY_TICKS_ALL, so the two metrics the note at line 90 asks the reader to compare are not measuring the same tick population.

findings.title: B4 reports the number of ticks in a week as a call ceiling and a page size
findings.claim: CopyTicksRange returns how many ticks exist in the requested range, not the largest number it is willing to return. Unless the call was actually truncated - which B4 has no way to detect, because it never asks for a range it knows is larger than any plausible cap - `cap` is a measurement of the broker's tick density over seven days, published as the 'practical ceiling of one CopyTicksRange call' and as the value that 'sets the page size for TickSource'. A quiet symbol therefore dictates a small page size and a busy one a large page size, for reasons unrelated to any API limit.
findings.evidence: Lines 95-101 issue exactly one call over a fixed seven-day window and assign its return to cap, with no comparison against a known tick count, no second call over a wider window, and no check of GetLastError(). The variable name and the metric note ('sets the page size for TickSource') both assert a ceiling the code cannot distinguish from data volume. Cost note: this is a COPY_TICKS_ALL fetch of a full week per symbol, up to InpMaxAuto=6 symbols, immediately after the comment at lines 60-64 explains that fetching a single day of ticks per probe 'went from seconds to looking hung'.

findings.title: C2's restart detector false-fails on every run after the first, and the event it hunts destroys its own evidence file
findings.claim: MT5 global variables persist on disk between runs and C2 never resets this one, so the second and every later run starts from a non-zero marker and no_restart FAILs even though the service never restarted - the verdict measures 'has this spike been run before', not 'did the service restart'. Line 127 asks the operator to delete the GV by hand between runs, which makes a correct result dependent on a manual step. Separately, the heartbeat CSV is opened with FILE_WRITE, which truncates it, so an actual mid-run restart erases every pre-restart row - destroying the record needed to show that the seq counter reset, which the header names as the PASS criterion.
findings.evidence: No GlobalVariableDel("SSR.c2.launches") appears anywhere in the file, and line 127 prints 'reset the launch counter before the next run: delete GV SSR.c2.launches'. Line 63 opens SSR_Spike\c2_heartbeat.csv with FILE_WRITE|FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI (no FILE_READ, no seek to end), so OnStart running a second time rewrites the header at offset 0. seq is a local initialised to 0 at line 51, so the only cross-restart evidence is the GV that is already unreliable. Header line 21: 'PASS: heartbeat counter never resets and no gap exceeds 3000ms.'

findings.title: C2's documented manual procedure stops the service 60 seconds before its own run-length gate is satisfied
findings.claim: The header's step-by-step procedure ends with 't+300s stop the service' while InpRunSec defaults to 360, and the gate requires uptime >= 342 s. An operator who follows the printed instructions exactly gets IsStopped() at 300 s, an uptime of 300 s, and a FAILED survived_full_run - so the correct execution of the procedure guarantees a failing verdict, and the spike's result cannot be read as evidence either way.
findings.evidence: Header line 19: 't+300s  stop the service'. Line 28: `input int InpRunSec = 360;`. The loop at line 69 is `while(!IsStopped())` and exits early on operator stop; uptime_s is then computed at line 106 from the real elapsed time. 300 < 360*0.95 = 342, so the verdict fails. The other two verdicts (no_restart, no_long_gaps) are unaffected, which makes the failure look like a partial result rather than an instruction/default mismatch.

findings.title: D3's throughput_stable gate still uses the minute-10 baseline that the same file documents as hiding the finding
findings.code:
SSR_Verdict("throughput_stable", rate_drop <= 10.0, "<=10% drop",
            StringFormat("%.1f%%", rate_drop), "");
findings.claim: rate_drop is computed from rate_first, which is only assigned once minute >= 10 (line 125-129). On the run the file describes - 12,000 ticks/s falling to about 780 before minute 10 - rate_first is already ~780 and rate_last is ~780, so rate_drop is near zero and throughput_stable PASSES on a run that lost 94% of its throughput. The remedy applied was to add rate_peak, rate_at_min1, decay_peak_to_end and decay_min1_to_end as metrics; the gate that produces the PASS/FAIL line and the verdicts.csv row was left on the window the comment says hides the problem.
findings.evidence: Lines 176-182: 'THE MINUTE-10 BASELINE HIDES THE FINDING... on this terminal most of the decay has already happened by then: the first run fell from ~12,000 to ~780 ticks/s before minute 10, then reported a comfortable PASS on what was left.' rate_drop at line 160 is 100*(rate_first-rate_last)/rate_first with rate_first taken at minute 10, and the else-branch verdict at 216-217 still consumes it. decay_peak_to_end is recorded at lines 187-190 but no verdict reads it.

findings.title: The TickWitness probe's assertion can pass without a single injected tick reaching the chart
findings.claim: OnCalculate is not a tick-only event: the initial calculation, a history update, a symbol or timeframe change and a chart refresh all invoke it. A threshold of g_calls > 1 is therefore met by chart housekeeping alone, so the designated FAIL signal for B1 can report PASS on a chart that received no injected tick. The counter that would actually testify - g_ticks, 'observed_price_changes', which only increments when the newest close changes - is recorded as a metric at line 51 and never asserted.
findings.evidence: g_calls is incremented unconditionally at line 66 on every OnCalculate entry. g_ticks is incremented at line 72 only when close[rates_total-1] differs from the previous value, which is the evidence the header describes ('Only an indicator running on that chart can testify that OnCalculate fired and that the forming bar moved') - and it appears in no SSR_Verdict. Report() is called from OnDeinit, which for an indicator also runs on timeframe change and recompile, so each of those writes a fresh env/results/verdict set.

findings.title: The spike CSVs are opened without FILE_SHARE_WRITE while three spikes require a concurrent probe writing the same file
findings.claim: Every metric and verdict of every spike goes through this one function, and it requests write access while granting other programs read access only. B2, D1 and D3 each instruct the operator to run SSR_Probe_UIJitter at the same time, and that probe appends four metric rows to the same results.csv every 10 seconds for the whole window. Whenever the two opens overlap, one of them gets INVALID_HANDLE and the row is dropped with nothing but a Print - so the jitter series that B2 and D1 declare their results meaningless without is the part most likely to develop silent holes.
findings.evidence: SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:93-108 is the single writer for env.csv, results.csv and verdicts.csv; FILE_SHARE_WRITE is absent from the flag set. SSR_B2_TickThroughput.mq5:10-12 ('Run SSR_Probe_UIJitter on a SEPARATE chart at the same time. Throughput without a responsiveness number is meaningless'), SSR_D1_SeedPerformance.mq5:11-12 and SSR_D3_SustainedRun.mq5:10 all mandate the concurrency. SSR_Probe_UIJitter.mq5:69-73 calls Report() every InpReportSec=10, and Report emits four SSR_Metric rows (lines 92-95). The failure is a Print, not a verdict, so a dropped row leaves no trace in the artefacts.

findings.title: Audit A19's translation-length check never runs: the language directory path contains MQL5 twice
findings.code:
langdir = os.path.join(ROOT, "MQL5", "Files", "SSReplay", "lang")
if os.path.isdir(langdir):
findings.claim: ROOT already points at the MQL5 directory (line 16: os.path.join(dirname(__file__), '..', 'MQL5')), so langdir resolves to <repo>/MQL5/MQL5/Files/SSReplay/lang, which does not exist; os.path.isdir returns False and the loop is skipped. The only check that any translated string fits MetaTrader's 63-character draw limit is dead code, and it passes silently - the precise vacuous pass that A18 and A19's own guards were written to prevent. A Persian string of 64+ characters would ship with its end invisible and no audit would say so.
findings.evidence: Verified by computation: ROOT = /home/user/academyss/mt5-replay/MQL5; langdir = /home/user/academyss/mt5-replay/MQL5/MQL5/Files/SSReplay/lang, isdir False; the real directory is /home/user/academyss/mt5-replay/MQL5/Files/SSReplay/lang and it contains fa.txt with 190 key=value pairs. The audit's own comment at lines 1414-1417 asserts the opposite: 'A translation makes this worse, not better... So every file under MQL5/Files/SSReplay/lang is checked too', and line 1446 tells the reader 'this is the only place it is checked'. None of fa.txt's 190 values currently exceeds 63 characters, so the silence is accidental rather than earned.

findings.title: Audit A20's regex matches only one exact function shape, leaving two drawing Ui surfaces unchecked
findings.code: want = re.compile(r"^   void\s+(Render|Repaint)\(void\)\s*$", re.M)
findings.claim: The pattern demands exactly three leading spaces, the names Render or Repaint, a literal (void) parameter list, and nothing else on the line. Any drawing function named otherwise is invisible, so A20 cannot enforce its rule on SSR_FirstRun::Show and SSR_KeyCard::Show, each of which builds a card out of Rect/Label calls. Both happen to call ChartRedraw today, so the audit's silence is luck: delete either call and A20 stays green while the regression it was written for - a card drawn on a paused chart that never repaints - returns.
findings.evidence: Applying the pattern across the Ui layer matches 8 functions in 7 files (SSR_Palette, SSR_Panel, SSR_RangeDialog, SSR_RevealCard, SSR_ReviewCard, SSR_SessionDialog, SSR_SetupPanel x2). SSR_FirstRun.mqh has 5 widget draw calls and no match (its drawing function is `bool Show(const long chart_id)` at line 81, ChartRedraw at line 118); SSR_KeyCard.mqh has 5 draw calls and no match (ChartRedraw at line 101). The docstring states the intent the pattern narrows: 'Checked per RENDER FUNCTION, not per file: a file whose Render is silent still passes a grep for ChartRedraw anywhere in it'. A20 is also limited to paths containing /Ui/, so drawing code in the Expert and the Chart layer is out of scope entirely.

findings.title: Audit A14 omits four of the eight text-drawing widget helpers that A19 already knows about
findings.code: WIDGET_TEXT = (("Label", 3), ("Button", 5), ("ButtonC", 5), ("Edit", 5))
findings.claim: A19's table of text-argument positions (SSR_DRAW_TEXT_ARG at line 1274) lists eight helpers - Label, Button, ButtonC, Chip, Group, Toast, Edit, Text - while A14's table lists four. A literal longer than 63 characters passed as the text of Chip(), Group(), Toast() or Text() is therefore never measured, even though the 63-character cut is the defect class this project has hit at least five times. A14 also has no vacuous-pass guard of the kind A19 carries at lines 1491-1496, so a future signature change that shifted the text index would make it read the wrong argument everywhere and report success.
findings.evidence: The two tables sit in the same file and disagree: line 894 versus line 1274. Scanning the tree for literal text arguments through Chip/Group/Toast/Text finds 2 such calls today, none over 63 characters, so the gap is currently latent rather than active. A14's loop also reads `raw = FILES[path]` (line 942) rather than the decommented or KEEPSTR view, so it measures widget calls that appear inside comments as if they were code.

findings.title: Audit A9 cannot see a duplicated pointer-returning method, the exact shape DECL_METHOD was fixed for
findings.code:
METHOD_DEF = re.compile(r'^\s*(?:virtual\s+|static\s+|const\s+)*'
                        r'[A-Za-z_][\w:]*\s*[\*&]?\s+'
                        r'([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\(([^)]*)\)')
findings.claim: METHOD_DEF requires whitespace after the optional * or &, so the codebase's own pointer style - `CSSRBarProvider *Bars(void)`, where the star hugs the name - never matches. A method of that shape defined twice in one class produces MetaEditor's 'member function already defined' and A9 stays silent, which is precisely the class of patch accident A9 was written to catch. The same declaration form is also invisible to A9's class-scope bookkeeping, so duplicates of other methods declared after it are still found only by luck.
findings.evidence: Line 426 is `r'[A-Za-z_][\w:]*\s*[\*&]?\s+'` - a mandatory \s+ after the star. The comment at lines 343-345 records the same bug being fixed in DECL_METHOD: 'the star hugs the NAME in this codebase - CSSRBarProvider *Bars(void) - so whitespace after it must be optional, or every pointer-returning method reads as undeclared. Three false positives said so immediately.' DECL_METHOD (line 346-349) uses `\s*[\*&]?\s*`; METHOD_DEF was not updated. METHOD_DEF's argument group `([^)]*)` additionally stops at the first ')', so a default argument containing parentheses ends the match.

findings.title: The UIJitter probe divides by its window-size input with no validation
findings.claim: InpWindow is an int input used unchecked as an array size (ArrayResize at line 34) and as a modulus. Set it to 0 - a plausible slip when someone wants the probe to keep no history - and the first OnTimer writes g_samp[0] into a zero-length array and then divides by zero, terminating the indicator. A negative value gives ArrayResize a negative size and the same modulus fault. The probe is the instrument three other spikes declare their results meaningless without, so it failing on attach is a silent loss of the responsiveness half of every throughput conclusion.
findings.evidence: OnInit does `ArrayResize(g_samp, InpWindow); ArrayInitialize(g_samp, 0.0);` with no clamp, and EventSetMillisecondTimer(InpPeriodMs) is likewise unvalidated. OnTimer's first statement after the timing arithmetic is the indexed write at line 65 followed by the modulus at line 66. Report() guards only against too few samples (g_count < 5 at line 79), not against a zero-length buffer. Compare CSSRTickSynthesizer::SetTicksPerBar (Core/SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:106), where the product clamps the analogous input: `m_ticks_per_bar = (n < 4 ? 4 : n)`.

findings.title: B2 recommends a batch size to 'lock into Feeder' without ever measuring how long one call blocks
findings.claim: best_batch is chosen purely by accepted-ticks-per-second of aggregate call time, a quantity that improves monotonically as per-call overhead is amortised, so the winner will be the largest fully-accepted batch - up to 50,000 ticks in one CustomTicksAdd. B2 never records the duration of a single call, which is the quantity the engine's pump budget (InpPumpMs, default 40 ms) actually constrains, and never joins its own numbers to the jitter probe it declares mandatory. The published recommendation can therefore be a batch that blocks the terminal far longer than one timer beat.
findings.evidence: Only aggregate figures are recorded per case: total_us accumulates across all rounds (line 132), and inject_time, ticks_per_sec and us_per_tick derive from that sum (lines 145-148). There is no max or p95 of a single CustomTicksAdd. best_rate/best_batch are selected at lines 156-160 from that aggregate rate alone. The header at lines 10-12 states 'Run SSR_Probe_UIJitter on a SEPARATE chart at the same time. Throughput without a responsiveness number is meaningless - a terminal can accept ticks fast while being frozen to a user', and lines 190-191 leave the join to the reader: 'read ui_jitter_p95 from the UIJitter probe for the same window'. The header also promises to show how throughput collapses 'as charts and indicators are added', but nothing in the spike attaches an indicator; only InpCharts varies, and InpLabel ('charts1_ind0') is typed by hand, so a mislabelled run is recorded under the wrong condition.

performance_notes: A3 is the most expensive spike by construction: 100 cuts x (CustomRatesDelete + CustomTicksDelete + CustomRatesUpdate of up to 3,888 bars + SSR_WaitSeries with a 10,000 ms ceiling). If SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED behaves as the kit documents (~9 s after a rewrite) the run takes ~15-17 minutes, nearly all of it in the flag wait, and that same wait is what avg_rebuild_time publishes.

D2 worst case: 6 MeasureDepth passes x (SSR_WaitSeries M1 up to 60 s + 10 repeats x 7 switches x up to 15 s) = up to ~1.8 hours, dominated entirely by SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED polling. The switches themselves are one ChartSetSymbolPeriod call each.

D1 with InpBig=false writes 500,000 bars in the chunk sweep plus 160,000 in the depth sweep, and each of the 8 cases can spend up to 60 s in SSR_WaitReadable plus 3 s in the capped SSR_WaitSeries. Generation is measured separately (generate_time) so it does not pollute the write figures.

D3 at default settings injects for 120 minutes with t_msc advancing 10 ms per tick.
