At the ~12,000 ticks/s the file cites for the first samples that is tens of millions of ticks and days of virtual time written into one custom symbol's tick store, which is a plausible confound for the memory_stable verdict: the test cannot separate a leak from the growth of the data it is deliberately writing, and it never deletes anything. It also creates ~720 sample points x 2 metrics = ~1,440 results.csv rows per run, each with its own case name t####s.

B4 issues one CopyTicksRange(COPY_TICKS_ALL) over a full week per symbol (up to 6 symbols), immediately after a comment explaining that a one-day COPY_TICKS_ALL probe per step made the audit 'look hung'. The 12-step depth walk is cheap by comparison (one hour, COPY_TICKS_INFO).

SSR_AggregateM1 calls ArrayResize once per output bar (kit:533). For A2's 4,320 M1 bars that is at most 4,320 resizes per timeframe and is negligible, but it is the wrong shape if a later spike aggregates 288,000 bars.

Inside an indicator SSR_Pause is a no-op (kit:199-204), so any kit wait loop called from SSR_Probe_* becomes a tight busy-spin on the indicator's thread. Neither probe currently calls one, but the kit is shared and the trap is undocumented at the call sites.

Every SSR_Metric and SSR_Verdict opens, seeks, writes and closes a CSV (kit:93-108). D3 emits 2 metrics per 10 s sample and A3 emits a verdict per detected leak, so a badly failing A3 (2,800 probes x 100 cuts) could write tens of thousands of rows one FileOpen at a time.

B2's own numbers are honest about acceptance but nothing measures the cost of building the tick buffer: the inner generation loop (line 116-128) runs 1.2 million times across the six cases and is excluded from total_us by design (line 100).
test_gaps: No spike measures the OHLC error that tick synthesis introduces. A2 proves the terminal aggregates written M1 bars correctly; nothing checks that a bar rebuilt from synthesised TICKS reproduces the source bar's high and low. B1's wick check is the only attempt and it is defeated by the generator (findings 1-2). Since the product ships InpTicksPerBar=8 and the engine uses the same interpolation, the error in stop-hit simulation at the default fidelity is unmeasured.

No spike exercises a gap in the data. SSR_GenM1 produces a contiguous minute-by-minute series and A2/A3 use 4,320 bars starting Monday 2024.01.08, i.e. exactly three weekdays with no weekend, no session break and no missing minute. Aggregation across a gap, and future-isolation when T falls inside a gap, are untested.
W1 and MN1 are never checked anywhere: A2 aggregates M5..H4 plus an informational D1, and A3's g_tf array stops at D1. The product allows arbitrary chart timeframes.

Nothing tests two custom symbols advancing on one clock, although CSSRReplayGroup supports up to three extra symbols. Every spike creates and feeds exactly one replay symbol (A2 and B1 create a second only to document a side behaviour).

No spike runs two SSReplay programs at once. C3's race test is single-threaded (finding 14), C1 and C2 each run alone, and the Service-writes / Indicator-reads topology that C1 and C2 exist to justify is never actually instantiated - so nothing measures IPC latency, ordering or loss between two real programs.

The concurrent-probe protocol is never verified. B1 says 'Attach SSR_Probe_TickWitness to the test symbol's chart first', but the test symbol is created by B1 (SSR_MakeSymbol drops and recreates it), the chart is opened by B1 at line 57, and SSR_DropSymbol closes that chart at the end - so the witness cannot be attached beforehand and nothing correlates its verdict with B1's. D4 has the same unreachable instruction for MA/RSI/Bollinger (finding 9).

Tick rejection is unobserved in four of the six spikes that inject ticks. B1, B2 and D3 count accepted ticks; B3 compares the return against a readback; C4 (line 70) and D2 (line 69) discard the return entirely, so a total rejection is reported as a clock or timing result.

No spike measures what happens when a custom symbol is fed ticks whose timestamps go BACKWARD or duplicate an existing stamp - the rule is documented in B2's comment from a past failure but never asserted anywhere, and D2 depends on it silently (finding 7).

The audits cannot see a call through a pointer. A11/A12 resolve receivers declared as `CSSRThing g_name;` or indented `CSSRThing m_name;` only; MEMBER_DECL and GLOBAL_DECL both fail on `CSSRThing *m_thing;`, so arity and existence checks do not cover pointer-held collaborators. This is documented as deliberate ('pointers and locals are left to A7, which is weaker but never wrong-headed') but it is the largest hole in the compile-error net.

A21's timeframe argument must be a bare identifier or Foo(); `Bars(sym, g_cycle[i])` (D2:82) and any cast expression are invisible to it, so the lazy-series rule is unenforced exactly where timeframes are chosen dynamically.

A19's i18n check is scoped to paths containing /Ui/, so user-visible text drawn from Experts/SSReplay/SSReplayStandalone.mq5 (7 ObjectSetString OBJPROP_TEXT calls) and Chart/SSR_TradeLines.mqh (2) is outside it; A17 documents a colour that shipped wrong for three builds for the same reason - it was styled in the expert, 'where the theme could not reach it'.

No audit checks that a spike records a verdict. Findings 12 and 13 would be caught mechanically by a rule as simple as 'every .mq5 under a Spike directory that calls SSR_Metric must also call SSR_Verdict outside an early-return branch', which is the same class of mechanical check the other 21 audits already are.

Nothing measures the audits themselves. The file's own standard is 'break the code on purpose, the audit must name it; put the code back, the audit must go silent... An audit that has never been seen to fire is not evidence' (lines 5-8), but there are no fixture files and no self-test, so a regression like finding 26 (a dead path) or a regex narrowing like findings 27-29 cannot be detected except by reading the source.

verdicts.reason: Traced fully and found no guard. `nb = cap` (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:401) overwrites the read count with no copy kept anywhere (verified every `nb` use in EmitWindow). The emit loop (L437) increments `bars_used` unconditionally per iteration and its only early exit `if(w <= 0) break` (L442) is unreachable — Synthesize/SynthesizeClose return 0 only on buffer shortfall, and m_ticks is resized to `need = (nb-first)*per_bar` at L418 with `base = written <= (i-first)*per_bar`. So `first + bars_used == nb` always after the loop, making the stop-short test at L524 dead precisely when the cap bit; `consumed_to` stays `hi` and L531 `m_cursor.Advance(hi,...)` moves the cursor past the unemitted bars. `SSRReplayCursor::PendingRange` starts the next window at `emitted_msc+1`, so they are never re-read, and nothing consumes `m_pump_deferred`/`Deferrals()` except metrics counters — no caller re-pumps. The bars therefore reach neither the custom symbol (no EmitTicks) nor the observers (no PublishBar/PublishSegment), so SL/TP inside them is never evaluated, while the pump is reported as merely deferred. The author's own comment at L519-522 documents the opposite intent.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The mechanism and the dead branch are exactly as described; two details need correcting. (1) Category: this is silent data loss (dropped market data), not future-data leakage — the horizon clamp at L325 is intact and nothing beyond the clock is emitted. (2) Reachability: `m_fidelity.Decide(hi-lo)` degrades any owed span >= 10 minutes to SSR_FIDELITY_BAR (SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:120, SSR_BULK_THRESHOLD_MSC = 10*60*1000), where per_bar = 1 so cap = MaxTicks() (floor 32 bars). The quoted PgDn case actually spans 9 bars (StepBars L1167-1170, owed ~9 min, just under the bulk threshold, per_bar = 8) and so needs measured UsPerTick > ~166us at the fixed 12 ms budget (SetPumpBudgetMs is never called outside T7). The most reachable trigger is instead a long FORWARD SeekTo (L1246-1258), reached via CSSRReplayGroup::SeekAllTo/JumpTo (SSR_MasterClock.mqh:300-325) and bookmark/session jumps (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1534, 3189): a jump of hours or a day feeds 120-1440 M1 bars into one EmitWindow at BAR fidelity, where the cap bites as soon as UsPerTick exceeds roughly 8-100us and hundreds of bars are dropped in a single call, leaving a gap in the custom symbol's series that no later pump fills. Fix: keep the pre-cap count (e.g. `int nb_read = nb;`) and compare `first + bars_used < nb_read`, or set `consumed_to` from the last consumed bar whenever the cap bit.

verdicts.reason: Could not refute. The "stop short" branch at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:524 is provably unreachable: the cap at 399-404 overwrites nb itself, the loop at 437 increments bars_used on every iteration, and its only escape (w <= 0, SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:120-121) cannot fire because m_ticks was resized to need = (nb-first)*per_bar while `written` accumulates only kept ticks, so offset never exceeds the buffer. Hence first + bars_used == nb always, consumed_to stays hi, and m_cursor.Advance(hi,...) sets emitted_msc = hi so the next PendingRange begins at hi+1 — the bars above the cap are never read again. Pump (996) and PumpTo (1072) each call EmitWindow exactly once per beat and there is no catch-up loop; JumpForward (1333) is not a recovery path since it bulk-writes via SeedBars and hands EmitWindow at most one partial bar. T7.6 (SSR_T7_Performance.mq5:287-293) only asserts TicksEmitted keeps rising, which later bars satisfy, so it cannot catch this. Every MQL5 assumption the finding relies on checks out: integer division in MaxBars with a floor of 1, the [32,32768] clamp and (int) cast in MaxTicks, long msc arithmetic with SSR_MSC_PER_MIN, and array bounds. The defect (a dead deferral branch whose comment documents the opposite intent, plus a cursor advance past unemitted bars) is static and unconditional; only its trigger frequency is machine-dependent, since the cap must first be calibrated (CSSRMetrics::IsCalibrated needs 16 pumps with cost; the uncalibrated fallback of 4096 ticks never bites) and must come out below the owed bar count.
verdicts.corrected_claim:
Accurate description: the per-pump budget cap in CSSRReplayController::EmitWindow silently DROPS bars instead of deferring them, because the deferral branch it relies on is dead code. Line 398-404 caps by overwriting the bar count itself (nb = cap), so the loop at 437 consumes bars first..nb-1 and leaves first + bars_used == nb; the guard at 524, `(first + bars_used) < nb`, can therefore never be true when the cap bit. consumed_to remains hi and m_cursor.Advance(hi, ...) moves emitted_msc past the bars that were never synthesised, so the next PendingRange starts at hi+1 and they are lost forever: no ticks in the custom symbol (a candle hole), no PublishBar/PublishSegment to the trading engine (any SL/TP inside those minutes is never evaluated), while m_pump_deferred/NoteDeferral report the work as merely deferred. The correct fix is to compare against the pre-cap bar count (save it before `nb = cap`), or to cap the loop bound rather than nb.

Corrections to the reported scenario, which do not change the mechanism: (1) StepBars calls EmitWindow directly at line 1183 — it is not `Play(); PumpTo(...)`. (2) PgDn from 10:05:59.999 with StepBars(10) yields target = 10:14:59.999 and a window of 9 M1 bars spanning 539,999 ms, which stays just under SSR_BULK_THRESHOLD_MSC (600,000) and so keeps SYNTHETIC_TICK; MaxBars(8) has a hard floor of 4 bars (MaxTicks floors at SSR_PUMP_MIN_TICKS = 32), so up to 5 of those 9 bars are dropped, not 6. (3) The cap only bites once CSSRMetrics::IsCalibrated() is true (>= 16 recorded pumps with measured emit cost) and the measured us/tick is high enough — before calibration MaxTicks is the 4096 fallback (512 bars at 8 ticks/bar) and the cap never fires in synthetic fidelity. (4) The larger exposure is the bulk path: a pump owing >= 10 minutes degrades to SSR_FIDELITY_BAR where cap = MaxBars(1) = MaxTicks, floored at 32 bars, while a stall at high speed (ladder tops out at 1000x) can owe hundreds of M1 bars — those hundreds are dropped in one pump. T7.6 exercises exactly that case (a 30-minute pump with a 2 ms budget) and does not detect it.

verdicts.reason:
Traced every step; no guard, clamp, or earlier check prevents it.

1) SSR_Time.mqh:27-43 — SSRBarOpenMsc floors to the period boundary; SSRNextBarOpenMsc = floor+60000. For now = open+59999, base = open+60000. Confirmed.

2) SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1169 — target = base + (bars-1)*60000 - 1. For bars==1 that is base-1 = open+59999 = now exactly. Nothing raises it: NextTimelineBarOpen -> CSSRMt5BarProvider::NextBarOpen (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:302-323) returns the first M1 open strictly greater than after_msc, which in dense data is exactly base, so the `nb > base` branch (line 1167-1168) does not fire (strict >, not >=). The generic fallback (SSR_IDataSource.mqh:150-165) returns the same value.

3) SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:142-149 — SeekTo assigns now_msc = clamp(target); it does not round or normalise. So StepBars ALWAYS leaves the clock at a bar's last millisecond (boundary-1), which is precisely the input state that makes its own next invocation degenerate.

4) SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1176 — `if(m_clock.now_msc > before)` is false on the second press, so PendingRange/EmitWindow is skipped and the function returns emitted == 0 after Publish(). No fallback emission exists.

5) Group/production path confirmed identically: SSR_Panel.mqh:2293-2294 (SSR_CMD_STEP_FWD -> StepBars(1), STEP_FWD_10 -> StepBars(10)) -> SSR_GroupPort.mqh:439-440 -> SSR_MasterClock.mqh:341-352 with the byte-identical formula, then PumpTo(t) per member; CSSRReplayClock::AdvanceTo (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:126-139) returns early on `t <= now_msc` ("never backward, never a no-op step"), so the members do not move either. The group returns `true`, so the UI cannot even detect the no-op. SSR_Publisher.mqh:278 (remote control) has the same behaviour.

Arithmetic check of the bars==10 case: from 10:00:00.000 base=10:01:00.000, target=10:09:59.999 -> bars 10:00..10:09 = 10 bars (correct). Second press from 10:09:59.999: base=10:10:00.000, target=10:18:59.999 -> bars 10:10..10:18 = 9 bars. So n-1 after the first press, exactly as claimed.

Test coverage claim verified: SSR_T1_CoreEngine.mq5:283-291 asserts `e1 > 0` on the first step and only `after10 > start` after nine more, which the first step alone satisfies; SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:743 calls StepBars(10) once. T11 line 218 calls group StepBars(10) once. Nothing asserts a position after repeated steps.

Additional manifestation found while tracing (strengthens, does not contradict): the `-1` also defeats the gap-skip the comment at lines 1159-1163 says it was written for. Across a weekend, nb = Monday 01:00 raises base, but target = base-1 = Sunday 23:59:59.999, i.e. one ms BEFORE the first existing bar — the clock jumps 33h and emits zero bars; it takes a further press (or two) before bar Monday 01:00 is emitted. That is the same "presses of '>' that moved nothing on a Sunday" symptom the code claims to have fixed.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as written. One addition worth folding in: besides StepBars(1) being a no-op and StepBars(10) advancing 9 after the first press, the same `-1` makes the gap-skip branch (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1167-1168 / SSR_MasterClock.mqh:349-350) land 1 ms before the first bar after a weekend gap, so the gap-skipping press also emits zero bars — the exact symptom the comment at lines 1159-1163 claims the gap-skip fixed. A correct target is `base + (long)bars * SSR_MSC_PER_MIN - 1` when `now` is already at a bar end (or, equivalently, compute base from `now + 1` rather than `now`), applied in both SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1165-1169 and SSR_MasterClock.mqh:347-351.

Silent, triggered by a documented shortcut, corrupts virtual trade outcomes. HIGH stands; not CRITICAL because the trigger depends on a calibration-dependent cap whose threshold is unmeasured, the loss per event is bounded by the cap floor, and a later backward seek (which truncates and re-emits) can repair the chart even though the booked trade result is already wrong.

verdicts.reason: The arithmetic is deterministic and fully source-verifiable; I could not refute it. Because every successful step leaves the clock exactly at bar_open+59999, the second and all later presses are no-ops. The production path is confirmed: SSR_Panel.mqh:2293 (SSR_CMD_STEP_FWD -> port.StepBars(1)) -> SSR_GroupPort.mqh:439 -> CSSRReplayGroup::StepBars (SSR_MasterClock.mqh:341-367), same formula, then PumpTo -> CSSRReplayClock::AdvanceTo which returns early on t <= now_msc (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:126-138); CSSRGroupPort is the wired port (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:201). Either way target == now, so no unverified terminal behaviour is load-bearing. Test gap confirmed: SSR_T1_CoreEngine.mq5:283-291 asserts only after10 > start, which the first step alone satisfies. SSR_MSC_PER_MIN is 60000 (SSR_Types.mqh:31).

It is every SUBSEQUENT step that is short, because the step always leaves the clock at bar_open+59999: from there StepBars(1) computes target == now and is a complete no-op (returns 0, emits nothing), and StepBars(10) advances only 9 bars. So '->' works exactly once per play/pause cycle, and PgDn drifts one bar behind per press. (2) The finding understates one case: across a data gap the first step sets base = nb (the gap-end bar open) and target = nb-1, so the clock jumps the gap but emits nothing, and from nb-1 every further step recomputes target == now — the step control is then permanently dead at the weekend boundary until Play is pressed, and the gap-end bar can never be reached by stepping.

The user presses '->' , sees one candle form, then presses again and again with a completely inert chart, no error, no status message. Finally, CSSRReplayGroup::StepBars returns true unconditionally, so the panel treats the dead press as a success and shows no error - the user gets silent inaction, not a message.

SeekTo (1236) and Reset (1285) do RewindTo(actual) unconditionally, which is the internal inconsistency. The visible symptom (rebuilt bar opening at the 8571 ms tick, 42.9% along the first path segment) rests only on standard documented MT5 semantics the whole product already depends on (BID chart mode, bars rebuilt from ticks). Mechanism verified in full, and no MQL5 semantic assumption in it is wrong.

1. RestoreSnapshot (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1630-1633) assigns `m_state = snap.state` wholesale. SSRReplayState (SSR_ReplayState.mqh:33-40) carries status, speed_x100, data_mode, fidelity, last_error, last_error_text. These are plain structs (SSRReplayClock/SSRReplayCursor/SSRReplayTimeline are all declared `struct`), so member-wise copy including the string members is valid MQL5 and is exactly what happens — the assumption is sound and it compiles today.

Verified in SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh: Decide() recomputes m_effective purely from m_requested, so the emission path (EmitWindow line 332) keeps running the user's real choice — m_state.fidelity is display/persistence only.

3. Reachability is easy, not theoretical: SSR_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_MSC is 5 replay minutes (SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:33), checkpoints are taken inside Pump/PumpTo (lines 1042, 1115), and StepBackward (1450-1457) restores the nearest checkpoint at-or-before the target for a single '<-'. verdicts.corrected_claim: The strict `<` at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1637 is a genuine off-by-one (SeekTo and Reset use RewindTo(actual) unconditionally), but it requires TWO coincidences, not one, and the finding names only the first. (1) The auto-checkpoint's taken_at_msc must fall exactly on an M1 boundary. The clock advances by wall_delta*speed/100 from a jittery GetMicrosecondCount delta (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2734-2736), so this is a per-checkpoint coincidence of roughly 1/600 (at integer speeds >= 100x, where the advance is always a multiple of 100 ms) down to ~1/60000; the finding's "fixed 40 ms pumps at 100x" case is arithmetically correct but not the real timing source. (2) Crucially, the step-back target must land in the SAME minute as the checkpoint (target == B). StepBackward calls JumpForward(target) whenever target > now (line 1449-1458), and JumpForward computes bar_lo = floor(emitted+1) == B and bulk-writes [bar_lo, last_bar-1] via SeedBars/CustomRatesUpdate with the broker's full OHLC (lines 1362-1391) - so any restore whose target is in a later minute silently repairs the bar at B before the user sees anything. Only target == B (where no JumpForward runs) leaves the bar to be rebuilt from ticks i=1..7. When both conditions hit, the observable effect is one candle - the one the user stepped onto - whose open sits ~43% of the way from the true open toward the first extreme, with tick volume 7 instead of 8; high/low/close normally survive. There is no money-math or future-leak impact: the trading engine receives bars through PublishBar(ClipBar(...)) computed from the full pre-trim synthetic tick array (lines 236-300, 438-458), and FingerprintUpTo reads broker bars rather than the custom symbol. So: real, one-character fix (`<` -> `<=`), but cosmetic and near-unreachable - LOW at best, bordering on IMPROVEMENT.

The comment should describe now+JumpTo, not the cursor. (b) SSR_BAR_READ_CEILING (line 42) is dead — referenced nowhere; the nearby ArrayResize(m_ticks, 8192) at line 547 uses a bare literal. Either delete the define or use it. (c) The bulk threshold is not off by one millisecond for PgDn. With base = next M1 open, target = base + (bars-1)*60000 - 1 (line 1169) and PendingRange from = emitted+1, StepBars(10) from an xx:59.999 rest point owes 539,999 ms — 60,001 ms below SSR_BULK_THRESHOLD_MSC. The exact 599,999 near-miss belongs to an 11-bar step, which nothing in the UI issues. The only defensible observation is that a ten-bar step can never be treated as bulk, which is arguably the intended behaviour; if the threshold is meant to be expressed in bars, say so in bars. (d) In CSSRFidelityPolicy::Decide the NO_TICK_DATA degradation short-circuits the bulk branch, so a FULL_TICK request on a symbol with no tick history runs a bulk window at SYNTHETIC (8 ticks/bar) instead of BAR. This does NOT affect jumps or long catch-ups: JumpForward bulk-seeds all whole bars with SeedBars and only hands the target's partial bar to EmitWindow. It bites only on a pump after a stall at high speed, and the per-pump budget cap (line 398) bounds the extra work by deferring the remainder — a throughput inefficiency, not a stall. The fix is to evaluate the bulk rule independently of the tick-availability degradation.

verdicts.reason: Traced the full path and found no guard. (1) The group is not optional: SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1320 adds the primary controller to g_group and line 2788 makes g_group.Pump the sole pump path, so the idle branch at SSR_MasterClock.mqh:208 is always live. (2) The idle counter genuinely reaches 25 mid-bar: EmitWindow keeps only ticks whose stamp falls in [lo,hi] (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:462-489) so a mid-bar pump returns 0, yet m_cursor.Advance(consumed_to=hi,...) (line 529) still pushes emitted_msc to the mid-bar instant. Clock scaling is wall_delta*speed_x100/100 (SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:94-111) and synthetic stamps are open+i*59999/(n-1) (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:147), so 25 pumps x 40 ms x speed < 8571 ms holds for any speed below ~8.6x with 8 ticks/bar (below ~60x at BAR fidelity, i.e. including the default 30x start speed). (3) NextTimelineBarOpen (1138) -> NextBarOpen (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:302) starts CopyTime at after_msc/1000+1 s, so the partially played bar B is excluded and nb is the next EXISTING bar; the 'nb > now + 2 min' test is indeed measured from the mid-bar clock, so it passes whenever the next existing bar is >= B_open+3 min. (4) SeekAllTo (296) -> member JumpTo (1484) -> JumpForward (1519/1333): lo = emitted_msc+1 (mid-bar), bar_lo = SSRBarOpenMsc(lo) = B_open, last_bar = nb-60000, 'last_bar > bar_lo' is true, so ReadBars(bar_lo, last_bar-1) includes bar B and m_sink.SeedBars writes it in bulk (1383), with m_cursor.Advance(last_bar-1,0,n) moving past it (1390). The guard horizon is target=nb-1, past B's close, so B is written whole rather than clipped. (5) No observer sees it: PublishBar/PublishSegment are reached only from EmitWindow (500-514), and the trailing EmitWindow after the bulk covers [nb-60000, nb-1], a minute with no bar, so it emits nothing. (6) The consumer confirms the harm: CSSRTradingEngine runs CheckPendings/CheckStops/CheckStopout only inside OnTicks (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:600-615); OnClock (617) only bumps m_now_msc and OnBarContext (593) is only issued from PublishBar, so B's high/low are never evaluated and the engine's bar context stays the clipped first-tick bar. The comment at 202-204 ('the pause between two live ticks - never more than a minute of bar time - is left untouched') is exactly the wrong assumption, because the threshold is anchored at now rather than at the current bar's end.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as described, with three refinements. (a) Scope of the rest-of-bar loss is one bar per gap - the bar the clock happens to be inside when the 25-pump idle window closes - and it requires the next two or more M1 minutes to be absent from origin history (last bar of an index/futures CFD trading day, Friday close, any 2+ minute hole in thin forex). (b) The statement 'JumpForward never calls PublishBar/PublishTicks' is true only for the bulk portion: JumpForward does call EmitWindow for the pending range after the bulk write (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1393-1400), but in this scenario that range is [nb-60000, nb-1], a minute with no bar in history, so nothing is published; OnClock is genuinely never called from JumpForward. (c) The most damaging symptom is a visible contradiction rather than a silent one: because SeedBars writes bar B whole via CustomRatesUpdate, MetaTrader draws the complete candle, so the trainee watches the finished bar sweep through their stop or target while the virtual account, which never received ticks 1..7, does not react until the next existing bar's first tick (a gap price). The fix direction given is right - anchor the gap test at SSRBarOpenMsc(now)+SSR_MSC_PER_MIN, or require m_cursor.emitted_msc to have reached the current bar's last synthetic stamp before allowing the skip.

verdicts.reason: Every link in the chain is verifiable from source and none of it rests on shaky MQL5 semantics. Status stays PLAYING through JumpForward, so this is an automatic play-time skip, not a pause. The only runtime-dependent premise is that broker M1 history contains >=2-minute holes, which is the exact premise the gap-skip feature itself was written for (index/futures session ends, weekend edges), so it does not reduce this to speculation.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The finding is real; two details are inaccurate. (a) JumpForward is NOT tick-silent: it calls EmitWindow(tlo, thi) at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1398 for the bar containing the target. In this scenario that bar (nb-60000) lies inside the history hole, so ReadBars yields nothing and nothing is published - the outcome stands, but the blanket claim 'JumpForward never calls PublishBar/PublishTicks/OnClock' is wrong (OnClock is also called every pump from PumpTo:1102-1104, just not from JumpForward). (b) At trigger time m_cursor.emitted_msc is the mid-bar CLOCK value, not B_open: each idle pump still calls m_cursor.Advance(hi, 0, ...) (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:411/492/524, consumed_to = hi). bar_lo = SSRBarOpenMsc(emitted+1) is B_open either way, so the bulk write still swallows bar B. Accurate statement: when the replay clock is inside a partially emitted M1 bar B and the next two or more M1 bars are absent from origin history, 25 idle pumps (~1 s of wall time at InpPumpMs=40, reached at any speed where the next synthetic tick is more than ~1 s of bar time away - i.e. <=~8x at 8 ticks/bar, <60x at BAR fidelity) trigger SeekAllTo(nb-1), whose JumpForward bulk-writes bar B with SeedBars. Bulk bars are published to no observer, so the trading engine never sees ticks 1..n-1 of bar B (its whole intrabar high/low/close path, or at BAR fidelity its only tick): its last price stays at B's open, its OnBarContext stays the first-tick-clipped bar, and any SL/TP/pending inside B's range is not evaluated until the first tick of the next existing bar (a post-gap price). The chart itself is correct (bar B is written whole and replay time has legitimately passed B's end); the loss is confined to observer notifications. The printed 'market closed from <mid-bar time>' is likewise misleading. Impact is one bar of tick fidelity per gap event, but it recurs at every session end on index/futures CFDs and at weekend edges, silently changing virtual trade outcomes - the product's core output. Fix direction as stated (measure the gap from SSRBarOpenMsc(now)+60000, or require m_cursor.emitted_msc >= SSRBarOpenMsc(now)+59999 before skipping) is correct.

Traced the exact path and found no guard, clamp or earlier check that prevents it.

1. Pump (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1006-1018): clock advances by wall_delta_ms; `m_cursor.PendingRange(now, lo, hi)` yields `lo = emitted_msc+1`, `hi = now` (SSR_ReplayCursor.mqh:54-57). EmitWindow(lo, hi) is called every pump where now > before.
2. Fidelity: `Decide(hi - lo)` with a 40 ms owed span is below SSR_BULK_THRESHOLD_MSC, so it returns the requested fidelity (SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:120-129) — SYNTHETIC_TICK or BAR, i.e. the bar-driven branch.
3. `bar_lo = SSRBarOpenMsc(lo, PERIOD_M1)` (line 380) is the open of the minute currently in progress. `CSSRMt5BarProvider::ReadBars` → `CSSRBarWindow::Read` copies bars whose open lies in the **inclusive** range [from_msc, to_msc] (SSR_BarWindow.mqh:253-286), so the in-progress bar is returned on every pump.
4. The "skip bars already consumed" loop at line 407-409 is `SSRToMsc(m_bars[first].time) < bar_lo`; since m_bars[0].time == bar_lo exactly, it is strictly-less and never skips it. `first` stays 0.
5. Line 441-442 calls Synthesize()/SynthesizeClose() on that same bar again, and `SpreadFor(bar)` is unconditional inside both (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:123 and :197). SpreadFor increments m_bars_recorded (+ m_spread_sum_pts, + max) or m_bars_fixed on every call (:54-65).
6. Trimming to (lo, hi] happens *after* SpreadFor, at lines 461-470, so a pump that keeps zero ticks still bumps the counter. Under BAR fidelity the single tick sits at bar_open+59999 and is kept only on the pump that crosses the minute end, yet the counter is bumped ~1500 times.
7. The ClipBar comment block at lines 445-457 explicitly documents "the second pump into one minute", i.e. repeated re-synthesis of the forming bar is the intended design — the counters were simply never made idempotent for it.
8. No reset exists on the live path: `ResetSpreadCounters` is referenced only in SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:2996, never in the controller or the EA, so the inflation also compounds across rewind/step-back re-emission.
9. Consumer: ReportSpreadOnce (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2234-2301) returns only when `total < 120 && g_timer_ticks < 500`, so total >= 120 alone fires it — reached inside the first M1 bar (120 pumps ≈ 4.8 s at 1x). It then prints "on %d of the first %d bars", and the author's own comment at :2253-2258 asserts "Bars are only counted when ticks are SYNTHESISED from them", which the code does not honour per-bar. Same counters are re-exported at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:657-660.

No guard found anywhere. Defect exists as described.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate, with two refinements. (a) WidestRecordedSpread is a running maximum (m_spread_max_pts, SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:60-61), so it is NOT distorted by the repeat counting — only BarsWithRecordedSpread, BarsWithFixedSpread and AverageRecordedSpread are. The average is pump-count-weighted per bar, so at a constant speed it stays approximately right and only skews when the speed varies (step-through and 0.1x bars weigh hundreds of times more than 200x bars). (b) The inflation is not limited to SYNTHETIC_TICK: under SSR_FIDELITY_BAR the same bar is passed to SynthesizeClose on every pump while its single tick is trimmed away (keep == 0), so counters rise for minutes during which nothing at all was emitted. It also compounds on rewind/step-back, since ResetSpreadCounters is never called outside QA smoke. The reported bar counts are therefore synthesis-call counts, which the printed line ("on N of the first M bars") and the controller getters both present as bar counts.

verdicts.reason: Every link verified in code. (1) The gap-skip is on the default path: SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1320 adds the primary controller to g_group unconditionally and line 2788 is the program's only pump, so InpAlsoSymbols is irrelevant. (2) Trigger arithmetic holds: InpPumpMs=40 (line 1574), synthetic stamps 8571 ms apart (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:132,147), so 25 idle pumps (1 s wall) are reached between two ticks of the SAME bar at any speed below ~8.5x (below ~60x at BAR fidelity). The 'nb > now + 2 min' test then passes only when two or more consecutive M1 bars after the current one are missing, so there is no false fire in dense data - but it does fire mid-bar at a gap edge (day/session close, broker rollover, thin-hour holes). (3) The bulk write of the unfinished bar is real: SeekAllTo -> CSSRReplayController::JumpTo (1482-1519) sends a forward target straight to JumpForward with no bar-boundary snapping; in JumpForward bar_lo = SSRBarOpenMsc(m_cursor.emitted_msc+1) is bar B's own open while B is partly emitted, last_bar = nb-60000 > bar_lo, ReadBars returns B, the guard horizon (target = nb-1) does not filter it, m_sink.SeedBars writes it whole and m_cursor.Advance(last_bar-1,0,n) steps past it. (4) Observers receive nothing for B: the only publish in JumpForward is EmitWindow(1398) over the bar containing target = nb-1, which is a non-existent gap minute, so zero ticks. (5) Impact is money-relevant: CSSRTradingEngine::OnTicks(600)/CheckStops(513-545) evaluate SL/TP per tick with no bar-range fallback, and StopFill(492-511) takes the worse of level and touching price - so a stop the visible candle traded through is either filled at the post-gap price (a larger loss than the real path) or missed entirely if the post-gap open is back on the favourable side, while the chart shows the full candle. Reachable in normal use at the 0.1x-7x speeds a trainee trades at (not at the 30x default), roughly once per replayed session boundary, and entirely silent. HIGH stands under the impact lens (distorts the virtual account's P/L and the core 'did my stop get hit' judgement the product exists to teach); it does not touch real orders or leak future data, which is why it is not CRITICAL.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Two small corrections to the description, neither affecting the defect. (a) JumpForward is not publish-free: it calls EmitWindow at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1398, which does PublishBar/PublishTicks (506/515). In this scenario that window covers only the minute containing target = nb-1, which is a missing gap bar, so nothing is published - the substance ('bar B's remaining ticks never reach observers') is correct, but the reason is 'the emitted window is empty', not 'JumpForward never publishes'. (b) Trigger needs a speed below ~8.5x at 8 ticks/bar (below ~60x at BAR fidelity), so it does NOT fire at the shipped default InpStartSpeed=30.0; it fires at the 0.1x-7x ladder stops a trainee manually trading actually uses. Additional consequence worth recording: after the skip the engine's next price is the next existing bar's open, and StopFill (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:492-511) takes the worse of the level and the touching price, so an orderly stop-out inside the visible candle is re-modelled as a gap - filled worse than the level, or, if the post-gap open is back on the favourable side, never filled at all - while MAE/MFE excursions and the ambiguous-bar labelling for that bar are also lost.

verdicts.reason: Every link in the chain is present in the code and none depends on unverified MQL5 runtime semantics. SSR_ReplayCursor.mqh:55 makes lo = emitted_msc+1 and Advance() pushes emitted_msc to hi each pump, so lo lands mid-minute; SSR_ReplayController.mqh:378 floors it with SSRBarOpenMsc (SSR_Time.mqh:33) to the current bar's open; CSSRBarWindow::Read (SSR_BarWindow.mqh:257-277) is inclusive at from_msc so that same bar comes back; the skip loop at :407-409 compares against the identical bar_lo and skips nothing; Synthesize/SynthesizeClose are then called for it (:441-442) and SpreadFor is unconditional inside both (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:123, :197). There is no last-counted-bar memo and no dedup: ResetSpreadCounters is only ever called from SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:2996, and the only product consumer of the counters is ReportSpreadOnce (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2234-2301), which presents them as 'N of the first M bars'. The QA test does call Synthesize directly three times and so cannot observe the inflation. The only runtime assumption is that a millisecond timer fires more than once per replay minute, which holds for every speed below ~1500x at InpPumpMs=40, so the direction of the defect is not speed-contingent even though its magnitude is.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Two details of the finding are wrong or overstated, but the defect is real. (1) WidestRecordedSpread is a running max (m_spread_max_pts, SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:61-62) and is NOT pump-weighted — re-counting the same bar cannot change the maximum, so 'widest' remains correct. Only BarsWithRecordedSpread, BarsWithFixedSpread and AverageRecordedSpread are corrupted; the average becomes weighted by how many pumps each bar was re-synthesised over, so bars replayed slowly or stepped through dominate bars replayed at 30x. (2) The inflation factor is ~pumps-per-bar, which is speed-dependent, not a flat ~1500: at the default InpStartSpeed=30 with InpPumpMs=40 each pump advances 1200 ms of replay time, so ~50 synthesis calls per M1 bar and the 'total >= 120' gate in ReportSpreadOnce is crossed after ~2.4 real bars, not after the first bar; ~1500 applies only at 1x. Either way the printed line names bar counts in the hundreds or thousands for a handful of actual bars. Additionally, the same per-pump re-synthesis inflates bars_used at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:531, which feeds m_cursor.bar_count -> m_state.bars_consumed and is displayed to the user as the 'Bars' figure in the Session tab (SSR_Panel.mqh:1687), and is also persisted by SSR_PositionFile.mqh:77 and cross-checked on snapshot restore (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1859) — a second, user-visible instance of the same double-count that the finding does not mention. The recommended fix (count only when the bar's open time differs from the last counted open) applies to both counters.

verdicts.reason: The mechanism is confirmed from code. PendingRange yields (emitted+1, now] — a 40 ms slice at 1x — and EmitWindow widens it to bar_lo = SSRBarOpenMsc(lo, PERIOD_M1), so ReadBars always returns the bar containing the clock; FutureGuard::FilterRates keeps it (open <= horizon = now) and the skip loop (time < bar_lo) cannot drop it since the two are equal. Synthesize/SynthesizeClose therefore run on the same bar every pump and SpreadFor is unconditional in both, so m_bars_recorded/m_bars_fixed count synthesis calls. bars_used++ and NoteBar() are also above the `if(keep > 0)` guard, so even a pump that emits no ticks counts a bar. Reachable on every session at default settings within seconds of pressing Play. Only the magnitudes in the claim are wrong, and the finding understates the scope: the same recount also inflates the panel's on-screen Bars row. No money-math or future-leak consequence (the per-bar spread applied to ticks is still correct), so MEDIUM is the right severity — a reporting/telemetry defect, visible but not corrupting.
verdicts.corrected_claim:
The root cause is as described (SpreadFor at SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:54 counts synthesis calls because the bar under the clock is re-synthesised every pump), but two details need correcting.

1) The printed numbers are NOT in the thousands. ReportSpreadOnce (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2259) fires as soon as `total >= 120`, so it prints total ~= 120 after ~120 pumps: at 1x/40 ms that is 4.8 s of replay time, i.e. still inside the FIRST M1 bar; at the default InpStartSpeed=30 it is ~2.4 min, i.e. 2-3 distinct bars. The line therefore reads entirely plausible while describing a 1-3 bar sample as 120 bars, which makes it undetectable rather than obviously broken. SpreadAverage/SpreadWidest degenerate to that one bar's spread, and the `recorded == 0` branch will state "NO bar in the first 120 carried a recorded spread ... This history has no spread in it" on the strength of a single bar.

2) The blast radius is wider than the spread counters. The same unconditional per-pump `bars_used++` feeds m_cursor.bar_count -> m_state.bars_consumed -> the panel Stats sheet's "Bars" row (MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_Panel.mqh:1687), the saved position file (SSR_PositionFile.mqh:77) and m_metrics.RecordPump. cursor.tick_count is correct (it adds only the window-trimmed `emitted`), so the two rows diverge visibly: one replayed M1 minute at 1x with 8 ticks/bar displays Bars 1500 / Ticks 8 on screen.

Fix: de-duplicate on bar open time — count a bar (both the spread counters and bars_used/NoteBar) only when m_bars[i].time differs from the last counted open, or move the counting into the controller at the point a bar is fully consumed.

(2) "the next k checkpoints destroy 5h of rewindable history at the far end" overstates the magnitude by ~an order of magnitude: the next k writes consume the k oldest slots (k x 5 min), which a correct ring would consume anyway; the real loss is that depth is capped at 64-k instead of returning to 64 for the following 64-k intervals. (3) The precondition is narrower than "user steps back through the last k checkpoints": DropFrom(now+1) runs after the restore, so k = the number of checkpoints strictly newer than the landing time — a 1-bar step back usually drops 0 and leaves no hole at all; holes need a rewind past the newest checkpoint (bookmark return, large jump), and the full-ring variant additionally needs >5h20m of replay in one session. Also: the recommended fix is unsafe as written. m_count is not a live count, it is the array fill high-water mark that NearestAtOrBefore and DropFrom use as the iteration bound over slots 0..m_count-1, which is valid only because writes always start at slot 0 and advance contiguously. Setting m_count to the survivor count on a full ring (live entries scattered over all 64 slots except h-k..h-1) would make NearestAtOrBefore iterate 0..63-k and miss live entries in the high slots — turning a wasted-capacity improvement into a real rewind defect. A safe fix is to rewind m_head only (to the slot after the newest survivor) and leave m_count as the fill mark, or add a separate live-count accessor for display.
